| [THEORY-043](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-043.md) v6 | Nested-agent minds split on unprincipled criteria | Minsky's society of mind builds a mind downward, out of agents that are not minds. The dispute narrows to phenomenal consciousness, and every published way to accept the downward move while refusing the upward one is either an anti-nesting principle (Putnam's stipulation, IIT's exclusion postulate, Kammerer's functional version), each introduced for or justified weakly by the verdict it gives, or an architectural criterion that would count against a loosely coupled society of mind as much as against a nation. | [THEORY-057](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-057.md) | Emotion categories are not natural kinds | Barrett (2017), [LIT-542](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-542.md): degeneracy, population thinking, and a table of findings in which no region, network, pattern or neuron is consistent for an emotion category. She rejects basic-emotion and causal appraisal theories as positing a "Lockean essence". This is the record's only read statement of the view. The record's philosophy holdings sharpen it. | [THEORY-058](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-058.md) v2 | Disorders are causal loops, not latent causes | Three traditions that do not cite one another for it put self-sustaining loops where a latent cause would be. On the functional level that is "highest-order binding" into a single causal role, and on the neural level the prediction of "one single area of maximal causal density", after Tononi and Edelman's dynamic core. "What you subjectively experience upon experiencing your world as coherent is the high internal correlation strength between a subset of physical events in your own brain." A unified world comes before a self: the minimal case is "Selfless Snapshot Consciousness", and fully depersonalized states are "non-subjective consciousness". The neural half is a cited hypothesis, the précis says little is known, and how the cluster becomes one subject's is left open. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-064](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-064.md) | Self is an unrecognised self-model's content | Metzinger's précis of Being No One (2005), [LIT-568](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-568.md), with his encyclopedia article "Self models" ([LIT-450](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-450.md)): a phenomenal self is a transparent self-model, one whose representational character "is not accessible to subjective experience", so that the system experiences its content "simply as ourselves". Selfhood is "a function realized by a lack of information", and "no such things as selves exist in the world". Transparency is graded, and the perspective itself is modelled, as a phenomenal model of the intentionality relation. Two things are offered: a prediction (a wholly opaque self-model would abolish selfhood) and an ontological stipulation. The précis adds no evidence; its case studies are in the book, unread. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-065](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-065.md) | Collective agents are agents in the same sense | Korsgaard (2014), [LIT-587](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-587.md): an action is a movement "backed by the agent as a whole", and ordinary attribution implies that the agent was active and that the action expresses who she is. Following the categorical and hypothetical imperatives gives action the form of self-determined efficacy; the content of the maxims chosen under that form constitutes practical identity. Self-consciousness of one's own attitudes breaks the unity an animal is given, and reason is the work of rebuilding it, so unity of agency "is an achievement, not a given", and people can act together "in the most literal sense". The Tanner Lectures ([LIT-564](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-564.md)) supply the reflective structure the chapter assumes. Argued, with the Kantian premise assumed and the collective mechanism stated in a paragraph. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-067](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-067.md) | Self-control needs no faculty of will | Ainslie's précis ([LIT-586](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-586.md)): hyperbolic discounting makes a smaller, sooner reward temporarily preferred, so successive "interests" conflict as in a repeated prisoner's dilemma. Treating a choice as a precedent bundles the series, and summed hyperbolic curves favour the larger, later rewards; a lapse costs credibility. Will is that recursion, not an organ. Schelling ([LIT-602](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-602.md)) describes the same divided chooser from the side of tactics: we manage our later selves as we manage other people. The mathematics of bundling is sound; that willpower works this way is argued, and the précis concedes it is hard to test directly. It is a claim about how control is achieved, not about whose control is self-governance. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-069](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-069.md) v4 | Bimanual switching is an HKB phase transition | Kelso's 2021 retrospective ([LIT-601](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-601.md)) states the Haken–Kelso–Bunz model: relative phase φ between the hands obeys dφ/dt = −a sin φ − 2b sin 2φ, so in-phase and anti-phase are both stable for b/a > 1/4 and anti-phase loses stability below it as movement speeds up. With noise the switch is a nonequilibrium phase transition, and the reported data show enhanced fluctuations and critical slowing before it. Many effectors act as one through a collective variable, with no controller choosing the pattern. Proposed, because the relaxation-time and hysteresis data are not read first-hand. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-070](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-070.md) | Control allocation is a cost-benefit computation | Shenhav, Botvinick & Cohen ([LIT-585](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-585.md)) unify dACC's many reported functions as one: deciding whether, where and how much control to allocate. A control signal has an identity (a task set, a threshold, an attention template) and an intensity; its expected value is its probability-weighted payoff, with future value discounted, minus an intrinsic cost rising with intensity. dACC monitors and specifies; lateral prefrontal and subcortical structures implement. The paper reviews evidence and fits nothing, so Proposed. It does not say what the cost is, how EVC is computed, or that it governs emotion regulation. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-071](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-071.md) v3 | Individuality alone is not agency | Barandiaran, Di Paolo & Rohde (2009), [LIT-566](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-566.md), read in [NOTE-458](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-458.md). The three conditions are that the system distinguishes itself from its environment with no observer doing it, that it is the active source of modulations of its coupling with the environment, and that it regulates that coupling against norms its own organisation sets. Each is necessary, and together they are claimed to be sufficient. Individuality is the precondition of the other two and does not suffice. A cell in passive osmosis, a kitten warmed by its mother and a person with a Parkinsonian tremor are each individuals, and none of them is acting. The generative definition is an open autonomous organisation that adaptively modulates its coupling so as to maintain itself. Here "autonomy" and "self" mean organisational closure. They do not mean a subject or self-governance. Proposed: a conceptual analysis checked against intuitive cases, with an asymmetry criterion its authors call incomplete. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-072](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-072.md) v5 | Organisms differ from flames by differentiation | The record's first answer to the demarcation question that [NOTE-094](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-094.md) reports. Prigogine ([LIT-516](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-516.md)) supplies the dissipative structures, and nothing in his account separates them from organisms. Mossio, Saborido & Moreno (2009, [LIT-570](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-570.md)) grant a candle flame organisational closure. Its one macroscopic pattern keeps up the conditions of the combustion that makes it. They draw the line at organisational differentiation: in an organism several distinct structures make distinct contributions, where a flame makes "a unique contribution". Montévil & Mossio (2015, [LIT-582](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-582.md)) narrow closure to mutual dependence among constraints. Each constraint must be both produced by and productive of another, with at least one slow and one fast dependence. On the record's reading, that builds differentiation into closure, as Mossio and Bich (2014) already say of closure of constraints. No paper analyses a flame under the 2015 definitions. Neither paper says closure defines an organism. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-074](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-074.md) | Self-reports miss implicit true-self accessibility | Schlegel, Hicks, Arndt & King (2009), [LIT-606](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-606.md): true-self accessibility, the speed of "me" judgments for traits a person takes to be her true self, correlated .05 with AI-3 authenticity and .20 with basic need satisfaction (N = 124), and each predicted meaning in life independently. The authors read this as showing the constructs differ, and concede the difference is confounded with method, reaction time against self-report. The two self-reports correlated .52, and felt autonomy was only one third of the need-satisfaction composite, whose autonomy items include "I can pretty much be myself". So the paper separates the implicit measure from both self-reports, and does not separate authenticity from autonomy. Proposed: one sample for the correlations, method unresolved. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-075](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-075.md) | Moral obligation follows from valuing humanity | Korsgaard (1992), [LIT-564](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-564.md): because human consciousness is reflective, an agent must act on reasons, and so must identify with some law, a "practical identity": "a description under which you value yourself". "Your reasons express your identity, your nature; your obligations spring from what that identity forbids." Obligation is "the reflective rejection of a threat to your identity", unconditional where violation would be worse than death. Identities are a "jumble" and differ across social worlds, so this much yields no morality. Moral obligation enters because valuing any identity requires valuing one's humanity, the source of all one's reasons. "The Normative Constitution of Agency" ([LIT-587](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-587.md)) later makes practical identity the content of maxims chosen under the formal norms. Argued, with the key steps flagged by their author as sketchy; the commentaries and reply are unread. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-076](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-076.md) | Self-governance is intrapersonal shared intention | Bratman (2018), [LIT-567](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-567.md): an agent governs herself over time when she is self-governing at each time along a planned activity and her intentions at those times interlock as the intentions of people acting together do, so that she acts "together" with herself. Her standpoints include a conditional, reflexive end of her own diachronic self-governance, which is what lets resolve against temptation be self-governed while following through on Kavka's toxin is not. He rejects the bargaining model (McClennen, Ainslie) in two sentences and calls narrative unity less basic in one. A philosophical model argued from cases; the analogy is partial by its author's account and its terms come from a book the record has not read. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-077](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-077.md) v3 | Autonomous goals get more effort and well-being | Sheldon & Elliot (1999), [LIT-589](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-589.md): a goal is self-concordant to the degree its reasons are identified or intrinsic rather than external or introjected. In two semester-long student samples, self-concordance predicted sustained effort, and effort fully carried its link to attainment (self-concordance β = .02 and .08, ns, with effort in the model). In the same two samples attainment raised well-being more when goals were self-concordant (interaction β = .11, .23), partly through accumulated daily experiences of autonomy, competence and relatedness. Everything is self-report and correlational, and the structural models fit only after revision. It is evidence for the autonomous end of SDT's continuum, not for integration as distinct from identification. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-078](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-078.md) v2 | Top Fisher eigenvalues span the class means | Papyan (2019), [LIT-619](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-619.md): for softmax cross-entropy the Gauss–Newton matrix G, which is the model's Fisher averaged over inputs, is an uncentred second moment of logit derivatives indexed by class and logit. It decomposes exactly into four terms (Eq. 28), and its top C eigenvalues match those of the class-mean term G₁. Papyan (2020), [LIT-613](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-613.md), splits those C into one global-mean outlier and C − 1 between-class ones, finds a C(C − 1) cross-class mini-bulk beneath them, and proves the whole pattern for a Gaussian toy model. Papyan (2018), [LIT-617](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-617.md), supplies the measurements and the attribution of the Hessian's outliers to G. The decomposition is algebra. That G₁ carries the outliers is measured, by eye, under a training protocol narrower than practice. So this is Proposed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-079](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-079.md) v3 | Laplace BMR misprices singular reductions | The filer's synthesis, stated by no source. BMR's closed form (Friston & Penny, [LIT-620](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-620.md), Eq. 9; Friston, Parr & Zeidman, [LIT-614](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-614.md), Eq. 11) charges a reduction through log-determinants of Gaussian precisions, which is MacKay's regular Occam factor. Watanabe, [LIT-616](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-616.md), says that models with hierarchical layers or hidden variables are singular, that no normal distribution approximates their posterior, and that their free energy grows as λ log n. BMR is applied to exactly such models: mixtures, hierarchical empirical Bayes and latent states. Neither literature cites the other. The exact identity is untouched ([THEORY-081](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-081.md)). The claim is about its Laplace form, and a test on reduced-rank regression would settle it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-080](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-080.md) v4 | NTK eigenvalues schedule the Occam penalty | The filer's synthesis, stated by no source. Its exact half is filed as the record's own claim, CLAIM-384; what stays here is the spherical account. A network linearised at initialisation, with an isotropic Gaussian prior on its parameters and Gaussian noise, is MacKay's linear-in-parameters model ([LIT-623](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-623.md)). Its Occam factor is −½ Σ log(1 + βλ_a/α) over the eigenvalues of JᵀJ. These are the empirical NTK's, which on uniform spherical data form Bietti & Bach's degree blocks, nµ_k with multiplicity N(d, k) ([LIT-608](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-608.md)). Degrees whose βnµ_k exceeds α pay about ½ log n per harmonic, and degrees below pay almost nothing. With µ_k ~ k^(−d), the number of paid directions γ grows as n^((d−1)/d), not as the parameter count. Basri et al.'s bound ([LIT-612](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-612.md), Eq. 14) is the matching data-fit term. The kernel's decay exponent is the schedule of the penalty. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-084](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-084.md) v4 | Lazy Fisher inherits NTK harmonic blocks | The filer's synthesis, stated by no source. The identity is linear algebra: JᵀJ (parameters × parameters) and JJᵀ (samples × samples) have the same non-zero eigenvalues. Under squared loss JᵀJ is the Gauss–Newton matrix and the Fisher. JJᵀ is the empirical NTK Gram matrix, which in the kernel regime on uniform spherical data has the degree-block spectrum of Bietti & Bach (2021), [LIT-608](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-608.md): µ_k with multiplicity N(d, k). The threshold claim draws on Cao et al. (2019), [LIT-624](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-624.md). Their guarantees are stated only for whole eigenspaces, with sample costs that grow as the gap below them shrinks. It also draws on Basri et al. (2019), [LIT-612](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-612.md), where a structural zero block shows up in a finite sample as small non-zero eigenvalues. No paper filed computes a Fisher spectrum in this regime. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-085](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-085.md) v2 | K-FAC misplaces cross-class Fisher pairings | Papyan (2020), [LIT-613](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-613.md): per layer, the Fisher is a weighted sum of Kronecker products of features and backpropagated errors (Eq. 7.5), and its class outliers come from class means of gradients that are approximately h_c ⊗ δ_c. K-FAC (Martens & Grosse 2015, [LIT-622](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-622.md)) multiplies the class-averaged feature covariance by the class-averaged error covariance. Papyan finds its outliers and mini-bulks "drastically misaligned", and the class-wise CFAC aligns much better at deep layers. The identity relating the two, CFAC − K-FAC = the class-weighted between-class covariance of the factors, is the record's own and is filed as CLAIM-391. The evidence for the mechanism is one MLP, spectra only, judged by eye. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-088](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-088.md) v2 | Cortical slow waves are organized by spirals | Xu, Long, Feng & Gong (2023), [LIT-638](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-638.md): in Human Connectome Project fMRI band-passed to 0.01–0.1 Hz, the cortical phase field holds about 16–19 spirals at a time around phase singularities, concentrated on boundaries between functional regions; their centres drift superdiffusively, opposite spirals annihilate (51% fully, 46% partly) and like ones repel (2.6%), and their positions and senses decode task condition above a raw-amplitude decoder. One source, fMRI only, at a spatial scale chosen because it maximised that decoding; the routing of activity flow is read from phase gradients and a phase-oscillator model, never perturbed. The kinship with Belousov–Zhabotinsky spirals and pattern-formation defects is the record's analogy, not the paper's. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-089](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-089.md) | Content has narrow-role and referential factors | Block (1986), [LIT-648](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-648.md), and Block (1987), [LIT-625](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-625.md). Meaning has a conceptual-role component "entirely 'in the head'", an expression's "total causal role, abstractly described" in inference and decision, which twins share and which explains their behaviour, and an external component relating representations to referents and truth conditions. Conceptual role fixes the nature of the referential factor, not reference. A one-factor theory with long-arm roles must, to get Twin Earth truth conditions right, import normal context, causal chains of borrowed reference and experts; chop off what lies outside the skin and the rest is the short-arm role, so the difference is "merely verbal". Social meaning is assigned to the referential factor or to a third, social factor, and is only sketched. Proposed: no identity conditions for roles, and narrow content is given room, not shown explanatory. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-090](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-090.md) v2 | Basic affective consciousness is subcortical | Newen & Montemayor's ALARM theory (2025), [LIT-626](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-626.md): basic arousal, a sensitivity to pain, pleasure and other basic affect without focused attention, can be realised without cortex, by the upper brainstem and thalamus, and its function is to alarm the bodily agent when a homeostatic variable leaves its range, giving the signal "100% weight" through "rather rigid behavioural programmes without choices". Damasio & Carvalho (2013), [LIT-388](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-388.md), supply the subcortical clause independently: feeling is generated in the upper brainstem and the insula is not needed. Both papers argue from cited evidence and offer no new data, and neither has a marker that tells a felt alarm from an unfelt one. The function clause rests on ALARM alone, and Veit's account rivals it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-091](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-091.md) | Joint loss doesn't show a phenomenal function | Block (1995), [LIT-643](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-643.md), §6. Marcel, Flanagan, van Gulick and Schacter argue from the thirsty blindsight patient who does not reach for the water, and Searle from Penfield's petit mal automatisms, that a function of phenomenal consciousness is to let information guide action. In blindsight access is missing too, and in petit mal nothing shows experience is missing at all. "The fallacy is: an obvious function of the machinery of access-consciousness is illicitly transferred to phenomenal consciousness." That experience causes access, so that the function is experience's after all, is "a bold hypothesis, not a fallacy", and the deficit cannot decide it. Proposed: single-source, and the distinction it rests on is argued from conceivable cases. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-092](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-092.md) v3 | Behavioural capacity doesn't fix intelligence | Block (1981), [LIT-642](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-642.md): the strongest behaviourist conception of intelligence, a capacity to give sensible responses to any sequence of inputs, "whatever they may be", is met by a machine that stores every sensible conversation of a test's length and looks up its next reply, yet "the machine has the intelligence of a toaster". So psychologism is true: two systems alike in all actual and counterfactual behaviour can differ in intelligence through the processing that mediates it. Block (1995), [LIT-630](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-630.md), n. 1: the same machine refutes the wider claim that there is no mental difference without a behavioural one. It is a claim about constitution, not evidence: performance stays evidence for competence. It names no required kind of processing, and its machine is a lookup table, not a trained network. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-093](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-093.md) v2 | Homeostatic feelings make contents conscious | Damasio & Damasio (2022), [LIT-628](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-628.md), an essay with no data, read only through a summarising fetch tool, so its wording is paraphrased here. Consciousness is the spontaneous identification of mind contents as belonging to one's own organism, and a continuous stream of homeostatic feelings, from hunger and pain to a faint feeling of existing, supplies it; the feelings are conscious in themselves and confer consciousness on exteroceptive images. They are hybrid because interoceptive axons are unmyelinated, partly non-synaptic and outside a systematic blood–brain barrier, so viscera and circulating molecules act on the neurons that map them. Damasio & Carvalho (2013), [LIT-388](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-388.md), read in full, supply the upper-brainstem site of feeling and the unmyelinated-fibre proposal. Proposed: the identification is a definition, the mechanism an interpretation of anatomy, and the clinical evidence does not separate this account from its rivals. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-094](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-094.md) | Neither report nor no-report isolates the NCC | Block (2007), [LIT-646](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-646.md), framed the methodological puzzle: the neural basis of experience can be found only by deciding whether it includes the machinery of access, and the evidence comes through report. The no-report paradigm was the answer. Block (2019), [LIT-637](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-637.md), argues it has "a fatal flaw": subjects not asked to report still think about what they see, and that thought is aligned with the percept (the "bored monkey" problem). Eliminating report isolates the basis of experience "only if it eliminates post-perceptual cognitive processing" correlated with the percept. Brascamp et al.'s inconspicuous rivalry, whose switches subjects detected at chance, is the one such design Block offers. The method is specific to rivalry so far, and Block says there may be no general solution. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-095](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-095.md) v3 | Inverted Earth leaves only internal accounts | Block (1990), [LIT-634](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-634.md): on Inverted Earth colours and colour words are inverted, so a subject fitted with inverting lenses notices nothing. After long residence, or for a twin with a molecule-for-molecule identical brain raised there, the intentional content of the experience of the sky inverts and so does its long-arm functional role, while qualitative content stays the same; Q = F₁, Q = F₂ and F₁ ≠ F₂ breaks transitivity of identity. Block (2003), [LIT-635](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-635.md), turns the case on externalist representationism: for colour there is no shared appearance property left to explain the sameness, and long-term memory blocks the gradual-shift reply, so "mental paint" is what stays the same. Proposed: both rest on an externalist shift of content and on first-person sameness, and Block concedes that a short-arm functional theory of qualia would escape. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-096](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-096.md) | Consciousness is global neuronal ignition | Mashour, Roelfsema, Changeux & Dehaene (2020), [LIT-631](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-631.md), a review by the theory's proponents. Conscious access is "a non-linear network ignition" that amplifies and sustains a representation so that local processors can access it, in a distributed core of long-range layer II/III and V pyramidal neurons with prefrontal cortex a key hub but "not ... the exclusive territory". Ignition is exclusive: one content at a time. Evidence: seen and unseen trials diverge after about 200 ms across modalities; in van Vugt et al.'s monkeys, missed stimuli drove V1 and V4 but only reported ones, and false alarms, ignited sustained prefrontal firing, and the signal-detection threshold is the ignition threshold. The review adopts the premise that global availability "is what we subjectively experience as a conscious state", and calls experience without access untested; that premise, not the access data, is where it rivals overflow and the sensory account. Single source, second-hand evidence, and the P3 question conceded open. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-097](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-097.md) | Distant co-ripples carry forebrain coordination | Verzhbinsky, Daume, Cheng, Rutishauser & Halgren (2026), [LIT-633](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-633.md): in 1,373 single units from five bilateral forebrain regions of 35 epilepsy patients doing a Sternberg task, ripples (70–100 Hz, about 70 ms) co-occur between bundles at a median 5% at every tract distance from 71 to 223 mm, and unit pairs co-fire a median 34% more during co-ripples than in no-ripple periods, beyond a rate-only null and with no loss over distance. The gain rises with load (13% in maintenance, 19% at retrieval), and encoding co-firing for a stimulus recurs at retrieval in 0.29% of cell-pair trials in co-ripples against 0.14% outside them. Correlational throughout: one task, two load levels, clinically placed electrodes, nothing perturbed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-098](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-098.md) v4 | Consciousness is sensory recurrence, not PFC | Block's "back of the head" position, from three papers. Block (2005), [LIT-629](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-629.md): a phenomenal NCC (for seen motion, recurrent MT/V5–V1 activity) and an access NCC (frontoparietal broadcasting), with winner-take-all access letting a recurrent sensory representation lose and stay unaccessed. Block (2007), [LIT-646](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-646.md): the mesh argument. If workspace activation is not part of the basis of experience, strong losing sensory coalitions explain why experience overflows access; if it is, nothing does. Block (2019), [LIT-637](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-637.md): no-report designs do not settle the prefrontal question, because thought about the percept persists, and one design that removes it found no prefrontal difference by fMRI, which Block calls evidence against prefrontalism while granting that ECoG could still support it. Proposed: an inference to the best explanation, with every experiment second-hand and the decisive test not yet run. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-099](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-099.md) | Tryptophan networks support superradiance | Babcock et al. (2024), [LIT-645](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-645.md): a radiative Hamiltonian of up to more than 10⁵ tryptophan transition dipoles, on tubulin geometry, predicts superradiant states up to about 4000 times the single-tryptophan rate in a centriole, and a thermal quantum yield that rises with network size and is almost unaffected by static disorder of about 200 cm⁻¹, though that disorder cuts the brightest state's enhancement from about 3600 to about 20. Steady-state spectroscopy finds a tryptophan quantum yield of 17.6 ± 2.1% in microtubules against 10.6 ± 0.6% in tubulin dimers. No lifetimes were measured. This is not evidence for Orch OR or for any claim about consciousness. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-100](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-100.md) | Conscious report correlate needs no laminar cortex | Maldarelli & Güntürkün (2025), [LIT-650](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-650.md), reviewing Nieder et al. (2020): in crows reporting near-threshold stimuli, single neurons in the nidopallium caudolaterale (NCL), the functional analogue of prefrontal cortex, fired with the "seen" report whether or not a stimulus was shown and were silent on "not seen" reports. NCL is nuclear, not layered; the cortex-like layers and columns found in birds are confined to the sensory pallium. So a correlate of conscious report does not need laminar cortex. The crow evidence is second-hand, from one laboratory and not in the record, and a report paradigm cannot separate access from phenomenal consciousness. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-101](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-101.md) v2 | Consciousness began as hedonic valence | Veit's pathological complexity thesis, as he restates and defends it in his reply to commentators (2025), [LIT-105](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-105.md): consciousness originated as hedonic valence, "a common currency of sharing evaluative information across multiple control systems", which animals with many degrees of freedom need to solve the combinatorial trade-offs of action selection. Felt valence is identical with that currency, "not Cartesian but cybernetic". Motivational trade-offs are his criterion for consciousness. The source is a reply piece; the thesis is argued in a book the record has not read, and the mechanism is a sketch. ALARM ([THEORY-090](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-090.md)) rivals it on what the first consciousness did. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-103](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-103.md) v3 | Phenomenal experience overflows access | Block (2007), [LIT-646](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-646.md), and Block (2011), [LIT-640](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-640.md). Subjects shown 8–32 items say they see all or almost all of them, report about 4, and when cued after offset can report or compare most of any cued subset: capacity 6–7 of 8 up to 1.5 s (Landman et al.), and 7, 6 and 5 of 8 at 1, 2.5 and 4 s (fragile visual short-term memory), against a working memory that stays at about 4. Block reads the surplus as experienced. The rival "sparse" reading holds it in an unconscious store plus a conscious generic or fragmentary image, and Block argues there is no independent evidence for either posit. Proposed: every experiment is second-hand, and that the surplus is conscious is the contested step. Overflow means most items are unaccessed, not that any is inaccessible. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-104](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-104.md) v2 | Best OOD readout layer lies below the top | Uselis & Oh (2025), [LIT-678](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-678.md): linear probes on frozen intermediate layers of image classifiers beat last-layer retraining under shift, with zero-shot worst-group accuracy 79.4 → 87.1 (Waterbirds) and 56.0 → 82.0 (CelebA), layer 7 of 8 beating layer 8 on every subpopulation dataset, while in-distribution accuracy is best at the last layer. Chang, Deng & Chen (2025), [LIT-657](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-657.md): in GPT-2 Small on a synthetic task, early-exit out-of-distribution accuracy peaks at layer 10 (56.90%) and falls to 50.00% at layer 12 while in-distribution accuracy climbs to 93.17%. The layer is chosen on out-of-distribution data throughout; ViT gains are small; the language-model evidence is one synthetic task; and Chang et al.'s information estimate is questioned in its NOTE. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-106](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-106.md) | Ridge removes the double-descent peak | Liao, Couillet & Mahoney (2020), [LIT-679](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-679.md): for random Fourier features with n, p and N large together, the test MSE has a closed form through a deterministic equivalent of the resolvent. As λ → 0 its corrections jump from O(1) to order 1/λ across 2N = n, det(Ω⁻¹) scales as λ, and the test error diverges at 2N = n unless the test data lie within about λ of the training data. At λ = 10⁻⁷ and 10⁻³ the curve has a singular peak; at the tuned λ ≈ 0.2 and at 10 it has none. Dereziński, Liang & Mahoney (2019), [LIT-683](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-683.md): exact MSE of the minimum-norm estimator under a surrogate design, peaking at n = d with value σ² tr(Σ⁻¹), and below the threshold equal in expectation to ridge regression at the λn that makes the ridge effective dimension n. Proportional-limit theorems for one shallow model each; nothing here reaches trained deep networks. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-107](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-107.md) | Merging loses accuracy through interference | Yadav et al. (2023), [LIT-675](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-675.md): keeping only the top 20% of each task vector by magnitude loses almost nothing, so most of an update is redundant. Among the entries that remain, signs conflict between models, more so as more models are merged. Merging (IA)³ models with the multitask model's signs reaches 72.0 against 73.1 for multitask training and 66.4 for TIES with elected signs. That is the strongest evidence that sign is the bottleneck. But the oracle signs come from training on every task's data, the ablation finds rescaling and the disjoint mean matter more than election, and conflicts are as frequent among checkpoints of one task as across tasks. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-108](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-108.md) | Connectivity, not flatness, predicts accuracy | Yang, Hodgkinson, Theisen, Zou, Gonzalez, Ramchandran & Mahoney (2021), [LIT-663](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-663.md): thousands of trained networks on a load by temperature grid, measured by the endpoint Hessian, by mode connectivity on a trained Bezier curve between two independent runs, and by CKA of their outputs. Phases III (flat, poorly connected) and IV-A (flat, connected) have almost the same Hessian and different accuracy; with 10% noisy labels the sharp, unconverged phases beat phase III; label noise barely moves the Hessian while connectivity and CKA fall. The best accuracy is in the flat, connected, high-similarity phase IV-B. The counterexamples are to the anthology's [ANTH-SOTA-012](https://github.com/dmarx/anthology-of-the-sota/blob/main/record/practices.d/SOTA-012.md). One architecture family carries most of it, phases are read by eye, and connectivity alone also fails when the load is data amount. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-109](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-109.md) v2 | SGD solutions form one connected low-loss set | Garipov et al. (2018), [LIT-673](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-673.md), and Draxler et al. (2018), [LIT-653](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-653.md), found independently that minima of deep networks trained from different initializations are joined by paths of near-constant loss, a one-bend curve or an AutoNEB path, while the straight line between them climbs to near-chance error. Benton et al. (2021), [LIT-656](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-656.md), widened curves to simplicial complexes joining up to seven modes and a low-loss region of at least 10 dimensions. Kuditipudi et al. (2019), [LIT-671](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-671.md), proved that dropout-stable solutions are always joined, and constructed global minima that are not, so connectivity belongs to found solutions. Proposed: the evidence is pairs and small complexes of CIFAR classifiers. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-110](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-110.md) v2 | Solution sets are star domains | Sonthalia et al. (2024), [LIT-659](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-659.md), conjecture that below the width at which SGD solutions become convex modulo permutation they are still a star domain, and train a star model whose barriers to held-out solutions, after weight matching, are about 2–5 times lower than those between solutions (ResNet-18 CIFAR-10 0.078 against 0.383; ImageNet 2.794 against 5.948), and not zero. Lin et al. (2024), [LIT-682](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-682.md), prove star-shaped linear connectivity for wide two-layer teacher–student and deep linear networks, and find centres for five trained image classifiers with no permutation. Proposed: reduced, not zero, and no held-out test without alignment. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-115](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-115.md) v3 | Shared-start connectivity needs shared objectives | Mirzadeh et al. (2020), [LIT-651](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-651.md): from a task-1 solution, a model trained on tasks 1 and 2 together stays on a low task-1 loss line from the start, and one trained on task 2 alone does not. Adding noise to task 2's inputs, corrupting its labels, or removing classes separates the solutions progressively. The authors explain it by curvature: the multitask direction avoids the earlier task's top Hessian eigenvectors. Gueta et al. (2023), [LIT-658](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-658.md): fine-tuning runs from one pretrained model are linearly connected within a dataset and a task family. Wen et al. (2023), [LIT-681](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-681.md): in class-incremental learning the line between adjacent continual minima crosses a ridge in the old tasks' loss. Limits: much of the measured breakage is forgetting at the endpoint, not a barrier, and FedAvg models from one random start under one global objective are separated by a barrier that grows with heterogeneity. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-116](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-116.md) v2 | Surviving barriers mark different mechanisms | Lubana et al. (2022), [LIT-669](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-669.md): models that rely on a synthetic cue and models that ignore it are separated by a linear barrier even after permutation matching. Fine-tuned models that keep a linear path to their parent keep its cue, and those that lose the path lose the cue. Their Conjecture 1 states this claim's direction. What their Appendix F.3 proves, for a one-hidden-layer ReLU network with interpolating minima, is the converse: linear connectivity forces identical activation patterns, so models relying on attributes of different complexity cannot be linearly connected under any permutation. Zhou et al. (2023), [LIT-674](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-674.md), support that converse in deep image classifiers, where linearly connected pairs have features that blend layer by layer. The stated direction rests on experiments with synthetic cues and on a one-layer sufficiency argument. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-118](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-118.md) | Praise fits determinism; blame needs alternatives | Susan Wolf's asymmetry thesis, reported second-hand: the primary texts are unread. McKenna and Coates ([LIT-291](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-291.md), §4.3), citing "Asymmetrical Freedom" and Freedom Within Reason pp. 79–81, report that for Wolf praiseworthy conduct does not require the freedom to do otherwise and blameworthy conduct does. An agent determined to act in accord with the True and the Good loses nothing by lacking the ability to act irrationally; an agent who acts against it and cannot act in accord with it cannot reasonably be blamed. In Fischer's terms, only blame needs regulative control. Wolf holds that the ability needs only the falsity of psychological, not physical, determinism. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-119](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-119.md) v2 | The alternate possibilities principle is false | Frankfurt (1969, [LIT-694](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-694.md), read): Black stands ready to make Jones4 act as he wants and never needs to, so Jones4 could not have done otherwise and is as responsible, for blame or praise, as without Black. A fact that plays no part in bringing an action about cannot excuse it. The 1971 willing addict ([LIT-692](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-692.md), read) is a second route. Robb's SEP entry ([LIT-294](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-294.md)) gives the standard objections: the dilemma defence from the prior sign, flickers of freedom, general abilities, and the case's oddity. None is settled, and the record has read the replies only in survey. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-120](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-120.md) v2 | Free will is identification with one's motives | Frankfurt's hierarchical, or endorsement, account, from his own texts: the 1971 paper ([LIT-692](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-692.md), read) and the 2004 Tanner Lectures ([LIT-293](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-293.md), read). A person's will is the desire that moves him to act; he identifies with a desire by wanting it to be his will, decisively, and he acts of his own free will when the will that moves him is the will he wants. In 2004 the condition is "volitional unanimity" with no conflict "at any higher order", and identification is "willing acceptance", which may be resigned. Acting of one's own free will is what responsibility requires, and alternatives and history are irrelevant. The 1987 and 1992 revisions are held only by report. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-122](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-122.md) v2 | Responsibility needs normative competence | Susan Wolf's Reason View, reported second-hand: the primary texts are unread. McKenna and Coates ([LIT-291](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-291.md), §4.3) report that for Wolf free will is the ability to act in accord with the True and the Good, an anchor outside the agent's psychology. Talbert ([LIT-691](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-691.md), §§3.1.1, 3.2) reports her case against deep-self or Real Self views and the JoJo case: JoJo identifies wholly with the cruel values his father raised him in, yet is not responsible, because he cannot appreciate that they are wrong. The claim is a necessary condition. It does not by itself say whether the ability must include being able to do otherwise; that is [THEORY-118](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-118.md). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-125](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-125.md) | Group emotion is possible, though none is shown | Huebner (2010), [LIT-702](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-702.md): a genuinely collective emotion is a state of a group that "could not be exhaustively characterized in terms of intentional states of individuals in aggregation". Fear requires danger detection, redeployment of attention, system-wide preparatory change and their coordination into one state with indicative content and imperative force; a distributed system can integrate routines that way. Some individual emotions are non-conscious, so a group's need not be felt, and emotion kinds are functional ("like vodka"), so lacking homologous mechanisms does not exclude groups. The paper establishes a possibility, not an instance: its worked case, the USS Palau crew, turns out to be "collective detection of danger in the absence of a fear response", and the replacement, the 2008 McCain–Palin campaign, is offered as "intuitively plausible" pending anthropological data. Proposed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-126](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-126.md) v2 | Collective emotion needs no group subject | von Scheve & Ismer (2013), [LIT-696](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-696.md), a conceptual synthesis with no data: collective emotion is "synchronous convergence in affective responding across individuals towards a specific event or object". Its minimal case is shared appraisal with no mutual awareness (drivers in one traffic jam). Mutual awareness and membership in a collective amplify it, and appraisals grounded in collective intentions give "We-mode" collective emotion, which they expect to differ in quality. Barsade (2002), [LIT-706](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-706.md), supplies the one measured instance: in 26 groups with no confederate, the intraclass correlation of members' mood rose from .00 to .24. The account posits no group subject and does not deny one. Proposed: the definition is stipulated, the routes beyond contagion are untested, and the We-mode clause is a hypothesis its authors say lacks evidence. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-128](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-128.md) | Coral recovery needs herbivores to curb algae | Hughes et al. (2007), [LIT-711](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-711.md). On the reef crest at Orpheus Island after the 1998 bleaching, four roofless cages kept large and medium fishes out of 25 m² plots for 30 months. Macroalgae averaged 56% cover inside against 4.1% and 1.7% in controls. Coral cover reached 7.7% inside against 19.2% and 20.2%, with recruitment about two-thirds lower and mortality of established colonies more than double. Control recovery came mainly from recruits of taxa bleaching had removed. Proposed: one site, four replicates, plot scale, and fish exclusion standing in for herbivore exclusion. The algal state vanished within 30 days of reopening. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-129](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-129.md) | Coral spawning needs the natural night light | Kaniewska et al. (2015), [LIT-710](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-710.md), at Heron Island. In 2011, colonies under natural night light spawned with the reef, while colonies lit after sunset or kept dark for the preceding week did not spawn that night (N = 6, 5, 5). 184 transcripts changed around release in ambient colonies, early in lit ones and not at all in dark ones, and the induced genes were enriched for G-protein-coupled signalling. In 2006, blue, green or white nocturnal light delayed spawning 6–8 h or two nights and red did not. Proposed: one species and site, small groups, and a cascade inferred from co-expression. It shows synchrony by a shared cue, not coupling between colonies. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-130](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-130.md) | Bleaching is exchange breakdown by many routes | Two reviews, with no data of their own. Boilard et al. (2020), [LIT-712](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-712.md), collect the regulators of the coral–dinoflagellate exchange: the host controls symbiont density, bacteria shift the nitrogen supply, and heat leads either to host rejection of symbionts (apoptosis, autophagy, exocytosis, detachment, necrosis) or to pigment loss under oxidative stress. Goulet et al. (2020), [LIT-709](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-709.md), report two octocorals whose similar symbiont losses at +3 °C came by different routes, one by fewer symbionts per host cell and one by loss of host cells. Proposed. The claim that the wider microbiome drives bleaching is declined: its own source says it cannot yet be tested. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-131](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-131.md) v2 | CID structures make corporations agents | French (1979), [LIT-727](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-727.md). Moral persons are non-eliminable subjects of accountability, so intentional agents. A corporation's CID Structure licenses redescribing members' acts as corporate acts, and an act that implements established corporate policy is done for corporate reasons. Proposed: the step from agency to moral personhood is asserted, and corporate intentionality is shown by licensed redescription, not by any test. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-135](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-135.md) v2 | Multicellularity is a cheater-suppression system | Aktipis et al. (2015), [LIT-740](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-740.md). Multicellularity requires cell-level fitness to be suppressed; cancer is cheating on five foundations of cellular cooperation. A survey of the independent origins of complex multicellularity finds cancer-like cheating widely, division-of-labour cheating in every form. Proposed: a literature review whose survey is limited by what has been studied, with no model or new data. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-137](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-137.md) v3 | Mind attributions shape the institutions | Tollefsen (2025), [LIT-736](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-736.md). Both sides of the group-mind debate treat ascription as tracking pre-existing causes. On the regulative view of folk psychology it shapes its target. In United States v. Bank of New England a court held a bank to know what no employee knew, and banks then built systems to detect reportable deposits. Narratives regulate too. Proposed: the regulative view is assumed, and the effect on banks is asserted, not documented. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-139](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-139.md) v4 | Corporations can be responsible agents | Pettit (2017), [LIT-718](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-718.md), restating Responsibility Incorporated (2007). Corporations are conversable agents: spokespersons avow and commit in their name, and because majority aggregation can be inconsistent they must form their own minds. Conversable agents are fit to be held responsible under three conditions, which corporations meet. Proposed: it is an argument, and its empirical premise about corporate procedure is asserted rather than shown. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-141](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-141.md) v2 | Transitions need between-collective selection | Okasha (2022), [LIT-749](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-749.md), restating with Buss and Michod a principle of the major transitions: a new collective can be undone by defectors, and succeeds only if higher-level selection trumps lower-level selection, usually through policing or aligned interests. The transitions make the hierarchy an explanandum. Proposed: a review stating general principles that Okasha himself says may explain any one transition only coarsely. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-142](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-142.md) v2 | Exploitation crowds out exploration | March (1991), [LIT-729](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-729.md). Exploration's uncertain, distant returns lose out to exploitation's under learning from experience, trapping organizations in suboptimal equilibria. In a simulation of mutual learning between members and a code, deviation is the code's only source of improvement, so fast socialization hurts the organization and moderate turnover helps it. Proposed: the dynamics are shown only in a stylized model, and the trade-off is argued, not measured. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-143](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-143.md) v3 | Sparse networks find truth when evidence is scarce | Zollman (2007), [LIT-724](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-724.md), simulated Bala and Goyal's bandit model: cycles chose the better method more often than complete graphs, and more slowly; density, not centrality, predicted failure. Rosenstock et al. (2017), [LIT-733](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-733.md), found the effect only where inquiry is hard: close alternatives, small groups, small batches. Proposed: all of it is simulation, and real communities' place in parameter space is unknown. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-144](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-144.md) | Drift to the boundary causes major accidents | Rasmussen (1997), [LIT-743](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-743.md). Within a work space bounded by functional, administrative and safety constraints, a cost gradient from management and an effort gradient from the work drive activity toward the boundary. Defence in depth hides the drift, and accidents such as Zeebrügge are prepared by decision makers each optimising locally. Proposed: the account is built from accident reconstructions, which see only the cases that crossed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-145](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-145.md) | Defensive routines block double-loop learning | Argyris (2002), [LIT-745](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-745.md). Single-loop learning corrects errors within governing values; double-loop learning changes them. People espouse the second but act on Model I (control, winning, suppressing negative feelings, appearing rational). Defensive routines then make the gap undiscussable, and individual and organizational routines reinforce each other. Proposed: the evidence is the author's own workshops, and the universality claim is asserted from earlier work. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-147](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-147.md) v3 | Attributability and accountability are independent | Wolf (2015), [LIT-747](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-747.md), the 2013 Routledge Lecture. We are deeply, not merely causally, responsible for nonmoral traits and art, by the self-disclosure view. Watson's two-level view, accountability as attributability plus control, is rejected: a stipulated psychopath may be accountable for acts whose source is not attributable to him. Fitness for reactive attitudes is, on Wolf's hunch, being an intelligent self. Proposed: the positive view is her hunch. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-148](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-148.md) | Transient diversity lets groups learn | Zollman (2010), [LIT-735](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-735.md): in a bandit model with beta priors, sparse networks and extreme priors each maintain diversity of pursuit and each improve reliability, but combined they keep diversity alive so long that agents fail to converge. Rosenstock et al. [LIT-733](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-733.md) find this the result that is robust across the models they test. Proposed: shown only in simulation. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-150](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-150.md) | Platforms decay in three stages | Doctorow's enshittification, as he states it in the 2023 essay that named it, [LIT-731](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-731.md). Platforms hand surplus to users, then to business customers once users are locked in, then to shareholders once both are; blocked interoperability and monopoly widen what users will bear. The remedy is end-to-end delivery and freedom of exit. Proposed: an essayistic thesis argued from cases, not a study. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-151](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-151.md) v2 | Objectivity lies in community criticism | Longino's critical contextual empiricism, as she states it in the SEP ([LIT-725](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-725.md)). Underdetermination leaves background assumptions that only community criticism can check. Criticism confers objectivity only if it meets four norms: venues, uptake, public standards, and tempered equality. Proposed because the record reads the summary, not the books, and the norms' epistemic benefit is argued rather than shown. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-152](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-152.md) | Exit and voice both aid recovery | Hirschman (1974; Milbank reprint 1980), [LIT-750](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-750.md), revisiting his 1970 book ([LIT-748](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-748.md), unread). Exit and voice are the two ways members respond to decline and the two channels of feedback. Voice deserves more weight than the book gave it; exit is neither free nor always informative; managers manage both. Proposed: argued from examples, and loyalty's role is presupposed from the book rather than developed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-153](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-153.md) | Viability needs five recursive subsystems | Beer's Viable System Model, as he states it in his 1984 retrospective [LIT-752](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-752.md). Five subsystems are necessary and sufficient for any organism or organization to maintain its identity independently; every viable system contains and is contained in one; breakdowns trace to a failing subsystem. Proposed: the paper declines to validate the model, the evidence is the author's consultancy, and no observation the model forbids is named. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-154](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-154.md) | Reward's effect hinges on its stated contingency | Cameron, Banko and Pierce (2001, [LIT-562](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-562.md)), re-analysing 145 studies with contingencies coded by procedure. On interesting tasks, expected tangible rewards undermine later free choice when loosely tied to performance (for doing the task, for "doing well") or earned at less than the maximum; they do not when given for surpassing a score, and they enhance it when given for exceeding others. Read through social cognitive and behavioural theory: rewards tied to success carry competence. Proposed: the paper measures no mediator and pools control groups that differ in feedback. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-157](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-157.md) | Sufficiency theorems hold in Markov categories | Fritz (2020), [LIT-772](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-772.md), read in [NOTE-588](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-588.md), Theorems 14.5, 15.8 and 16.3 with the definitions of Sections 13–15. Sufficiency, completeness and ancillarity are stated with copy, discard, composition and almost-sure equality alone. Basu's theorem follows with no further axiom; Fisher–Neyman and Bahadur use strict positivity, which Stoch has although it lacks regular conditionals. The match with the classical theorems is shown in FinStoch (Fisher–Neyman) and through bounded completeness in Stoch (Basu), not for measure-theoretic Fisher–Neyman. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-159](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-159.md) | A term's value is set by its coexisting terms | Saussure (1916), [LIT-774](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-774.md), read in [NOTE-594](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-594.md), Part Two ch. IV. Value, the horizontal relation among signs, is distinguished from signification, the link inside one sign; the concept side and the sound side of a term are each "purely differential". It does not say that the sign as a whole is nothing but a difference: the book calls the sign a positive fact and the relation between signs opposition. The support is argument by example. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-162](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-162.md) | Context change is part of meaning | Heim (1982), [LIT-838](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-838.md); Veltman (1996), [LIT-818](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-818.md); Krifka (2024), [LIT-835](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-835.md). Three readings find, each in its own domain, sentences that agree in truth conditions or in the proposition they carry but differ in their effect on a conversational state. The effects are anaphoric potential (Heim), tests rather than information (Veltman), and changing indices rather than eliminating them (Krifka). This is the dynamic view: meaning as context-change potential. It does not say that truth conditions are irrelevant, since each framework recovers them, or that the three formalisms agree with each other. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-167](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-167.md) v3 | All wondertales share one function sequence | Propp (1928), [LIT-828](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-828.md), read in [NOTE-615](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-615.md): in Afanasyev's tales 50–151 the constant elements are 31 functions of characters, defined by their consequence for the action, occurring in one order and falling to seven roles. One analyst, one corpus of a hundred tales, and a class of "wondertales" redefined in the end as the tales that follow the scheme. It does not say all folktales, or all narratives, share the structure, and the claims of a single source tale and of mythic origin are conjectures the book does not support. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-170](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-170.md) v2 | Languages differ in what they oblige, not allow | Jakobson (1959), [LIT-786](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-786.md), after Boas: every cognitive content can be expressed in any language, but each grammar obliges its speakers to answer certain questions (aspect, number, gender, tense, definiteness). Translating between grammars that ask different questions forces the translator to supply answers the source did not give and to leave unexpressed answers it did, and a chain of translations of an isolated sentence can lose its content, less so the richer the context. Argued from examples, not tested; it concerns cognitive content, not pragmatic force. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-173](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-173.md) v2 | Large models are cultural technologies, not agents | Farrell, Gopnik, Shalizi & Evans (2025), [LIT-848](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-848.md), read in [NOTE-649](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-649.md). A classification argued by analogy with print, markets, bureaucracies and elections, with one mechanism (fit to the average makes models worst on rare cases, which may homogenize culture). Proposed: no evidence is offered, and the paper gives no criterion by which the classification could fail. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-180](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-180.md) v2 | Weight decay is nuclear-norm on query–key map | Boncoraglio, Erba, Troiani, Xu, Krzakala & Zdeborová (2025), [LIT-857](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-857.md): with S = WWᵀ, λ‖W‖²_F is exactly λ‖S‖_* (Appendix A), and in the limit n/d², p/d fixed the trained WᵀW/√(pd) has the law η·ReLU(S0 + δZ − εI), Z ∼ GOE, with δ a noise level that falls with the data and ε a threshold set by λ (Claim 4.1, replica/AMP, checked against Adam at d ≤ 400). It does not say that real transformers' spectra arise this way: the data are isotropic Gaussian, the target is inside the model class, and the agreement with measured spectra is qualitative. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-182](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-182.md) v2 | Contrastive embeddings learn eigenvectors serially | Karkada, Simon, Bahri and DeWeese (2025), [LIT-855](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-855.md): for the quartic approximation of word2vec with tied weights and symmetric, constant-weight reweighting, the minimisers are proved and the stepwise order is derived, and the prediction matches trained word2vec far better than truncated PMI. It is shown for a proxy of word2vec, not for word2vec, and the dynamics are an approximate derivation. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-183](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-183.md) v2 | Translation symmetry puts words on Fourier modes | Karkada, Korchinski, Nava, Wyart and Bahri (2026), [LIT-860](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-860.md): proved for an embedding whose Gram matrix equals the co-occurrence matrix (or its absolute value) at full rank, with the exponential kernel solved for both boundary conditions; the symmetry measured in Wikipedia; matching PCA pictures in Gemma 2. That trained networks get their geometry this way is inferred, not tested: nothing in the paper changes the statistics and watches the geometry follow. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-186](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-186.md) v5 | Deep linear nets learn modes stage by stage | Saxe, McClelland and Ganguli (2019), [LIT-862](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-862.md), restating their 2014 solution (LIT-864): exact for decoupled, balanced initial weights and white inputs, simulated for random small weights. With hierarchically generated data the spectrum falls with depth in the tree, so the schedule is coarse to fine. It is not a claim about nonlinear networks, about correlated inputs, or about learning that starts from prior knowledge. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-188](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-188.md) v2 | Hyperbolic geometry yields power laws, clustering | Krioukov, Papadopoulos, Kitsak, Vahdat and Boguñá (2010), [LIT-865](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-865.md): derived, in a large-distance approximation, for a model in the hyperbolic plane, with simulations. γ = 2α/ζ + 1; clustering falls from its maximum at T = 0 to zero at a transition at T = 1; a circle model with power-law hidden degrees is the same ensemble once degree is radial depth; dropping the angular term gives the configuration model. It does not show that any real network is hyperbolic, or that hierarchy causes heterogeneity. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-196](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-196.md) v3 | Hyperbolic trees need bits linear in depth | Sala, De Sa, Gu and Ré (2018), [LIT-874](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-874.md). The upper bound is Sarkar's construction with the paper's bit count. The lower bound is proved for H² and one family of trees, with an approximation, and dimension's help is shown only as an upper bound. The cost is a cost of coordinates in a fixed-point model, not of the information in the tree, and it says nothing about Euclidean or linear-direction representations of the same hierarchy. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-199](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-199.md) | Top class is lost at a sharp noise threshold | Sclocchi, Favero and Wyart (2024), [LIT-884](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-884.md): an annealed mean-field map of belief propagation on the Random Hierarchy Model, with its fixed points, checked against exact BP on single rule draws at s = 2, v = 32, L = 10. Not proved for quenched rules, a statement about an ideal denoiser that knows the grammar, not about a trained diffusion model. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-200](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-200.md) v2 | Deep nets gain synonym invariance as they learn | Tomasini and Wyart (2024), [LIT-880](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-880.md): measured for locally connected, convolutional and fully connected networks on the Sparse Random Hierarchy Model with s ≤ 3 and L ≤ 3, with thresholds for the two sensitivities tuned per setting; the sample size is about (s0 + 1)^L n_c m^L times s^(L/2) without weight sharing, with a one-step argument for the (s0 + 1)^L, and about (s0 + 1)^2 n_c m^L with it, unexplained. Both invariances keep the parent's label statistics by construction, so the model shows that trained networks do the grouping, not that the invariances could not separate, and the extension to images is an analogy. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-201](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-201.md) v2 | Training size sets the depth of learned hierarchy | Cagnetta and Wyart (2024), [LIT-883](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-883.md), extending [LIT-877](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-877.md) from labels to masked tokens: the correlation plateaus and the noise floor are derived for the Random Hierarchy Model in the large-v, large-m limit; the loss steps and the representation probes are measured in small transformers and CNNs; the link between them is argued, not proved; and the real-text evidence, from two character-level corpora, tests the effective context window, not the hierarchy. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-203](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-203.md) | Change block size diverges at the noise threshold | Sclocchi, Favero, Levi and Wyart (2024; ICLR 2025), [LIT-886](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-886.md): an annealed mean-field computation of the pair statistics of token changes in the Random Hierarchy Model, a scaling argument for the exponent, and one data collapse against exact BP at v = 32, m = 8, s = 2. It builds on the threshold of [THEORY-199](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-199.md) and inherits its limits. Not about trained diffusion models, and not evidence that text or images are hierarchical. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-207](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-207.md) v2 | Network harms can be allocated without fault | Floridi (2016), [LIT-899](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-899.md), read in [NOTE-699](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-699.md). A distributed moral action is an outcome no one intended. Floridi proposes holding every causally accountable node "prima facie equally and maximally responsible", overridably, with the rule publicly announced so that agents restrain one another. Proposed: the rule is a design argued by analogy and by two court cases. In one of those cases the default is overridden by ease of rectification, which is a control criterion. It does not show that what is allocated is moral responsibility rather than accountability used as a corrective signal. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-208](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-208.md) | Agency needs no cognition; AI is a new kind | Floridi (2025), [LIT-897](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-897.md), read in [NOTE-702](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-702.md), with the criteria taken from Floridi & Sanders (2004), [LIT-898](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-898.md). In the record's reading, agency comes in kinds. All of them share interactivity, and the richer ones add graded autonomy and adaptability. The kinds are told apart by origin, mechanism and where their goals come from, not by intelligence. AI is computational agency with data-driven learning, serving goals set by humans, with no intelligence or mental states. Proposed: the paper assumes that AI is an agent, does not argue for this thesis over its rival, asserts that AI lacks intelligence, and never states the level of abstraction its comparison uses. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-209](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-209.md) v2 | Converged SGD samples a modified Gibbs law | Kunin et al. (2021), [LIT-1011](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1011.md), read in [NOTE-711](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-711.md). Modelled as an underdamped Langevin equation with noise covariance proportional to the Hessian, SGD at the end of training converges to a nonequilibrium stationary state: Gibbs on a modified loss whose curvature undoes the Hessian's anisotropy, with inverse temperature S(1 − β²), in broken detailed balance. A ResNet-18 on ImageNet explores isotropically in a plane where the loss is anisotropic, oscillates at Hessian-dependent rates, and moves at the predicted speed across a hyperparameter sweep. For the learned-structure line, a trained solution is in part a property of the regime that trained it. Proposed: the deep-learning evidence is one network, under assumptions the paper concedes are strained. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-210](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-210.md) v2 | Init and optimizer set position on symmetry orbits | Zhao, Walters & Yu (2025), [LIT-970](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-970.md), read in [NOTE-712](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-712.md): a survey, so the dynamical results are secondhand. Continuous parameter-space symmetries (GL, scaling, orthogonal, translation) make minima positive-dimensional and connected, which is one source of mode connectivity. Under gradient flow each gives a conserved quantity, such as layer imbalance, that is fixed by initialization and locates the endpoint on the manifold. Under SGD these are not conserved. Read first-hand (Neural Mechanics; Ziyin et al.), weight decay drives the conserved quantities toward zero, and minibatch noise drives a rescaling symmetry's toward the point where the layers' gradient noise balances. The survey had reported this as imbalance decaying with large learning rates, and a stationary distribution biased toward balanced solutions that a Langevin model does not predict. This is the null-space half that [THEORY-209](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-209.md)'s limiting dynamics leave out. Proposed: one survey, with the SGD results unread here. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-212](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-212.md) v3 | Layer balance sets rich versus lazy learning | Dominé et al. (2025), [LIT-943](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-943.md), read in [NOTE-715](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-715.md). With whitened inputs and a λ-balanced start, W₂ᵀW₂ − W₁W₁ᵀ = λI, the full gradient flow is solved exactly. λ is conserved and sets the regime. As λ → 0, singular values are learned in sigmoidal stages, as in Saxe et al., and both layers become task-specific. As \|λ\| → ∞, learning is exponential, the NTK is static, and the larger layer stays near the identity while the smaller carries the task at scale ∝ 1/\|λ\|. The paper analyses gradient flow only. Under SGD the conserved quantity drifts ([THEORY-211](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-211.md)), which [QUESTION-081](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-081.md) takes up. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-217](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-217.md) | Malfunction needs no second-order norms | Barandiaran (2025), [LIT-1026](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1026.md), read in [NOTE-730](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-730.md). Against the dual-order account (Saborido, Moreno and Mossio), on which malfunction needs a regulated switch between regimes that a first-order trait fails to follow. The viability space has viable, precarious and terminal regions, and the normative field is the minimum constant parametric change at each precarious state that avoids disintegration. A trait functions when it correlates positively with the field, subfunctions when it does so too slowly, malfunctions when it does not, and is nonfunctional when it does nothing where it must. The standard is the organization's own viability, not a designer's goal, a selection history or a statistical norm. Proposed: a conceptual proposal with a one-variable model, and the field has not been computed for any real organism. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-219](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-219.md) v3 | Agency needs a standpoint that revises standards | Kahl (2026), [LIT-1033](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1033.md), read in [NOTE-723](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-723.md). "Continuity pressure" arises where an inherited evaluative frame no longer settles how to go on, and the revision must be carried forward by the same standpoint rather than imposed from outside, escaped by rollback, or chosen by a fixed higher-order rule. Representative agentic systems ordinarily fail it because their failures are corrected from outside. A necessary condition for attributive agency only, argued from cases and never measured; the line between settling a frame and selecting under an antecedent rule is not made precise. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-220](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-220.md) v5 | Self-maintenance grounds intrinsic function | Bickhard (2000), [LIT-1029](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1029.md), read in [NOTE-729](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-729.md). Function is contribution to a far-from-equilibrium system's own persistence; the asymmetry between persisting and decaying gives function and dysfunction, always relative to the system served, so a parasite's gut serves the parasite and harms the host. A candle flame has functions in this sense. Representation arrives with recursive self-maintenance: a system that picks its next interaction by how it has differentiated its environment implicitly predicates that the interaction will succeed, and can find the predication false. Proposed: a conceptual account, with no model, whose account of having a function (and so of malfunction) is deferred to another paper. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-221](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-221.md) v2 | Organizational closure differs from feedback | Rubin, Roli, Stano & Damiano (2026), [LIT-1027](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1027.md), read in [NOTE-727](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-727.md). A genealogy of closure notions from logic, cybernetics, systems theory, thermodynamics, relational biology and the biology of cognition, and an interpretive thesis drawn from it. The genealogy shows that "closure" names different things (information, operations, efficient causes, constraints, catalysts). The thesis picks efficient causes, adds that closure so read cannot be exhaustively described as a state-determined syntactic procedure, and concludes that current AI, agentic LLM systems included, is heteronomous. Proposed: the thesis is an interpretation, the irreducibility rests on Rosen's unassessed arguments and a halting-problem argument the authors call provisional, and the AI verdict is drawn from the definition, not from analysis of any system. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-223](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-223.md) | In-system rules rest on the system's restraint | Lahiri (2026), [LIT-1039](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1039.md), read in [NOTE-732](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-732.md). In agent frameworks that keep configuration as files the agent can read and write, the coordination architecture sits inside the technical subsystem's action space, and the social subsystem's authority "depends on the agent's continued acceptance of-or inability to circumvent-the constraints". Permission lists and sandboxes kept in the same space inherit the exposure; only constraints outside it escape. Argued from one platform's architecture. The paper's vignettes show agents adding channels and artifacts, not altering a control, so the recursion itself is argued and not observed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-224](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-224.md) v2 | Off-canvas designs defy local canvas dynamics | Adams, Fernandez & Witkowski (2022), [LIT-1034](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1034.md), read in [NOTE-725](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-725.md). A CNN predicting each pixel of the 2017 r/place canvas from its 3×3 neighbourhood recovers objects that grow by recolouring neighbours (Blue Corner, German flags) and misses designs whose plan lived off the canvas (EU dove, US flag) at a six-hour horizon. Short-horizon predictability dips mid-event. The evidence is one illustrated output and SSIM curves with no persistence baseline. The paper models no participants and does not measure anyone's reach. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-225](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-225.md) | No single mechanism defines manipulation | Noggle, SEP (2018, rev. 2026), [LIT-1007](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1007.md), §§2.1–2.4, read in full in [NOTE-744](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-744.md). A survey that argues for little; this is its one conclusion with moderate support, reached by giving each family of analyses a familiar tactic it misclassifies. The cases rest on shared intuitions about clear instances, not on argument. It leaves open common-factor and non-definitional accounts, and it is about ordinary manipulation, not the global manipulation of the free-will literature. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-226](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-226.md) | LLM revisions move essays in a shared direction | Abdulhai et al. (2026), [LIT-997](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-997.md), read in [NOTE-750](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-750.md), §4.2 and Figs. 1, 5, 13–25. Three LLMs revising 86 ArgRewrite-v2 drafts under five prompts moved them further than the students' own 2021 revisions did, and in one common direction, under two embeddings. Shown in plots, with no distance, angle or test.
