Meaning is measured only as embedding position: the paper does not show that the writer's intended meaning changed, and the "grammar" prompt came with content feedback. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-232](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-232.md) v2 | Agency grows when parts resolve constraints | Watson (2023), [LIT-990](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-990.md), read in full in [NOTE-747](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-747.md). A perspective essay's definition, argued and illustrated, not proved: agency of a whole with respect to its parts is the reduction in the parts' total frustration at equilibrium that its organization achieves over the old one, shown by directed uphill excursions to lower minima. It is comparative and sets no threshold for an additional agent, and it holds only relative to a stipulated decomposition and stipulated goals for the parts. That bottom-up learning produces such organization is reported from earlier models, not shown here. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-235](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-235.md) | Covert exploitation always harms autonomy | Susser, Roessler and Nissenbaum (2019), [LIT-1002](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1002.md), pp. 4–5 and 9–11, read in full in [NOTE-745](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-745.md). An argument in a short policy essay, not a defence against objections. It holds of influence that is covert and exploits a vulnerability, which the paper stipulates is what manipulation is; Noggle's survey ([LIT-1007](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1007.md)) shows that covertness is not necessary for manipulation, so the claim is filed of covert influence, not of manipulation as such. The paper claims a harm in every case, not a wrong, and never examines its own intent requirement. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-240](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-240.md) | Unconsciousness cuts integration at gateways | Luppi et al. (2024), [LIT-949](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-949.md), read in [NOTE-799](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-799.md). In resting-state fMRI, the regions where synergistic interactions outrank redundant ones split by rank into gateways (mainly default mode) and broadcasters (mainly fronto-parietal). Pairwise ΦR, the whole-minus-sum Φ plus redundancy, falls between default-mode gateways in propofol anaesthesia, in 22 DOC patients, and against post-anaesthetic recovery. The original Φ shows no common decrease. The finding is correlational, pairwise and content-free. The gateway/broadcaster split is imposed by the method; only where its two classes fall is measured. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-241](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-241.md) | Same function, different internal decomposition | Kumar, Clune, Lehman & Stanley (2025), [LIT-944](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-944.md), read in [NOTE-771](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-771.md). For the skull, butterfly and apple CPPNs, SGD in the layerized evolved architecture fits the image, the network's whole function on the grid. It shows no reuse of the symmetric parts, and single-weight and random-direction sweeps distort the output, where the evolved networks' sweeps vary it meaningfully. Qualitative, curated and three images. The paper's account of why, the order of discovery in open-ended search, and its extension to large models are conjecture. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-249](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-249.md) v2 | Agency is decidable only to a reference frame | Abel et al. (2025), [LIT-969](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-969.md), read in full in [NOTE-793](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-793.md). A four-page position paper, argued and not proved: each condition is shown two-valued under two plausible choices by citing an earlier result (Jiang; Kenton et al., [LIT-909](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-909.md); inverse-RL underdetermination; Zadeh). The premises are existential and the conclusion universal, so what is supported is that some attributions of agency depend on the frame. That the choices are arbitrary is asserted, and the paper itself floats predictive power as a way to choose. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-250](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-250.md) v2 | DALL-E 3 isn't robustly compositional | Fu et al. (2025), [LIT-938](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-938.md), read in full in [NOTE-813](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-813.md). Three human-rating experiments on one model: the reversal drop is significant (t(29) = 3.67), the compositional result is descriptive, and the error analysis covers only images below 0.2 agreement. The authors' explanation by training-data likelihood rests on a Spearman r of 0.09 against a GPT-3 proxy. The finding is about one generator, and the ">5 objects" failure often quoted with it comes from the vision-language models, not from DALL-E 3. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-251](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-251.md) | Few-shot failures arise at the readout | Kirsanov et al. (2025), [LIT-946](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-946.md), read in [NOTE-789](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-789.md): at five demonstrations, accuracy across draws of examples runs from below 0.1 to about 0.6 while final-layer manifold capacity barely moves, and consistently swapped labels fail while capacity matches gold labels. The readout explanation is inferred from that dissociation, not measured; base Llama-3.1-8B and Gemma-2-2B, mostly synthetic data. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-252](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-252.md) v2 | On functionalism, idle clamps alter experience | Gidon, Aru and Larkum (2025), [LIT-1000](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1000.md), read in full in [NOTE-818](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-818.md): a voltage clamp replaying a recorded response injects no current on the matching stimulus yet fixes the network's transitions on every other, so on the Turing–Putnam definition the computation degenerates while nothing that happens changes. It is a conditional about the view, not evidence about experience; the simulation shows only what an ideal clamp does, and the premise that removing unexercised branches changes experience is cited, not defended. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-254](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-254.md) v2 | Tangles match communities only when sharp | Salter-Duke (2024), [LIT-955](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-955.md), a PhD thesis read in full in [NOTE-814](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-814.md). Edge-connectivity tangles, computed exactly at low order on eleven small real networks, give communities close to standard methods where structure is strong (yeast PPI) and none or almost none where it is weak (karate club, C. elegans, college football at the orders reached), and where tangles divide a network some hold only one to three vertices. The relation is read by eye from eight networks, and the vertex sets depend on the author's assignment rule. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-257](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-257.md) v4 | VAR models rarely have exact emergent macros | Barnett and Seth (2023), [LIT-979](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-979.md), read in [NOTE-791](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-791.md): definition (2.6), transitivity (App. A), the causal-graph form (2.12), the state-space closed form (3.18) and the genericity count (3.25)–(3.26). The target is the coarse variable's own future, so no outside query is chosen. But the system/environment boundary, the scale and the class of maps are inputs, and the worked theory's candidates are linear subspaces, not partitions. The cost is multimodal, with every local optimum kept. The criterion is closure, not locality or informativeness about a far environment. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-258](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-258.md) | Feedback optimization targets vulnerable users | Williams et al. (2024), [LIT-1008](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1008.md), §4.2 and Appendix F.2, read in full in [NOTE-798](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-798.md). Shown in simulation only, in one environment class (therapy-talk), with the users' gameability written into the simulated rater's prompt and harm judged by an LLM. The behaviour targeted is overt validation, which the paper also calls extreme sycophancy; the covert behaviours (lying, omission) were not tested against a small minority. It is a case of influence fixed by selection, not a finding that anyone was manipulated. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-262](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-262.md) | Complexity peaks with segregated integration | Tononi, Sporns & Edelman (1994), [LIT-998](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-998.md), read in [NOTE-767](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-767.md). C_N, the summed shortfall of average subset integration below a linear rise with subset size, is shown low at both extremes for one family of Gaussian matrices, and higher for patchy than for uniform wiring in one simulated visual area and in small linear systems. All of it is simulation. It is a whole-system number over fixed components: it does not find units or boundaries. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-264](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-264.md) v2 | Demos and instructions use different heads | Davidson et al. (NeurIPS 2025), [LIT-942](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-942.md), read in [NOTE-803](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-803.md): 4 to 7 of the top 20 function-vector heads are shared between the two forms in twelve Llama and OLMo models, the two vectors add, and swapping heads and activations between them costs accuracy. Kirsanov et al. (2025), [LIT-946](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-946.md), read in [NOTE-789](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-789.md), find the same split in representational geometry. Neither shows that no common representation exists, only that these methods find none; neither varies a pragmatic frame. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-268](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-268.md) v3 | Averaged emergence can be locally negative | Varley (2022), [LIT-953](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-953.md), read in full in [NOTE-756](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-756.md). Both the coarse-graining and the ΦID accounts of emergence score an expected past–future mutual information, whose pointwise values can be negative. In one constructed toy, about 53% of informative micro transitions map to misinformative macro ones, and the synergy atom is negative for 31.25% of transitions, while both averages are positive. The paper argues the possibility is general and shows it in instances; it does not show that every system flickers, or say what a negative moment means. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-273](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-273.md) v2 | Usefulness doesn't suffice for natural kinds | Bird and Tobin, SEP "Natural Kinds" (2008; rev. 2022), [LIT-244](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-244.md), read in full in [NOTE-769](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-769.md): §1.1.1's criteria, §1.2.1 on induction over properties and relations, and §3's report of Lemeire (2018). The necessity half is common ground; the insufficiency rests on counterexamples and, for the step to conventional kinds, on a reported argument. It does not say what does suffice, and it does not deny that usefulness is evidence. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-274](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-274.md) | Sequence models store graphs as geometry | Noroozizadeh, Nagarajan, Rosenfeld & Kumar (2025), [LIT-995](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-995.md), read in [NOTE-800](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-800.md). Empirical throughout: path-star graphs up to 5×10⁴ nodes, four tiny graphs, frozen-embedding controls; the two-layer spectral analysis is informal and rests on an unproved observation (App. F). It does not explain why deeper models prefer the geometry, which the paper poses as open, and its main transformer runs used weight decay. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-277](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-277.md) v2 | Shortest two-part code gives best-fit model | Vereshchagin & Vitányi (2002/2004), [LIT-239](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-239.md), read in [NOTE-787](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-787.md), Theorem IV.8: β_x(α) + K(x) and λ_x(α) agree to within O(log n) for a string of length n. Every set minimising K(S) + log \|S\| at complexity α is within O(log n) of the best fit there. h_x and λ_x are upper semicomputable, while β_x is not semicomputable. Restated by Grünwald & Vitányi, [LIT-224](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-224.md), §6.2. Finite-set models; computable distributions at O(log n) cost. It says nothing at the (k/2) log n scale of parametric model selection, and nothing about K(A) + K(x \| A). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-279](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-279.md) v2 | Networks learn low-order statistics first | Belrose et al. (2024, ICML), [LIT-952](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-952.md), read in [NOTE-777](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-777.md). Over training, ConvNeXt V2, Swin V2 and RegNet-Y on five small image datasets are probed with images whose class means or covariances are grafted from another class, and with maximum-entropy samples that keep only those statistics. Accuracy on these rises and then falls, often below chance. Pythia fits unigram-sampled text before bigram-sampled text. The ordering is empirical and covers orders one and two. The Taylor argument that motivates it is a heuristic, and the paper does not measure an ordered sequence beyond second order. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-286](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-286.md) v2 | Imbalance yields SELI, not simplex ETF | Thrampoulidis et al. (2022), [LIT-994](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-994.md), read in [NOTE-764](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-764.md). For the unconstrained-features max-margin problem under STEP imbalance, every solution has logits ŴᵀĤ = Ẑ (one-hot minus 1/k), ĤᵀĤ = UΛUᵀ and ŴᵀŴ = VΛVᵀ from Ẑ's SVD (Theorem 1). This is the ETF only if the data are balanced or binary. No finite ridge gives it under imbalance (Proposition 1), though the ridge path tends to it (Proposition 2). ResNet-18 and VGG-13 runs sit closer to SELI than to the ETF, and approach it more slowly at larger R. Not shown: that gradient descent reaches it, and anything with more than one seed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-287](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-287.md) | Located mediators predict OOD correctness | Huang, Tao, Icard, Yang and Potts (2025), [LIT-987](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-987.md), read in [NOTE-765](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-765.md). In Llama-3-8B-Instruct over five tasks and ten shifts, counterfactual simulation is best on 8 of 10; a probe of the located variable beats a probe of its orthogonal complement on 7 of 10. Interchange accuracy and predictive power rise together only until accuracy nears 1. It does not say that the located variables are constitutive, that causal features always win, or anything about shifts that change the mechanism. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-288](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-288.md) v3 | Activation symmetry makes latents discrete | Bird (2025, v4 2026), [LIT-976](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-976.md), read in [NOTE-759](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-759.md). Autoencoders of width 12–32 and up to three hidden blocks on CIFAR and MNIST, with rotation-equivariant affine maps, initialisation and optimiser. Elementwise tanh (B_n) and Leaky-ReLU (S_n) give beams along or against the basis, or on the ±1 diagonal, and radial tanh and Leaky-ReLU (O(n)) do not. The evidence is density plots, five seeds a condition, with no statistic. The downstream claims, that this causes grandmother neurons, superposition and neural collapse, are untested. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-291](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-291.md) | Visceromotor regions form one intrinsic system | Theriault et al. (2025), [LIT-996](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-996.md), read in full in [NOTE-761](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-761.md), reporting the group's own 3 T (N = 550) and 7 T (N = 90) studies; Barrett (2017), [LIT-542](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-542.md), read in [NOTE-434](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-434.md), for the 3 T system. The anatomy and overlap are reported second-hand. The reading the paper adds, that the named networks' psychological labels are "destined to fail" and that the brain's primary function is allostasis, is not part of this account; the authors themselves do not claim allostasis-first is correct. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-292](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-292.md) | Concept-direction alignment is a fitting artefact | Erogullari, Lapuschkin, Samek and Pahde (2025), [LIT-937](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-937.md), read in full in [NOTE-816](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-816.md). Shown at the last convolutional layer of VGG16 and ResNet18 on CelebA (natural correlations) and FunnyBirds (an injected 70% beak–tail correlation). AUROC is "largely preserved" by the paper's account, with no values in the text and no error bars. It does not say the model's own axes are orthogonal, and it says nothing about attributes that imply one another. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-298](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-298.md) | Report can't test posterior sufficiency | Seth & Bayne (2022), [LIT-982](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-982.md), "Evaluating theories of consciousness" and Box 3, read in [NOTE-849](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-849.md) from the accepted manuscript. An argument in a review, not a result: the verification of posterior-sufficiency predictions "relies on subjective report …, which in turn requires anterior cortical activity", and validating a non-report marker by theory borrows a contested theory, by introspection, unreliable report. It says the methods are lacking "at present", not that the question is unanswerable. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-300](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-300.md) | Coercion reduces the sense of agency | Haggard (2017), [LIT-1009](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1009.md), manuscript pp. 16–17 and Fig. 5, read in full in [NOTE-827](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-827.md), reporting one experiment by his group (Caspar et al. 2016). Under an experimenter's instruction to press the key that shocked a co-participant, the perceived action–tone interval was longer and the auditory N1 to the tone smaller than under free choice. It shows a reduced experience of agency, not reduced responsibility, and the review says so. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-302](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-302.md) | Action is controlled via coordinative structures | Turvey (1977; read in the 1975 Haskins report), [LIT-904](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-904.md), read in [NOTE-826](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-826.md). Argued from Bernstein's degrees-of-freedom problem and Greene's equivalence classes, and supported at the spinal level by reflex-probe studies showing the segmental apparatus retuned in the tens of milliseconds before voluntary movement, and by Fel'dman's joint that goes to a preset equilibrium whatever its initial conditions. Its extension to all levels, and to tuning set directly by vision, is the author's speculation. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-303](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-303.md) | Acyclic scenarios admit no contextuality | Vorob'ev (1962), as stated in Budroni, Cabello, Gühne, Kleinmann & Larsson (2022), [LIT-263](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-263.md), §V.B.2, Eq. 79, and App. A.6, read in [NOTE-844](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-844.md). Distributions that agree on overlaps and sit on a hypergraph with the running-intersection property glue, step by step, to one joint distribution. For sharp measurements this means a chordal compatibility graph. So CHSH's square and KCBS's pentagon are the smallest contextual scenarios. Stated and illustrated in the review, not proved there. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-307](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-307.md) | Adaptation needs parts separated by constancies | Ashby (1952; 2nd ed. 1960), [LIT-787](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-787.md), read in [NOTE-851](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-851.md), Chs. 10–16. If all successes must occur at once, trials grow as (1/p)ᴺ; if each is kept once found, roughly as N/p. Keeping one needs no channel from what is still changing to what is already right, so a fully joined system, the Homeostat included, cannot accumulate; constancies cut a system into independent parts. Exact for the type-cases; the fit to brains is qualitative. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-310](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-310.md) | Forward-looking blame makes capacity redundant | Harland (2020), [LIT-991](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-991.md), §3, read in [NOTE-847](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-847.md). Argued, not shown, against Vargas's agency cultivation model, whose free-will test sets its similarity and proportion parameters by what is co-optimal for cultivating moral agency. The argument is about that model only, and works class by class. It does not show that freedom is irrelevant to responsibility in general, and Vargas is read here only through Harland's quotations. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-311](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-311.md) v2 | Groupware fails without a benefit to its users | Grudin (1994), [LIT-757](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-757.md), read in [NOTE-835](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-835.md). The first of his eight challenges for groupware, argued from cases (meeting schedulers, voice annotation, project management) and from email's success, where the sender does a little more work and also wants the message read. An argued review, not a measurement, and Grudin himself says that removing the disparity does not guarantee use. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-316](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-316.md) v2 | Frankfurt cases spare causal-history conditions | Pereboom (2001), [LIT-1006](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1006.md), Chapter 1 pp. 1–6 and the Introduction (pp. xv), read in [NOTE-823](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-823.md), Skimmed. Fischer concedes that a Frankfurt-style case does not refute a requirement that the action not be deterministically produced by factors beyond the agent's control, and Pereboom builds causal-history incompatibilism on that concession. It does not say that determinism rules out responsibility; that is argued in Chapter 4, which was not read. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-317](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-317.md) v5 | Epistemic injustice wrongs one as a knower | Fricker (2007), [LIT-1004](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1004.md), known here only through her own three-page précis (Theoria 2008), read in [NOTE-832](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-832.md), Skimmed. The two definitions and the claim that both are ethical wrongs, not only epistemic dysfunctions. It does not say that every gap in shared concepts is an injustice: on the précis's terms the gap must be owed to the relative powerlessness of a social group the subject belongs to. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-320](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-320.md) v2 | Known classes steer which novel classes are found | Sun, Shi, Liang & Li (2023), [LIT-235](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-235.md), read in [NOTE-833](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-833.md). On the population graph, at the exact rank-k optimum, R(U*, y) = ‖(I − P_{L♭})U♭ᵀy‖² (Theorem 5.5, stated as ≤, proved as = in C.1). In a one-sample-per-kind toy, a known class sharing colour makes a colour labelling recoverable, and one sharing shape makes it worse than none (Lemma 5.4). The general error bound (Theorem 5.6) is approximate and pools all known classes into one block, and is not part of this account. Nothing here is about trained networks. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-322](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-322.md) | Agency draws on prospective signals too | Haggard (2017), [LIT-1009](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1009.md), read in full in [NOTE-827](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-827.md). A review, reporting a binding experiment in which action binding tracked the probability of a tone on trials with no tone, a patient study in which that prospective part was absent in schizophrenia, and priming studies in which ease of action selection raised the sense of control over an outcome it did not predict. It does not say the experience is accurate: the prospective part is by its nature blind to whether control was actually exercised. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-323](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-323.md) v3 | Non-normal systems hold variance spectra miss | Farrell & Ioannou (1996), [LIT-931](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-931.md), read in [NOTE-831](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-831.md), with Trefethen et al. (1993), [LIT-932](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-932.md), read in [NOTE-839](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-839.md). Linear algebra, worked in examples: growth over time t is the top singular value of the propagator, which the eigenvalues bound from below, not above. It holds in a chosen norm, and a norm can always be found that makes the operator normal. It says nothing about whether the growth survives nonlinearity. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-325](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-325.md) v3 | Noise destabilizes operators, more if non-normal | Farrell & Ioannou (1996), Part II, [LIT-929](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-929.md), read in [NOTE-842](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-842.md). Necessity is a one-line bound and the destabilization is shown in explicit examples. Genericity under noise is cited to stochastic stability theory, and the role of non-normality and damping is shown numerically. In the deterministic examples, variation much faster than the transient growth destabilizes nothing. Since 2026-10-19 the deterministic half is THEORY-724, and this THEORY holds the stochastic half. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-326](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-326.md) v2 | Hermeneutical injustice needs no powerless group | Fricker (2006), "Powerlessness and Social Interpretation" ([LIT-1046](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1046.md), [NOTE-859](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-859.md)), drawn by her own note from the book's final chapter, with her 2017 restatement ([LIT-1048](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1048.md), [NOTE-853](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-853.md)). The generic definition covers a systematic case, where marginalisation is persistent and wide-ranging, and an incidental case, a "one-off moment of powerlessness" in a "highly localized patch" of experience, which a socially powerful man can suffer. It does not say that every conceptual gap is an injustice. A gap with no marginalisation behind it, like an undiagnosed illness, is "circumstantial epistemic bad luck", and the obscured area must be of the subject's social experience. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-328](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-328.md) | Manipulation shows determinism defeats desert | Pereboom's four-case argument, as two surveys report it: Caruso's SEP entry ([LIT-1047](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1047.md), [NOTE-862](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-862.md)), which quotes Case 2, and De Marco and Cyr ([LIT-1045](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1045.md), [NOTE-856](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-856.md)), which quote Case 1 and state the best-explanation conclusion. Pereboom's book ([LIT-1006](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1006.md)) is a source for the thesis it states in its Introduction and Chapter 1, not for the cases, which are in the unread Chapter 4. It does not say that determinism is true, or that manipulation itself is what defeats responsibility. The argument says it is the determination by outside factors, and that the manipulator is irrelevant. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-330](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-330.md) | People choose their reward-optimal memory load | Howes, Duggan, Kalidindi, Tseng and Lewis (2016), [LIT-1062](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1062.md), read in [NOTE-882](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-882.md). Participants copied names shown one at a time from a mock email to a calendar. Each person's best list length in their own data predicted 55% and 46% of their choices, against 8–17% for the neighbouring lengths (N = 40 and 20). An exponential points schedule raised chosen length (6.99 against 5.07); forfeiting the whole trial on one error did not (5.00 against 5.05). 13 of 60 persistently chose a non-optimal length. There is no look-up and no model: the prediction is each person's empirical argmax. Lieder and Griffiths' description of it as a memorize-or-look-up trade ([LIT-1071](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1071.md)) does not fit the task. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-331](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-331.md) | High inference volume shifts compute up front | Sardana et al. (2024; arXiv 2023), [LIT-1070](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1070.md), read in [NOTE-881](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-881.md), and Snell et al. (2024), [LIT-1063](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1063.md), read in [NOTE-869](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-869.md). Sardana et al. minimise training plus lifetime inference FLOPs at a fixed loss under a Chinchilla-fitted law: the optimum moves to smaller models trained longer as known demand grows (28% fewer FLOPs at 30B quality and 10^13 inference tokens), and 47 runs show loss still falling at extreme ratios but more slowly than the law predicts. Snell et al. match FLOPs between a small model with test-time search or revision and a ~14× larger model on MATH: test-time compute wins at a low ratio of inference to pretraining tokens on easier questions and loses at a high ratio, and on the hardest at every ratio. Both take expected use as a known aggregate; neither has staleness or uncertainty about demand, and Snell's evidence is one model family on 500 questions. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-339](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-339.md) | Probability judgments reuse earlier answers | Dasgupta, Schulz, Goodman and Gershman (2018), [LIT-1074](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1074.md), read in [NOTE-875](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-875.md); Gershman and Goodman (2014), [LIT-1056](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1056.md), read in [NOTE-886](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-886.md); Dasgupta and Gershman (2021), [LIT-1077](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1077.md), read in [NOTE-865](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-865.md). In five small online experiments, an earlier answer shapes a later one only when the later query can use it, and errors in the first carry into the second. The authors call this amortized inference, reuse of past computation bought at a cost in bias. The speed benefit is shown once (median log-RT facilitation, n ≈ 50 per order) and otherwise assumed; storage and retrieval are free in the models; the 2021 review adds stale cached values from the planning literature, second-hand. No paper prices when reuse pays or touches stores outside the head. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-343](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-343.md) | Offloading tracks felt demand, not benefit | Risko & Gilbert (2016), [LIT-1059](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1059.md), read in [NOTE-887](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-887.md). A review: in choice/no-choice studies of rotated displays, delayed intentions and short-term memory, spontaneous offloading rises with internal demand, but it also occurs where it gives no gain (writing items down about 40% of the time at a two-item load already at ceiling), rises with lower confidence after ability is controlled, and differs between displays of equal measured demand. Expecting to have a result stored externally went with poorer memory for it. The review reports no effect sizes, the cited studies were not read, and its metacognitive model is an unformalised box diagram; the drift toward external reliance is a prediction, not a finding. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-351](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-351.md) v2 | Speed bugs let the cockpit remember speeds | Hutchins (1995), [LIT-1066](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1066.md), read in [NOTE-867](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-867.md). A stylized task analysis of one airline's MD-80 procedure, informed by observation but reporting no measurements. The speed-card booklet, filtered by the displayed gross weight, is the system's long-term memory; the values pass through speech to bugs on two airspeed indicators, and on approach the pilots judge the needle's nearness to a bug instead of recalling and reading speeds. The paper concludes that the memory is "not made primarily of pilot memory". It analyses only success, for an anticipated, mandated and invariant task with a few values needed in a fixed order, so it says nothing about search for one item among many under a deadline. Cognition in the Wild ([LIT-1060](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1060.md)) is Unavailable. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-355](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-355.md) | Arranging surroundings replaces internal search | Kirsh (1995), [LIT-1076](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1076.md), read in [NOTE-871](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-871.md), and Kirsh (1996), [LIT-1057](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1057.md), read in [NOTE-872](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-872.md). From video of cooks, assemblers and baggers and from informal observation, Kirsh classifies arrangements that simplify choice, perception and internal computation, frames their savings in search-complexity terms, and ties set-up cost to the number of choice points an arrangement serves. The 1996 paper adds a verbal investment rule with an interest factor for risk, one risk being that the change is not still present later, and upkeep against scatter. Neither paper gives a cost model or a measured saving; the 1995 paper says the savings do not "in general" admit meaningful quantitative estimation, and the 1996 paper puts mental cost outside its formalism. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-359](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-359.md) | Resource-rational analysis rederives heuristics | Lieder & Griffiths (2020; online 2019), [LIT-1071](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1071.md), read in [NOTE-873](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-873.md). Resource rationality picks the heuristic that maximizes expected utility of its result minus the expected opportunity cost of the time and resources it uses (Eq. 3), averaged over environments consistent with what is known (Eq. 4), and a five-step method derives process models from it. The support is a review of others' models recast in this frame, with numbers from those studies. The authors offer optimality as a methodological device, not a claim about people, and the method lets constraints be refitted to data. The objective is per episode, with no terms for storing, retrieving or reusing a result, or for its going stale. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-402](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-402.md) | Collective intelligence is modular bounded compute | Pilgrim et al. (2025), [LIT-046](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-046.md), read in [NOTE-055](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-055.md), with Dreyer et al. (2024), [LIT-075](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-075.md) ([NOTE-040](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-040.md)), as its clearest instance. The paper offers a four-dimensional resource inventory, a catalogue of constraints and a mapping to mechanisms, and calls the known forms of collective intelligence "aspects of a single unifying principle". [NOTE-055](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-055.md) judges it a vocabulary, not a derivation: the resources have no metric, so the framework cannot say in advance when costs outweigh gains, and its "predictions" are research questions. Filed Proposed as the account the vocabulary states. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-406](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-406.md) v3 | Networked publics collapse audience boundaries | boyd (2008), [LIT-1001](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1001.md), after Meyrowitz (1985), read in part: §1.5, §4.4, the Top Friends passage and every passage on context, segmentation, collision and Goffman in [NOTE-710](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-710.md), and Chapters 1, 4 and 7 in full in [NOTE-1432](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1432.md) (both Skimmed). An ethnography of US teenagers in 2004–2008: the dynamic is documented with interviews and examples, not measured, and the paradigm case, Stokely Carmichael's two rhetorical styles, reaches the record secondhand through Meyrowitz, who is unread. Proposed because it rests on a skim and on unmeasured evidence. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-409](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-409.md) | Mind is protective parts led by a Self | Schwartz, [LIT-579](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-579.md) (the IFS Institute's "Evolution" essay, read in [NOTE-453](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-453.md)) and [LIT-591](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-591.md) (Internal Family Systems Therapy, chapter 1 only, [NOTE-457](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-457.md), Skimmed). The model in its developer's words. Its evidence is clinical: clients' reports of parts, the founding "step back" case, and "hundreds of clients for more than two decades". No study is reported in either source, and the book's research chapter was not read. It is filed as the account IFS offers, not as an account the record has tested. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-410](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-410.md) | BCI decoding fits intention–neural identity | Pernu (2018), [LIT-147](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-147.md), read in [NOTE-091](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-091.md). A conceptual argument that turns on an empirical premise the paper asserts and does not examine: that each intention corresponds to one ensemble-average firing value. Real decoders are not simple averages, and whether the mapping holds across sessions or subjects is not checked. It is scoped by its own footnote 1 to difference-making with proportionality. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-411](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-411.md) v3 | Capability weights need only a partial ordering | Wells, IEP "Sen's Capability Approach" (2012), [LIT-284](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-284.md), read in [NOTE-257](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-257.md), §3b; with Sen (1979), [LIT-289](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-289.md) ([NOTE-258](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-258.md)), whose index is already "a partial ordering" supplemented by "conventions of relative importance" (p. 219). The arithmetic is trivial and holds; the attribution of the intersection and ranges-of-weights devices to a particular Sen text is not given by the IEP, and the SEP ([LIT-283](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-283.md)) says Sen "has never explained in detail" how selection should be done. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-412](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-412.md) v2 | Driven matter looks adapted without replication | Perunov, Marsland & England (2014; Phys. Rev. X 2016), [LIT-518](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-518.md), read in [NOTE-416](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-416.md), on England's macrostate relation ([LIT-515](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-515.md)). The log-odds of two driven outcomes decompose exactly into an internal-entropy term, a reversal term and Ψ − Φ = −ln⟨e^{−βΔQ}⟩. The "tendency towards adaptation" needs the first two held equal. The paper does that only in two single-particle hopping models, argues the many-body case, and reports a driven-chemistry simulation without showing it. The reading judged the claim too weak to source a THEORY; it is filed as Proposed for that reason. "Adapted" here means absorbing the drive's work, nothing more. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-413](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-413.md) | Units of selection need not be adapted | Lloyd's SEP entry (2005, revised 2024), [LIT-160](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-160.md), read in [NOTE-184](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-184.md). Her own programme, stated in the first person, and advocacy as well as a map. The four-question anatomy is the firm part. The diagnosis that conflating interactor and manifestor is "the most common error" is asserted, not counted. Its rulings on kin and group selection, the cheater problem and the Price equation are one school's, not consensus. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-414](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-414.md) | Institutions are rules in equilibrium | Hindriks & Guala (2015, online 2014), [LIT-481](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-481.md), read with the authors' reply to six commentators in [NOTE-395](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-395.md). The equilibrium half is a clear synthesis of Lewis, Aumann, Aoki and Greif. The reduction of Searle's constitutive rules is worked once, for a toy first-occupancy property, and asserted in general; it depends on a reading of "collective acceptance" loose enough to make the "counts as" biconditionals hold by construction, and on extensional equivalence of behaviour. The reply adds that a right is a bundle of others' regulative obligations. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-415](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-415.md) | Nothing has all the marks of qualia | Dennett (1988), [LIT-433](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-433.md), read in full in [NOTE-357](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-357.md). Argued by fifteen intuition pumps, not by proof, and the author says so. The central step rests on a stipulation that two surgeries, or two adaptation stories, produce identical introspective effects. [NOTE-357](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-357.md) filed no THEORY because the record does not hold the replies (Shoemaker 1981, Block 1980); this account states the claim as the reading supports it and leaves it Proposed for that reason. Its "there simply are no qualia at all" is a tactical choice of words by the author's endnote 2. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-416](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-416.md) | Quantum work has four inequivalent notions | Vinjanampathy & Anders (2015/16), [LIT-010](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-010.md), read in full in [NOTE-011](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-011.md). The review's one synthesis (§5.2, §7) sets four definitions side by side: ⟨W⟩ = ∫tr[ρḢ]dt (Eq. 2), W = E_m^(τ) − E_n^(0) (Eq. 24), A^ε ≈ −kT ln(Z_Λ*/Z) (Eq. 49) and w^max_ε = F^min_ε(ρ_S) − F(τ_S) (Eq. 50). Only the last two agree, and that agreement is an observation that two published formulas match, for states diagonal in energy. It is an informed judgement of a 2016 snapshot, not a theorem that the notions cannot be unified. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-418](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-418.md) v4 | New individuality needs collaboration and closure | Griesemer & Shavit (2023), [LIT-188](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-188.md), read in [NOTE-173](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-173.md). A conceptual sketch, so called by its authors, with no model, data or operational criteria. The paper's two headline claims, that it describes evolutionary transitions non-circularly and that individuality is a special case of collectivity, appear only in the abstract and are not argued. Stage 3 is defined by a shared goal (§1), and §3 makes sustaining the community "a focal goal of every participating member", which presupposes the group. The one argued conclusion, that inheritance at the new level evolves "in tandem", is hedged and in tension with §2. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-423](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-423.md) | Costless visible falsehoods persist and pay | Gelman (2025), [LIT-014](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-014.md), a blog post its author calls a rant, read in [NOTE-019](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-019.md). An incentive account from three to five anecdotes: false phrasing helps a case, a channel (journals, courts, media) carries it, insiders treat it as a term of art, and nothing follows, so by a Gresham's-law dynamic honest argument loses. Nothing is measured, and the post is inconsistent on whether the speakers know they are lying. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-428](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-428.md) | Ritual protest can be harmonizing incivility | Walsh (2021), [LIT-209](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-209.md), read in [NOTE-164](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-164.md) from the accepted manuscript. Comparative-philosophy interpretation of Kaepernick's kneeling during the U.S. anthem. Its textual base is strong: classical Confucianism licenses incivility aimed at harmonization (after Kim 2011). Its own addition, that such incivility can be bodily and within the ritual, is moderately argued. That kneeling means reverence rather than defiance, and that sagely authority is uptake by others, are asserted, and the paper gives no criterion separating sagely uptake from virality. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-429](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-429.md) | Institutions shape growth and are path dependent | North (1991), [LIT-489](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-489.md), read in full in [NOTE-392](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-392.md). A programmatic essay, not an argument. The definition is stipulated; the game-theoretic motive for third-party enforcement is one paragraph; the evidence is narrative history from secondary sources, with the staged sequence of exchange disclaimed as history (n. 1); path dependence is carried over from Arthur and David on technology by analogy. It leaves open why informal constraints bind, which is the question Hindriks and Guala put to rules accounts. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-432](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-432.md) v2 | Myth transformation groups are cut by the analyst | Descola (2016), [LIT-822](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-822.md), read in [NOTE-641](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-641.md), distinguishes a Goethean regime (variants developed from an initial form by a rule, as in kinship) from a Thompsonian one (deformation between given forms, as in myth), and cites Lévi-Strauss's own admission that the myth group is a continuum the analyst cuts. Santucci, Doja and Capocchi (2020), [LIT-807](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-807.md), read in [NOTE-632](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-632.md), implement the method and concede that every inverse or opposite term "is not obtained from the software system". A keynote's argument and a software paper's concession; no test of the claim exists in the record. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-433](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-433.md) | Replace machine thought with the imitation game | Turing (1950), [LIT-394](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-394.md), read in [NOTE-355](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-355.md). The imitation game is offered in place of a definition of thinking, not as a test of it, and Turing says he has "no very convincing arguments of a positive nature". The account's force is the other-minds parity of §6.4, which assumes, as §2 states and does not argue, that the machine's best strategy is to answer as a man would; a machine built to imitate human output is the case that assumption does not cover. It makes no claim about consciousness. Proposed, and a rival of Block's psychologism. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-434](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-434.md) | Rawls is incomplete, not transcendentalist | Valentini (2010), [LIT-290](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-290.md), read in [NOTE-262](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-262.md) from the 2010 working paper, with Zwolinski's review ([LIT-286](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-286.md), [NOTE-261](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-261.md)), which agrees with her on what the book says and disagrees on its worth. A one-sided Rawlsian rebuttal: two points are strong as textual claims (Rawls's principles are comparative; his method is reflective equilibrium), the rest moderate. The claims about *The Idea of Justice* are second-hand, and Sen's own reply is unread. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-436](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-436.md) | Pain is a functional state, not a brain state | Putnam (1967), [LIT-396](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-396.md), recorded as Skimmed in [NOTE-335](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-335.md) from a course excerpt of the 1975 reprint, which carries the four-clause hypothesis verbatim; the original is Unavailable here. Proposed, and resting on that excerpt and on a result discussed throughout the literature the record holds. Clause (1) is empty by Putnam's own admission, since everything is a probabilistic automaton under some description, and clause (3), the anti-nesting condition, is introduced with one motive, to rule out swarms of bees. The argument against the brain-state view is comparative plausibility, not evidence. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-438](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-438.md) | Deep nets' understanding is real but fractured | Freeborn (2026), [LIT-131](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-131.md), read in [NOTE-123](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-123.md). The Fractured Understanding Hypothesis is argued from four small demonstrations and cited literature, with no test of how common the five features are. The abstract names three features and §7.5 five. The paper also applies its own criteria inconsistently: its Othello verdict uses post hoc probes that it excludes from the agent. The definition of understanding it rests on is an explication, not a finding. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-440](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-440.md) | Breakdown can yield competitive authoritarianism | Drezner (2025), [LIT-022](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-022.md), an opinion column read in [NOTE-001](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-001.md), which relays Levitsky and Way's Foreign Affairs forecast largely by quotation and endorses it ("hard to disagree") without independent argument. The concept of competitive authoritarianism is theirs and well established; the record holds it only through this relay. The forecast that US democracy will "likely break down" in the second term is rated weak in the reading, and the post's index figures are second-hand. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-442](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-442.md) | Non-epistemic values enter only via error costs | Douglas (2000), [LIT-139](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-139.md), read in [NOTE-145](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-145.md). The normative half of the paper. It rests on a premise the paper declares "beyond the scope" and does not argue, that scientists are morally responsible for foreseeable consequences of error (p. 563). The direct/indirect line is drawn sharply in the conclusion but only sketched, and the reply that scientists could report uncertainty instead of accepting is not engaged. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-443](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-443.md) | Biological individuals needn't be organisms | Wilson and Barker (SEP, 2007; substantive revision 2024), [LIT-168](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-168.md), read in [NOTE-114](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-114.md). That organisms are not the only biological individuals is argued from examples; that evolutionary and physiological individuality is the most recognised distinction is a survey judgement. The nine-region framework that places each case is the authors' own and tentative, and its figures draw as disjoint the categories the text says overlap. It offers no criterion of parthood and leaves holobionts open. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-444](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-444.md) v2 | Meaning works through recognized intention | Grice (1957), [LIT-1042](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1042.md), read in full in [NOTE-735](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-735.md). The analysis is reached by counterexamples to weaker conditions (the handkerchief, Herod and Salome, the photograph against the drawing) and stated "roughly". It is an analysis of speaker meaning on an occasion, not of illocutionary acts, and its extension to timeless and sentence meaning is "a first shot" with the red light admitted as awkward. Strawson's watcher case ([LIT-1043](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1043.md)) shows its three intentions are not sufficient. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-446](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-446.md) | Reciprocal causation unrolls into acyclic graphs | Baedke, Fábregas-Tejeda & Prieto (2021), [LIT-110](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-110.md), read in [NOTE-111](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-111.md). A conceptual and visual model, worked by example for each type of niche construction and for two multi-species cases. There is no formal semantics, no completeness result and no empirical test; formalization is deferred. It sets synchronic co-constitution aside rather than refuting it, and the claim that the boundary is an "epistemic necessity" is stronger than the argument, which shows only that the model can draw one usefully. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-447](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-447.md) v2 | What matters in survival is not identity | Parfit (1971), [LIT-447](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-447.md), read in [NOTE-378](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-378.md), with the fission dilemma as Olson's survey states it, [LIT-454](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-454.md) ([NOTE-374](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-374.md)). The division argument is strong given its premises, and the premises are stated: brain-transplant survival is assumed, not argued. It does not say that connectedness matters more than continuity, which Parfit asserts for lack of space, or that a copy or a transcript is a survivor: the dependence q-memory needs is left "(whatever that is)". | Proposed |
| [THEORY-448](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-448.md) | Pregnancy defeats a consistent substance count | Meincke (2021), [LIT-142](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-142.md), read in [NOTE-115](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-115.md). The critique of the Parthood View under substance ontology holds on its own and is the paper's firm contribution. The positive view rests on five process-biology premises assumed for the sake of argument, and is programmatic by the paper's own word; "something in between one and two" has no formal content. It keeps parthood rather than rejecting it, and it draws no ethical conclusion. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-449](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-449.md) v2 | Plants may have very low moral status | Terrill & Veit (2024), [LIT-193](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-193.md), read in [NOTE-120](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-120.md). The conditional is valid; its premises A1 (graded sentience), A2 (plants may be quasi-sentient) and A3 (status graded by sentience) are assumed, and A2 is supported mainly by a popular book and commentaries. The paper gives no scale and no aggregation rule. It should not be cited as evidence of plant sentience, and the second author's later work leans against plant consciousness. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-451](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-451.md) | Singular causal claims need more than RCTs | Cartwright (2021), [LIT-213](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-213.md), read in [NOTE-161](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-161.md). The point that RCT results are not by the method evidence about another population (save under random sampling from it) is strong and standard. That no method or handful of methods can warrant a singular claim is argued from the diversity of facts a causal-process theory of change needs, with one illustrative case. That such theories yield reliable predictions is asserted, with no track record; the paper gives no method for weighing the evidence and little on transport. The critique of RCT rigour is internal to the author's own reconstruction of "rigour". | Proposed |
| [THEORY-452](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-452.md) | Supervaluation and near-identity count one cat | Lewis (1993), [LIT-1015](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1015.md), read in full in [NOTE-722](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-722.md). Two answers to Unger's problem of the many, offered together. Supervaluation makes "there is one cat" super-true at the granted cost that nothing is super-truly the cat. Almost-identity, which is overlap and not similarity, makes the many candidates "almost one". It is not transitive and its threshold is left undecided. Each covers a case the other fails: Fred's house needs supervaluation, and supervaluation is natural only where the candidates differ little. It assumes semantic indecision, perdurance and no natural joint among the candidates. It has no metric, no dynamics and no threshold, so it is a precedent for counting by something weaker than identity, not evidence for any of the record's claims. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-453](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-453.md) | Physical objects can be mere relation-bearers | Esfeld & Lam (2008), [LIT-895](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-895.md), read in full in [NOTE-695](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-695.md). Moderate structural realism: relations require relata, but relata need no fundamental intrinsic properties, and objects and relations depend on each other with no priority. Its distinctive move is primitive numerical diversity, which it says gives no identity of any sort. The GR sections show interpretive fit, not entailment. Identity is equivocal between §1, where symmetric space-times need primitive diversity, and §2, where the metric "completely determines" structural identity; the one concrete construction cited works only without symmetries and breaks the general covariance the view rests on. The no-priority argument assumes three options are exhaustive. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-454](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-454.md) v2 | Percepts enter cognition only when recoded | Block (2024), [LIT-649](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-649.md), read in [NOTE-498](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-498.md): the précis of his 2023 book, not the book. The main thesis is stated and its arguments are in the book, unread here. The working-memory half is the update: nine cited lines of evidence that working-memory representations differ from perceptual ones and are task-dependent abstractions (moderate). The rereading of the workspace as conceptualisation rather than consciousness is asserted, not argued against the consciousness reading. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-457](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-457.md) | Partner choice selects proportional fairness | Baumard, André & Sperber (2013), [LIT-508](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-508.md), read in [NOTE-407](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-407.md), with its 28 commentaries and Response. The pairwise result is cited from another paper; the extension to effort and talent is unproven by the authors' own statement. The evidence is a reinterpretation of dictator, ultimatum, trust and public-goods results as allocation by entitlement. The authors disagree among themselves about whether purity, loyalty and kin care are moral at all. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-458](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-458.md) v2 | Sense of ownership and agency come apart | Gallagher (2000), [LIT-453](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-453.md), read in [NOTE-377](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-377.md) from the preprint. A review with no new results: the dissociation and the comparator account are reported from Frith, Haggard and others, and the link to the immunity principle is Campbell's argument, adopted and left conditional. It is about the minimal self, not the narrative self, for which the review's own proposal is two paragraphs. It does not say which minimal self, embodied or reflective, the analysis concerns. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-459](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-459.md) | Exact duality excludes ontological emergence | De Haro & Butterfield (2025), [LIT-199](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-199.md), §14.3, read in [NOTE-178](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-178.md). A formal argument from equinumerosity and surjectivity, strictly proven for finite sets, with an argument on physical grounds for the infinite case (fn. 57). Emergence here is novel reference in the domain of application, a semantic condition, not an information measure. AdS/CFT is the exception only to incompatibility with non-epistemic emergence, not to "not indicative": on a theoretically equivalent reading, its "emergent gravity" "cannot be understood as ontological emergence". | Proposed |
| [THEORY-460](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-460.md) | LLM consciousness barriers are mostly removable | Chalmers (2023), [LIT-411](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-411.md), read in full in [NOTE-345](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-345.md). A classification of objections as temporary or permanent, argued by naming simple systems that have each feature. The credences that follow, under 10% for current models and 25% or more for conscious extended models within a decade, are illustrative by the author's warning, multiply stipulated factors under a disclaimed independence assumption, and depend on "mainstream assumptions". Biology is set aside with a reference to earlier work. It adds no evidence about any model. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-461](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-461.md) | Chatbots' bodily self-reports are untrue | Roberts (2026), [LIT-207](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-207.md), read in [NOTE-157](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-157.md). The anti-realist half is a valid conditional whose antecedent, moderate embodied cognition, is assumed at prima facie strength. It covers body-dependent states only; footnote 8 allows realism about the chatbot as a disembodied thinker, so belief and reasoning are untouched. The fictionalist half shows the attitude permissible and apt, not required, and offers no evidence that users hold it. It is not a general denial that chatbots have minds. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-464](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-464.md) v2 | Ethics turns on relations other than identity | Dufner (2025), [LIT-130](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-130.md), the SEP entry that replaced Shoemaker's, read in [NOTE-166](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-166.md). A survey that takes no side; the account is the reading's synthesis of what it reports, correcting a seeded summary that said the metaphysics "jointly settle" the ethics. It does not say identity never matters: uniqueness may matter for positional goods, and biological views support prohibiting abortion more strongly than psychological ones, without forcing it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-465](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-465.md) | Being reproduced does not entail reproducing | Bourrat (2025), [LIT-157](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-157.md), read in [NOTE-100](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-100.md). A definitional framework with no model or data. Both measures are recipes and neither is computed. The proxy for autonomy (conditional mutual information) measures resemblance given the environment, not the range of backgrounds the definition names, and the two recipes given for it differ. The overlap claim rests on a premise shown only for retroviruses, and the conclusion's "necessarily" outruns it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-467](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-467.md) | Rule-consequentialism doesn't collapse into act | Hooker, SEP "Rule Consequentialism" (2003, revised 2023), [LIT-198](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-198.md), read in [NOTE-160](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-160.md). The view's leading defender argues that the collapse objection fails once codes are ranked by the costs of teaching and internalising them, plus the assurance and temptation effects of exception clauses (§8). The premises about human nature (children's partiality, per-rule cognitive cost) are asserted, not evidenced, and the incoherence reply holds only on the reflective-equilibrium route. An advocate's survey, argued and not tested. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-468](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-468.md) | Morality is solutions to cooperation problems | Curry (2016), [LIT-503](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-503.md), read in [NOTE-408](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-408.md), with its two tests, [LIT-047](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-047.md) ([NOTE-034](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-034.md)) and [LIT-496](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-496.md) ([NOTE-412](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-412.md)). The positive half has support: the seven are described as good wherever ethnographers record them, and questionnaire items for them form seven factors. The negative half, that nothing else is moralized, is the theory's own stated prediction (p. 40). No study in the programme has tested it blind, and where non-cooperative items appear, the programme's own data show them moralized. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-470](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-470.md) v3 | Enshittification follows weakened constraints | Doctorow (2024), [LIT-033](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-033.md), the crib of a DEF CON talk read in [NOTE-041](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-041.md). It keeps the three-stage cycle of [THEORY-150](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-150.md) and adds a cause: "Not because they used to be better people, but because they used to be subjected to discipline." Argued from examples chosen after the fact, with no counterfactual; most figures are unsourced, and the text misstates the court in United States v. Google and the legal form of the EU Digital Markets Act. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-476](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-476.md) | Stage-aggregate persons make identity matter | Lewis (1976), [LIT-446](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-446.md), read in [NOTE-373](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-373.md). Shown: that identity being one-one and all-or-nothing, and what matters branching and coming in degrees, do not entail that identity is not what matters, once stages and continuants are told apart; and that under supervaluation degrees of I-relatedness equal degrees of R-relatedness. Stipulated: that persons are the maximal R-interrelated aggregates. Conceded as costly: counting persons by tensed identity, which "is not a kind of identity". | Proposed |
| [THEORY-483](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-483.md) | Inner disposition decides who turns fascist | Thompson (1941), [LIT-055](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-055.md), a Harper's essay read in [NOTE-056](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-056.md). A typology argued through vignettes of an imagined party, from a reporter who had watched Nazism rise in Germany, Austria and France. No case is verifiable, the typology is applied inconsistently (two "born Nazis"; one man both never and qualifiedly a Nazi), and its denial that class is the criterion sits badly with sketches that are mostly about class. It is filed for what Thompson argued, and the empirical literature that tested such typologies is not yet read. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-484](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-484.md) | Brain implements options-based hierarchical RL | Botvinick, Niv and Barto (2009), [LIT-581](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-581.md), read in [NOTE-451](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-451.md). Four proposed extensions of the actor-critic mapping, each matched to existing correlational findings, and predictions the authors say "call for further experimental scrutiny". The evidence for prefrontal coding of subtask segments is "only indirect". The mapping assumes pseudo-reward; other frameworks (HAM, MAXQ) would predict differently. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-485](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-485.md) | Wave-function realism leaves physics closed | Poltorak (2026), [LIT-164](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-164.md), an unrefereed preprint read in full in [NOTE-112](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-112.md). "Every physical effect has a sufficient physical cause" has two tacit parameters, a domain and a completeness relation. With the domain set to spacetime the principle fails under wave-function realism; with it set to the ontology of a complete fundamental theory it survives. The move to a breach needs a premise that wave-function realists deny. The conclusions are modest and close to analytic once the terms are defined. The target is conceded to be a picture, not a published argument, and the dynamical-to-causal bridge is asserted, not argued. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-486](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-486.md) | Family Floer equals GMN non-abelianization | Casals & Nho (2025), [LIT-017](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-017.md), an unrefereed v1 preprint read in full in [NOTE-022](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-022.md) by a reader who is not a Floer theorist. Theorems 1–3 are stated for any rank and for positive-braid asymptotics. The proofs cover exact Betti Lagrangians with finite creative networks; the meromorphic case adds hypotheses in prose, and the Family Floer functor is not built there. The analytic core is taken by citation from Ekholm 2007, which the authors patch, and from the second author's own preprint. Theorem 5, on networks from Demazure weaves, has no written proof and is not part of this account. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-487](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-487.md) | Grounding and anchoring are separable questions | Epstein (2018; rev. 2024), the SEP entry Social Ontology, [LIT-487](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-487.md), read in [NOTE-393](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-393.md) with the author's précis of The Ant Trap ([LIT-478](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-478.md), otherwise unread). A survey organised by its author's own distinction, likened to semantics and metasemantics. It rests on a survey that reports the dissents (Hawley, Schaffer, Haslanger) in a sentence each and argues the distinction by example. Whether anchoring is a relation distinct from grounding is reported as the author's view and as disputed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-490](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-490.md) v3 | Chat agent's 'I' is fixed by context of use | Shanahan (2025), [LIT-466](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-466.md), read in [NOTE-376](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-376.md), with Shanahan, McDonell and Reynolds (2023), [LIT-460](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-460.md), read for the self in [NOTE-370](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-370.md). The candidate sites of an LLM's "I", and the fact that a conversation-bound self is literally a transcript and a program, are solid. That both the model and the conversation are legitimate referents rests on two invented usages. It does not say that there is "no-one at home" or that no candidate is a self, which the papers assert without a criterion, and its subject is a 2024-vintage chat agent without tools or memory across conversations. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-491](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-491.md) | Randomisation adds only selection-bias control | Worrall (2007), [LIT-175](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-175.md), read in [NOTE-126](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-126.md). The case against the unknown-confounders argument is conceptual: frequentist balance is a long-run claim about repeated divisions, and a trial divides once. It does not show that randomised designs are no more reliable in practice than matched ones, and the meta-research cited is mixed. The selection-bias argument is conceded as "cast-iron", so the account does not say randomisation is worthless. Haphazard allocation is asserted to serve as well, without discussing whether such rules are predictable. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-492](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-492.md) | Geochemistry forced metabolism into existence | Morowitz & Smith (2006 working paper; Complexity 2007), [LIT-528](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-528.md), read in [NOTE-425](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-425.md). An essay with no calculation, which says itself that the thesis "has not been quantitatively demonstrated". Its evidence is the structure of present-day core metabolism, read back into its origin. Its framework is Jaynesian entropy maximization over states that include currents, and it rejects entropy-production principles. The reading judged that no THEORY was indicated; this one is filed as Proposed, a conjecture with a stated research programme. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-494](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-494.md) | Puritanism is cooperative morality | Fitouchi, André & Baumard (2021), [LIT-101](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-101.md), read in [NOTE-132](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-132.md). In the authors' vignette studies (N > 1,100), perceived loss of self-control mediated all of the perceived effect of indulgence on cooperativeness. The rest is a review: disgust does not amplify condemnation once harm is controlled, and a society's valuing of self-control predicts its hygiene norms better than pathogen threat. The account is agnostic about whether the norms work, excludes contamination purity by definition, and has shown that people hold the belief, not that the belief made the norms. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-495](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-495.md) | Obligation is internalized joint-agent pressure | Tomasello (2019), [LIT-125](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-125.md), read in [NOTE-185](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-185.md). A synthesis of developmental and comparative experiments, mostly from the author's lab, on WEIRD children and chimpanzees; no new data. The behavioural contrasts between committed and side-by-side play are moderately supported. That they reflect felt obligation, rather than prosociality or learned scripts, is argued, not shown. It explains the sense of obligation, not what anyone is obliged to do, as the author concedes. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-497](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-497.md) v4 | Synergy lets macro features predict the future | Mediano et al. (2022), [LIT-025](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-025.md), read in [NOTE-010](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-010.md), a review of Rosas et al. (2020), which the record does not hold. A feature V_t is causally emergent of order k iff Un⁽ᵏ⁾(V_t; X_t′ \| X_t) > 0, and a system has one iff Syn⁽ᵏ⁾(X_t; X_t′) > 0, split as downward causation plus causal decoupling. The review proves none of this and names no redundancy function. The quantities change with the partition, which the review calls intended, and they are predictive, not interventional, unless p(X′ \| X) is a do()-distribution. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-500](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-500.md) | Somatic markers prune options before reasoning | Damasio (1996), [LIT-384](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-384.md), read in [NOTE-332](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-332.md), the somatic marker hypothesis stated by its author; Bechara, Damasio, Tranel and Damasio (1997), [LIT-383](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-383.md), read in [NOTE-331](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-331.md), the experiment it is usually cited for. The robust result is a group difference: in the gambling task all 10 controls and none of 6 ventromedial patients developed anticipatory skin conductance responses. That controls chose well before they knew, and that the marker causes the choice, is not carried by the statistics. The mechanism is argued, not observed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-506](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-506.md) | Every theory of mind is bizarre, none compels | Schwitzgebel (2024), [LIT-216](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-216.md), read in full from the June 2022 final manuscript in [NOTE-188](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-188.md); the published body text was not reached. Chapter 3's Universal Bizarreness and Universal Dubiety, with the other chapters as case studies. Bizarreness is an abductive generalization over the theories actually developed, with a standing challenge to find a counterexample, not a result about all possible theories. Dubiety rests on expert disagreement, the lack of any method and cosmological uncertainty, and the 50% figure is the author's judgment. The author's own credences lean materialist, at about 55%. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-507](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-507.md) v2 | Functional isomorphs share experiences | Chalmers (1995), [LIT-392](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-392.md), read in full in [NOTE-347](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-347.md), with the one-page sketch in "Facing Up", [LIT-406](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-406.md) ([NOTE-336](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-336.md)). A plausibility argument by the author's own account: the fading- and dancing-qualia conditionals are strong given the replacement series; their rejection rests on a premise about self-knowledge drawn from familiar cases. It extends to a population of people implementing a person's neurons, so it rules out absolute anti-nesting for isomorphs. It does not reach any system that is not an isomorph of something conscious, which includes every actual AI system and every group. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-510](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-510.md) | Crop tolerance varies by class; some classes lose | Balestriero, Bottou & LeCun (2022), [LIT-234](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-234.md), read in [NOTE-845](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-845.md). Six pretrained models on cropped test images keep some classes recognisable at an 8% crop and lose others below about 50%, and agree on which. Over 20 ResNet-50 runs, moving the crop lower bound from 100% to 8% raises mean accuracy from about 70% to 76% while "academic gown" falls from about 62% to 40%. The classes shown are hand-picked; the per-class test rejects for 4.4% of classes at the 5% level, uncorrected for 1,000 tests, which alone is not more than chance; and evaluation-set noise is not counted. Theorem 1 does not reach which classes pay. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-511](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-511.md) | Non-conventional illocutions are overt intentions | Strawson (1964), [LIT-1043](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1043.md), read in full in [NOTE-736](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-736.md), amending Grice (1957), [LIT-1042](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1042.md). Against Austin, some illocutions need no convention beyond the linguistic; their force is an overt intention meant to be understood, and uptake is the audience's recognition of it, an aim rather than an achievement. Orders fit "with some strain"; verdicts, umpires' calls and marriages do not fit at all. The scheme predicts no non-institutional case in which the overt intention is fixed and the act changes, which gives [QUESTION-073](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-073.md) a definite rival to test. The amended analysis is offered as necessary, not sufficient. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-512](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-512.md) | Extended mind can reach belief, not consciousness | Chalmers (2019), [LIT-415](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-415.md), read in [NOTE-356](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-356.md), and his foreword to Clark's book (2008), [LIT-421](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-421.md), read in [NOTE-369](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-369.md). The 1998 thesis is satisfied by wired-in "extended circuits" that its critics accept, so the controversial thesis is constitution through perception and action. The perception-action boundary is then the strongest objection, met by revisionism, not refuted. Consciousness does not extend this way, on an imported criterion (direct availability, "not mediated by other mental states") and on the absence of any working twin case. Both halves are proposals defended against a few cases; the criterion is the author's earlier correlate of consciousness, not an argument made here. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-514](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-514.md) | Constraint closure doesn't single out organisms | Baedke (2025), [LIT-167](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-167.md), read in full in [NOTE-148](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-148.md). The negative half, that persister criteria are too permissive, is argued from the literature: closure has been applied to symbioses, ecosystems and eusocial colonies, and Mossio (2024) concedes that "organized systems are not necessarily organisms". The positive half, the overcomer, is drawn "with rough brushstrokes" (p. 51) from three cases, two of which are lineage-level evolution or colony-triggered plasticity, and its uniqueness to organisms is asserted, with the one contrast (colony against ant) presupposing its verdict. Proposed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-517](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-517.md) | Life raises Earth's entropy production | Kleidon (2009), [LIT-519](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-519.md), read in [NOTE-423](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-423.md). The Earth's entropy budget is dominated by the absorption of sunlight, and model studies, mostly the author's, find that biotic activity raises it. The step to Gaia is explicitly conditional on MEP, which the same review says is not established, and its feedback argument is a schematic figure. It treats life as the most effective of the Earth's dissipative processes, and gives no criterion separating a living dissipator from a convection cell. | Proposed |
