| [THEORY-518](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-518.md) | Holism's meaning instability is local and graded | Grindrod, Porter and Hansen (2024), [LIT-208](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-208.md), read in full in [NOTE-158](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-158.md). The conceptual reply to the instability objection is argued; the empirical half is four hand-picked words in two before-and-after demonstrations (a count model on Stein plus a Hemingway story; Word2vec on Wikipedia plus the SEP), top-10 lists, one run each, no metric. The abstract's proportionality of resistance to frequency is not measured, the criterion used (a preserved neighbour list) is not the one defined (relative distances), and static embeddings only are tested. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-520](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-520.md) | Interaction can gain autonomy of its own | De Jaegher and Di Paolo (2007), [LIT-571](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-571.md), read in [NOTE-456](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-456.md). A conceptual account built on coordination dynamics, with illustrative evidence: the corridor, charades, mother–infant timing and the perceptual-crossing experiments of Auvray et al., reported, not new. [NOTE-456](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-456.md) declined a THEORY because the source carries no claim beyond its definition. The claim with some support is the perceptual-crossing one; the autonomy of the interaction is a definition, and the implications are called "speculative at this stage" by the authors. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-521](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-521.md) | Generalization error can jump at critical load | Martin & Mahoney (2017), [LIT-672](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-672.md), read in [NOTE-542](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-542.md), restating Seung, Sompolinsky & Tishby (1992) and Haussler, Kearns, Seung & Tishby (1996), which the record does not hold. Generalization is set by maximizing s(ε) − α ln(1/(1 − ε)). For weights on a sphere s(ε) ~ ln ε and ε ~ 1/α; for ±1 weights s(ε) ~ −(π²/2)ε² ln ε, the first-order condition has no solution past a critical load, and the error drops to zero. Uniform bounds that see a class only through its size or VC dimension are smooth and blind to this. That deep networks have such a phase diagram is the authors' conjecture, and their mapping of label noise to load and early stopping to temperature is an analogy. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-523](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-523.md) | PCI is a proxy for Φ, not an approximation | Barrett, Milinkovic, Mediano, Rosas, Bor, Barnett & Seth (2026), [LIT-185](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-185.md), read in full in [NOTE-122](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-122.md). A position paper by sympathetic insiders, with no new formal result. The ill-definedness is restated from Barrett & Mediano (2019), which the record does not hold. That brains are non-Markovian under typical grainings rests on one 1998 citation about ion-channel currents. The proxy point follows from a definition: an approximation needs a well-defined target and an error bound. The paper's defences of IIT (the multi-dimensional measure, the "proto-consciousness" panpsychism) are revisions of the theory, not readings of it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-525](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-525.md) | Refusing persona change denies recognition | Archer & Robb (2025), [LIT-172](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-172.md), read in [NOTE-186](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-186.md). Three structural asymmetries (attention, communication, epistemic) yield an identity asymmetry, after Cocking & Kennett's directive and interpretive influence; on Darwall's and Lindemann's accounts, refusing uptake of a presented self is a wrong. Informal argument from one main case (Taylor Swift, 2018). The duties derived are fans' only, though the abstract promises celebrities' too. It needs a person on the far side, so it does not carry over to AI companions without an argument about their moral status. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-528](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-528.md) | Embedded cognition explains extended cases | Rupert (2004), [LIT-422](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-422.md), read in [NOTE-343](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-343.md). The past-endorsement dilemma is strong: without it, directory assistance makes Otto believe every listed number; with it, the organism's endorsement is the final authority. The memory comparisons are moderate: the internal side is cited research, the external side is thought experiment, and no experiment on an external store is run or cited. The step from "different fine-grained kinds" to "no useful coarse kind" is a challenge plus conservatism. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-529](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-529.md) | Representation is efficient transmission | Martínez (2025), [LIT-149](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-149.md), read in [NOTE-165](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-165.md): a position paper with no new theorem or data. Its sharpest point is a standard result: by the data-processing inequality, mutual information about a car/no-car decision can only fall from retina to IT, so a mutual-information criterion would place the decision at the earliest stage; explicitness is better read as ease of decoding. The rest is a proposal supported by selected examples. Complexity has no operational measure, teleofunctions are needed to fix the distortion measure or every system is efficient for some loss, and misrepresentation and engineered systems are not addressed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-531](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-531.md) v2 | First vs third person: opposite identity verdicts | Williams (1970), [LIT-462](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-462.md), read in [NOTE-387](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-387.md). The strongest step is shown given its premise: the last step of the series that turns amnesia into a body exchange changes nothing for the subject. The premise, that psychological change cannot remove the reason to fear pain, is argued from cases. Williams claims no criterion of identity, calls his resolution "rather shaky" and "risky", and does not treat fission. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-532](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-532.md) | Life degrades applied gradients faster | Schneider & Kay (1994), [LIT-533](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-533.md), read in [NOTE-415](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-415.md). A "restated second law" (systems moved from equilibrium "utilize all avenues available to counter the applied gradients") is offered as a corollary of Kestin's equilibrium stability result and not derived from it. Bénard convection and a draining vortex show organized structures raising dissipation. One stressed marsh, airborne thermal scans and a satellite comparison are read as ecosystems developing to degrade more sunlight; all are correlational and confounded with water. The reading judged the claims too weak to source a THEORY; filed as Proposed. The paper itself says thermodynamics cannot tell the living from the non-living. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-533](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-533.md) | Selective shutdown pay hands the President power | Moynihan (2026), [LIT-061](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-061.md), a commentary post read in [NOTE-084](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-084.md). The memo of 27 March 2026 directs payment of TSA staff from "funds that have a reasonable and logical nexus to TSA operations", citing 31 U.S.C. 1301(a) but naming no account; that much is confirmed. That the payment is illegal rests on quoted scholars, with no GAO or court ruling, and the post does not engage the memo's own appeal to §1301(a). The binary choice it gives the Speaker is the author's framing. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-535](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-535.md) | Quasi-sets count indistinguishable particles | Holik, Jorge, Krause & Lombardi (2021), [LIT-107](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-107.md), read in full from the preprint in [NOTE-127](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-127.md). The Lombardi–da Costa ontology of properties makes a quantum system a bundle of instances of universal type-properties, with no principle of individuality. Krause's quasi-set theory Q, reinterpreted over property-instances, represents an atomic bundle as a qset taking one instance from each qset of indiscernibles, guaranteed by Q's Axiom of Choice, and N particles as a subqset of quasi-cardinal N. The new formal content is about two pages (§6), the printed proofs contain errors, and states, actualization and dynamics are not formalized. The claims about Kochen–Specker and non-separability are recharacterizations by definition, not results. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-536](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-536.md) | Group attitudes are real and non-redundant | List & Pettit (2012), [LIT-730](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-730.md), their replies to an Episteme symposium on Group Agency, read in [NOTE-582](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-582.md). The claim is argued in a few pages against one commentator, Sylvan, whose paper was not read, and it points to the book ([LIT-391](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-391.md), unread). The authors grant that non-redundancy is a matter of degree and that the book takes the existence of group agents "mostly ... for granted". A position on explanation, not a proof, and not a claim that groups have experiences. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-537](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-537.md) | Causal warrant comes from eliminating rivals | Reiss (2015), [LIT-118](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-118.md), read in [NOTE-197](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-197.md) from the 2015 Durham working paper; the refereed version was not read. A conceptual proposal with one historical illustration, the 1950s smoking and lung cancer controversy, which the author says is not a test. What counts as relevant, and when to stop probing, is handed to context, and the four grades of warrant are admitted to be arbitrary. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-538](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-538.md) | Belief is intentional-stance predictability | Dennett, "True Believers", [LIT-398](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-398.md), read in [NOTE-353](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-353.md) in the revised text of 1987/1997. The criterion is substrate-neutral and silent on experience. Its adverbs are not quantified, the lectern is excluded only by gain over a baseline the essay leaves informal, and the Martian argument is an intuition pump that assumes the intentional patterns are not captured physically. "Most beliefs are true" rests on a way of counting beliefs Dennett doubts exists. Proposed, and a rival of both Block's psychologism and Searle's causal-powers account. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-539](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-539.md) | Sanctity descends from pathogen avoidance | Graham, Haidt et al. (2013), [LIT-499](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-499.md), read in [NOTE-396](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-396.md); its first statement, Haidt & Joseph (2004), [LIT-502](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-502.md) ([NOTE-400](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-400.md)); and the MFQ-2, Atari et al. (2023), [LIT-500](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-500.md) ([NOTE-398](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-398.md)). Pluralism has moderate support. The particular list does not: its evidence table gives Sanctity no primate or infant evidence and Authority no infant evidence, the foundations were matched to existing evolutionary models rather than derived, and the disgust findings behind Sanctity were later disputed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-540](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-540.md) | BCI software can be a body part, server not | Register (2025), [LIT-138](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-138.md), read in full in [NOTE-151](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-151.md). An argument from cases. It assumes that BCIs can be body parts and that no part of a person may be owned by another, and uses depth to reconcile the user's unqualified bodily ownership with the operator's property in the server. The two moral principles are its operative premises, and it says they do not depend on the real-definition ontology, which only explains them. The threshold for "high-level" is context-sensitive and unfixed, and the step that software and server are distinct coinciding objects is hedged. The conflict over servers is narrowed, not dissolved. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-541](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-541.md) | Hand-built representations give away the answer | Chalmers, French & Hofstadter (1992), [LIT-414](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-414.md), read in [NOTE-359](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-359.md) from the preprint, with Burns's review of Fluid Concepts (1995), [LIT-457](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-457.md), read in [NOTE-375](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-375.md). The BACON critique is strong; the SME critique moderate, with no alternative encoding run; the two arguments against a representation module informal. Burns turns the charges on Copycat: its Slipnet holds the domain's relevant relations, and the symbol-grounding objection to SME applies to it equally. Nothing is measured in either text. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-542](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-542.md) | Inferring speaker intent improves word learning | Frank, Goodman & Tenenbaum (2009), [LIT-815](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-815.md), read in [NOTE-611](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-611.md). On about twenty minutes of video from two dyads, annotated by the authors, the intentional model's lexicon scores precision .67 and F .55 against .06–.15 and .10–.22 for five baselines. The behavioural fits are qualitative, the baselines also produce mutual exclusivity, and the Baldwin case supplies the intention rather than inferring it. The reading said no THEORY, because the findings are specific to a small corpus and the record held nothing they correct; this account is filed Proposed for that reason. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-546](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-546.md) v2 | Persons persist by psychological continuity | Locke (1694), [LIT-464](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-464.md), read in [NOTE-385](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-385.md), with the repairs as Olson's survey ([LIT-454](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-454.md), [NOTE-374](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-374.md)) and Parfit ([LIT-447](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-447.md), [NOTE-378](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-378.md)) give them. Locke shows that same man, same substance and same person can be given different conditions; that the person's are those of consciousness he asserts and illustrates. The repaired criterion is the majority view in the survey, and its author, an animalist, argues it implies two thinkers in every chair. It is a criterion of persistence, not an account of what matters or of what we are made of. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-549](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-549.md) | Groups with same members can still be two | Ritchie (2013, online 2012), [LIT-479](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-479.md), read in [NOTE-390](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-390.md), with its 2018 sequel [LIT-486](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-486.md) ([NOTE-389](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-389.md)). Six criteria for a theory of groups, each defended by one example, rule out non-singular pluralities, Sider's fusions, Burge's aggregates and Effingham's sets; the decisive one is Coincidence. Groups as realized structures meet all six. The refutations are strong given the criteria; the criteria rest on single cases, and the positive view is a four-page sketch with no persistence conditions. It says nothing about agency or minds. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-551](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-551.md) | Russian info-war narrative isn't Kremlin-made | Fridman (2017), [LIT-088](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-088.md), read in [NOTE-070](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-070.md), traces the narrative to Messner, Dugin and Panarin and follows it into Putin's and Lavrov's rhetoric, the 2015 National Security Strategy, five laws and Levada polling. That it is present in official discourse is strongly supported; that its politicisation was not Kremlin-led rests on chronology that fails for Dugin, and the doctrine-to-law order is reversed for four of five laws. Clark (2020), [LIT-023](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-023.md), read in [NOTE-012](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-012.md), finds the same belief in military writing and also rejects the merely-cynical reading. The two share no evidence. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-554](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-554.md) v2 | Standing grounds don't secure human priority | Schwitzgebel & Sinnott-Armstrong (2026), [LIT-166](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-166.md) ([NOTE-116](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-116.md)), with the SEP survey of animal moral status ([LIT-146](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-146.md), [NOTE-181](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-181.md)) for the failure of capacity-based human exceptionalism. A conditional, defended as one: the reviewers "take no stand on ponens vs. tollens" (p. 6) and do "not endorse" the radical conclusion (p. 38). The scientific premises are called "not unreasonable" and not argued, so the account is only as strong as they are. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-556](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-556.md) v2 | Algorithms evidence kinds but don't define them | Watson (2023), [LIT-187](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-187.md), read in full in [NOTE-172](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-172.md). Three pairs of theses, one per task: the epistemic one (EC, EA, EG) accepted, the ontological one (OC, OA, OG) rejected, each on the same computability ground. The rejection is a bare possibility argument with no example of an uncomputable kind, and the acceptance is hedged ("or something very much like them") so far that it is hard to falsify. The pragmatic, context-relative view of kinds is asserted, not defended. Self-supervised learning and foundation models are outside its scope. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-557](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-557.md) | Mode connectivity holds beyond image classifiers | Li et al. (2025), [LIT-676](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-676.md), read in [NOTE-529](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-529.md): GCN node classifiers from different seeds, on 12 real graphs and synthetic CSBM graphs, show linear barriers that a fitted quadratic Bezier curve removes. Yao, Zhang & Tian (2026), [LIT-660](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-660.md), read in [NOTE-534](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-534.md): one pair of DDPMs and one pair of small CLIP models joined by chains of checkpoints whose training loss stays under a threshold, where AutoNEB's paths rise steeply on CLIP. The evidence is plots without barrier numbers in the first, one pair per model and retrained anchors in the second. Zhang & Blei's claim of flat paths between LDA's ELBO maxima ([LIT-677](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-677.md)) reports no results. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-558](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-558.md) | Moral judgment is intuition; reasoning post hoc | Haidt (2001), [LIT-511](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-511.md), read in [NOTE-403](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-403.md): the social intuitionist model. Its case rests mostly on non-moral evidence about automaticity, motivated reasoning and confabulation, carried over by argument. Its direct moral evidence is that harmless taboo violations are condemned and that affect predicts the condemnation better than perceived harm. The author calls it "a plausible alternative", not "an established fact". The disgust manipulations that were its direct causal evidence were later disputed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-560](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-560.md) | Gut–stress link strong in rodents, weak in people | Forssten et al. (2022), [LIT-915](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-915.md), read in [NOTE-703](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-703.md). A narrative review with no search method, by employees of a probiotics manufacturer, which documents its own translational failures: L. rhamnosus JB-1 had no effect on any outcome against placebo after "comprehensive preclinical evidence". The rodent half is well documented; the human half rests on one meta-analysis of healthy volunteers and trials with nulls. Proposed because the source is a narrative industry review; the gap it describes runs against its authors' interest. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-561](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-561.md) | Moral thresholds make group good non-additive | Floridi (2013), [LIT-901](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-901.md), read in [NOTE-698](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-698.md). A model with two moral thresholds and four positive examples; it proves nothing and reports no data. That morally loaded wholes can arise from negligible parts follows once thresholds are granted, and the reading rates it moderate. The analogy with distributed knowledge is inexact: every example sums like contributions, the threshold's value is left open, and so the line between distributed morality and a sum of loaded acts is a free parameter. Responsibility for such outcomes is not given here. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-562](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-562.md) | REST2 replica mixing doesn't show sampling | Koneru, Reid & Robustelli (2025), [LIT-076](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-076.md), read in full in [NOTE-076](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-076.md). A how-to chapter whose one load-bearing methodological point is that high swap acceptance "is not, in isolation, sufficient evidence of robust conformational sampling or convergence" (p. 18). The reason the reading draws out is that REST2's upper rungs are unphysical Hamiltonians on which disordered chains over-collapse, so replicas can swap freely without the chain rearranging. The chapter argues this and shows a passing example; it shows no failed run, and its convergence criteria have no quantitative threshold. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-563](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-563.md) v2 | Consciousness is a coarse real pattern | Taylor (2024), [LIT-461](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-461.md), read in full in [NOTE-379](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-379.md). An interpretation of Dennett offered as consistent, explicitly not as correct or as what Dennett meant. Its argument for indeterminacy in masking rests on Dennett's idealised description of the cases, which Taylor calls "somewhat simplistic". It does not say which real pattern consciousness is, or what makes a real pattern a conscious one rather than a belief pattern. Filed as the account the reading states, at the strength the reading gives it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-564](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-564.md) v2 | Model can grow its own structure, unreliably | Smith, Schwartenbeck, Parr and Friston (2020), [LIT-615](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-615.md), read in [NOTE-485](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-485.md). Expansion works in the toy domain over eight runs per condition, and only for novel stimuli. Reduction is the weak half: over 100 runs, the true number of concepts won in 45–80% of runs for four to seven, never for two or three, and in every run when the likelihood was given. Table 1 is the record's only measurement of how often reduction picks the generating structure when the parent model was itself learned. One initialisation; eight concepts, six binary features. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-565](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-565.md) v3 | Diffusion maps can recover Laplace–Beltrami | Coifman et al. (2005), [LIT-981](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-981.md), read in full in [NOTE-1441](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1441.md). The finite construction and its isometry are [THEORY-728](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-728.md); the paper's own diffusion distance is the one ã^(m) induces, not the inverse-stationary-weighted one. Theorem 2.1 and the α-family are stated without proof; the companion ([LIT-1246](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1246.md), [NOTE-985](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-985.md)) proves the α-family's limit, Active without boundary as [THEORY-744](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-744.md), and its heat-kernel step is [QUESTION-231](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-231.md). Self-adjointness comes from the kernel's symmetry, and "directed diffusion" is anisotropic, not a non-reversible chain. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-570](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-570.md) | Emotions are resource selections, like thinking | Minsky (2006), The Emotion Machine, [LIT-432](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-432.md), read in [NOTE-348](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-348.md) from the author's 2005 draft. A design argued from examples, thought experiments and the author's own AI programs, with no experiment; Minsky marks several parts as his untested conjecture. It disagrees directly with the body-state views of emotion and of feeling. On Elliot it proposes the reverse causal order to Damasio's, with no evidence offered. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-571](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-571.md) | Brain states are metastable landscape dynamics | Vohryzek, Cabral, Vuust, Deco & Kringelbach (2022), [LIT-080](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-080.md), read in full in [NOTE-054](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-054.md). A perspective that reports no data: the landscape (Fig. 6) is illustrative, adapted from earlier work, and no study measures depressed and psychedelic states on a common scale. The psychedelic evidence is small cited studies of broader substate repertoires and higher signal diversity; the depression evidence is three studies, one in remitted patients, though the abstract calls depression "excessively rigid". The modelling section is heavily self-citing. Proposed: a framing, with the record's rival description of the same dynamics as continuous in [THEORY-088](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-088.md). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-572](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-572.md) | Replication can't delineate an unclear effect | Feest (2019), [LIT-161](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-161.md), read in [NOTE-196](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-196.md) from the PSA 2018 manuscript; the version of record was not read. An informal argument with one historical case, the Mozart effect, declared "typical" without further evidence. The claim that direct replication says "nothing" about systematic error is overstated: multi-lab replications vary some tacit lab-level factors. The conclusion is scoped by the author to effects not yet well conceptualised, and to internal validity; the title and abstract drop that hedge. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-573](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-573.md) | Pooled fluency signals help unify experience | Winkielman, Ziembowicz & Nowak (2015), [LIT-190](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-190.md), read in full in [NOTE-146](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-146.md). An opinion piece whose main evidence is the authors' own three experiments (Ziembowicz et al. 2013), summarised without statistics and not read by the record. The authors state that direct evidence is still needed that the effects run through changed experience and that its integration is causal. No study cited measures unity of experience. The LIT is itself Proposed; this account carries its promotion condition. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-575](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-575.md) | Social groups are two kinds of thing | Ritchie (2020, online 2018), [LIT-486](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-486.md), read in [NOTE-389](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-389.md), building on her 2013 view ([LIT-479](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-479.md)). A social structure is one constitutively, not merely causally, dependent on social factors. Organized groups realize internal structures; feature groups are positions in external ones, which can be intersectional. A framework offered to "motivate", in the author's word: accounts of gender are shown to fit it, not argued for against rivals, and the work of excluding arbitrary collections is done by a restriction the framework imports. Silent on agency; the record uses it to say which groups the agency questions are about. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-577](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-577.md) | Hard-problem judgments are an easy problem | Chalmers (2018), [LIT-425](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-425.md), read in full in [NOTE-354](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-354.md). The meta-problem follows from the physical explicability of behaviour; the challenge is a constraint argued from it, "not a knockdown argument". It assumes that a zero-Φ simulation has the same intuitions on a functional reading, which an IIT theorist can deny. The paper's own favoured solution, opaque introspective models attributing primitive relations of acquaintance, is "closer to a fleshed-out explanandum" than an explanation, and the data the programme needs mostly do not exist. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-578](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-578.md) | Fisher–Rao geodesics can be low-loss paths | Tan, Long, Zhao & Laine (2023), [LIT-662](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-662.md), read in [NOTE-521](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-521.md). Two ResNet-20s at 4× width with LayerNorm, CIFAR-10, permuted by Git Re-Basin's weight matching: the straight line between them still has a large loss barrier, and a chain of 25 models optimised from it to minimise Σ JSD between neighbours on unlabelled training images keeps train and test loss low. One pair, one figure, no numbers in the text. The hypothesis that every geodesic between SGD solutions is mode-connecting is stated, not tested, and a chain whose neighbours agree in output may be low-loss almost by construction. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-579](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-579.md) v2 | Constantly used external stores can hold beliefs | Clark & Chalmers (1998), [LIT-097](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-097.md), read in [NOTE-180](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-180.md), with Clark's reply to the critics (2005), [LIT-403](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-403.md), read in [NOTE-363](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-363.md). Otto's notebook plays for him the role Inga's memory plays for her, so on role-functionalism it carries his standing belief, and Twin Otto, a duplicate from the skin in, believes otherwise. The constitutive step is carried by role-functionalism, the parity sentence and explanatory simplicity, none of them defended; the four coupling features mark a clear case and are explicitly not necessary and sufficient. Proposed: the step from causal coupling to parthood is the open point. The thesis is about vehicles of standing beliefs, not about consciousness. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-583](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-583.md) | Living systems are many nested agents | Levin (2019), [LIT-439](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-439.md), a hypothesis-and-theory essay read in full in [NOTE-341](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-341.md). A definition of the Self as a goal-pursuing collective, tied to a mechanism, gap-junctional coupling, from cited experiments on patterning and cancer. It has no model, no measurement of the light cone and no new data. Its goals are cybernetic set points, so any homeostat is a Self. Its Self is an agent and an individual, not a subject. The sentence against IIT's single Self is a bracket, and the closing remarks on experience are labelled speculation. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-586](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-586.md) | ψ-ontic states can still represent knowledge | Hance, Rarity & Ladyman (2021), [LIT-090](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-090.md), read in full in [NOTE-072](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-072.md). The formal ψ-ontic/ψ-epistemic split is contradictory by stipulation, while the informal "ontic" and "epistemic" are not exclusive. So PBR and the related theorems bound the geometry of µ_ψ, not the interpretation of ψ. The paper proves nothing; its positive criterion (Eq. 6) is predictive incompleteness, and its Appendix A makes claims the record's readings contradict. The defensible paraphrase of PBR is "not ψ-epistemic in the overlap sense, given preparation independence". | Proposed |
| [THEORY-588](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-588.md) | Separate lemma stage fails polysynthesis, idioms | Krauska and Lau (2023), [LIT-031](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-031.md), read in full in [NOTE-029](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-029.md). A Hypothesis and Theory article with no new data and no implementation. Its diagnosis of named models (Levelt, the Consensus Model, lexically sized increments, treelets) is strong as textual analysis; the case that they fail on Inuktitut, Vietnamese collocations and Hiaki suppletion is argued from a few examples each, and Eberhard et al. are conceded to handle Hiaki in part. The 8-stage replacement model and its aphasia predictions are a verbal sketch, and this account does not rest on them. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-589](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-589.md) | No mereological principle is merely definitional | Varzi, SEP "Mereology", [LIT-124](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-124.md), read in full in [NOTE-163](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-163.md). The entry's verdict, reached by surveying counterexample families: Antisymmetry "can hardly be regarded as constitutive", and most ordinary-language objections to Reflexivity and Transitivity equivocate, leaving the metaphysical ones. It is the author's informal argument, and he is a known extensionalist who gives that side the last word on extensionality. Its headline that "all composition principles turn out to be controversial" is stronger than its own verdict that bounds for overlapping things are "rather uncontroversial". It corrects the record's earlier summary, which called the partial-order core uncontroversial. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-590](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-590.md) | Autonomy's self is not identity's self | Velleman (2002), [LIT-292](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-292.md), read in [NOTE-268](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-268.md). A critique of Frankfurt's late (1990s) view that autonomy is governance by the essential character of the will, an essence that is also the condition of one's identity. It argues by counterexample (Winnicott's False Self, the Agamemnon sequel), from Freud's Rat Man, and by debunking genealogy. The positive view, that "self" marks reflexivity and that autonomous action is motivated in part by the understanding, is stated "briefly" and argued elsewhere. Frankfurt's reply is unread. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-591](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-591.md) | Cognition is contingently bound to the brain | Adams & Aizawa (2001), [LIT-438](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-438.md), read in [NOTE-368](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-368.md), restated against Clark in 2010, [LIT-455](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-455.md), read in [NOTE-380](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-380.md) from a draft. Both marks are assumed: the first on a claimed consensus, the second on how mature sciences individuate kinds. The authors grant the parity principle and that cognition could extend; the claim is that it does not. The "no science of tool use" half is offered as a bet. Rupert, the other critic, rejects the derived-content argument as question-begging. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-593](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-593.md) v3 | Perceptual learning can reshape individuation | Ivy & Mroczko-Wąsowicz (2025), [LIT-099](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-099.md), read in [NOTE-150](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-150.md). A conceptual proposal: a frame is installed by learning, often top-down, and then runs as a perceiver-specific structural principle of objecthood, so the system-level and episode-level questions about cognitive penetration come apart. The support is others' results reread through the concept, and one eye-tracking study of the authors'. The paper does not say what "bottom-up" means once priors sit in early processing, calls a frame "a specific top-down prediction" in §3.iii, and shows different weightings, not different objects. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-594](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-594.md) | Inequivalent representations needn't sink OSR | French (2010 draft; SHPMP 2012), [LIT-170](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-170.md), read in [NOTE-162](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-162.md) from the unpaginated preprint. Every technical step is imported (Wallace, Earman, Ruetsche, Halvorson & Müger, Baker); the paper's contribution is interpretive and informal. The DHR result that statistics and charge kinds follow from the algebra is strong physics; that it favours OSR is French's reading. The modal "trans-world" structure is proposed, not developed, and the combined third option "obviously requires further elaboration". | Proposed |
| [THEORY-596](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-596.md) | Believers are rational-system idealisations | Dennett (1971), [LIT-440](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-440.md), read in [NOTE-350](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-350.md), and his reply to Stich (1980), [LIT-456](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-456.md), read in [NOTE-371](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-371.md). Belief ascription presupposes optimal design relative to goals, so "a false belief system is a conceptual impossibility" and, following Quine, the evidence for ascribing p is the best evidence against ascribing a contradictory q. In 1980 Dennett concedes the price: the intentional system, and the person, is "an unrealizable idealization". Argued from the logic of ascription and from evolution by assertion; no data. It is a claim about what ascription requires, not about what is in heads. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-600](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-600.md) | Justice alone can't define disease | Veit (2025), [LIT-098](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-098.md), read in [NOTE-097](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-097.md) from the PhilSci-Archive preprint. The target is Kukla's institutional definition: a condition is a health condition iff medicalising it would be best for collective wellbeing. The argument is informal and has two horns. One is a thought experiment (p. 14). The other rests on an asserted, undocumented premise about how medical tools evolve (p. 15). The extension from Kukla to "any purely normativist account" is asserted, not shown case by case. Veit concedes the first horn bites only without moral consensus. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-604](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-604.md) v2 | Most dualities are adjunctions to an opposite | Corfield (2017), [LIT-115](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-115.md), read in [NOTE-141](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-141.md). A short programmatic paper. That most dualities of interest are covered by constructions around adjunction is shown by worked exposition of standard cases, not proved. There is unlikely to be "a single monolithic account" (pp. 59–60). Reserving "duality" for structural reversal is a stated preference, and the verdicts on string dualities are a paragraph each. The proposal that philosophers of physics need homotopy type theory is an expectation. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-606](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-606.md) | Disembodied chat agents aren't candidates | Shanahan (2024), [LIT-465](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-465.md), read in full in [NOTE-382](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-382.md) from the arXiv v2 preprint. A conditional, and the condition is the paper's method: a later-Wittgensteinian reading of consciousness language, summarised, not defended. The candidature test is stipulated and illustrated by the octopus and an imagined alien cube. The verdict on chat agents follows from it. Calling functionalism and identity theory "dualistic" is a definition, not an argument. The two passages on the self (no "self worth preserving", no "person behind the mask") are asserted and are not part of this account. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-607](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-607.md) v2 | Evolved individuals are coarse-grained summaries | Bourrat (2023), [LIT-049](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-049.md), read in full in [NOTE-064](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-064.md). The formal criterion is accuracy only: δC = C_T − C_P < θ across many traits, conditioned on the environment where ecology could fake coherence. As written it is degenerate, since the identity partition gives δC = 0. The cost that is meant to stop that is argued separately, by a 100-operation toy, and never put into the criterion. Nothing is computed on any model. The abstract's "cannot be dismissed as merely epistemic" is stronger than the body, which says one "pretend[s] as if" the level of selection changed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-610](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-610.md) | Structure, not ontology, survives theory change | Worrall (1989), [LIT-315](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-315.md), read in [NOTE-297](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-297.md). Epistemic structural realism, credited to Poincaré, offered as the one position that keeps both the no-miracles argument and the pessimistic induction. The support is one worked case, which Worrall himself calls unrepresentative because the equations survive intact, and an appeal to the correspondence principle with one further example. "Structure" and "structural approximation" are undefined. The view is agnostic about what there is; the ontic turn, Ramsey sentences and the Newman objection belong to later work. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-612](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-612.md) | Niche construction can't cause selection itself | Hazelwood (2023), [LIT-156](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-156.md), read in full in [NOTE-137](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-137.md). A dilemma against strong reciprocal causation in the extended evolutionary synthesis, aimed at Laland and colleagues. Emergence is Wilson's synchronic dependence plus autonomy, cashed out as composition; causation is Woodward's interventionism with independent fixability. Its force rests on a process/product split for selection and a compositional reading of realization, both defended by citation and flagged as contestable, and its second horn considers only two non-emergent options. The weak sense, that organisms and environments affect each other, is granted as unobjectionable. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-613](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-613.md) | MFQ-2's six foundations fit across 19 nations | Atari, Haidt, Graham, Koleva, Stevens & Dehghani (2023), [LIT-500](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-500.md), read in [NOTE-398](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-398.md). 36 items, developed in 25 populations, fit six factors in 19 nations (ESEM CFI .979). Equality and Proportionality correlate .21 on average, from .47 to −.04. Purity alone fails intercept invariance, and it carries the headline that Purity is the least WEIRD foundation. The samples are online and about 200 per nation. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-614](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-614.md) v3 | ICL can be Bayesian inference over concepts | Xie, Raghunathan, Liang & Ma (2021), [LIT-797](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-797.md), read in [NOTE-633](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-633.md). Theorem 1 is proved under Assumptions 1–5 and a distinguishability condition; Theorems 2–3 give roughly 1/k excess risk without it. The proofs were not followed in the reading. [NOTE-633](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-633.md) declined a THEORY because the result is conditional on exact fit to a specific generative model, so it is a consequence of that model, not a fact about language models. It is filed Proposed under the owner's ruling, with the condition in the title. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-615](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-615.md) | Status distrust of experts can be rational | Desmond (2022), [LIT-158](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-158.md), read in [NOTE-113](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-113.md). A "how-possibly" argument, not a demonstration: a five-step scheme (§6, pp. 16–17) from status vulnerability and service doubt to distrust "in virtue of" prestige. The paper says it shows validity only. It leaves open whether the premises ever hold in a liberal democracy, gives no data linking status to distrust, and does not compare its account with testimonial injustice or the empirical predictors of conspiracy belief. The abstract's "justifiably" claims more than the body. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-616](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-616.md) v2 | LLM attitudes belong to instances, not models | Goldstein & Lederman (2025), [LIT-206](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-206.md), read in [NOTE-138](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-138.md) from the preprint. Conditional on objective interpretationism, which the authors do not defend. The instance thesis is moderately argued; the presumptive case for attitudes rests on a tractability comparison never operationalised or measured; HHH+0 is "provisional", and its discriminating test is a conjecture. All the empirical support is second-hand and qualitative. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-618](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-618.md) | Hyperbolic neural geometry evidence is thin | Sharpee (2019), [LIT-875](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-875.md), read in [NOTE-670](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-670.md): a four-page programmatic review with no new result, whose reading filed no THEORY because its claims are conjectures. Filed here as Proposed because the record holds two tests of the conjecture, odour statistics ([LIT-872](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-872.md), [THEORY-191](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-191.md)) and CA1 place-cell correlations ([LIT-876](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-876.md), [THEORY-192](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-192.md)), and no general statement. The Zipf step shows a shared exponential count of states, which any system with extensive entropy has, not a shared metric, and the rigidity argument for three dimensions cites Mostow's theorem, which concerns finite-volume manifolds and says nothing about noisy point clouds. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-621](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-621.md) | Relative facts resolve Wigner's friend | Rovelli (2021), [LIT-177](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-177.md), read in full in [NOTE-174](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-174.md). For a fact a and exclusive facts bᵢ, the collapse rule Σᵢ\|W(c,bᵢ)\|²\|W(bᵢ,a)\|² and the unitary rule \|Σᵢ W(c,bᵢ)W(bᵢ,a)\|² differ by interference; RQM applies the first only when the bᵢ and c are relative to the same system. Decoherence makes some relative facts stable. The core rule is postulated, not derived, and inter-observer consistency gets one sentence. The chapter is expository, and several of its headline claims outrun its support. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-622](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-622.md) | Wholes of separate bodies are fiat objects | Smith & Varzi (2000), [LIT-1024](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1024.md), read in full in [NOTE-721](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-721.md). A typology with a formal sketch: ordinary closure topology for bona fide boundaries, and a Brentanian theory of coinciding boundaries for fiat ones, which are parts of what they bound. The test is whether a discontinuity is there, not who or what made it. The theory is spatial, synchronic and pitched at the common-sense level; it has no models or consistency result, and the typology is stipulated by examples. It does not map onto the record's produced/imposed distinction, and it classifies the record's combined forms as fiat without choosing among them. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-625](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-625.md) v2 | Institutions are accepted status functions | Searle (2006), [LIT-482](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-482.md), read in [NOTE-388](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-388.md) in its Papers printing, the record's readable statement of The Construction of Social Reality ([LIT-485](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-485.md), unread). Conceptual analysis, not argument: the three primitives are asserted to suffice, collective intentionality is referred to an unread 1990 paper, and the animal line is hedged. The paper revises the book: some Y terms have no X, and the general form is "We accept (S has power (S does A))". Hindriks & Guala's rules-in-equilibrium account is its rival on what a constitutive rule adds. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-626](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-626.md) | Moral judgment depends on relational model | Rai & Fiske (2011), [LIT-507](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-507.md), read in [NOTE-405](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-405.md). A theoretical review with no new data. Its strongest support is cited work on relational framing and on morally motivated violence. Which model is in force is read off after the fact, so the central claim risks being unfalsifiable as stated. Purity and ingroup loyalty are assigned to one motive, Unity, by argument. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-627](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-627.md) | Learned nudges need cognitive inspection | Schmauder et al. (2023), [LIT-179](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-179.md), read in [NOTE-171](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-171.md). An argument by analogy from Hausman's reply to Friedman: a test drive is not enough if you must repair the car. Its evidence is reported from others: an RL agent moved choices of a target lottery from 50% to 70% by exploiting documented biases (Dezfouli et al. 2020), and AI advisers learned dishonest advice against simulated clients. No case of an undocumented bias is given; that is the paper's conjecture, and its oversight proposal is unspecified. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-628](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-628.md) v2 | Graded intrinsic norms need adaptivity | Di Paolo (2005), [LIT-1017](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1017.md), read in full in [NOTE-719](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-719.md). A conceptual argument against Weber and Varela: autopoiesis in its original formulation entails conservation, not active homeostasis, so a bacterium whose intake is below consumption does not seek food "just because" it is autopoietic, and balancing at a cliff edge and falling over it both conserve autopoiesis. Adaptivity is defined, graded and recursive; pathology becomes failure of adaptivity while autopoiesis continues. There is no formal model, and the viability set is defined in one sentence. Proposed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-630](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-630.md) | Protective measurement needn't show ψ ontic | Gao (2016), [LIT-121](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-121.md), read in full in [NOTE-140](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-140.md). Under Zeno protection the pointer shifts by exactly ⟨A⟩ with no entanglement (eqs. 1.9–1.13), and projectors on regions plus a current operator give ρ and j (eqs. 1.14–1.16). Gao argues three routes from this to ψ-ontology, claimed to need no preparation independence. All three rest on the premise that the protection does not "know" ψ, which Gao's own fn. 10 partly concedes is false. The random-discontinuous-motion ontology and the collapse model built on it are further, weaker steps. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-631](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-631.md) | Unitary and open QT can't be ranked neutrally | Cuffaro & Hartmann (2021), [LIT-037](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-037.md), read in full in [NOTE-077](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-077.md). Stinespring dilation one way and dropping Lindblad terms the other make the two frameworks a tie on ontic dependence (OntFund-1) and on justification (EpFund-1). The verdict for the open theory comes from OntFund-2, which holds only if orthodox and Everettian readings are all that count, and from EpFund-2, which rests on imperfect preparation. Explanatory fundamentality is effectively abandoned. The paper proves nothing formal, and its "tout court" conclusion outruns §4. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-633](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-633.md) v2 | Experiences have no phenomenal properties | Frankish (2016), [LIT-458](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-458.md), read in [NOTE-384](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-384.md), names the view and the "illusion problem"; Dennett's reply to Chalmers (1996), [LIT-397](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-397.md) ([NOTE-346](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-346.md)), gives its earlier form, that subtracting every function from one's consciousness leaves only a conviction; Frankish (2025), [LIT-103](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-103.md) ([NOTE-143](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-143.md)), applies it to valence. A research programme, not a theory: Frankish proposes no mechanism, the instability of weak illusionism is argued by challenge, the case is abductive, and Dennett's subtraction is an introspective assertion. It keeps consciousness in an inclusive, functional sense and denies only phenomenal properties. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-637](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-637.md) | Unlimited sharing can harm open science | Leonelli (2023), [LIT-189](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-189.md), read in [NOTE-098](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-098.md). An openly normative argument from four illustrative cases (GISAID, software stigma, crop-data linkage, the reproducibility debate) and the author's earlier qualitative work. That sharing-first open science can reduce diversity and worsen injustice is moderately supported; that this degrades reliability is argued, not measured. The positive proposal, openness as judicious connection, gives no decision rule, and the critique targets an ideal type the author admits many initiatives do not fit. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-638](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-638.md) | Running a program isn't understanding | Searle (1980), [LIT-400](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-400.md), read in [NOTE-349](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-349.md) (target article only). The room is a full implementation run by a person, and his first-person verdict is read as the system's. The decisive step against the systems reply ("the system is just a part of him") is asserted, not shown, and which causal powers matter is left empirical. The argument is about understanding and intentionality, not consciousness, and it grants that machines, including artifacts with the brain's causal powers, could think. Proposed; Dennett's intentional strategy is its rival. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-643](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-643.md) | One component can build words and phrases | Bruening (2018), [LIT-071](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-071.md), read in full in [NOTE-065](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-065.md). Phrases feed English word formation productively, ellipsis and focus reach sub-word units, and claimed differences of principle (locality, adjuncts, headedness, idiosyncrasy) fail; extraction, coordination and the no-phrase constraint are restated over X0 vs XP and affix selection, with no mention of "word". The English evidence of §§2–3 is the strong part. Several sub-arguments are provisional by the author's own account, and Müller's reply in the same volume disputes extraction, coordination and the resultative argument. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-644](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-644.md) | Panpsychism's combination problems stay unsolved | Chalmers (2016/2017), [LIT-395](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-395.md), read in full in [NOTE-358](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-358.md) from the April 2015 draft. A map of the problem, not a solution or an impossibility proof, and the author says so. The dilemma is argued case by case; the strongest arguments against constitutive panpsychism, subject-summing and structural mismatch, rest on conceivability premises and on a structure-preservation principle called plausible, not shown. The verdicts on which responses are most promising are judgements of promise. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-646](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-646.md) | Rep skepticism doesn't motivate fictionalism | Drayson (2025), [LIT-112](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-112.md), read in [NOTE-117](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-117.md), against Toon's Mind As Metaphor (2023). Toon's negative argument needs "committed to internal, intentional, causal attitudes ⇒ committed to RTM", which non-representational functionalism (Lewis, Putnam, Loar) makes false; and his metasemantic case against inner representation mistakes one motivation for RTM for part of it. His positive argument faces a dilemma: a merely behavioural overall state gives fictionalism no causal advantage, and a causal one is a reason to identify it with the belief. It argues against two motivations, assumes fictionalism coherent, and sketches the functionalist alternative by citation in one paragraph. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-647](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-647.md) v2 | Ultraclose credence dissolves the lottery paradox | Wenmackers (2011), [LIT-163](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-163.md), chapter 3, read in [NOTE-139](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-139.md). Stratified Belief, B(x) iff P(x) ≃_V 1 in Hrbacek's relative analysis, satisfies a Stratified Conjunction Principle for a standard number of conjuncts (proved) and fails for an ultralarge number. The proofs hold inside the framework. That belief works this way is argued: any explicit threshold collapses the model back to the Lockean one, the author calls it "crude", and knowledge is set aside. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-648](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-648.md) | Social facts constrain from outside | Durkheim (1894; book 1895), chapter I of Les Règles de la méthode sociologique, [LIT-484](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-484.md), read in French in [NOTE-391](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-391.md). A definition argued from examples, which its author calls "un simple résumé des données immédiates de l'observation" (n. 3). Its two load-bearing steps are asserted: that what is neither organic nor individual-psychic must have society as its substrate, and that constraint is present even where no one feels it. It is a claim about the object of sociology, not a group-mind thesis. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-650](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-650.md) | Diachronic self-identity is level-relative | Floridi (2011), [LIT-136](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-136.md), read in [NOTE-130](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-130.md). The deflation of diachronic identity is an informal argument from examples that rests on the method of levels of abstraction, assumed from elsewhere; that this "is not relativism" is one sentence, and that individuation comes before identification is asserted. It is not, as its title suggests, a criterion of personal identity, and its positive answer to the synchronic question, the three-membranes model, is "somewhat figurative" by its author's word. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-655](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-655.md) v3 | Behaviour weighs kin fitness by relatedness | Hamilton (1964), Part II, [LIT-506](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-506.md), read in full in [NOTE-410](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-410.md), on Part I's model ([LIT-497](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-497.md)). Two general principles, offered as an "unrigorous" generalization, are applied to alarm calls, kin recognition in gulls and terns, clones and colonies, Hymenoptera, and fights. The evidence is anecdotal. The author calls his positive indications for distant relatives "rather few and feeble", reports Australian halictines and multiple mating as running against the hymenopteran hypothesis, and explains anomalies case by case. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-656](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-656.md) | Holistic power can't ground effective ψ | Dorato (2015), [LIT-176](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-176.md), read in full in [NOTE-105](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-105.md). Against Esfeld et al.'s holistic dispositionalism: when a subsystem effectively decouples, its Hamiltonian's masses must be intrinsic dispositions of its particles, so the holistic view must alter its ontology between the universal and the effective wave function (pp. 14–15). The argument is moderate and posed partly as questions. The paper's wider thesis, that events are a common primitive ontology for GRW, Bohm and ψ-antirealist views, shows compatibility only, and Dorato concedes the difference from Esfeld could be verbal. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-657](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-657.md) | Emergence marks are independent of novelty | McKenzie (2025), [LIT-141](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-141.md), read in full in [NOTE-124](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-124.md). The book stipulates novelty as the definition and runs twelve further characteristics over about thirty cases. The Kondo effect is novel and continuous; the liquid–gas transition is discontinuous and adiabatically connected; BKT and the hexatic phase were predicted before they were found; Butterfield's cases are novel and reduced. [NOTE-124](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-124.md) says no THEORY follows from the book as a whole, since its definition is stipulated and the logical relations among the characteristics are left open by its own account (§24). This is the part of it that the counterexamples carry. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-658](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-658.md) | Teleology line depends on the account's purpose | Nahas & Sachs (2023), [LIT-192](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-192.md), read in [NOTE-094](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-094.md) from the accepted manuscript. A metatheoretical argument: naturalising teleology serves at least two relatively autonomous projects, advancing biology and settling the naturalism debate, with different success criteria. It is worked on one dispute, the demarcation from dissipative structures. The positive pluralism (Deacon for naturalism, Walsh and the organisational approach for biology) is only "tempting to suggest", and the boundary between the projects is never drawn. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-660](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-660.md) | Branching minimises surface, not length | Meng, Piazza, Both, Barzel & Barabási (2026), [LIT-069](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-069.md), read in full with the SI in [NOTE-075](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-075.md). Only two symmetric motifs are solved, each by a local, penalised optimiser started from the Steiner layout; the "exact" mapping to string worldsheets holds for a problem the paper does not solve. The random-terminal prediction is a sigmoid fitted to one tetrahedron, trifurcations are partly made by a merging rule, the one robustness check moves the key statistic 4.3-fold, and the sprouting breakpoints are chosen per dataset with no null. Real motifs are about 25% longer than Steiner, which the model leaves unexplained. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-662](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-662.md) | Fluency is inferred processing precision | Brouillet and Friston (2023), [LIT-957](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-957.md), read in [NOTE-785](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-785.md). A perspective essay with no model and no new data. It joins Whittlesea's discrepancy-attribution hypothesis to precision-weighting. The part with moderate support is the reviewed finding that fluency judgements follow discrepancy from expected fluency (the hension effect and its extensions), reported secondhand. The precision reading and the felt/unfelt levels are proposals. "Felt" here means attended and reportable, not phenomenal, and fluency is not offered as affect. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-663](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-663.md) | Reciprocal altruism can evolve between non-kin | Trivers (1971), [LIT-510](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-510.md), read in full in [NOTE-402](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-402.md). A verbal model, with a Prisoner's Dilemma sketch Hamilton communicated, followed by a functional account of the human emotions that would regulate reciprocity. The model is plausible and was later formalized. The psychology is fitted to 1960s social-psychology findings, mostly on American students, and the heritability of the dispositions is assumed. Trivers knows "of no psychological studies on the detection of sham moralistic aggression and sham guilt" (p. 51). His "unfairness" is inequity in exchange, not the division of a disputed resource. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-665](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-665.md) v2 | Assertion is commitment in deontic scorekeeping | Brandom (1994), [LIT-794](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-794.md), skimmed in [NOTE-622](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-622.md): the Preface and the core of chapter 3 only. This states the deontic scorekeeping model of assertion, not the book's arguments for it, and rests on a skim. By the author's account the model is an idealization limited to semantic inference, with implicature left to an outer shell. It gives no single objective score, only scores kept from each perspective. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-666](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-666.md) | Autopoiesis gives organisms intrinsic purpose | Weber & Varela (2002), [LIT-1018](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1018.md), read in full in [NOTE-720](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-720.md). An essay of exegesis and convergence: Kant's natural purposes read non-reductively, Jonas's metabolism-based philosophy of the organism, and autopoiesis. The step from self-production to purpose is asserted ("Bluntly stated"), the step to subjectivity is Jonas's phenomenological inversion, and no observable is proposed for the "empirical feature" the conclusion claims. What sets autopoiesis apart from dissipative structures is placed in "concern", not in organisation. One paragraph runs from self-maintenance to a right to life. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-667](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-667.md) | Gender and race are hierarchical positions | Haslanger (2000), [LIT-480](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-480.md), read in [NOTE-394](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-394.md). An explicitly ameliorative ("analytical") account: the definitions are chosen for what a critical theory needs, and the author is "less committed to saying that this is what gender is and what race is" (p. 52). It is tied to a descriptive claim, that our gender and race talk tracks social kinds obscured by its manifest content (p. 34), which the paper asserts and does not test. Its empirical premises about race are uncited. Not a discovery about bodies, and not a claim that every female is a woman in its sense. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-669](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-669.md) | Nomological ψ pays in the theory of laws | Chen (2018), [LIT-204](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-204.md) ([NOTE-175](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-175.md)), maps the realist readings and splits the nomological one into strong and weak. Belot (2011), [LIT-100](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-100.md) ([NOTE-110](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-110.md)), ranks the costs of ψ-as-law: time-indexed laws are the serious obstacle, grades of necessity tolerable. Allori (2021), [LIT-200](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-200.md) ([NOTE-154](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-154.md)), makes ψ an ingredient of the law, which may be time-dependent and non-unique, and so concedes Belot's point that ψ behaves like an initial condition. Each move is an informal argument. Chen reports, without endorsing, the objection that the weak reading is too cheap, and Allori's reply embraces the case it treats as a reductio. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-670](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-670.md) | Dispositions are restricted possibilities | Vetter (2014), [LIT-109](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-109.md), read in full from the penultimate draft in [NOTE-125](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-125.md). A proposal, which the paper says it does not show superior to the conditional conception (pp. 6, 26). Its strongest part is negative: for any ideal world, an Achilles'-heel block that breaks only there counts as fragile, so closeness grading fails. The positive proportion measure is not defined, and the finite, maximally varied set of cases it counts over is admitted to be non-unique. The evidence is '-able' semantics and a COCA count in which none of 226 relevant uses of "disposed to" ascribes a standing tendency to an inanimate object. Finks and masks are left unsolved, and dispositions of fundamental science are set aside. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-671](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-671.md) | Open systems settle at maximum entropy production | Kleidon (2009), [LIT-519](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-519.md), read in [NOTE-423](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-423.md), states the principle and its Earth-system applications; Dewar (2003), [LIT-521](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-521.md), read in [NOTE-426](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-426.md), is the derivation it cites. The applications are model fits, mostly reported, many by the author. The derivation needs a mean-field step and an unargued assumption about path counts, and does not reach far from equilibrium ([THEORY-676](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-676.md)). "Sufficient degrees of freedom" is never made operational, so a failure can always be read as too few. The advocate's own verdict: "no one would argue that MEP is well established". | Proposed |
| [THEORY-673](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-673.md) v2 | Price equation is a generalization-sketch | Luque (2016), [LIT-205](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-205.md), read in [NOTE-101](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-101.md) from the PhilSci manuscript. The derivation and the diallelic re-derivation are strong; the generalization-sketch reading is a moderate argument by analogy with f = ma plus two case studies, whose authors recovered results already derivable otherwise. The reply to "tautology" answers the word, not the critics' point, which Luque concedes in §7.2. The paper's prescription, that biologists should adopt the equation, is asserted without comparison. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-675](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-675.md) | Linear barriers depend on data structure | Li et al. (2025), [LIT-676](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-676.md), read in [NOTE-529](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-529.md): on synthetic CSBM graphs the barrier between GCNs from different seeds falls with density and feature separability and peaks at middling homophily; GCN, GraphSAGE and GAT barriers are similar, an MLP's differ. Zhou, Zhang & Tsang (2023), [LIT-666](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-666.md), read in [NOTE-517](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-517.md): FedAvg global models from one random start under more heterogeneous clients are separated by a larger line barrier, joined by a one-bend chain, and the barrier falls with width. Both readings named this account and held it back. The GNN proofs are missing and its barriers are plots; the federated bound treats heterogeneity as isotropic noise, and its lemma and theorem conditions conflict as written. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-678](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-678.md) v2 | Boosting attention restores neglected subjects | Chefer, Alaluf, Vinker, Wolf & Cohen-Or (2023), [LIT-806](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-806.md), read in [NOTE-639](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-639.md), with T2I-CompBench++ ([LIT-798](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-798.md), [NOTE-610](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-610.md)) for the binding measurement the paper lacks. Evidence is on 276 templated two-subject prompts by CLIP image–text similarity, BLIP-caption similarity and a 65-person preference study (77–91% preferred it); no neglect rate is reported, before or after. [NOTE-639](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-639.md) filed no THEORY, because the paper's method is machine-learning practice; the account of why subjects go missing is a finding about the model and is filed here as Proposed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-680](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-680.md) | Emotion regulation differs by point of action | Gross (1998), [LIT-554](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-554.md), read in [NOTE-429](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-429.md), the founding review. It reports no data. The five families (situation selection, situation modification, attentional deployment, cognitive change, response modulation) are "working distinctions". The antecedent and response contrast rests on a handful of film studies it cites: reappraisal lowered negative experience, suppression did not reliably do so and raised sympathetic activation. The paper's own first open problem is whether regulation can be told apart from generation at all. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-681](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-681.md) | The self is a bundle of perceptions | Hume (1739, with the Appendix of 1740), [LIT-451](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-451.md), read in [NOTE-386](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-386.md). The negative half is as strong as the copy principle. The mechanism of the fiction is argued by analogy from cases of usage. The account of what unites the bundle is withdrawn by its author, who names the two principles he cannot reconcile. It does not say there is no self in any sense, and it leaves identity "as it regards our passions" to Book 2. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-682](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-682.md) | Two-stage cascade can read signal frequency | Folz, Wettmann, Morigi & Kruse (2018; PRE 2019), [LIT-034](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-034.md), read in full in [NOTE-067](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-067.md). The period independence is proved, for signals that differ by a time rescaling only; the two-stage readout is shown numerically and in the Heaviside limit; the loop's minimum length and ω ≈ √3 v/L for long axons come from linear stability analysis. The length control is a lumped delay-differential model with one parameter set and the motor velocity v never stated, so its absolute lengths, about 125 µm, cannot be reproduced. A proof of mechanism, not a model fitted to axons. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-684](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-684.md) | Narrativity isn't needed for a good life | Strawson (2004), [LIT-452](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-452.md), read in [NOTE-383](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-383.md). The separation of Diachronicity, form-finding, story-telling and revision is strong as conceptual analysis. That many normal people are Episodic rests on testimony, the author's and that of writers he classifies, with no measure. It does not say that the remoter past did not happen to the human being, only to the self one now experiences oneself to be, and that metaphysical claim is asserted from earlier papers. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-687](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-687.md) | Naive duals need metaphysics to pick a world | Le Bihan & Read (2018), [LIT-113](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-113.md), read in [NOTE-152](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-152.md) from the accepted manuscript. A nontechnical survey whose central argument is informal. It assumes a duality relates empirically equivalent models (weaker than De Haro & Butterfield's isomorphism of a bare theory), that each model is read naively and internally, and that structuralism is set aside. Its reading said it supports no existing THEORY directly; this files the conditional verdict the survey argues for, and nothing more. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-690](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-690.md) | Dualities give no real underdetermination | De Haro & Butterfield (2025), [LIT-199](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-199.md), read in [NOTE-178](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-178.md). A case-by-case argument over the book's examples, with a logico-semantic fallback (each dual entails the common core) for a hypothetical genuine case. The rich-core verdict is argued from exact cases (bosonization, electric–magnetic duality, T-duality) and does not reach AdS/CFT or M-theory, where structural-realist readings were proposed and the common core is "partial … ongoing work in physics!". The commitment holds only where an interpreted common core exists, which the authors say is not true in general. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-691](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-691.md) | The self is a narrative centre of gravity | Dennett (1992), [LIT-442](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-442.md), read in [NOTE-364](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-364.md) from a copy-edited transcription. Argued by analogy and by thought experiments whose premises are stipulated, notably that a mindless machine could write a passable novel. It does not say the self is an illusion: a centre of gravity is a legitimate posit that figures in explanations. It is a claim about selves, not about consciousness or about what makes a person persist. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-693](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-693.md) | Evaluation, positioning, alignment: one stance | Du Bois (2007), [LIT-779](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-779.md), read in full in [NOTE-590](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-590.md). Argued from short excerpts of American English conversation (Santa Barbara and Longman corpora), with no counts. The co-occurrence of the three aspects is shown in chosen examples, not tested for separability; the too/either result rests on a separate study (Du Bois 2004) whose figures are not given. It does not treat a speaker who animates someone else's stance, which it sets aside for Goffman. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-694](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-694.md) | Experience resists any functional explanation | Chalmers (1995), [LIT-406](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-406.md), read in full in [NOTE-336](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-336.md), with Nagel (1974), [LIT-096](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-096.md), read in [NOTE-089](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-089.md), for the subjective character it starts from. The test is whether "you have explained the function but not the phenomenon" is a conceptual mistake: it is for life and reportability, not for experience. The decisive premise, that any physical process could conceptually occur without experience, is asserted and deferred to a book the record holds unread. Nagel's conclusion is weaker than Chalmers's: physicalism not refuted but not yet understandable. Naturalistic dualism and the double-aspect theory of information are the proposals built on the gap, not part of it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-699](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-699.md) v2 | Insentient self-maintainers have a good | Bruckner (2025), [LIT-120](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-120.md), read in [NOTE-093](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-093.md). Proposed by abduction from agreed cases, not deduced (§4): an entity that "sustains, maintains, and renews itself in a way that responds and adapts to its environmental conditions" is a welfare subject. Plants and the hypothetical car Tessler qualify; governors, thermostats and missiles do not. The "autopoiesis" is a loose behavioural notion, not Maturana and Varela's self-production, and the thermostat line is supported only comparatively. The answer to absurd obligations borrows Bradford 2023 and makes phenomenal consciousness decide how much such welfare matters. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-703](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-703.md) | Weak emergence measured by Granger autonomy | Seth (2010), [LIT-1170](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1170.md), read in full in [NOTE-935](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-935.md). The definitions are exact; the evidence is two hand-built agent-based models. Seth concedes that the measure is epistemic: positive with missing micro factors or a limited predictor, zero with the system as predictor. Proposed until it is tested against an independent criterion. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-747](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-747.md) | Finite-memory MZ closure rivals Smagorinsky | Parish and Duraisamy (2017), [LIT-1259](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1259.md), read in [NOTE-973](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-973.md). The closure is [THEORY-760](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-760.md)'s finite Markovian augmentation. Here is how it did, as far as the paper's plots show: close to filtered DNS in integral quantities, comparable to dynamic Smagorinsky in equilibrium turbulence, clearly better on a transitional flow, and with the subgrid transfer peaked at the cutoff where DNS puts it but about 40% too deep. The paper calls the predictions "excellent" with no numbers. Its fitted memory length shortens as the resolved dynamics speed up, so the memory belongs to the cutoff as much as to the flow. | Proposed |
