| [THEORY-759](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-759.md) | Network fits low frequencies first regardless | Rahaman et al. (2019), [LIT-1261](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1261.md), Experiment 1, read in full in [NOTE-983](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-983.md). With equal amplitudes, and with amplitudes rising from 0.1 at 5 cycles to 1 at 50, the normalised fit \|f̃(k_i)\|/A_i reaches 1 at low frequency first. This is the reverse of the order by strength that [THEORY-186](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-186.md) gives for a deep linear network. One architecture, one optimiser, a 1-D input, ten runs averaged. The paper's theory gives a bound on speed, not this order. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-763](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-763.md) v2 | Euler solutions below 1/3 can dissipate | Isett (2018), [LIT-1255](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1255.md), skimmed in [NOTE-974](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-974.md): the negative half of Onsager's conjecture. With [THEORY-749](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-749.md) (Constantin, E and Titi, the positive half) it makes 1/3 the threshold. For the record, its point is that below 1/3 the energy flux into vanishing scales can survive the limit, which is the half of A3's point that THEORY-749 could not give. It does not say that this flux is a dissipative cascade. Isett's solutions start from rest, gain energy and lose it again, so the surviving flux takes both signs. Nor does it say that such solutions are limits of Navier–Stokes or describe turbulence. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-767](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-767.md) v2 | Heartbeat signals feed body ownership | Seth (2013), [LIT-1263](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1263.md), read in full in [NOTE-1000](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1000.md). An opinion article that reports, at second hand, that a virtual hand pulsing with the heartbeat was owned more (Suzuki et al. 2013, the author's own group), that a virtual body pulsing with it was identified with more (Aspell et al. 2013), and that people with lower heartbeat-detection sensitivity are more susceptible to the rubber hand illusion (Tsakiris et al. 2011). None of the studies was read here, and no control separates the heartbeat from any other periodic signal. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-768](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-768.md) v2 | Minimal self is whole-body identification | Blanke & Metzinger (2009), [LIT-1274](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1274.md), read in full in [NOTE-1002](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1002.md), with Lenggenhager et al. (2007), [LIT-1279](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1279.md), read in full in [NOTE-999](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-999.md), for the full-body illusion it leans on. Minimal phenomenal selfhood is given three dimensions: global self-identification, self-location and a weak first-person perspective. Out-of-body experience, heautoscopy and full-body illusions vary them; the rubber hand illusion is said not to. The necessity and sufficiency claims are asserted, and the agency thesis rests on adults whose agency was intact. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-769](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-769.md) v2 | Body ownership is causal inference | Apps & Tsakiris (2014), [LIT-1262](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1262.md), read in full in [NOTE-991](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-991.md), with Botvinick & Cohen (1998), [LIT-1277](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1277.md), for the illusion it explains. The rubber hand, enfacement and rubber-voice illusions are read as one inference: unimodal surprise from synchronous stimulation is explained away by shifting the probability that a part is "me". The account fits the findings; its authors grant there is little direct evidence and that it is hard to falsify with standard fMRI. It does not say why such a model is experienced as a self. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-772](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-772.md) v2 | Euler solutions can confine dissipation to pipes | Giri, Kwon and Novack (2023; Annals 2026), [LIT-1289](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1289.md), skimmed in [NOTE-1022](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1022.md): the L³-based strong Onsager theorem. Below 1/3, in Constantin, E and Titi's own scale of spaces ([THEORY-749](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-749.md)), there are weak Euler solutions satisfying the local energy inequality. In the proof the Duchon–Robert measure is a prescribed smooth function, positive in a periodic array of pipes and zero elsewhere. So the coarse-grained flux into vanishing scales is one-signed locally in space and time, in the limit, and not only for the whole box as in [THEORY-776](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-776.md). Its location and rate are inputs of the construction; it is a smooth density on a few pipes, not concentrated on a thin set; nothing is said about the sign at a positive scale or about vanishing viscosity. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-776](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-776.md) v3 | Euler solutions can follow any decreasing energy | Buckmaster, De Lellis, Székelyhidi and Vicol (2017; CPAM 2019), [LIT-1300](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1300.md), read in [NOTE-1013](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1013.md): the admissible version of Isett's negative half of Onsager's conjecture ([THEORY-763](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-763.md)). Any smooth positive energy profile can be imposed on a C^β solution, β < 1/3, so a strictly decreasing one gives solutions whose total energy only falls. Through [THEORY-749](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-749.md)'s energy balance, the coarse-grained flux then runs into the vanishing scales on every time interval. That is the one-way transfer [THEORY-763](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-763.md) could not give. It is one-way for the box as a whole, not at every point (no local energy inequality is proved); the same theorem gives increasing energy as readily, so the direction is a choice of the construction; and nothing ties these solutions to Navier–Stokes, to a constant-flux inertial range or to uniqueness. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-777](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-777.md) | Decimation keeps only relevant Fisher directions | Machta, Chachra, Transtrum and Sethna (2013), [LIT-1299](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1299.md), Fig. 3, read in [NOTE-1018](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1018.md). One lattice size, one temperature, at most six steps of b = √2 (so b^n ≤ 8), no error bars, and no fitted rates. The groups and their rates are bands the authors drew. The value y = 0 is not an operator of the 2D Ising model: it is the rate at which any direction without singular support loses information as sites are discarded. The caption's rate 2^(−d−y) disagrees with the bands and with the supplement's b^(2y−d). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-780](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-780.md) | Transcriptional regulation alone can store memory | Zhao, Wytock, Reynolds and Motter (2024), [LIT-854](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-854.md), read in full in [NOTE-655](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-655.md). Their abstract and discussion carry the model result to cells: one genotype may hold several heritable expression states without epigenetic marks, and history picks among them. They predict that a transient crp knockdown leaves zraR, melR or rhaRS changed ([NOTE-655](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-655.md), C8, untested). [THEORY-178](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-178.md) is the model result this rests on. No such perturbation has been done in cells ([QUESTION-172](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-172.md)). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-781](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-781.md) | Strong SGD noise makes symmetric subspaces attract | Ziyin (2024), [LIT-1014](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1014.md), read in [NOTE-716](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-716.md). Beyond the exact half that [THEORY-213](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-213.md) holds, the paper argues by a Lyapunov-exponent analysis that strong SGD noise makes a mirror's subspace attracting even at a strict saddle, and reads sparsity, low rank and identical neurons in trained networks as its result. That analysis rests on a second-order, diagonal- Hessian approximation, and the network evidence is a ResNet18's correlation blocks. The test is [QUESTION-206](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-206.md). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-782](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-782.md) | Grokking onset: pairs fix the representation | Liu, Kitouni, Nolte, Michaud, Tegmark and Williams (2022), [LIT-858](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-858.md), read in [NOTE-662](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-662.md), with Power et al.'s critical fraction ([LIT-341](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-341.md)). The paper presents the critical training fraction as where the training set's equations fix the embedding. [THEORY-181](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-181.md) holds the theorem for the ideal model and the match at the one size measured, p = 10 with 1D embeddings. Held to addition: for S₃ the networks generalise beyond this mechanism. The multi-size test is [QUESTION-199](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-199.md). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-783](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-783.md) v2 | Adam makes skills compete and emerge in sequence | Liu, Liu, Michaud, Gore and Tegmark (2025), [LIT-951](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-951.md), read in [NOTE-794](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-794.md). The paper explains the Domino effect, skills starting as others finish, by a coordinate-wise optimizer's competition for update signs. [THEORY-253](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-253.md) holds the simulation in their Geometry model and the rotated quadratic. The paper also shows dependent skills starting after their prerequisites (C5), so the optimizer is one source of sequential onset, not the only one. The test in a trained network is [QUESTION-193](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-193.md). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-784](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-784.md) | Data-limited loss falls as context horizon grows | Cagnetta, Raventós, Ganguli and Wyart (2026), [LIT-888](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-888.md), read in [NOTE-689](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-689.md), building on Cagnetta and Wyart's effective context window ([LIT-883](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-883.md)). The paper presents the horizon as the reason the data-limited exponent is γ/(2β). [THEORY-204](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-204.md) holds what it showed: the derivation under assumed scaling forms, and the measured overlap on TinyStories and WikiText-103 up to about 10^8 tokens. Whether the horizon is why is the test [QUESTION-233](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-233.md) asks. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-785](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-785.md) | Meaning depends on what speaker could have said | Frank and Goodman (2012), [LIT-821](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-821.md), and Goodman and Frank's review (2016), [LIT-816](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-816.md), present listener inference as the inversion of an informative speaker, the rational speech act account. The record holds as shown, in [THEORY-172](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-172.md), the fits of that model to mean bets in one-shot reference games and Bergen, Goodman and Levy's signalling-game result. This is the mechanism the fits were offered for, filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 when the narrowing dropped it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-786](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-786.md) | Nets learn grammar when correlations beat noise | Cagnetta, Petrini, Tomasini, Favero and Wyart (2023), [LIT-877](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-877.md), propose that deep networks learn compositional data by detecting the correlations between input patches and the class, and that the sample complexity is where those correlations emerge from sampling noise. The record holds as shown, in [THEORY-195](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-195.md), the measured law and the synonym-invariance it coincides with. This is the mechanism, filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 when the narrowing dropped it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-788](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-788.md) | Training past zero error yields neural collapse | Papyan, Han and Donoho (2020), [LIT-618](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-618.md), title their paper on the "prevalence" of neural collapse and present it as a pervasive outcome of the terminal phase of training. The record holds as shown, in [THEORY-083](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-083.md), only what their runs measured: three architectures with cross-entropy on seven balanced datasets without augmentation. This is the general law, filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 when the narrowing dropped it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-789](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-789.md) | Max-information coarse-graining finds RG variables | Koch-Janusz and Ringel (2017), [LIT-873](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-873.md), propose that their mutual-information criterion finds a system's relevant degrees of freedom with no prior knowledge of them. What the record holds as shown, [THEORY-194](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-194.md), is that it recovered variables renormalization already uses, on 2D models whose answer was known. This is the general thesis that result was offered for, filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 when the narrowing dropped it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-790](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-790.md) | SGD noise balances rescaling-symmetric groups | Ziyin, Li & Ueda, [LIT-1012](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1012.md), read in [NOTE-714](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-714.md), with the Itô term from [LIT-1013](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1013.md). The law of balance is proved in the SDE model of SGD, and that part is the Active [THEORY-211](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-211.md). The authors present the law as general to networks with rescaling symmetry, but test it only on small synthetic networks. This THEORY holds the general claim, for deep networks on real data, which no measurement in the record yet supports. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-791](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-791.md) | Colour naming lies near the IB bound | Zaslavsky, Kemp, Regier & Tishby (2018), [LIT-810](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-810.md), read in [NOTE-631](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-631.md), using the bound of [LIT-338](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-338.md). Their fit covers the World Color Survey languages and English, with the need distribution over meanings estimated from the same naming data, and that measured part is the Active [THEORY-163](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-163.md). The authors present the result as a property of the world's languages. This THEORY holds that general claim. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-792](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-792.md) | Orthogonal init keeps deep linear training fast | Saxe, McClelland and Ganguli (2014), [LIT-864](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-864.md), read in [NOTE-667](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-667.md). The exact depth law is proved only from decoupled, balanced starts, and that part is the Active [THEORY-187](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-187.md). Beyond it, the paper argues from MNIST runs and random-matrix simulations that random orthogonal layers are such a start in effect, because their product is an isometry, while scaled Gaussian layers are not. This THEORY holds that wider claim, which is argued and simulated and not derived. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-793](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-793.md) | Barlow Twins learns eigenvectors one at a time | Simon et al. (2023), [LIT-242](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-242.md), read in [NOTE-741](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-741.md). The stepwise dynamics, the minimum-norm end point and the kernel-PCA form are proved from aligned initialization, and that part is the Active [THEORY-229](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-229.md). Generic small initialization rests on the paper's Result 4.6, which its authors style a result and derive informally in App. C, with numerical checks at d = 3. This THEORY holds that generic case. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-794](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-794.md) | Compositional generalization needs diverse combos | Uselis, Dittadi & Oh (2025), [LIT-667](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-667.md), read in [NOTE-525](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-525.md). Their title and abstract present diversity of combinations, not data volume, as what drives compositional generalization in vision models. Their evidence is ResNet-50s trained from scratch on two-concept grids, with checkpoints chosen on the unseen pairs, and that measured part, with the factorization theorem, is the Active [THEORY-117](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-117.md). This THEORY holds the general causal claim. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-795](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-795.md) | Lasting r/place art is repaired, not unattacked | Wu & Silva (2024; v3 2026), [LIT-1032](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1032.md), read in [NOTE-724](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-724.md), claim C6 (weak). The persistence thesis drawn from ten illustrated lifecycles, filed apart from what the 2017 log measured ([THEORY-216](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-216.md)) under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4. It is the population form of what [CLAIM-280](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-280.md) needs. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-796](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-796.md) | Question-order effects obey the QQ equality | Wang, Solloway, Shiffrin & Busemeyer (2014), [LIT-795](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-795.md), after Wang & Busemeyer (2013), [LIT-834](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-834.md). The general law the PNAS paper proposes, filed apart from what its 66 Pew surveys and 72 studies measured ([THEORY-166](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-166.md)) under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4. The equality is a symmetry of Lüders projectors and a classical model with order events can meet it, so the law does not by itself favour quantum probability. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-797](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-797.md) v2 | MSE nets reach collapse along the central path | Han, Papyan & Donoho (2021; ICLR 2022), [LIT-974](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-974.md), read in [NOTE-783](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-783.md). The paper's proposed explanation of neural collapse under MSE in real networks, filed apart from its measured central-path proximity and its derivation in a renormalized model ([THEORY-278](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-278.md)) under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4. Renormalization is imposed, not measured, and every experiment used weight decay, which the derivation excludes. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-798](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-798.md) | Encoders differ by an angle-preserving map | Moschella, Maiorca, Fumero, Norelli, Locatello & Rodolà (2022; ICLR 2023), [LIT-849](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-849.md), read in [NOTE-652](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-652.md). The hypothesis behind relative representations, filed apart from what their experiments measured ([THEORY-175](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-175.md)) under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4. The source assumes it and tests it only through its consequences; it never fits a map between two spaces. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-799](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-799.md) | Geometric coarse-graining drives degree as r^ν | The degree flow that [THEORY-190](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-190.md)'s title carried before the promotion audit (batch 048) narrowed it to the asymptotic closure of the S¹ connection law. García-Pérez, Boguñá and Serrano (2017), [LIT-869](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-869.md), derive it to first order by treating the coarse-grained graph as an S¹ model at every separation. The record's exact computation shows that treatment fails between nearby supernodes, so the flow is unproved. Filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-800](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-800.md) | Hopfield stores ~0.15N; forgetting keeps recent | The large-N and forgetting clauses that [THEORY-272](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-272.md)'s title carried before the promotion audit (batch 051) narrowed it to Hopfield's simulations at N = 30 and 100. Hopfield (1982), [LIT-918](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-918.md), expects the 0.15N figure "for all large N" from a crosstalk estimate, and states in words that overload makes every memory irretrievable unless old ones are forgotten, with saturating couplings as the mechanism. Filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-801](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-801.md) v2 | Agents are systems that would adapt their policy | The definition and verdicts [THEORY-527](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-527.md)'s title carried before the promotion audit (batch 055) narrowed it to the recovery theorem. Kenton, Kumar, Farquhar, Richens, MacDermott and Everitt (2022), [LIT-909](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-909.md), propose the definition and argue the verdicts from it in §1 and §4; that it "reliably classifies humans as agents" is asserted. The verdicts are relative to the variables chosen, which the paper states. Filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-802](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-802.md) v3 | Causal abstractions are fixed only up to basis | The general reading that [THEORY-243](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-243.md) held before the promotion audit narrowed it to the three-unit network it proves (batch 062). Wu et al. (2024), [LIT-961](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-961.md), conjecture that complex models have "multiple distinct fully correct abstractions" and that the causal-abstraction framework cannot settle structural equivalence; Makelov et al. (2023), [LIT-968](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-968.md), §8, grant that crossing component boundaries makes "illusory" tenuous, and answer by privileging components. Filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 so the wide form stays a thesis evidence can confirm or reject. Its only support is the constructed tie. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-803](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-803.md) | Real networks self-similar under renormalization | The empirical claim [THEORY-190](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-190.md) set aside when the promotion audit (batch 048) narrowed it to the model. García-Pérez, Boguñá and Serrano (2017), [LIT-869](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-869.md), find six embedded real networks self-similar under the renormalization and call this new evidence of hidden metric spaces. The collapse was judged by eye over two to five layers with no null ordering of the circle. Filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-804](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-804.md) | Ince's I_ccs correctly measures redundancy | The thesis [THEORY-714](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-714.md)'s title carried before the promotion audit (batch 056) corrected and narrowed it to what I_ccs is and which properties it has. Ince (2017), [LIT-1201](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1201.md), proposes I_ccs as the redundancy measure and reads its negative atoms as misinformation and mechanistic redundancy. Filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4. The re-derivation found that I_ccs fails subset equality, the property Ince argues licenses the lattice, which counts against the thesis without settling it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-805](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-805.md) | Volume-maximizing SSL's equal-cluster prior hurts | The general reading that [THEORY-306](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-306.md) held before the promotion audit narrowed it to the explicit priors of MSN and SwAV and to one experiment with two to eight classes per batch (batch 033). Assran et al. (2022), [LIT-231](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-231.md), read in [NOTE-850](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-850.md), argue the prior for the whole class, VICReg through an informal reduction to K-means and SimCLR through a cited equivalence, and read it as the cause of the degradation reported on real long-tailed data. Filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 so the wide form stays a thesis evidence can confirm or reject. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-806](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-806.md) | Translation without parallel data is learnable | The general reading that [THEORY-270](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-270.md) held before the promotion audit narrowed it to the common-nonsense model its bound is proved in (batch 044). Goldwasser, Gruber, Kalai and Paradise (NeurIPS 2023), [LIT-941](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-941.md), read in [NOTE-804](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-804.md), motivate their framework by translating animal communication and state its lesson for translation in general, while saying their stylised models are not intended to capture natural language. Filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 so the wide form stays a thesis evidence can confirm or reject. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-807](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-807.md) | Concept combination has a quantum emergent layer | Aerts's reading, which [THEORY-255](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-255.md)'s title carried before the promotion audit narrowed it (batch 018) to the impossibility Theorem 9 proves. Aerts (2009), [LIT-934](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-934.md), read in [NOTE-808](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-808.md), fits the ∆-type deviations with one emergent subspace per pair and reads thought as two superposed layers. The narrowing was right that the theorem does not force an emergent concept, only dropping the meet or the monotone weight; this entry is the emergence reading as Aerts's thesis. Filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 so the wide form stays a thesis evidence can confirm or reject. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-808](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-808.md) | Transformers learn factored belief subspaces | The general reading that [THEORY-256](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-256.md) held before the promotion audit narrowed it to the five Mess3 and Bloch Walk factors and the 4-layer GPT-2-style models tested (batch 019). Shai et al. (2026), [LIT-986](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-986.md), read in [NOTE-758](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-758.md), present next-token training (the paper is titled “Transformers learn factored representations”) as yielding factored, orthogonal belief representations; [NOTE-758](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-758.md)'s claims C2 to C4 are each shown on one family of synthetic processes. Filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 so the wide form stays a thesis evidence can confirm or reject. It does not include the paper's inference that the preference is architectural (C5), which App. D.4 leaves open, or the claim that the factored form persists at convergence under strong noise, which Fig. 12 contradicts. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-809](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-809.md) | LMs learn facts at the capacity-optimal point | The link that [THEORY-293](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-293.md)'s title asserted before the promotion audit narrowed it (batch 036) to the optimal learner's theorem and the observation of a threshold in Pythia models. Gu, Lyu, Li and Zhang (2025), [LIT-984](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-984.md), read in [NOTE-796](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-796.md), explain the trained models' thresholds by the optimal learner's. The one quantitative check, a size exponent of 1.152 against a predicted 1.283, is recorded against it. Filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 so the wide form stays a thesis evidence can confirm or reject. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-810](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-810.md) | Market prices keep arbitrary shocks for weeks | The general reading that [THEORY-267](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-267.md) held before the promotion audit narrowed it to the 817 Manifold play-money markets measured. Rasooly and Rozzi (2025), [LIT-958](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-958.md), read in [NOTE-778](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-778.md), set the result against the received view (Wolfers and Zitzewitz, 2004) that manipulation matters only briefly, and offer it as a finding about prediction markets. Their evidence is one platform, at play-money stakes. Filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 so the wide form stays a thesis evidence can confirm or reject. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-811](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-811.md) | Kernel quantum entropy approximates KL to O(σ²) | The general reading that [THEORY-313](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-313.md) held before the promotion audit narrowed it to the one kernel family on the torus that the rate is shown for. Bach (2022), [LIT-255](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-255.md), read in [NOTE-837](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-837.md), asserts that other translation-invariant kernels and kernels on compact groups behave alike, and sketches a leverage-score argument without completing it. Filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 so the wide form stays a thesis evidence can confirm or reject. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-812](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-812.md) | ℓ₁ phase transition is universal across ensembles | The general reading that [THEORY-391](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-391.md) held before the promotion audit narrowed it to what 2,948,000 optimizations at three problem sizes showed. Donoho and Tanner (2009), [LIT-1160](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1160.md), read in [NOTE-933](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-933.md), state it as the hypothesis of "weak universality" and pose the class of ensembles it holds for as an open problem. Nothing about non-Gaussian ensembles is proved. Filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 so the wide form stays a thesis evidence can confirm or reject. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-813](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-813.md) v2 | Lazy training doesn't produce neural collapse | The general reading that [THEORY-294](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-294.md) held before the promotion audit narrowed it to the one-dimensional, zero-bias, two-class case it proves. Kothapalli and Tirer (2024), [LIT-985](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-985.md), read in [NOTE-774](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-774.md), draw it as their conclusion: the lazy regime does not collapse anything, so the data-dependence of collapse has to come from a kernel that moves with the data. Beyond the solved case their support is simulation on two-class Gaussian data, where the NTK comes out less collapsed than the NNGP. Filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 so the wide form stays a thesis evidence can confirm or reject. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-814](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-814.md) | Reproducibility needn't indicate true consensus | The general reading that [THEORY-295](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-295.md) held before the promotion audit narrowed it to the memoryless consensus model it proves. Devezer, Nardin, Baumgaertner and Buzbas (2019), [LIT-988](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-988.md), read in [NOTE-792](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-792.md), present the decoupling of reproducibility from truth as a lesson for science, not only for their model. Their model has no beliefs, no learning and no memory in the consensus. Filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 so the wide form stays a thesis evidence can confirm or reject. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-815](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-815.md) | Hierarchical NSW gives logarithmic search cost | Malkov and Yashunin (2020), [LIT-1098](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1098.md), read in [NOTE-916](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-916.md), argue that HNSW's hierarchy is what makes greedy search logarithmic: constant cost per layer over O(log N) layers, against the polylogarithmic cost of their earlier flat graph. The record holds as measured, in [THEORY-365](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-365.md), logarithmic-or-better cost on uniform data in 8 dimensions and a saturating beam width in 4. The bound is derived only for exact Delaunay layers, which HNSW does not build, and on 200 million SIFT vectors the paper's own scaling departs from a logarithm, so the thesis is stated for low intrinsic dimension. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-816](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-816.md) | Size principle follows from informative speakers | Frank, Goodman, Lai and Tenenbaum (2009), [LIT-824](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-824.md), read in [NOTE-627](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-627.md), derive the size principle from an informative speaker and present the word learner as inverting that speaker. The record holds as shown, in [THEORY-472](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-472.md), the derivation and one experiment in which mean bets matched the inversion; in those displays an informative-speaker learner and a plain size-principle learner coincide, so whether learners reason about the speaker is open. [THEORY-785](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-785.md) is the same inversion for listeners in reference games. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-817](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-817.md) | Max prediction isn't max work under feedback | Fiderer et al. (2025), [LIT-041](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-041.md), read in [NOTE-032](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-032.md), prove that without feedback the work-efficient agents are exactly the maximally predictive ones that randomise and forget their actions, and that with feedback one binary memoryless channel separates predictive, max-entropy-action and efficient agents; from that they assert that with feedback maximally predictive agents are generally inefficient. The record holds as proved, in [THEORY-026](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-026.md), only the one channel. It does not say that efficiency under feedback is a trade-off between prediction and forgetting: in the proved example the efficient agent is memoryless. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-821](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-821.md) | Locally dissipative Euler solutions exist, α<1/15 | Isett (2017; ARMA 2022), [LIT-1305](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1305.md), skimmed in [NOTE-1027](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1027.md): the first continuous, indeed C^α with α < 1/15, weak Euler solutions satisfying the local energy inequality with nonzero dissipation, and a Cantor family of them sharing one initial datum and one dissipation measure. In the construction the dissipation measure is a function of time alone, so in the limit of vanishing scale the energy flux runs one way at every place, as in [THEORY-772](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-772.md), but in a Hölder class and spread uniformly over the torus rather than set in pipes. It is switched on only while the constructor drains the solution's energy to zero at the end of its life. Where, when and how fast the energy goes are inputs; the exponent is far from 1/3; nothing ties these solutions to Navier–Stokes. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-823](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-823.md) | Tetris rotations are epistemic actions | Kirsh and Maglio (1994), [LIT-1054](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1054.md), read in full in [NOTE-878](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-878.md), with Kirsh (1995), [LIT-1076](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1076.md), read in [NOTE-871](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-871.md), argue that the extra, early and checking moves of Tetris players are epistemic actions: physical moves whose primary function is to cut the space, time or unreliability of the player's own computation. The record holds as shown, in [THEORY-360](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-360.md), only the early-rotation timing and the drop-length difference after the wall check. Over-rotation and the rise of the check with drop height rest on figures without printed numbers, and the saving is argued from a three-player pilot, not measured. Filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 when the narrowing dropped it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-824](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-824.md) | Design-based identification rose fourfold | Garg and Fetzer (2024; arXiv v2 2026), [LIT-079](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-079.md), read in full in [NOTE-083](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-083.md), read the rise in their extraction's design-backed share as a change in economics: "economic papers have increasingly incorporated causal inference methods to substantiate their claims over the past three decades". The record holds as shown, in [THEORY-674](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-674.md), only the extraction's series, whose edges were never checked against human labels and whose per-decade slope nearly vanishes with method-mix and graph-volume controls. This is the paper's reading, filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 when the narrowing dropped it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-825](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-825.md) | Hyperbolic embeddings don't put roots at origin | Yang, Zhou, Ying, Chen & King (2023), [LIT-871](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-871.md), read in [NOTE-669](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-669.md), assert for hyperbolic graph models in general what they measured for HGCN on two synthetic trees: the root is not innermost and radius reads level only partly. The general form was the lead clause of [THEORY-421](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-421.md) until that account was narrowed to the measurement on 2026-10-20 ([ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4); it is filed here so that it stays a thesis evidence can confirm or reject. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-826](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-826.md) | Pleasant mood contagion improves group cooperation | Barsade (2002), [LIT-706](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-706.md), read in [NOTE-551](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-551.md), presents emotional contagion as a general phenomenon of work groups and states its effect on group process causally: "this contagion improved cooperation, decreased conflict". The record holds as shown, in [THEORY-123](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-123.md), only what her two studies measured: ad hoc student groups, one actor as the source, and a process link that is a correlation with measured contagion. This is her wider claim, filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 when the narrowing dropped it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-827](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-827.md) | Rubber hand illusion isn't driven by expectation | Ehrsson et al. (2022), [LIT-1264](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1264.md), read in [NOTE-997](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-997.md), conclude that the rubber hand illusion is a perceptual illusion driven primarily by multisensory mechanisms ([NOTE-997](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-997.md), C8), from the synchrony difference's independence of hypnotisability in Lush et al.'s 353 participants. Lush and Seth's reply, [LIT-1267](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1267.md), shows that uniform but unequal expectations predict the same null. The record holds as shown, in [THEORY-766](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-766.md), only the report differences and that the standard controls do not equalise expectations. This is the perceptual reading, filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 when that narrowing set it aside. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-828](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-828.md) | Weight averaging moves fine-tunes inward | Gueta, Venezian, Raffel, Slonim, Katz and Choshen (2023), [LIT-658](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-658.md), read in [NOTE-515](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-515.md), conclude that fine-tuning "typically" yields models on the boundary of a region whose centre is better, and read model soups and SWA as picking points inside it (§§8–9). The record holds as shown, in [THEORY-105](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-105.md), only the probe-loss comparisons of hull points with members and the BitFit result, for RoBERTa-base on English classification. This is their geometric thesis, filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 when the narrowing dropped it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-830](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-830.md) | Sustained seeing rests on a stable sensory code | Vishne, Gerber, Knight and Deouell (2023), [LIT-644](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-644.md), read in full in [NOTE-499](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-499.md), conclude from their intracranial recordings that sustained visual experience may rest on a stable sensory representation, with frontoparietal representation serving discrete updates, and propose a stable "experience subspace". Their measurement, in ten patients and for images up to 1.5 s, is the Active [THEORY-102](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-102.md). This is the general claim that measurement was filed to support, held Proposed until a second method or cohort and a case where percept and input come apart test it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-832](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-832.md) | Fagin's Algorithm is optimal for independent lists | Fagin (1996/1999), [LIT-1108](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1108.md), as reported by Fagin, Lotem and Naor (2001), [LIT-1115](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1115.md), Sections 1 and 3, read in [NOTE-924](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-924.md): "his algorithm is optimal with high probability in the worst case if the aggregation function is strict ... and if the orderings in the sorted lists are probabilistically independent." Strict means the combined grade is 1 exactly when every grade is 1. Not read in the original; not re-derived. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-834](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-834.md) v2 | Trained outsiders-within best spot anomalies | Collins (1986), [LIT-1312](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1312.md), read in an authorized Portuguese translation in [NOTE-1042](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1042.md): the "outsider within". An argument from the sociology of knowledge and Kuhn, illustrated by anomalies Black feminist sociologists did detect. It does not say that every outsider within sees them, that insiders cannot, or that what the outsider within reports is true; and it offers no comparison of who detects what. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-838](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-838.md) | Media set what people think about, not what | The agenda-setting hypothesis, as McCombs and Shaw (1972), [LIT-1335](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1335.md), state it after Cohen and the Langs, read in [NOTE-1046](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1046.md). Their evidence is an aggregate correlation in one sample, held as [THEORY-842](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-842.md); the direction from media to public is argued there, not identified. The later literature the programme produced is not read here. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-841](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-841.md) | Prices convey dispersed local knowledge | Hayek (1945), [LIT-1337](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1337.md), read in [NOTE-1036](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1036.md). An argument, not a result: the essay gives examples (the tin shortage, the shipper, the arbitrageur) and an analogy to the rates of substitution a single mind uses, and no model of how well prices convey what decisions need. It says nothing about what prices fail to carry, and it does not argue that removing any particular public constraint decentralizes decisions. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-853](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-853.md) | More information shrinks what designers achieve | Bergemann and Morris (2019), [LIT-1313](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1313.md), read in [NOTE-1034](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1034.md), §4.2. A third face of Blackwell's order: the better-informed receiver is the harder one to steer. For many players the right order is not the statistical sufficiency of their joint information. Bayesian players only; for bounded ones a garbling can make a receiver easier to steer and easier to inform at once. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-854](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-854.md) v2 | Rankings can make their own noise real | Espeland and Sauder (2007), [LIT-1330](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1330.md), read in [NOTE-1050](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1050.md). The paper defines self-fulfilling prophecy so that it covers reactions that "increase the validity of the measure by encouraging behavior that conforms to it", and points to two channels that close through the ranking's own inputs. The paper does not measure either channel. Nor does it show that the starting differences were noise rather than quality, beyond citing Sauder and Lancaster. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-857](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-857.md) | Access and transparency remedies can backfire | James, Hynes, Whelan, Dreher and Humphry (2023), [LIT-1342](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1342.md), read in [NOTE-1041](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1041.md). "Access is however bidirectional, and access 'down' for powerful players is politically consequential"; under Robo-debt transparency "was arguably demanded of welfare recipients". The paper does not show that such remedies usually backfire, or say when they will. It also does not claim that transparency is worthless. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-858](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-858.md) | Insulating regulators entrenches designers' aims | Schram and Ule (2024), [LIT-1340](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1340.md), read in [NOTE-1053](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1053.md). The authors' general conclusion. Its evidence is one laboratory study in which capture was assigned and independence was a fixed price, so it says nothing yet about real independent agencies, about how capture arises, or about designs between the two extremes. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-859](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-859.md) | Capture can work through evaluative frameworks | Short, Hill and Brown (2025), [LIT-1327](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1327.md), read in [NOTE-1051](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1051.md). The definition is theirs; the evidence for the case is their survey ([THEORY-833](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-833.md), Active) and a history drawn from secondary sources. It does not say that every expert–public disagreement is capture, that capture is always wrong (its strength depends on the experts' claim to truth and on whether public views were heard), or that the mechanism is a self-reinforcing loop. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-864](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-864.md) | AI testimonial injustice via credibility excess | Kay, Kasirzadeh and Mohamed (2024), [LIT-1338](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1338.md), read in [NOTE-1049](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1049.md): "In the algorithmic setting, the injustice requires a credibility excess assigned to the algorithm". A conceptual analysis, illustrated with reported cases. It does not say that users do overtrust models (the paper measures nothing), that deliberate fabrication is testimonial injustice in Fricker's sense, or that the amplification is a loop with any stated condition. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-867](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-867.md) v2 | Colour space geometry misses unique hues | Aldé (2026), [LIT-1348](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1348.md), read in full in [NOTE-1055](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1055.md). Two arguments, the unique hues objection and the opposing dimensions objection, from colour facts the paper takes as accepted. The decisive premise of each, that no adequate geometric property marks the facts, rests on inspection of CIELAB and extrapolation to better models; no analysis is reported. The target is similarity structuralism only. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-868](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-868.md) v2 | Structuralist evidence supports only weak thesis | Negro (2025), [LIT-1346](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1346.md), read in full in [NOTE-1054](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1054.md). The distinctions (three structuralisms; having, being in and being a structure) are sound and the arguments valid. Each argument's decisive premise is an intuition or a conceivability claim, and a structuralist such as Lyre ([THEORY-880](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-880.md)) accepts the holism Negro takes to be absurd. The paper also says that making judgement constitutive saves the view only by aligning it with eliminativism, which bears directly on [CLAIM-412](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-412.md). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-872](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-872.md) | The self is real as a pattern, not a substance | Gładziejewski (2025), [LIT-1360](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1360.md), read in full in [NOTE-1056](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1056.md), §4.1, after Hohwy & Michael (2017) and Letheby & Gerrans (2017), neither of which the record holds. An interpretation, not a result. The paper calls its self section "an initial sketch". It does not say that the self-model exaggerates the self's unity, though the exchange that filed the work said so. It says the single common cause is a compression, and that the verdict on selves turns on criteria. Its one candidate for a self-model that misdescribes is a dissociative case better compressed by two narrative selves. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-873](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-873.md) v2 | Consciousness claims caricature attention | Graziano (2024), [LIT-1358](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1358.md), read in full in [NOTE-1071](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1071.md): the attention schema theory and its "deep illusionism", in an essay with no new data. Arrow B is an argument. The identification of the target with attention rests on covariation with report cited from others, and the merging of attention, workspace and integration is asserted. Its "small" illusionism keeps the modelled process real and denies the reported phenomenal essence, so it is the strong illusionism of [THEORY-633](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-633.md) with a named target, not the weak kind. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-874](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-874.md) | Organicism is orthogonal to embodiment | Ward (2026), [LIT-1356](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1356.md), read in the accepted manuscript in [NOTE-1065](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1065.md). Views differ on where cognition's processes are (skull or brain–body–world) and, separately, on what the meaning of mental states depends on (information, or organization distinctive of the living). Embodied predictive processing, extended functionalism and cybernetics are embodied and informationalist; the enactive approach is organicist, and further marked by experiential primacy and reciprocity. The sharp edge: it is a taxonomy argued from examples and exegesis. It does not argue that organicism is true, and the line between distinctive and characteristic properties of life is left without a criterion. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-875](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-875.md) | Phenomenal binding modelled as a sheaf condition | Lee-Youngzie, Tsuchiya, Robinson, Dietz & Monti (2026), [LIT-1352](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1352.md), read in full in [NOTE-1059](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1059.md). A hypothesis article with no data. It proposes the presheaf and two readings of its failure, disunity for rivalry and context dependence for the Ebbinghaus illusion, without a criterion between them. It does not identify unity with a global section, since it assumes unity always holds. Its global section is measured data, its worked topology example is malformed, and by its own definition of gluing the rivalry case is not a sheaf failure. It answers [QUESTION-255](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-255.md) only by showing that a sheaf failure need not be disunity. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-876](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-876.md) | Consciousness needs an embodied generative model | Safron, Klimaj & Sheikhbahaee (2026), [LIT-1345](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1345.md), read in full in [NOTE-1057](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1057.md): Integrated World Modeling Theory as restated in a symposium paper, whose earlier, fuller statements (Safron 2020–2023) were not read. Asserted, not argued here. The sharp edge is that the theory does not require current sensory coupling, so its quarrel with grounding- free accounts is about developmental grounding and the capacity for coupling. "Embodied grounding" comes in "sufficient degrees (and kinds)", with no threshold. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-877](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-877.md) | Manifest image is structural; envatted alike | Gładziejewski (2025), [LIT-1360](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1360.md), read in full in [NOTE-1056](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1056.md), §§2–3, drawing on Chalmers's structuralism and veridicalism (2018, 2022), which the record does not hold. The cognitive half rests on a realist reading of predictive processing and on an analogy between free energy and description length. The veridicalism follows only if manifest content is wholly structural, which is assumed. Projective properties (cuteness) are allowed at one end of a continuum. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-878](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-878.md) | Reappraisal partly runs apart from generation | Bo et al. (preprint 2023, published 2024), [LIT-1359](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1359.md), read in full from the bioRxiv v2 preprint in [NOTE-1061](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1061.md). Two fMRI samples (n = 182 and 176), voxelwise Bayes factors, every effect replicated in both. Sixteen regions are engaged by reappraisal and show 10:1 evidence of no response to negative against neutral pictures without it; fourteen, the larger set, are engaged by both. The selective set best predicts how much reported negative affect falls. One instructed strategy, one stimulus type, BOLD only; nothing shows the selective regions do the regulating. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-879](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-879.md) | Sensory quality alone doesn't make experience | Lycan (2000; rev. 2023), [LIT-1355](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1355.md), read in full in [NOTE-1068](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1068.md). The entry defends the distinction in its own voice (§4.2, §5.1), crediting Carruthers (2000) for the distinction and Armstrong, Nelkin, Rosenthal and Lycan for the claim that qualities can go unnoticed. It is argued, not shown. Its one case, the driver "on autopilot", is the case Block reads the other way, and the entry gives no evidence that the driver's perception was not experienced and forgotten. It concerns the quality experienced, not emotion or affect, and it does not say what awareness is. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-880](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-880.md) v2 | Quality space fixes phenomenal character | Lyre (2022), [LIT-1344](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1344.md), read in full in [NOTE-1060](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1060.md): neurophenomenal structuralism as a programme. The thesis is assumed and motivated, not shown. Its neural evidence is one cited imaging study of colour in V4. The reduction it draws rests on metaphysically necessary supervenience, which the author says he cannot argue for. It is filed so that the objections read with it, Negro ([THEORY-868](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-868.md)) and Aldé ([THEORY-867](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-867.md)), have a stated target. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-881](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-881.md) | Anaesthesia lowers integrated information ΦR | Luppi et al. (2026), [LIT-1357](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1357.md), read in full in [NOTE-1064](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1064.md) from the open-access version of record. It extends the same group's 2024 result ([LIT-949](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-949.md), [THEORY-240](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-240.md)) from human propofol and disorders of consciousness to four species and six regimes, and adds a causal reversal in two macaques. The sharp edge: the state measured is responsiveness, which the authors call "presumably consciousness" and grant is "an imperfect marker of unconsciousness"; the measure is pairwise, linear-Gaussian and content-free; and one mouse regimen fails the main analysis. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-882](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-882.md) v2 | Consciousness requires epistemic depth | Laukkonen, Friston & Chandaria (2025), [LIT-1363](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1363.md), read in full in [NOTE-1063](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1063.md) from PsyArXiv v3. A conceptual proposal with no data and no simulation. The three conditions are asserted necessary; their joint sufficiency is argued for AI and then withdrawn for phenomenal experience in a footnote. The formal part (Table 1) is a hierarchy with layer-wise precision hyper-parameters, from which none of the properties the text gives epistemic depth is derived. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-883](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-883.md) | Conscious contents are policy-informing posteriors | Whyte, Corcoran, Robinson, Smith, Moran, Parr, Friston, Seth & Hohwy (2026), [LIT-1364](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1364.md), read in full in [NOTE-1062](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1062.md) from arXiv v2. The "hard core" the paper reads off the active inference models of rivalry, access, no-report, interoception and meta-awareness. The first two parts follow from the framework; the criterion of access is "an inference to the best explanation" from what the models needed in order to report. The authors scope it to humans and similar animals and are agnostic elsewhere. Neither prediction has been tested in the paper. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-885](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-885.md) | Politics is more path dependent than markets | Pierson (1997 working paper; published 2000), [LIT-1372](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1372.md), read in full in [NOTE-1076](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1076.md) through its precursor only, the EUI Jean Monnet Chair Paper 44. An argument with no data and one illustration (two failed US health-care reforms, 1993–96). It extends North's claim for institutions in general ([THEORY-429](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-429.md)) to a claim about politics as a domain. It does not show that any political outcome was locked in by an early contingent event. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-886](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-886.md) | Prediction error spikes mark event boundaries | Zacks, Speer, Swallow, Braver & Reynolds (2007), [LIT-1382](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1382.md), read in full in [NOTE-1084](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1084.md) from the PMC author manuscript. Event segmentation theory: a theory and review, with a partial network simulation and mostly correlational evidence. Prediction error is never measured in people, and the one neural prediction checked (anterior cingulate responses at boundaries) failed. It is a theory of a passive observer of others' activity; it does not cover one's own intentions, and does not mention the doorway effect. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-887](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-887.md) v2 | Rare attributes can look majority locally | Lerman, Yan & Wu (2016), [LIT-1390](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1390.md), read in full in [NOTE-1085](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1085.md) from the PLOS ONE version. The "majority illusion": with 5% of nodes active, 60–80% of nodes in a heavy-tailed synthetic network can see an active majority among their neighbours; in disassortative real topologies, 60–70% with 20% active. A binomial model from the joint degree distribution predicts the share. The edge: the attributes are assigned by the authors on every network, real ones included, so this shows what topology permits, and nothing about what people perceive, believe or do. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-888](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-888.md) | Doorways impair memory via event interference | From the Radvansky lab's doorway studies, [LIT-1392](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1392.md), [LIT-1384](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1384.md) and [LIT-1385](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1385.md), read in full in [NOTE-1083](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1083.md), [NOTE-1082](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1082.md) and [NOTE-1081](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1081.md), and the independent conceptual replication of McFadyen et al., [LIT-1387](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1387.md), read in [NOTE-1079](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1079.md). The pattern (a cost on the carried object, worse after two new rooms, not helped by returning) replicates within the lab's paradigm; the interference account is reached by eliminating alternatives, and the independent study found no loss of hits, only more false alarms under load. It is about recognizing object labels, not intentions. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-890](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-890.md) | Culture supplies a toolkit, not ends | Swidler (1986), [LIT-1367](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1367.md), read in full in [NOTE-1075](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1075.md) from a course copy of the published article. A theoretical argument against the Parsonian values model, built on illustrations (the culture-of-poverty debate, the Protestant ethic, Walzer's Calvin) and on the paper's Figure 1. It reports no data, and its research questions, which would test it, are left open. It does not say that values are inert: within an established strategy they "fine-tune the regulation of action". | Proposed |
| [THEORY-892](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-892.md) v2 | Psychopathy is one dimension, not a type | Hare and Neumann (2008), read in [NOTE-1094](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1094.md). The PCL-R's twenty items load on four correlated factors, which pair into Factor 1 (interpersonal, affective) and Factor 2 (lifestyle, antisocial) and are explained by one superordinate factor. The affective features are tied to the antisocial ones, so the authors deny that any component is the disorder's core, and they read the evidence as dimensional. Filed for the record's question on corporate psychopathy, which asks which of these features could be said of a corporation. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-893](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-893.md) v3 | Wanting can rise without liking | Berridge and Kringelbach (2015), read in [NOTE-1110](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1110.md). Reward splits into 'liking', 'wanting' and learning. 'Liking' has objective, cross-species orofacial markers. Lateral-hypothalamic stimulation and incentive sensitization raise 'wanting', which can grow "even if the drug became less pleasant". Objective 'liking' reactions can occur "without any subjective pleasure feeling at all". Filed because it bears directly on the record's reading of valence as ordering-potential ([CLAIM-440](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-440.md)). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-895](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-895.md) v2 | Drugs sensitize wanting, not liking | Berridge and Robinson (2016), [LIT-1461](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1461.md), read in [NOTE-1109](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1109.md) from the PMC author manuscript. A review by the theory's authors. Strong in rats and moderate in people for drugs; weak for behavioural addictions, where the authors call the evidence emerging and the mechanism unknown. Filed separately from [THEORY-893](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-893.md), which holds the liking–wanting dissociation, because what [QUESTION-267](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-267.md) and [CLAIM-433](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-433.md) need is the sensitization result: a ranking whose strength is re-keyed to cues, cut loose from both pleasure and the person's goals, and lasting. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-905](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-905.md) | Finite imitation populations lock on a suboptimum | Soma et al.'s simulations and limits section, read in [NOTE-1132](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1132.md). With ten options and arbitrary parameters that the authors call qualitative, swarms of about 500 track the replicator dynamic and smaller ones often lock onto worse options. The authors state that pure imitation can delete a type and has no mechanism for escape in non-stationary environments. Hybrids that compare qualities are faster. Simulation-scoped, not a theorem. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-914](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-914.md) v2 | Extinction adds inhibition, does not erase | Craske, Treanor, Conway, Zbozinek & Vervliet (2014), [LIT-1500](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1500.md), read in full from the PMC author manuscript in [NOTE-1137](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1137.md). The paper summarizes Bouton's model and the four return-of-fear phenomena that support it, and translates them into exposure practice. The evidence is cited, not reported: the source is a clinical translation, and a promotion needs the primary literature. It does not show that exposure therapy in patients works by inhibitory learning alone. The authors allow that habituation also plays a part. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-916](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-916.md) v2 | Influence power accumulates by centrality | Jia, MirTabatabaei, Friedkin & Bullo (2015), [LIT-1146](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1146.md), read in [NOTE-1135](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1135.md) from the version of record posted on the author's site; proofs skimmed. Theorems about a model, not findings about groups. The empirical companion, [LIT-1482](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1482.md) ([THEORY-902](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-902.md)), uses anchored dynamics and a changing network, whose attractor is autocracy rather than this interior equilibrium. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-919](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-919.md) v2 | Blockade-shielded French regions industrialized | Juhász (2018), [LIT-1489](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1489.md), read in full from the December 2015 draft in [NOTE-1122](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1122.md). A difference-in-differences on 88 departments, then the trade-cost shock as an instrument for 1812 spinning capacity. The long-run first stages are weak (Kleibergen-Paap F 3–8). The protection was a war blockade, followed by post-war tariffs, so this is persistence of a protected industry's location, not evidence about how protection ends. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-931](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-931.md) | Opponent shaping reaches tit-for-tat | Foerster et al.'s LOLA (AAMAS 2018), read in full in [NOTE-1150](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1150.md) from arXiv v4, with the update rule re-derived. Empirical, in two small games and a grid game. Shaping here is mutual and produced cooperation, not capture; in matching pennies, a harmonic game, it damped the cycling of naive learners. Table 3's naive-learner tit-for-tat figure (20.8%) does not square with their return (−1.98), and the NOTE says so. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-934](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-934.md) | Bush–Mosteller drives probability matching | Börgers & Sarin (JET 1997; working paper 1993), [LIT-1505](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1505.md), read in full in [NOTE-1149](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1149.md). When reinforcements may be negative, probability removed from a punished strategy is redistributed, and the limit is dp_j/dt = p_j(Ū_j* − p\|Ũ\|q) + Ū_j*(σ_j* − p_j). With payoffs of equal absolute size only the matching term remains. The limit is stated with its proof omitted. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-935](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-935.md) | Capacity shifts deep Q-learners' cooperation | Leibo, Zambaldi, Lanctot, Marecki and Graepel (2017), read in full in [NOTE-1151](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1151.md) from arXiv v1. A descriptive simulation with no seeds or spread reported, policies classed by training environment, two agents, fixed conditions, apples on a fixed respawn timer, and a mismatch between the text's and Figure 7's settings for batch and network size. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-936](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-936.md) | Softmax RPS learners show Hamiltonian chaos | Sato & Crutchfield (arXiv 2002; PRE 2003), [LIT-1520](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1520.md), read in full in [NOTE-1144](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1144.md), pp. 2–3 and Figs. 1–3. Numerical results for one game, two agents and the parameters shown; the zero-decay, zero-sum case was first reported in Sato, Akiyama and Farmer (PNAS 2002), which is not held. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-938](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-938.md) | Cross learning converges to pure profiles | Börgers & Sarin (JET 1997; working paper 1993), [LIT-1505](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1505.md), read in full from the 1995 working paper in [NOTE-1149](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1149.md). Two players running Cross's rule with payoffs in (0, 1): expected change equals the discrete replicator step (Proposition 3); the slow-learning limit is the Taylor replicator dynamic at each finite time (Proposition 4); for every step size the process is absorbed in a pure profile with probability one (Proposition 5). The equivalence is pointwise in time, not uniform. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-939](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-939.md) | Factored private utilities align agents | Wolpert & Tumer's NASA report ([LIT-1506](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1506.md)), read in full in NOTE-1153 because their Advances in Complex Systems paper ([LIT-1515](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1515.md)) could not be reached. The characterisation is stated with its proof deferred; the "if" half and the WLU's factoredness were checked when filed. Factoredness is ordinal, member by member, and needs no scale shared among members. The WLU is not a causal counterfactual: it re- scores the actual history with one member's part replaced. Removal was not the best clamp. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-941](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-941.md) | Regret matching reaches correlated equilibria | Hart & Mas-Colell (Econometrica 2000; handout 1996), [LIT-1521](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1521.md), read in full in [NOTE-1142](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1142.md). Convergence is of time-averaged joint frequencies to a set, not of play to an equilibrium; the common history is the correlating device; inertia is needed; and interior correlated equilibria that are not pure Nash cannot be the limit. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-947](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-947.md) | Partial-monitoring approachability at T^-1/3 | Kwon and Perchet (2017), [LIT-1526](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1526.md), read in [NOTE-1159](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1159.md). The rates are for the average payoff's distance to the target, uniformly over Nature's choices, with approachability assumed (Perchet's condition). Optimal means not improvable in the worst case over games. It gives no guarantee for individual stages or rolling windows, and none when the signal law is unknown. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-949](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-949.md) | LoRA turn schedule matters, not just shares | Zhong et al. (2024), [LIT-1529](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1529.md), read in [NOTE-1160](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1160.md). An ablation of LoRA Switch judged by GPT-4V against weight merging. It says that equal shares of steps do not fix the outcome; it does not say how large the order effect is beyond noise, or how much each LoRA contributes to the image, which was not measured. The authors' explanation, that core elements should come first, is theirs and untested. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-950](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-950.md) | RelExp3 regret needs only local constants | Lattimore and Szepesvári (2019), [LIT-1524](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1524.md), read in [NOTE-1162](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1162.md). For the class of games Bartók (2013) studied, the leading constant of the √n regret depends only on K_loc, F and log K, asymptotically. It is the first such result against adversaries. The constant reached before the asymptotics set in still depends on large game constants. It is a bound for one algorithm in a sub-class of the easy games, not a characterisation of the constant. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-959](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-959.md) | Constancies are invariants within experience | Isaac (2025), [LIT-1361](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1361.md), read in [NOTE-1163](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1163.md): the group-theoretic layer of a structuralist account of experience. The paper's evidence supports the weaker half: constancy needs invariance under transformations internal to experience. The stronger half, that this invariance is what makes experience objective and induces a subject–object distinction, is Cassirer's, argued from the co-presence of two levels of experience, and the paper gives no way to tell invariant extraction with a subject from invariant extraction without one. "Group-theoretic" is used loosely: the paper's own examples are groupoids or toy models. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-965](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-965.md) | SAE features are units the model computes with | Templeton et al. (2024), [LIT-1533](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1533.md), read in [NOTE-1178](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1178.md), with Bricken et al. (2023), [LIT-1545](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1545.md), for the one-layer case. The thesis of both papers: features are the model's own units, shown by steering. The authors' own hedges: steering needs features clamped beyond their observed range; the reconstruction error rides along; "we haven't rigorously evaluated our features against other steering methods". The record holds a result against it for known causal variables ([THEORY-968](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-968.md)). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-967](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-967.md) | Attention heads are repurposed during training | Wang, Hoogland, van Wingerden, Furman and Murfet (2024), [LIT-1535](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1535.md), read in [NOTE-1188](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1188.md). "Heads 0:1, 0:4, 0:7 ultimately become the two previous-token heads and (layer 0) Dyck head respectively. However, these heads appear to start out as simple n-gram heads." Layer-0 multigram heads lose information about simple n-grams from stage LM3, as path patching and composition scores show them coming to feed layer-1 bracket-matching heads. The "ago" n-gram moves from head 0:0 to head 1:0. Whether the late roles are built from the early ones, or merely follow them in time, is not tested. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-982](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-982.md) | Claude 3.5 Haiku plans ahead within a pass | Lindsey et al. (2025), [LIT-1541](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1541.md), read in [NOTE-1181](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1181.md): the introduction ("Claude 3.5 Haiku routinely uses multiple intermediate reasoning steps 'in its head'"; "It displays signs of forward planning") and the discussion's sections on plan formation and working backward from a goal. The case studies show each mechanism on chosen prompts, and the same article has a case without it: on a jailbreak the model "doesn't know what it plans to say until it actually says it". The authors report a satisfying graph for about a quarter of the prompts they try. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-986](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-986.md) v2 | Similar features recur across networks | Olah et al. (2020), [LIT-1543](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1543.md), read in [NOTE-1182](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1182.md): Claim 3, the universality hypothesis. Curve detectors and high-low frequency detectors are reported in AlexNet, InceptionV1, VGG19 and ResNetV2-50, with InceptionV3, a Places365 model and conv nets trained from scratch named in the text. The authors: "the only evidence we can offer today is anecdotal". | Proposed |
| [THEORY-989](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-989.md) | hLDA beats flat LDA on held-out JACM abstracts | Blei, Griffiths and Jordan (2010), [LIT-1542](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1542.md), §6.3 and Fig. 9, read in [NOTE-1176](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1176.md). One corpus, five-fold cross-validation, hyperparameters integrated out. It is evidence that a single-path hierarchy can earn its constraint in prediction, near its own size. It is not evidence that a hierarchy predicts better than a flat mixed-membership model in general: the paper itself says the flat model should dominate at large topic counts. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-990](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-990.md) v2 | Induction heads drive most in-context learning | Olsson et al. (2022), [LIT-1538](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1538.md), read in [NOTE-1173](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1173.md). The paper's thesis: circuits with the induction head's mechanism, matching "[A*][B*] … [A] → [B], where A* ≈ A and B* ≈ B are similar in some space", "implement most in-context learning in large models". For large models the authors grade their own evidence correlational (Argument 1), weakly interventional (Argument 2), plausibility (Argument 4) and analogy (Argument 6). Their strongest alternative is that other composition heads, formed in the same window, carry more of it above some size. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-995](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-995.md) | Backup name movers arise from dropout | Wang et al. (2022), [LIT-1540](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1540.md), read in [NOTE-1167](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1167.md), §3.4: "We hypothesize that this compensation phenomenon is caused by the use of dropout during training. Thus, the model was optimized for robustness to dysfunctional parts." The compensation is real (a 5% loss of logit difference after knocking out the three name movers); the cause is not examined. Appendix F: "Both the reason and the mechanism of this compensation effect are still unclear." | Proposed |
| [THEORY-997](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-997.md) | Fine-tuning rewires existing circuits | Wang et al. (2025), [LIT-1539](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1539.md), read in [NOTE-1183](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1183.md). Their EAP-IG circuits (top 5% of edges) change edges 2.8–4.3 times as much as nodes over LoRA fine-tuning on five arithmetic tasks. A record simulation shows that a fixed edge budget on a transformer-sized graph gives the same contrast when only edge-level noise is resampled, so the counts do not yet show reorganization. Fine-tuning only, one model for most results, arithmetic only. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1000](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1000.md) v2 | Corrected attribution patching is a good prefilter | Kramár, Lieberum, Shah & Nanda (2024), [LIT-1531](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1531.md), read in [NOTE-1190](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1190.md). The measured case is four Pythia models, three prompt pairs and two small distributions. The paper's own diagnostic is what would let a single new setting be checked without exhaustive patching. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1001](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1001.md) | Circuits sharing units cooperate; rivals compete | Musat et al. (2026), [LIT-1530](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1530.md), read in [NOTE-1177](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1177.md). In projected SGD training of a three-layer single-head attention-only transformer on in-context bigrams, three induction circuits are possible, and the winner depends on initial strengths outside the winner itself. The authors explain the pattern by cooperation through a shared unit and competition for layers. The evidence is one scan over two initial strengths with every other coordinate zeroed, in projected training. | Proposed |
