| [THEORY-1004](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1004.md) | Agreement features shift from tokens to grammar | Bayazit, Mueller and Bosselut (2025, ACL 2026), [LIT-1555](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1555.md), read in [NOTE-1186](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1186.md). Crosscoders trained jointly on the middle layer of two or three checkpoints, with features scored by their relative indirect effect on agreement minimal pairs at each. The reconstruction quality (C1) and RelIE's agreement with single-feature ablations (C2) are measured; the trends in this title are read by the authors from annotated features. It describes; it does not predict later checkpoints, and it cannot tell a feature carried forward from one re-learned in the same direction. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1008](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1008.md) | MMSB memberships predict protein function | Airoldi, Blei, Fienberg and Xing (2008), [LIT-1553](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1553.md), §4.3.2 and Figs. 10–12, read in [NOTE-1179](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1179.md). The batch's one check of inferred mixed memberships against labels the model never saw. The reported margin is over a weak baseline, so it shows less than it seems: probably some information, not yet how much. It says nothing about whether the fifteen blocks are the fifteen functions. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1013](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1013.md) v3 | Features and circuits are units of understanding | Olah et al. (2020), [LIT-1543](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1543.md), read in [NOTE-1182](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1182.md): Claims 1 and 2 of the essay. The evidence is a set of examples in InceptionV1 (curve, high-low frequency and dog head detectors; the curve, oriented dog head and car circuits), argued with feature visualization, dataset examples, synthetic stimuli, tuning curves and the weights. The essay names polysemantic neurons as the main obstacle. It gives no count of how much of a layer is understood. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1014](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1014.md) | One-mechanism behaviours run on several pathways | Marks et al. (2025), [LIT-1532](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1532.md), read in [NOTE-1187](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1187.md): §3.3, §5 and Appendix C. Agreement across a relative clause: subject-number features promote verb forms directly, and a second pathway carries the number to the clause's end through PP/RC boundary features. Cluster 475: one mechanism detects verbs and adjectives that take infinitival objects, another nominal objects before an object complement. Cluster 382: general succession features and token-specific induction features. "While the clusters … seem at first to each represent a single mechanism, circuit-level analysis reveals in both cases a union of distinct mechanisms." | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1016](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1016.md) v2 | SAE feature count is not well-posed | Bricken et al. (2023), [LIT-1545](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1545.md), read in [NOTE-1191](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1191.md), Feature Splitting and Discussion; and Templeton et al. (2024), [LIT-1533](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1533.md), read in [NOTE-1178](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1178.md), for the same splitting at 1M, 4M and 34M features in a large model. In a one-layer model one base64 feature becomes three, then more; in Claude 3 Sonnet a San Francisco feature becomes two, then eleven. The authors offer two pictures, an idealized set seen at varying resolution and feature manifolds with no finite description; both deny that one width is the right one. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1021](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1021.md) | Attribution patching fails on large, early patches | Nanda (2023), [LIT-1581](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1581.md), read in [NOTE-1201](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1201.md). The post's map of where the first-order estimate can be trusted. The record holds it from one task in the post, from the mathematics of the estimate ([THEORY-1023](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1023.md)), and in part from Kramár et al.'s test on Pythia ([THEORY-996](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-996.md)), which found misses behind saturated attention, as this predicts, and tested no residual-stream nodes. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1022](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1022.md) v2 | Curve units detect curves as such | Cammarata et al. (2020), [LIT-1575](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1575.md), read in [NOTE-1198](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1198.md). The article's four claims (causality, generality, purity, family) taken together, as the authors state them. Generality and the family are measured ([THEORY-1028](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1028.md)). Causality rests on feature visualization and attribution. Purity rests on feature visualization with a diversity term and activation-binned labels, while most of the unit's firings, and 45% of its contribution to expected value, are not shown to be curves. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1026](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1026.md) | Localizing a fact differs from editing it | Hase et al. (2023), [LIT-1578](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1578.md), read in [NOTE-1194](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1194.md), §6: "Causal Tracing answers a question about where factual information is carried in representations in a Transformer forward pass, and this question turns out to be a different question than the editing question of where is best to intervene"; and, for why edits work where facts are not traced, "Many layers could store a fact, and it happens that some do". The authors note that this would be surprising, since layers cannot be swapped freely. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1027](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1027.md) | SAEs add to black-box hidden-objective audits | Marks, Treutlein et al. (2025), [LIT-1584](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1584.md), read in [NOTE-1193](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1193.md): §§4–5 and Appendix F. In the blind game the fastest team used SAE features, but semantic search with its query finds the same documents. Post hoc and unblinded, SAE features surface RM-bias knowledge from bias demonstrations and from the Assistant token, where semantic search fails. The model's objective is named in its training data. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1030](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1030.md) v2 | Feed-forward units are key–value memories | Geva et al. (2021), [LIT-1576](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1576.md), read in [NOTE-1200](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1200.md): "feed-forward layers in transformer-based language models operate as key-value memories, where each key correlates with textual patterns in the training examples, and each value induces a distribution over the output vocabulary", and "we thus expect our qualitative empirical observations to hold across diverse settings". Evidence in one model, correlational only. ROME's storage hypothesis ([THEORY-1011](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1011.md)) borrows the name and reads keys and values at another level. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1035](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1035.md) | Polysemanticity is loss-optimal capacity sharing | Scherlis et al. (2022), [LIT-1625](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1625.md), read in [NOTE-1205](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1205.md). The paper's account of polysemanticity in general: capacity allocation at the loss optimum, driven by sparsity, with architecture deciding block size. The general first-order condition holds for any loss under two stated assumptions; its application to trained networks, and the role of architecture, rest on toy models only. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1039](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1039.md) | Any middle MLP layer could store a fact | Meng et al. (2022), [LIT-1536](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1536.md), read in [NOTE-1166](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1166.md), §2.3: "we conjecture that any fact could be equivalently stored in any one of the middle MLP layers". It was one clause of [THEORY-1011](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1011.md), which is Rejected for its other part, the claim that the traced middle layers are where a fact is stored. Hase et al. (2023), [LIT-1578](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1578.md), read in [NOTE-1194](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1194.md), measure edits succeeding at nearly every layer of GPT-J whatever tracing says ([THEORY-1024](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1024.md)). That is what this conjecture predicts, but it is not evidence of storage, since an edit can work wherever a layer can write the needed output ([LIT-968](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-968.md)). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1040](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1040.md) | Early vision units form cross-model families | Olah et al. (2020), [LIT-1624](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1624.md), read in [NOTE-1206](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1206.md). The article's organizing hypothesis: early vision's units come in families, some of them real structure (said to be recoverable by factorizing weight matrices), and the families recur across models. The census ([THEORY-1042](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1042.md)) is by eye in one model; neither the factorization nor a second model's sorting is shown. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1044](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1044.md) | Beam sampler beats Gibbs for the iHMM | Van Gael, Saatci, Teh and Ghahramani (2008), [LIT-1622](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1622.md), read in [NOTE-1204](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1204.md). Two synthetic designs (an almost cyclic 4-state HMM, length 800, 20 runs; persistent 4-state HMMs with self-transitions to 0.999, length 4000, 60 starts), a well-log series and a text task. The beam sampler is exact by construction ([THEORY-1037](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1037.md)); how much faster it mixes is shown only in iterations and by eye. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1047](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1047.md) | Curve circuit is a readable, simple algorithm | Cammarata et al. (2021), [LIT-1629](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1629.md), read in [NOTE-1207](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1207.md). The article's account of how curve detectors are built, and its claim that the account is the circuit. The family structure and the echo edit are measured ([THEORY-1038](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1038.md)); that the description is complete, and that the reimplementation matches the natural units beyond strong cases, is shown by figures only. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1052](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1052.md) | Rate tipping is failed time-scale separation | Ashwin, Wieczorek, Vitolo and Cox (2012), [LIT-1654](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1654.md), read in [NOTE-1215](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1215.md). Shown for the linear tipping-radius model, where the sufficient condition for tracking is a rate comparison, and stated for a fast-slow example ("rate dependent tipping occurs when the slow and very slow timescales are no longer separable"). Proposed because for nonlinear systems the paper says "no exact analogy possible" and gives no general condition. It bears on [CLAIM-478](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-478.md), whose constraints hold over a window between time scales. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1055](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1055.md) | Redundant pointer records mark objectivity | Zurek (2009), [LIT-1640](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1640.md), section II and Figs. 2–3, read in [NOTE-1229](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1229.md). Redundancy R_δ = 1/f_δ, the number of disjoint fragments each holding (1 − δ)H_S of the information about S, is large for states made by decoherence and absent for random states, and peaks sharply at the pointer observable. Those are model results the review cites. The step from redundancy to objectivity ("Large redundancy implies objectivity") is an identification. The later caveat, that mutual information alone does not guarantee independently accessible records, is not in the paper. Proposed for that step. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1056](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1056.md) | Spectral synchronization is near-optimal | Singer (2011), [LIT-1655](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1655.md), §§2, 4 and 5, read in [NOTE-1224](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1224.md) from arXiv v2. The threshold p > 1/√n comes from a cited rank-one deformation theorem adopted to a non-Gaussian mixture and a heuristic comparison with random correlation, confirmed by simulation at n = 100 and 400; the near-optimality ratio compares it with an information bound for a different success criterion. Proposed for both steps. It does not say that recovery is cheap on every graph, under every noise model, or for fine angular resolution. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1073](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1073.md) | Slow aggregates become environments parts tune to | Flack (2017), [LIT-1630](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1630.md), read in [NOTE-1216](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1216.md), §6. Argued informally, with social institutions and the macaque power distribution as illustrations, and no model or data. Proposed. It does not say slowness makes an aggregate accurate, or that separation alone makes the components use it: in Flack the aggregate constrains only through the components' tuning to it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1086](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1086.md) v2 | Social theory's independence is contingent | Jaksland (2024), [LIT-1673](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1673.md), read in [NOTE-1230](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1230.md), reconstructing an argument Barad "only ever alludes to". It is a conditional and the author leaves its antecedent open: whether any ontological feature is all-or-nothing is "an open question". He finds individualism "immediately more agreeable" as approximable, and the dualisms the harder case. The contingency half is argued (a counterfactual on Planck's constant); the no-approximation half is a candidate list, not a demonstration. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1091](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1091.md) | Agential realism can't answer measurement problem | Faye & Jaksland (2021), [LIT-1672](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1672.md), read in [NOTE-1220](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1220.md), §5. Proposed: the authors present it as a challenge ("There might be other more subtle ways"), and conclude only that consistency with quantum mechanics is unshown ("a leap of faith"), not that agential realism is incoherent. The exchange of 2026-10-27 reported it as "an unresolved measurement problem", which is the strength the text supports. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1092](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1092.md) | Discrepancies can pinpoint a faulty sensor | Robinson (2017), [LIT-1658](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1658.md), Example 24, Case 2 (pp. 26–28 of arXiv v3), read in [NOTE-1221](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1221.md). One simulated case, one noise realization, read from a figure. Proposed until a stated procedure is tested over trials, including faults in the restriction maps, which enter the discrepancies in the same way as faults in the data. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1095](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1095.md) | Flocks keep long-range order in 2D | Toner and Tu (1995), [LIT-1670](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1670.md), read in [NOTE-1228](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1228.md) from the arXiv preprint. The linear theory's loss of order in d ≤ 2 and the relevance of the convective nonlinearity below d = 4 are calculations. The survival of order in d = 2 follows from χ = −1/5 < 0, which is exact only if a cubic vertex stays irrelevant ("we strongly suspect"), or from χ = (z − d)/3 with z < 2, which is expected "on physical grounds". The change-of- neighbours mechanism is a heuristic. Proposed for those two steps. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1097](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1097.md) | No Markov blanket formulation individuates | The wider claim dropped when [THEORY-073](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-073.md) was narrowed to Friston's 2013 formulation and promoted on 2026-10-27 ([ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4: a narrowing's dropped claims go to Proposed entries). Both critiques argue the general form, and the record holds neither of the later formulations it would have to reach. Its promote_when is [THEORY-073](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-073.md)'s own, moved here unchanged. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1111](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1111.md) | Commodification shifts fans to flâneurs | Giulianotti (2002), [LIT-1150](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1150.md), read from the author's pre-review text. Four ideal types: supporters (traditional/hot: kin-like, topophilic, obligatory), followers (traditional/cool: nested, mediated allegiances), fans (consumer/hot: non-reciprocal intimacy, authenticated by consumption) and flâneurs (consumer/cool: cosmopolitan window-shoppers of clubs). Hypercommodification is said to move identification from supporter towards flâneur, while the spectacle flâneurs consume depends on supporters. Proposed: a conceptual classification with no data, and a trend claim that is asserted, not measured. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1112](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1112.md) | Groupness needs inferred collective intention | Skorich (2025, v2 2026), [LIT-1765](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1765.md), a preprint. Categorization with accentuation makes members interchangeable, not one, since a category is a set and a set is internally differentiated. Groups such as orchestras and families need no similarity. Groups are holistic entities perceived from cues to shared mental states, much as faces are perceived from configuration. Reported support: four experiments under review in which groups defined by a mental state (a chosen T-shirt colour; seeing the duck or the rabbit) drew more favouritism and tracking than groups defined by a physical property. Proposed: the argument is conceptual and the evidence is unpublished. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1113](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1113.md) v2 | Rivalry boosts cohesion via reciprocity | Berendt & Uhrich (2016), [LIT-1147](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1147.md): an SEM of 571 Bundesliga stadium attendees. Rivalry intensity: public collective self-esteem relative to the rival's fans −.31. Perceived distinctiveness +.27, cohesion +.20, and regard from other clubs' fans +.09, with direct paths null and indirect effects via perceived reciprocity .18–.20. Disidentification carries almost none. Proposed: one cross-sectional sample, a single-item predictor, a new reciprocity scale, and causal order assumed by the model. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1114](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1114.md) v3 | Metacontrast sets salient self-categories | Self-categorization theory as restated by Turner, Oakes, Haslam and McGarty (1994), [LIT-1794](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1794.md), and reviewed by Hornsey (2008), [LIT-1742](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1742.md). Personal and social identity are levels of self-categorization. Salience is perceiver readiness times fit, comparative fit being the metacontrast ratio. The level, kind, content and prototype structure of self-categories shift with the comparison set: Americans read as less aggressive beside Iraq than beside the Soviet Union, and a group's extreme members become more prototypical in an intergroup context. Proposed: every result in the record comes through the theory's authors, reported without data, and the account's stronger claim, that the self is generated rather than stored, is not part of it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1115](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1115.md) v2 | We-identity needs no depersonalization | León (2023), [LIT-1721](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1721.md). Self-categorization theory claims depersonalization as "the basic process underlying group phenomena", for groups of any size, friendship groups included (Turner et al. 1987, pp. 50, 103, as quoted), and phenomenologists have taken it as the account of the "we". But close relationships yield we-identities while their members grasp each other as non-substitutable, and relationship research on couple resilience finds the "we" more adaptive the more differentiated the "I". Proposed: the argument is conceptual, and the cited evidence was not analysed by the source or read here. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1116](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1116.md) | Fans can hold a European identity too | Biel (2026), [LIT-1133](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1133.md): a four-country quota survey of 3,685 fans. Club, national and European fan-community identification average 6.1, 5.6 and 5.3 of 10. The European item loads on its own factor in a two-factor solution. It goes with trust in a European fan from elsewhere (b = .34), viewing of foreign leagues, positive views of fans and attachment to Europe, and not with critique of football governance. Proposed: single items, a Heywood case in the factor solution, percentages whose denominator does not match the analysed n, and cross-sectional associations. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1124](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1124.md) | Log co-occurrences act as Euclidean distances | Hashimoto, Alvarez-Melis and Jaakkola (2016), [LIT-1801](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1801.md), §3, read in [NOTE-1329](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1329.md). The correlation follows a normalization chosen to maximize it; the two nearest-neighbour statistics are necessary conditions, the corpora exceed the asymptotic centrality bound and pass only a non-asymptotic range, and the free-association data fail the reciprocity criterion the paper states. Proposed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1126](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1126.md) | Development imposes regularity on variable cells | Nicholson (2026), [LIT-1821](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1821.md), read in [NOTE-1340](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1340.md). Weiss's "determinacy in the gross despite demonstrable indeterminacy in the small", shown as a redrawn schematic (Fig. 5) and supported by citations to work on stochastic gene expression and cell-fate decisions. This is the only one of the paper's four critiques that rests on evidence, and the paper presents none of the evidence itself. Proposed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1127](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1127.md) | CycleGAN hides photo detail in faint map signals | Chu, Zhmoginov and Sandler (2017), [LIT-1800](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1800.md), §§2–4, read in [NOTE-1346](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1346.md). One trained model on one dataset. The noise curve (Fig. 3, 50 photographs) is the only quantitative result; the hidden details, the composing edits and the attack are shown by examples. Proposed: an empirical finding about one model, said by the authors to recur on other datasets, not shown. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1131](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1131.md) | LLMs choose Indic pragmatic readings, lean literal | Singh et al. (2026), [LIT-1817](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1817.md), read in [NOTE-1345](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1345.md) from the Findings of EMNLP 2026 PDF. MCQ beat NLI in 20 of 20 model–language pairs (recomputed). 59.1% of wrong MCQ answers took the literal distractor, against 33.3% by chance, and 53.8% of Contradiction items were labelled Entailment. The gold answers are each language's one item author's reading, cells hold 5–16 items, and the MCQ and NLI sets are different items. So "recognizing and reasoning about pragmatic meaning are distinct competencies" is the authors' gloss, not a finding. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1136](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1136.md) | Poincaré embeddings differ by more than isometry | Alvarez-Melis, Mroueh and Jaakkola (2020), [LIT-1808](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1808.md), §§5–7, Figs. 1–2, Tables 1–2; read in [NOTE-1323](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1323.md). Proposed: single runs, one embedding method for the matching experiments, and GW, the obvious isometry-free baseline, is not run. It does not say why seeds disagree (the paper conjectures negative sampling), nor that the matching preserves the hierarchy's direction, which it does not enforce. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1137](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1137.md) | Compatibility cost wins with rich interventions | Felekis et al. (CLeaR 2024), [LIT-1806](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1806.md), §§4.2 and 6 and Appendices C and E, read in [NOTE-1342](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1342.md). Two synthetic models (STC, LUCAS) and one real two-lab dataset (EBM), all discrete, evaluated by leaving one intervention pair out. The ω-cost wins on STC with parent-free interventions and on LUCAS, loses on STC with two interventions on tar and on EBM. The explanation, a nearly uniform cost when interventions are few, is argued and fits the four cases. Proposed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1143](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1143.md) | Round-trip agreement says nothing of fidelity | Chu, Zhmoginov and Sandler (2017), [LIT-1800](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1800.md), §2 and §5, read in [NOTE-1346](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1346.md). The authors argue it from the many photographs a single map stands for, and support it with [THEORY-1127](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1127.md)'s evidence on one model; they propose, and do not run, the test of adding capacity to the smaller domain. Proposed. It is the converse of the record's collapse case for [CLAIM-496](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-496.md): there routes agree because nothing travels, here because everything does, out of sight. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1144](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1144.md) | Politeness classifier transfers but trails natives | Srinivasan and Choi (2022), [LIT-1799](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1799.md), read in [NOTE-1339](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1339.md). XLM-R fine-tuned on 1,926 English requests reaches 0.808 mean accuracy on the balanced top/bottom-quartile sets (250 per language), 0.801 on Google Translate input; GPT-3 zero-shot 0.706 (Table 3). Leave-one-out human accuracy is around 90% (Fig. 3).
