[THEORY-870](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-870.md), Active, holds what the one study measured; whether practitioners in general report more pure awareness, robustly to demand, and whether EEG separates the practice from other effortless ones, is this entry's question. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1242](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1242.md) | Early vision tracks retinal info, losses central | The thesis Geisler's review asserts, filed beside [THEORY-336](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-336.md) by the status review of 2026-10-30 ([ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md) §3; [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) kind 1). [THEORY-336](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-336.md), Active, holds what the review reports; whether the parallel holds is this entry's question, and none of the primary stage-by-stage studies (Geisler 1989; Banks, Geisler and Bennett 1987) is read. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1243](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1243.md) | Endosymbiotic dependence precedes cohesion | The inference Athreya, Czuppon and Gokhale draw for nature, filed beside [THEORY-1050](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1050.md) by the twenty-fourth status review ([ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md) §3; [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) kind 1). [THEORY-1050](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1050.md), Active, holds the model result and its dependence on the trait mapping; whether real symbioses are dependence-first is this entry's question, with [THEORY-1050](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1050.md)'s old condition. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1244](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1244.md) | No access method optimizes read, update, memory | The RUM conjecture as its authors intend it, filed beside [THEORY-344](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-344.md) by the status review of 2026-10-30 ([ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md) §3; [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) kind 1). [THEORY-344](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-344.md), Active, reports the conjecture and what its formal wording and toy extremes do and do not show; whether the trade holds, quantified, is this entry's question. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1245](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1245.md) | Recursive EFE makes active inference tree search | The general form of Friston, Da Costa, Hafner, Hesp and Parr (2020), [LIT-577](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-577.md), under [THEORY-426](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-426.md)'s old title. It was kept here when the twenty-fourth status review narrowed [THEORY-426](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-426.md) to the paper's runs and promoted it ([ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md) §3; [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md), kind 1). The paper shows the planning claim only in single deterministic runs on a T-maze and an 8 × 8 maze ([NOTE-454](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-454.md), C2). It argues tractability from pruning and sparsity and counts evaluations for one maze (C3). It tries no problem where many outcomes stay plausible, and runs no Bayes-adaptive planner beside it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1246](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1246.md) | 'Contentless' meditation states aren't, nor alike | Woods, Windt and Carter's thesis about the experiences, filed beside [THEORY-866](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-866.md) by the twenty-fourth status review ([ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md) §3; [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) kind 1). [THEORY-866](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-866.md), Active, holds what the teachers' texts describe; whether practitioners' experience is so is this entry's question, with [THEORY-866](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-866.md)'s old condition. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1251](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1251.md) | Organization is posited a priori, not found | Mossio, Montévil and Longo (2016), [LIT-1888](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1888.md), §§1 and 4, read in [NOTE-1461](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1461.md); the definitions are Montévil and Mossio's ([LIT-582](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-582.md), [TERM-070](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-070.md)). The paper states the principle's status and scope and supports it by history and analogy; it derives nothing from it here. Proposed: what the principle buys is untested in this paper. It does not say that closure is observed in every organism, nor that only organisms realize it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1262](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1262.md) | Dropping MTP's target term from the trunk helps | Teoh (2026), [LIT-1896](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1896.md), §6 Figs. 3–4 and Tables 2–6; read in [NOTE-1470](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1470.md). Proposed: one run per scale, four scales, no seeds or variances, margins of one to two percent. It does not show that data-anchored correction is dispensable: the output head keeps it, and the paper attributes the explicit-KL variant's weaker head to its absence there. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1263](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1263.md) | Self-distillation from verified trajectories helps | Hossain, Kousar and Tourni (2026), [LIT-1883](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1883.md), Tables 1, 2 and 5; read in [NOTE-1479](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1479.md). Proposed: single training runs, Qwen3 only, the teacher's advantage measured at two of three scales, and a second candidate cause, per-entry clipping, left in every run. It does not show that the teacher's privileged knowledge is useless; it shows that it is hard to transmit where the student cannot see what it rests on. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1271](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1271.md) | Closure both stabilizes and propagates variation | Mossio, Montévil and Longo (2016), [LIT-1888](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1888.md), §5, read in [NOTE-1461](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1461.md). The conditional is close to definitional. That regeneration actually recovers is a dynamical claim the paper does not model, and the contrast with non-organized systems rests on three examples. Proposed. It does not say how large a variation closure can absorb, nor that recovery follows whenever the structural condition holds. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1272](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1272.md) | Late SGD weights drift sub-diffusively | Hennick and De Baerdemacker (2025; ICLR 2026), [LIT-1879](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1879.md), read in [NOTE-1467](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1467.md). Late-training displacement fits R(t) ∝ t^α with α below ½ on MNIST MLPs, TinyStories models and ImageNet convnets fine-tuned with SGD, read through the Alexander–Orbach relation as α = d_s/(2λ) with d_s ≤ λ. Proposed: d_s is obtained by fitting that same relation, so the fits test the power law and not its link to the LLC; Kunin et al. report super-diffusion in another regime. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1277](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1277.md) | Persons and organizations are coexisting levels | Bencherki & Iliadis (2021), [LIT-1922](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1922.md), read in [NOTE-1483](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1483.md), with Bencherki (2017), [LIT-1901](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1901.md). The claim behind the parent paper's dissolution of the scaling-up problem ([LIT-1902](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1902.md), p. 1364). Proposed: a conceptual proposal, illustrated by one meeting excerpt, with no criterion that fixes a level independently of the analyst. It redescribes the problem; it does not show that aggregation never occurs. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1278](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1278.md) | Communication is transduction, not exchange | Bencherki, Brummans and Vézy (2024), [LIT-1902](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1902.md), read in [NOTE-1484](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1484.md), pp. 1355–1358 and 1363–1365. Simondon's transduction made into a theory of organizational communication. Proposed: argued from examples, with the dissolution of scaling up asserted. The examples (a synapse, a hunger pang, a piston) show the notion applies to any change, which is its strength as a vocabulary and its weakness as a theory. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1279](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1279.md) | Radial categories change as they are applied | Tsoukas & Chia (2002), [LIT-1913](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1913.md), pp. 573–575, read in [NOTE-1489](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1489.md). The paper's mechanism for organizational becoming, built on Lakoff's and Johnson's prototype theory and Hart's penumbra of legal rules. Proposed: it is supported by illustrative cases, not tested. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1280](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1280.md) | Agency is affective force, agents its effects | Bencherki, Brummans and Vézy (2024), [LIT-1902](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1902.md), read in [NOTE-1484](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1484.md), pp. 1349–1357. The paper's central proposal, after the Spinozan formula for affect that Massumi offers as a proposition, not a definition, and Simondon's individuation. Proposed: argued, and illustrated by one reanalysed meeting. It has no criterion that would let an observation count against it, and it builds the augmenting direction into the definition of agency. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1281](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1281.md) | Conversation-analytic focus limits ventriloquism | Wilhoit (2016), [LIT-1923](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1923.md), read in [NOTE-1487](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1487.md). An argument about method in a five-page reply to Cooren. It is not a claim that ventriloquial analyses entify agents, which is what Bencherki, Brummans & Vézy ([LIT-1902](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1902.md), pp. 1363–1364) cite it for. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1283](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1283.md) | Micropolitics co-patterns discord inclusively | Massumi (2017), [LIT-1910](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1910.md), p. 64, read in [NOTE-1486](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1486.md); anticipated in the 2009 interview ([LIT-1905](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1905.md), p. 12) as "a symbiosis: a cross-fertilization of capacitations". It is an aim, which Massumi grants "sounds utopic" and calls "always-as-yet unknowable". Bencherki et al. ([LIT-1902](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1902.md), p. 1358) quote it exactly and use it to say what organizational becoming is constituted by. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1284](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1284.md) | Organization is a secondary effect of change | Tsoukas & Chia (2002), [LIT-1913](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1913.md), read in [NOTE-1489](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1489.md). The thesis of organizational becoming, which Bencherki, Brummans & Vézy 2024 ([LIT-1902](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1902.md)) say their theory parallels. Proposed: it is argued from process philosophy and illustrated from others' ethnographies. The change it describes is carried by human actors, not agent-free. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1285](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1285.md) | Whose action it is results from individuation | Bencherki (2017), [LIT-1901](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1901.md), read in [NOTE-1482](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1482.md), with Bencherki & Iliadis (2021), [LIT-1922](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1922.md). The proposal of which Bencherki, Brummans & Vézy's "agency without agents" ([LIT-1902](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1902.md)) is a development. Proposed: argued, and illustrated by three excerpts from one documentary. Nothing identifies disindividuation apart from the affect it is inferred from, and the account needs, but disclaims, a standard of whose action it rightly was. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1286](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1286.md) | Affect is reactivated, not transmitted | Massumi (2009), [LIT-1905](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1905.md), read in [NOTE-1488](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1488.md), pp. 6 and 9: affect "is not a content that can be transported from one event to another ... an event logic, not a logic of transmission or communication", and there is "affective difference in the same event". This sits uneasily with the "excess action" that Bencherki et al. ([LIT-1902](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1902.md)) have passing between individuation processes. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1291](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1291.md) | Interlevel causes are mediated by constitution | Craver and Bechtel (2007), [LIT-1928](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1928.md), read in [NOTE-1491](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1491.md). Parts and wholes are not distinct events. So, given transmission, distinctness or asymmetry views of causation, they cannot be cause and effect, and the symmetry of interlevel experiments is explained by constitution. The six worked cases translate. The account says nothing about whether a feedback loop crossing the mechanism's boundary changes the analysis, and its generality is assumed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1292](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1292.md) | Drive removal tells self-sustained from damped | Bechtel and Abrahamsen (2010), [LIT-1936](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1936.md), §3.6, p. 328, read in [NOTE-1492](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1492.md). Peripheral clocks were once taken for "slaves" of the SCN, damping without it. Later evidence suggested they keep oscillating and lose synchrony, so the SCN is "a conductor" rather than "a ringmaster". The paper's reading is that models of both kinds "can reveal the empirical signatures that each may leave". This is a biological instance of the record's question where maintenance is realized. It is also a case outside [CLAIM-522](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-522.md)'s ideal limit: the outside drive does not reproduce the inside law, so a perturbation of state may tell them apart. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1294](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1294.md) | Constitution is inferred only abductively | Baumgartner & Casini (2017), [LIT-1939](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1939.md), §§4–5, their No De-Coupling account, developing the fat-handedness criterion of Baumgartner & Gebharter (2016), [LIT-1934](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1934.md), pp. 20–22. Read in [NOTE-1490](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1490.md) and [NOTE-1493](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1493.md). Proposed: a definition offered with no operationalization and no case from practice, which the authors say themselves. It does not say how far a variable set must be expanded, and it takes parthood as given. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1296](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1296.md) v2 | Deliberation selects from mind-wandering's stream | Metzinger (2017), [LIT-1945](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1945.md), pp. 11–17, read in [NOTE-1496](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1496.md). The "cognitive affordance hypothesis": mind-wandering is "mental sleep-walking" that "sets up the inner world" of candidate mental actions, and frontal control "latch[es] onto the best candidate". Offered as a hypothesis after Clark and Cisek's affordance competition, with no data. The second clause is the chapter's own statement that the data "do not help to decide" what the epistemic agent model does, which takes back the principle the 2015 paper stated. "Best" is not defined, so the hypothesis does not say whether selection is by the candidates' content or by relations that govern them. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1297](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1297.md) v2 | Mind-wandering takes half, not two-thirds, of time | Metzinger (2013), [LIT-1942](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1942.md), restated in 2015, [LIT-1941](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1941.md); read in [NOTE-1495](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1495.md) and [NOTE-1497](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1497.md). The identification is conceptual: an episode of unintentional mind-wandering cannot, while it runs, be suspended or ended at will, and veto is what M-autonomy turns on. The share is computed from others' figures, and recomputed here: 631 of 1207 conscious minutes, 52%, against the "roughly two thirds" both papers state. Proposed: no measure of veto during episodes is reported, and the 30–50% figures count task-unrelated thought, which includes deliberate daydreaming the definition excludes. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1298](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1298.md) v2 | Self-model claims control's return as one's act | Metzinger (2015), [LIT-1941](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1941.md), pp. 289–292, read in [NOTE-1497](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1497.md); first in 2013 ([LIT-1942](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1942.md), pp. 4, 11) and widened in 2017 ([LIT-1945](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1945.md), pp. 20–21) to the sense of origination in agency generally. It rests on Schooler et al. (2011) and Wegner (2002), neither read, and on the argument that a self-model which must represent itself as always having had the ability cannot represent its return as caused from outside. A hypothesis: no episode is reported in which the cause of a return and the report of it were recorded apart. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1299](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1299.md) v2 | Pure awareness models tonic alertness, selflessly | Metzinger (2020), [LIT-1946](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1946.md), read in full in [NOTE-1498](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1498.md), and Metzinger (2024), [LIT-1943](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1943.md), skimmed in [NOTE-1499](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1499.md). MPE is "an inner representation of tonic alertness", "non-egoic self-modelling" that "definitely has representational content". In the 2024 sketch it is "a highest-level but nonegoic self-model" of the system's epistemic openness, which "really endows the content generated on all lower-order levels with phenomenality". It is a hypothesis fitted to retrospective reports. It does not say that consciousness needs no model of the system, only that it needs no model of a knowing self. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1300](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1300.md) | Mind-wandering hides veto, doesn't remove it | Metzinger (2015), [LIT-1941](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1941.md), pp. 280–283 and 296, read in [NOTE-1497](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1497.md); anticipated in 2013 ([LIT-1942](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1942.md), p. 3, note 4). The "moderate, nuanced position": what is lost is "not the ability itself" but "conscious knowledge of our potential for second-order mental action", with the "principle of 'Autonomy by Phenomenal Self-Representation'". Both are stated, not argued, and neither is tested. Metzinger's 2017 chapter ([LIT-1945](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1945.md), pp. 13–14) says the data cannot decide whether the self-model constitutes, enables or only accompanies control, which withholds the principle's causal reading. "Deliberately" also does work: inhibition can be wholly subpersonal. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1302](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1302.md) | Mind sets the landscape, not the state | Sánchez-Cañizares (2026), [LIT-1992](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1992.md), read in full in [NOTE-1506](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1506.md). The interpretation is the paper's (pp. 6–7, 18–20); the last clause is this reading's description of the control architecture it implies, from the model and simulation of pp. 8–12, in which the choice between wells is settled by initial condition and noise. Proposed: the paper says IAT* "cannot be tested with empirical results without further assumptions" (p. 7). Bears on [CLAIM-533](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-533.md) and [QUESTION-071](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-071.md). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1308](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1308.md) | Need effects hold across cultures and values | Chen et al. (2015), [LIT-2000](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2000.md), read in [NOTE-1527](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1527.md). Two cross-sectional studies, N = 683 and 1,051. The relations and the null moderations are as reported. Proposed because universality is inferred from failures to reject, with fewer than 150 per country in the test half, and because explicit valuation and desire are the only measures of need strength. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1311](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1311.md) | BPNSFS frustration is a keying artefact | Murphy et al. (2023), [LIT-1978](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1978.md), read in [NOTE-1530](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1530.md); Kermavnar et al. (2024), [LIT-1988](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1988.md), read in [NOTE-1509](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1509.md), adopt it. The item content and the keying structure ([THEORY-1316](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1316.md)) are shown. That the frustration scales are therefore low satisfaction is the authors' conclusion, held "probably" and "likely primarily", and by their own account cannot be decided with data in which keying and construct are confounded. Proposed for that step. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1314](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1314.md) | Contextual emergence needs a functional boundary | Jennings (2026), [LIT-1963](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1963.md), §§4–6, read in [NOTE-1508](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1508.md), with Bishop and Atmanspacher 2006 ([LIT-1987](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1987.md)) and Bishop, Silberstein and Pexton 2022 ([LIT-1993](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1993.md)), both unread, for contextual emergence. The boundary condition is the paper's own addition (fn. 15). Proposed, with a sharp edge: the paper's reason that the boundary resists micro redescription is that its properties "are macro-level ones" (p. 20), which is the point at issue, and its neural evidence fits weak emergence too. Bears on [CLAIM-334](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-334.md), whose supervenience premise it denies. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1319](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1319.md) | Extrinsic attainment adds no well-being | Niemiec, Ryan and Deci (2009), [LIT-1960](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1960.md), read in [NOTE-1520](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1520.md) from the PMC author manuscript. N = 147 at two years post-college; latent SEM and residualized-change models, all self-report. The intrinsic result and the extrinsic null are as reported; the null holds only with intrinsic attainment in the model. Proposed because one small correlational sample cannot show that extrinsic success fails to raise well-being. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1321](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1321.md) | Irruption model can't tell motivation from noise | Froese (2023), [LIT-1950](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1950.md), read in full in [NOTE-1521](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1521.md). The first half is the paper's proposal (§§4, 5.2.3, 6); the second half is this reading's observation about the model it cites, from the paper's own description of it ("reset to an arbitrary configuration"). Proposed because the proposal is stated as potential ("holds potential to provide") and no model with motivated irruptions is given. It bears directly on [CLAIM-533](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-533.md) and on the luck objection ([THEORY-328](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-328.md), [THEORY-040](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-040.md)). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1324](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1324.md) v2 | Controlling reward feedback lowers motivation | Ryan, Mims and Koestner (1983), [LIT-1970](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1970.md), read in [NOTE-1522](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1522.md) from the scan on the SDT site. One experiment, N = 96, n = 16 per cell, ANCOVA on initial interest. The framing effect is F(1, 89) = 4.25 and the reward effect against feedback-matched controls F(1, 89) = 4.34; recomputed from the cell means without the covariate, about 4.9 and 3.4 (p ≈ .07). Felt pressure was higher under controlling conditions; mediation was not tested. Proposed for replication and mediation. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1325](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1325.md) | Autonomy aids well-being across cultures | Chirkov, Ryan, Kim and Kaplan (2003), [LIT-1989](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1989.md), read in [NOTE-1513](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1513.md) from the published PDF on selfdeterminationtheory.org. N = 559, cross-sectional self-report. The positive relation held in every country and for every type of practice (β = .15–.42 within country); "no moderation" is twelve non-significant interactions in samples of 94–195. The primary study for SDT's claim that autonomy is not individualism, which it supports empirically only in this form. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1326](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1326.md) | Fixation breaks value ties in hard choices | Voigt (2022), [LIT-1976](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1976.md), an Opinion article read in [NOTE-1517](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1517.md). The model is the author's "tentative" synthesis, resting mainly on Voigt et al. 2019 (not held) in which fixation duration and dlPFC and precuneus activity predicted later preference change; the causal role of gaze is imported from other studies. Proposed. The sharp edge for its use by Jennings ([THEORY-1341](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1341.md)): the attentional step is bottom-up capture by salience, not top-down prefrontal feedback. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1328](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1328.md) | Indeterminism hinders effort, not responsibility | Kane (2009), [LIT-1984](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1984.md), pp. 39–44, read in [NOTE-1518](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1518.md). Proposed: the reply rests on analogies whose structure differs from the self-forming case (one aim and an outside obstacle against two aims, each the other's obstacle), and it does not meet the rollback form of the luck objection ([THEORY-328](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-328.md) is the record's nearest neighbour). Its concession, that indeterminism lessens control, is what [CLAIM-533](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-533.md) turns on. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1329](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1329.md) | Conflict stirs chaos making choices undetermined | Kane (2009), [LIT-1984](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1984.md), p. 39, read in [NOTE-1518](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1518.md). Kane's neural hypothesis, stated without evidence in this paper. Proposed: it is an empirical claim about brains for which the paper gives none, and the record holds nothing that measures it. It is the attribution [CLAIM-533](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-533.md) makes to Kane, now checked against his text. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1334](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1334.md) | Prompts and finetuning share persona directions | Chen et al. (2025), [LIT-1998](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1998.md), read in [NOTE-1524](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1524.md). The mediating reading is the authors' framing and PSM's use of the paper ([LIT-1952](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1952.md): training-time shifts "can be regarded as conditioning"). What the paper shows is correlation of shift with expression, and steering effects in both directions; that the regularizer against the shift fails, with the trait moving to other directions, counts against a single direction being the carrier. Proposed for that gap. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1336](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1336.md) | Empowerment-greedy cart-pole balances upright | Klyubin, Polani and Nehaniv (2008), [LIT-1951](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1951.md), pp. 4–7, read in [NOTE-1514](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1514.md). A single simulation of one model with two actions, computed by the authors; the robustness of the off-centre maxima is stated, not shown. Proposed for want of a reproduction and a second system. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1343](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1343.md) | Weak noise makes near-conserved Q slowest mode | Yang and Abanin (2025), [LIT-1958](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1958.md), §IV, read in [NOTE-1534](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1534.md). Proposed because the argument assumes fully chaotic operator growth for the complement, is checked numerically only at nine sites, and is qualified by the authors themselves: hydrodynamic modes give a continuum of slow modes in the Mori limit, so the gap "might not exist at all" outside sectors orthogonal to them. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1351](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1351.md) v2 | Shared interests, not policing, drive transitions | West et al. (2015), [LIT-2003](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2003.md), read in [NOTE-1538](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1538.md). A colloquium review: the definition and the two steps are the authors' framework, and the explanatory claim is drawn from the comparative literature they cite. Proposed because they call it "tentative", and because the theory for transitions between species is missing on their own account. It differs from [THEORY-141](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-141.md) on mechanism: group formation, not policing, does the work. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1353](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1353.md) | Circuits form when last parts align at once | Dong (2026), read in [NOTE-1540](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1540.md). One rate equation, sites × attempts × drive × e^(−βK) minus destruction, with K the missing parts. Forward, a capability ignites above a data-concentration floor that is a saddle–node; backward, plasticity loss is site depletion, silent in the loss and repaired by a query–key reset; and no native SGD knob is a temperature. Evidence: a toy grid, ablation on Pythia (32 of 32 cells below partial credit, 22 of 32 on the preregistered criterion) and six seeds for the reset. Proposed: single-author, unreplicated, mixing unproved. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1354](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1354.md) | People learn abstract causal functional forms | Lucas & Griffiths (2010), [LIT-2018](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2018.md), read in full in [NOTE-1543](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1543.md). Five blicket-meter experiments: training that suggests a conjunctive, noisy-disjunctive or deterministic form changes judgments of new objects in an identical test block, and more within a domain than across; a two-parameter sigmoid model fits the mean ratings (r = 0.98–0.99). Proposed: small samples, in-sample fits against rivals that cannot vary between conditions, one reversed prediction, one marginal effect, and no preregistered replication read. The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1355](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1355.md) v2 | Extinction is learned as a new latent cause | Gershman, Blei & Niv (2010), [LIT-2011](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2011.md), read in [NOTE-1547](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1547.md). A Chinese restaurant process mixture over trials, inferred online by a particle filter, reproduces acquisition, extinction, ABA and ABC renewal and context-specific latent inhibition in simulation; with the concentration set to zero it reproduces the loss of context-dependence after hippocampal lesions and in young rats. Proposed: the support is qualitative simulation beside replotted data from other labs, with no fitted parameters and no quantitative comparison with rival models. The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1356](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1356.md) | People build latent task-sets unprompted | Collins and Frank (2013), [LIT-2012](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2012.md), read in [NOTE-1545](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1545.md). Proposed: positive transfer replicated across the paper's two experiments (N = 33, N = 35) but is modest (t = 2.37, p = .024 in Experiment 1), and the negative-transfer interaction was significant over the whole group only in Experiment 1, a trend in Experiment 2. The EEG follow-up re-analyses Experiment 2's participants, so it is no independent replication. The account is behavioural; it does not say people perform Bayesian inference over task-sets, which the authors disclaim, nor that the Chinese-restaurant reuse prior is what people use, which they leave untested. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1358](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1358.md) | Causal schemas enable one-shot causal learning | Kemp, Goodman & Tenenbaum (2010), [LIT-2008](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2008.md), read in [NOTE-1551](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1551.md). A causal schema, a CRP partition of objects with category-level causal models, features and pairwise interactions, sits above object-level causal Bayes nets; four adult experiments in one paradigm show one-shot and zero-shot causal learning and overruling, matched qualitatively better than two baselines, with two misfits. The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1359](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1359.md) | Interventions also seek causal overhypotheses | Jiang & Lucas (2024), [LIT-2014](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2014.md), read in [NOTE-1546](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1546.md) (appendices not read). Two preregistered online blicket experiments. Learners that ignore form information or hold one fixed form barely beat random at predicting interventions; the model that does not transfer edges the full model on average (.059 against .055), while per participant the full model is best for the largest group, whose fitted weights mostly favour form information. Proposed: the transfer clause is the weakest, failing at the group level. The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1360](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1360.md) | Observers infer whether cues share a cause | Körding et al. (2007), [LIT-2010](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2010.md), read in full in [NOTE-1541](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1541.md). Proposed: one experiment of the authors' own (19 subjects) and a refit of Wallace et al.'s (2004) published data support it, against forced fusion, segregation, a MAP rule and two interaction priors, but the rule that commits to the more probable structure was not compared and only a split-half check tests held-out prediction. It does not say how the prior over causal structure is learned, that the inference is automatic, or that the model is hierarchical; that word is A's, from the owner's pasted synthesis. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1361](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1361.md) | Mind reading is inverting a rational planner | Baker, Jara-Ettinger, Saxe and Tenenbaum (2017), [LIT-2013](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2013.md), read in full in [NOTE-1549](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1549.md). Proposed: two experiments (16 and 176 adults) support it against the lesioned models, but the motion heuristic tied on Experiment 1 beliefs, the desire fit carries no information within scenario type, and the test is cross-validation over the authors' own scenarios. It is a computational-level claim, not an account of the algorithm; it does not say the model is hierarchical, a word that is A's, from the owner's pasted synthesis. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1362](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1362.md) | HGF updates take the same form at every level | Mathys et al. (2014), [LIT-2015](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2015.md), read in [NOTE-1548](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1548.md). The Hierarchical Gaussian Filter's update equations for n levels: the same precision-weighted prediction-error form at every level above the first, a value prediction error at level 1 and a volatility prediction error above. Proposed until the updates are re-derived. It says nothing about how close the approximation is to exact inversion, whether the parameters can be recovered, or whether people learn this way. The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1363](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1363.md) | Shape bias is a learned hyperparameter | Kemp, Perfors & Tenenbaum (2007), [LIT-2017](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2017.md), read in [NOTE-1544](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1544.md). Learning a constraint is inference over a hierarchy's higher-level parameters (α, β): low within-category variability of shape is the shape bias. The model reproduces Smith et al.'s first- and second-order generalization qualitatively, with no new experiments, and misses the no-name condition. Computational level; the structure and top prior are given. The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1364](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1364.md) | Task-set structure shows in prefrontal EEG | Collins, Cavanagh and Frank (2014), [LIT-2007](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2007.md), read in [NOTE-1550](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1550.md). Proposed: one sample, the participants of Collins and Frank's (2013) Experiment 2 (N = 35; 33 for ERP, 32 for classification), with several uncorrected topographic tests and an early-positivity window chosen from the grand average. The late switch negativity tracked the context dimension but did not predict transfer; the early positivity, absent at group level, and the decoder did (ρ = 0.5, ρ = 0.35), and agreed with each other only marginally. The context dimension is assigned from behavioural switch-costs, so the EEG does not read out the structure independently. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1365](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1365.md) | HGF updates take Rescorla–Wagner form | Mathys et al. (2011), [LIT-2016](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2016.md), read in [NOTE-1552](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1552.md). A derivation with illustrative simulations: closed-form trial-by-trial updates for a three-level hierarchy of volatility, of Rescorla–Wagner form, with a learning rate that is the agent's posterior variance and grows with its volatility estimate, and with per-agent coupling parameters standing for individual differences. Proposed until the updates are re-derived. It says nothing about how close the approximation is to exact inversion, or about whether people learn this way. The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1366](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1366.md) | Action functionals govern small-noise long times | Freidlin and Wentzell (3rd ed. 2012; Russian original 1979), [LIT-2035](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2035.md), read in [NOTE-1562](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1562.md) from the front matter only, where the Introduction outlines this programme (pp. xix–xxi). Proposed: the theorems are in chapters not read. Berglund's survey, [LIT-2037](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2037.md), restates the exit-time theorem but not the stationary-distribution result. It does not give sharp times, only logarithmic ones, and it is about diffusions, not about organizations or capabilities. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1367](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1367.md) | Compliant underactuated hand grasps open-loop | Dollar and Howe (2010), [LIT-2040](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2040.md), read in [NOTE-1575](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1575.md). Proposed: the experiments are small, success was judged by eye, and no fully actuated hand was tested alongside. It is about power grasps of medium objects; the hand cannot pinch. It does not say that the hand computes, or has goals, or that one actuator suffices for dexterous manipulation. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1368](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1368.md) v2 | Kirigami rigidity needs more links than connection | Chen, Choi & Mahadevan (2020), [LIT-2064](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2064.md), read from arXiv v2 in [NOTE-1574](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1574.md) (main text; the SI with the proofs was not read). Proposed: the minimal counts are proved by construction in the SI, which was not read; the thresholds are numerical, and the rigidity threshold is a peak of a second derivative with a heuristic explanation. Planar quad kirigami and infinitesimal rigidity only; no experiments. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1369](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1369.md) v2 | Marginal origami carries topological polarization | Chen, Liu, Evans, Paulose, Cohen, Vitelli and Santangelo (2016; arXiv 2015), [LIT-2049](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2049.md), read in full in [NOTE-1624](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1624.md). Proposed: the strip result has the authors' own experiment, but the domain-wall result is numerical and the 2D origami claim is a conjecture on numerics. It does not say that joining rigid parts creates freedom in general: equal polarizations give no wall mode, and walls of the other orientation are stressed lines that carry load. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1370](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1370.md) v2 | Large deviations fix only exit time's exponent | Berglund (2011), [LIT-2037](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2037.md), read in [NOTE-1590](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1590.md), a review registered as a stand-in for Freidlin and Wentzell ([LIT-2035](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2035.md)). Proposed: the survey sketches and cites the proofs rather than giving them. It does not say the prefactor is unknowable for non-gradient systems in general, only that large deviations do not deliver it and that in the cycling case it has no limit. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1371](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1371.md) | Incentive design for returning agents is open | Ratliff, Dong, Sekar and Fiez (2019), [LIT-2097](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2097.md), read in full in [NOTE-1566](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1566.md) from the authors' manuscript. A perspective's judgement of the state of three literatures, not a theorem; Proposed until a later review states the same. It does not say the problem is unsolvable, and it leaves out the economics of dynamic contracting with limited commitment, which treats one case of it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1373](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1373.md) v2 | Moving origami switches reconfigures logic | Hu, Tan, Chen and Yan (2025), [LIT-2082](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2082.md), read in [NOTE-1608](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1608.md). The rotatable gate, the 30-gate array and a third-order cube switching between full adder and full subtractor were built and tested over all inputs; the densities per cube order and the gate savings are counts against the authors' own baselines. It does not say that the computation is purely mechanical, since outputs and inter-gate signals are electrical, or that the material reconfigures itself. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1374](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1374.md) v2 | Freedom spaces compose in parallel and series | Hopkins (2013), [LIT-2069](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2069.md), read in full in [NOTE-1580](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1580.md). Proposed: the rules follow from linear reciprocity of screw spaces and are stated with design examples, but there is no experiment and no independent check, and the library's completeness rests on Hopkins (2010), [LIT-2042](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2042.md). It excludes interconnected limbs, is kinematic only, and its over-constraint test says nothing of misfit stress. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1377](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1377.md) v2 | Facet planarity tunes origami rigidity | Li & Choi (2026), [LIT-2068](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2068.md), read in [NOTE-1564](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1564.md) (main text; the Supplementary Notes were not read). Proposed: one group's simulations on ten patterns. The n − 3 count is proved; the dependence of the critical density on rule, pool size and triangular-facet ratio is numerical, and the formula for it is fitted, not derived. Rigidity is infinitesimal at one folded configuration, and the "critical density" is a fixed-size statistic, not a thermodynamic threshold. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1380](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1380.md) v2 | Finite CSPs are in P or NP-complete | Zhuk (2017; J. ACM 2020), [LIT-2023](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2023.md), read in part in [NOTE-1555](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1555.md) (the introduction, outline, definitions, Theorem 5.1 with proof and the conclusions). Proposed: the main proofs were not read. It is about deciding existence of a solution, for fixed finite languages on finite domains. It does not say anything about infinite domains, where the author shows CSPs can be undecidable, about quantified CSPs, or about the connectivity of the solution space. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1382](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1382.md) v2 | Weak NU polymorphism makes CSPs polynomial | Bulatov (2017), [LIT-2115](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2115.md), read in part in [NOTE-1572](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1572.md) (§§1–2 and the opening of §3; the proofs not read). Proposed: the tractability algorithm and its 80 pages of proof were not checked. It concerns decision problems over a fixed finite language on a finite domain. It does not classify systems or single instances, and says nothing about infinite domains or about moving between solutions. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1383](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1383.md) | Saddle instability thins passive walker's basin | Obayashi, Aoi, Tsuchiya and Kokubu (2016), [LIT-2110](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2110.md), read in [NOTE-1586](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1586.md), as a neighbour of McGeer (1990), [LIT-2108](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2108.md). Proposed: the figures were read by caption, and the mechanism is argued, not proved. It is about one idealised model; it does not say that every passive walker's basin is shaped this way, nor anything about McGeer's own walkers. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1384](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1384.md) | Maximizing survival saves more than coverage | Erkut, Ingolfsson and Erdoğan (2008), [LIT-2089](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2089.md), read in [NOTE-1556](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1556.md). Proposed: the comparisons are the paper's own, on one city's data, with survival functions for cardiac arrest assumed for all urgent calls and a non-optimal heuristic for the richest models. The account is about expected survivors under the authors' survival functions and evaluation model; it does not say coverage is useless, since by the paper's Table 6 coverage with either source of uncertainty reaches the best-known value. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1385](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1385.md) | Spaced digital education modestly beats massed | Martinengo, Ng, Ng, Ang, Jabir, Kyaw & Tudor Car (2024), [LIT-2102](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2102.md), read in [NOTE-1610](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1610.md): 23 trials, immediate post-intervention outcomes. It does not say that spacing improves retention of skills over months, nor anything about long non-use; and for simulation the abstract and body give different pooled estimates (SMD 1.15 and 1.24). Proposed: one meta-analysis over studies mostly at unclear or high risk of bias. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1386](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1386.md) | Neural net inverse-designs Kresling energy curves | Kang, Kim, Yang and Ryu (2025), [LIT-2086](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2086.md), read in [NOTE-1619](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1619.md). Forward and inverse results are checked against a beam-truss FEA that shares the network's truss abstraction; the folding order is checked also in one scaled PET prototype, where barriers differ from prediction and are compared after normalizing to the bottom layer. It does not say the truss model captures the mechanics of real cells. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1387](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1387.md) | Rimless wheel gait is stable by geometry | Asano (2012), [LIT-2050](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2050.md), read in [NOTE-1578](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1578.md), as a neighbour of McGeer (1990), [LIT-2108](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2108.md). Proposed: the derivations were read, not redone. The eigenvalue and the minimum slope come from a linearised stance phase. It is about the rimless wheel alone; it does not say that walkers with a swing leg are stable for the same reason, or where on steep slopes walking ends. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1391](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1391.md) | CVaR minimization is convex and yields VaR | Rockafellar and Uryasev (2000), [LIT-2052](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2052.md), read in full in [NOTE-1623](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1623.md) from the authors' 1999 manuscript (Theorems 1 and 2 with their proofs, §3). Proposed until a second source states the same. It holds for loss distributions without atoms, at a fixed β, in one period; it says nothing about how large a sample the rare scenarios need, which the paper's own examples show can be large. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1393](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1393.md) | Rigid folding from flat needs a bird's foot | Abel, Cantarella, Demaine, Eppstein, Hull, Ku, Lang and Tachi (2016), [LIT-2093](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2093.md), read in full in [NOTE-1589](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1589.md) (arXiv v1). Proposed: the proofs were followed in one reading but not checked against the journal version or reproduced. It does not say anything about multi-vertex crease patterns, about folds far from flat, or about motions in which the paper passes through itself. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1397](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1397.md) | Resource theories are monoidal categories | Coecke, Fritz & Spekkens (2014; Information and Computation 2016), [LIT-2032](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2032.md), read in [NOTE-1591](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1591.md) (main text; Examples 3.13–3.18 and Appendix A skimmed). Proposed: the appendix proof and the sketched lemmas were not checked. The morphisms of such a theory are free: it says nothing about costs attached to transformations, which the authors leave open as "epsilonification", and nothing about time, rates or a free set that changes. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1399](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1399.md) v2 | Square-twist folds by bending, can be bistable | Silverberg et al. (2015), [LIT-2100](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2100.md), read in [NOTE-1554](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1554.md) (the letter in full; SI pp. 1–2 skimmed). Proposed: one group's experiments on paper and gel with matching simulations, on a single unit cell. The general thesis that the number of degrees of freedom changes with the energy scale probed is the authors' framing; what was shown is this one structure. Tessellations are proposed, not tested. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1400](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1400.md) v2 | Mobile actuator programs origami logic arrays | Chen, Tan and Yan (2025), [LIT-2030](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2030.md), read in [NOTE-1559](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1559.md). Built and tested for 2- to 4-input arrays (half and full adder and subtractor, 2-bit adder or multiplier); generality to any function is by construction over pre-built minterm modules. It does not say that the device programs itself: the address path is fixed by a magnet layout designed outside it, and the robot runs on electric motors. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1402](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1402.md) | Rigid foldability from flat is NP-hard | Akitaya et al. (2020), [LIT-2071](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2071.md), read in [NOTE-1579](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1579.md) (model and main text in full, reduction gadgets skimmed). Proposed: the gadget constructions behind Theorems 15 and 16 were not checked line by line. It does not say that the problem is in NP in general, which is open, or anything about the mechanics of folding a real sheet. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1403](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1403.md) | Laser-rewritable magnetization reprograms films | Deng, Sattari, Xie, Liao, Yan and Lin (2020), [LIT-2034](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2034.md), read in [NOTE-1565](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1565.md), as a neighbour of Yeow, Yang and Ren (2024), [LIT-2113](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2113.md). Proposed: the figures were read by caption, and the supplement on cycling only by its caption. It does not say that the film can be rewritten in place without an external laser and field, nor anything about an actuator coupling to and decoupling from a separate structure. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1405](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1405.md) | Bistable truss becomes single-piece frame | Kinoshita and Ohsaki (2009), [LIT-2029](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2029.md), read in full in [NOTE-1597](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1597.md). Proposed: the conversion is shown on one seven-node example, in simulation, with equivalence judged by overlaid force–displacement curves. It does not say that the frame is bistable without the obstacle, that the method finds frames without a truss to start from, or that a fabricated frame behaves as computed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1408](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1408.md) | Topological count fixes isostatic zero modes | Kane and Lubensky (2014; arXiv 2013), [LIT-2078](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2078.md), read in full in [NOTE-1601](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1601.md), the supplementary proof included. Proposed: the theorem is proved and the two models agree with it; an independent case is what promotion asks. Chen et al. ([LIT-2049](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2049.md)), read in this batch, apply the topological polarization to an origami strip and to kirigami and are a candidate. It does not say that every boundary mode is topological, or that the linear zero modes extend to finite motions. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1409](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1409.md) | Miura-ori cannot uniquely self-fold | Hull and Tachi (2018), [LIT-2033](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2033.md), read in full in [NOTE-1603](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1603.md) (arXiv v1). Proposed: the theorems were read with their proofs, which rest on the authors' 2016 criteria, not checked here. It does not say anything about stiffness, bending energy or noisy actuators, which the model leaves out, or about tessellations beyond monohedral quadrilateral ones. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1410](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1410.md) | Partial roll-over beats use-it-or-lose-it | Siemroth (SSRN 2021; IER 2024), [LIT-2103](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2103.md), read in [NOTE-1594](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1594.md) from the February 2022 working paper. Proposed: the results are the paper's propositions, whose proofs (in the appendix) were not read, and the version of record, which may differ, was not reached. Within the model they are stated for two periods, risk-neutral parties and uniform needs; the threshold audit holds in year 2 and in year 1 absent saving, an interval rule otherwise. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1411](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1411.md) v2 | Creased sheet can learn to classify forces | Stern, Arinze, Perez, Palmer and Murugan (2020; arXiv 2019), [LIT-2116](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2116.md), read in [NOTE-1615](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1615.md) from the arXiv v1 preprint, titled differently; the PNAS text and the Supplementary Notes were not read. Proposed for that reason. It is a result about a model: it does not say that any physical sheet has been trained, that the sheet learns without an external supervisor, or that it scales beyond small two-class tasks. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1415](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1415.md) v2 | Kresling stacks are Preisach memories | Jules, Reid, Daniels, Mungan and Lechenault (2022), [LIT-2072](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2072.md), read in [NOTE-1617](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1617.md). Shown in experiment on one four-barrel stack and its softer twin, with the Preisach graph confirmed and defect states found by twisting by hand. It does not say that the 64 counted states were all observed (39 of 48 single-defect states were), that the readout identifies every state, or that loading alone can create a defect in a decoupled stack. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1419](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1419.md) v2 | Self-stress decides if counting predicts rigidity | Damavandi, Hagh, Santangelo and Manning (2022; arXiv 2021), [LIT-2041](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2041.md), read in full in [NOTE-1570](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1570.md). Proposed: a single paper's derivations, with the hardest case left open by the authors. It does not say that a system with states of self-stress is never energetically rigid, nor that the shear modulus measures rigidity; and it covers Hookean energies only. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1420](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1420.md) v3 | Persistent homology extends disconnectivity graphs | Mirth, Zhai, Bush, Alvarado, Jordan, Heim, Krishnamoorthy, Pflaum, Clark, Zhang and Adams (2021), [LIT-2047](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2047.md), read in [NOTE-1616](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1616.md), appendices with the full proofs skimmed. The first two parts are standard correspondences the paper states and illustrates; the closed form is its Theorems 1 and 2. It treats one scalar energy only: nothing here covers several resources at once, which would need multi-parameter persistence. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1421](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1421.md) | Expiring budgets cause year-end waste | Liebman and Mahoney (NBER 2013; AER 2017), [LIT-2028](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2028.md), read in [NOTE-1553](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1553.md). Proposed: the model derives the mechanism; the spike and the quality drop are shown in US federal procurement only, the quality drop on rated I.T. projects only; the rollover effect on volume rests on one agency's authority, its effect on quality on one project; and the title's most of the waste is a calibrated welfare share, not a measurement. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1425](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1425.md) | Pruning ~1% of bonds tunes network response | Rocks, Pashine, Bischofberger, Goodrich, Liu and Nagel (2017; arXiv 2016), [LIT-2060](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2060.md), read in [NOTE-1607](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1607.md) from the arXiv v1 preprint; the PNAS text was not reached. Proposed for that reason and because the Supporting Information was not read. It is a linear, athermal result for central-force networks made rigid first: it does not say why the chosen bonds work, that the network could find them itself, or that allostery in proteins works this way. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1429](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1429.md) | Critical transitions leave slow manifolds | Kuehn (2011), [LIT-2048](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2048.md), read in [NOTE-1598](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1598.md) from the arXiv v2. Proposed: the propositions' proofs are short normal-form computations that were read but not redone here. It is about one slow variable and one-dimensional (planar for Hopf) fast normal forms; it does not say when the jump comes, which drift delays and noise can advance, nor that observed indicators reliably reveal the exponent. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1431](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1431.md) v2 | Multistable origami can be a reservoir computer | Liu, Fang, Xu and Wang (2023), [LIT-2026](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2026.md), read in [NOTE-1600](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1600.md). The comparison with the raw inputs (90.4% against 87.2% on binarized MNIST) and the memory result are simulations with a least-action model; the experiment covers ten 5×4-pixel digits on a 4×2-cell prototype. It does not say that the material learns: only the linear readout is trained. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1433](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1433.md) v2 | Compliant mechanisms via topological derivative | Krishnakumar and Suresh (2015), [LIT-2099](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2099.md), read in full in [NOTE-1582](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1582.md) from a lab-posted manuscript, as a stand-in for Sigmund (1997). Proposed: hinge-freedom is shown by pictures of a handful of coarse-mesh designs, and the η trade-off on one example. It is the authors' account of their own method, not of Sigmund's; it does not say that the designs stay hinge-free under stress constraints or large deformation, or that they were built. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1436](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1436.md) | Origami springs fit 3D curves with few actuators | Liu, Zhang and Fang (2023), [LIT-2077](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2077.md), read in [NOTE-1558](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1558.md) (the main text; the supplement skipped). Proposed: the figures were read by caption and text, and the experimental comparisons are in the unread supplement. It is kinematic and about static shapes. It does not say how good the virtual-crease model is for a flexible spring, that the grouping found is optimal or unique, or anything about moving between shapes. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1438](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1438.md) | DNA origami joints give one designed DOF | Marras, Zhou, Su and Castro (2015), [LIT-2118](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2118.md), read in [NOTE-1635](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1635.md) (main text and figure captions; the Supporting Information unread). Proposed: the conformational statistics are negative-stain TEM fractions on a surface, which the authors call upper bounds, over 52 to 918 particles with misfolds excluded, and one actuation cycle is reported. It does not say that the mechanisms fold with high yield, that switching survives repeated cycles, or that the grid fractions are those in solution. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1439](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1439.md) | Staple choice steers degenerate origami folds | Dunn, Dannenberg, Ouldridge, Kwiatkowska, Turberfield and Bath (2015), [LIT-2135](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2135.md), read in [NOTE-1643](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1643.md). The shift is shown by AFM shape counts on one tile, one anneal ramp and one buffer, with 36-62% of candidate objects fitted; the trapping figure (52% misfolds with full seams, 1% with broken ones) is the model's. The equal stability of the final folds is the authors' design argument, not a measurement, and the model is not thermodynamically self-consistent. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1459](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1459.md) | Earned tax revenue builds state capacity | Moore (2004), [LIT-2182](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2182.md), read in [NOTE-1663](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1663.md): the fiscal (social) contract proposition and its rentier-state converse, with aid counted as a strategic rent, and the further point that easy concessional finance turns governments from negotiating with taxpayers. Proposed: a review that argues from European history and others' cross-national evidence, convincing for oil and, by the author's own account, weak and possibly reverse-caused for aid. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1460](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1460.md) | Large sustained aid can weaken institutions | Moss, Pettersson & van de Walle (2006), [LIT-2144](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2144.md), read in [NOTE-1661](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1661.md): a review of the tax-effort and state-building literatures. Besides the two mechanisms in the title they name a third, fragmented donor practice drawing capacity from the civil service, and hold that a state becomes self-sufficient by learning to tax. Proposed: the authors call the aid–revenue evidence negative on balance but "not a conclusive result", and their own analysis is bivariate. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1475](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1475.md) | Gifts oblige giving, receiving and returning | Mauss (1925), [LIT-2191](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2191.md), skimmed in [NOTE-1658](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1658.md) with the introduction, chapter I, the Northwest-coast section and the conclusion read in full. Proposed: the ethnographic half is Mauss's reading of others' fieldwork, and the hau half rests on one informant's text in a translation Mauss calls abridged; the modern half is moral and political argument. It does not say that an unconditional gift exists, that reciprocity needs lost capability, or anything about aid. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1476](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1476.md) | Urban renewal targeted black neighbourhoods | LaVoice (2024), [LIT-2142](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2142.md), read from a 24-page 2021 draft in [NOTE-1680](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1680.md), not from the version of record. Proposed: the draft defers its complete results to the full paper; its income gain is given as 18% and as 16% without reconciliation, so no income figure is asserted here; controls are slums in other cities, with black-share pre-trends that differ; and the welfare result is the model's, not a measurement. It does not track the displaced or measure the social ties the clearances broke. It complements the city-level [THEORY-1470](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1470.md). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1477](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1477.md) v2 | Tree nuclei keep facilitating; perches decay | Holl, Reid, Zahawi, de Siqueira & Brancalion (2024), [LIT-2172](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2172.md), read in [NOTE-1676](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1676.md): an opinion article by the senior author of the unread Corbin & Holl (2012), [LIT-2179](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2179.md), read as its stand-in for mechanism and nucleus size. A planted tree is support that becomes the capacity; a perch stands in for that capacity and then rots. Proposed: the article argues from the literature rather than showing data, its 64 m² minimum is cited from Zahawi & Augspurger (2006) and Holl et al. (2020), and it says itself that spread is rarely measured. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1483](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1483.md) | Aid can erode tax capacity past a threshold | Azam, Devarajan & O'Connell (1999), [LIT-2156](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2156.md), read in full in [NOTE-1682](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1682.md). Proposed: the derivation of the dynamics and of the steady-state roots was rechecked symbolically for this reading, but the stability of the two points and the myopic threshold rest on the paper's phase diagrams, which were not re-derived. It is a model with unit slopes, tax inefficiency the reciprocal of experience and fixed spending; it says nothing measured about any country. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1500](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1500.md) | Kerr solitons exist in a detuning window | Herr, Brasch, Jost, Wang, Kondratiev, Gorodetsky and Kippenberg (2014), [LIT-2204](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2204.md), read in [NOTE-1692](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1692.md) from arXiv v3; experiment in one MgF2 resonator, simulation of the coupled-mode (Lugiato-Lefever) equations without thermal effects, and approximate analytics. Proposed: the window rests on an infinite-domain analysis the record has not read, and the equations were read from a page image because extraction drops square roots. It does not say that formation shows hysteresis (no reverse sweep is reported), how fast a soliton vanishes after switch-off (not measured), or how the number of solitons varies between experimental runs (reported for simulations only). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1501](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1501.md) | Solitons survive collisions unchanged | Zabusky & Porter (2010), [LIT-2208](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2208.md), read in full in [NOTE-1689](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1689.md), an encyclopedia article by the co-author of the 1965 letter. Filed as the read neighbour of Zabusky & Kruskal (1965), which was not reached. The definition is the article's, after Scott (2005); the collision property is illustrated by the article's own simulation, not proved there; the history is Zabusky's later account of his own work. It holds for integrable equations: the article says the relatives do not in general share the interaction property. The wording is the filer's, from the reader's report; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1506](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1506.md) | Bubbles settle into long-lived oscillons | Copeland, Gleiser & Müller (1995), [LIT-2200](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2200.md), read in full in [NOTE-1699](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1699.md). Shown by numerical simulation, with a one-degree-of-freedom Gaussian ansatz explaining the lower radius bound and the end; spherical symmetry throughout, stability tested only against radial perturbations. It does not explain the upper radius bound, give an analytic lifetime, or define the plateau's endpoints formally. The wording of the title is the reader's condensation of the paper's §§III–IV and VII. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1507](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1507.md) v2 | Topological charge bounds soliton energy | Tong (2005), [LIT-2207](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2207.md), read in NOTE-1694 for the topological charge and the kinks (§1.1, §2.1, §§3.1–3.2, §3.8.3, §§4.1–4.3.2). Standard topological soliton theory, stated by Tong for instantons, monopoles, vortices and domain walls in gauge theories. The thesis that a topological soliton cannot decay except by annihilation with an opposite charge or by a change at the boundary is the reader's inference from these points, not Tong's statement, and is not part of this account. A neighbour of Copeland, Gleiser & Müller (1995), [LIT-2200](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2200.md), for the protection oscillons lack. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1509](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1509.md) v2 | Damped solitons shrink and shed a shelf | Grimshaw, Smyth & Stepanyants (2018), [LIT-2198](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2198.md), read in full in [NOTE-1687](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1687.md), for the Benjamin–Ono equation with six kinds of weak loss, by first-order adiabatic theory checked against direct numerics. Filed as the read neighbour of Kivshar & Malomed (1989), whose central method for damped solitons it carries in one equation. The KdV laws, which make the title's "integrable wave equation" more than one case, are quoted in the paper from earlier work, not derived, and so are not shown here. It says nothing of NLS, of gain or supply, or of strong loss. The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |

The authors track some 40 million English-language headlines (BIG4: New York Times, Guardian, Times of India, ABC News Australia from 2000; the News on the Web corpus from 2010) for lexical, syntactic and sentiment features that earlier work linked to clickbait style or to higher click-through rates, with an Upworthy corpus (clickbait benchmark) and arXiv titles (contrast) as fixed reference points. Headlines grew longer, more negative, more often contained verbs, pronouns and wh-words, and moved away from the noun-phrase format, i.e. moved toward the Upworthy profile. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1649](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1649.md) | Informed consent is a resilient core plus a rim | Eyal, read in [NOTE-1800](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1800.md) (Read). A survey of informed consent in bioethics: why it is required, what it consists in, and its status. §2 canvasses seven candidate justifications — protection (welfare), autonomy, prevention of abusive conduct, trust (forward- and backward-looking), self-ownership, non-domination, and personal integrity — and argues each faces serious objections, with autonomy (dominant since the 1970s) treated at length and found hard to ground as a complete justification. §§3–5 analyze consent itself (behavioral vs psychological; presumed/hypothetical consent), the information requirement, and voluntariness (coercion, undue inducement, "no choice" situations). §8 distinguishes natural-right, legal, epistemic and trust-based accounts of the requirement's status. §9 relates medical consent to sexual, contractual and political consent. §10 argues for a resilient "core" (risky, value-laden, invasive, refused interventions) and a weaker, more overridable "rim". | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1650](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1650.md) | Mereology fit to a norm can't support it | Mereological implications of the ethics of pregnancy (Dranseika, J Med Ethics 2026), read in [NOTE-1751](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1751.md) (Read), standing in for [LIT-2409](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2409.md). Dranseika accepts Devanesan's thesis that a mereology of pregnancy changes the route to an ethical conclusion without entailing it, and adds the converse: normative commitments can legitimately shape which mereology one adopts, but a mereology chosen to fit a commitment is then no independent evidence for it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1651](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1651.md) | Up to 17% of ML reviews were LLM-modified | Liang et al. The authors estimate, at corpus level, the fraction α of text substantially modified or generated by an LLM, by maximum likelihood over word-frequency distributions estimated from human-written and AI-generated reference corpora, validated on semi-synthetic mixtures. Applied to peer reviews, α rose sharply after ChatGPT's release at ML conferences (ICLR 1.6% to 10.6%; NeurIPS 1.9% to 9.1%; CoRL 2.4% to 6.5%; EMNLP about 16.9%) but not in Nature-portfolio reviews. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1652](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1652.md) | OTOF therapy makes infant genetic testing needed | Reisinger and Cederroth, read in [NOTE-1801](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1801.md) (Read). Comments on the FDA's approval (announced 23 April 2026) of Regeneron's Otarmeni, the first gene therapy for a genetic hearing loss (DFNB9, OTOF), and on convergent results from other programmes. Because the therapy is gene-specific and time-sensitive, infants with bilateral hearing loss need genetic diagnosis; clinical sequences should change so that children with profound loss and intact otoacoustic emissions get a genetic diagnosis before a cochlear implant. | Proposed |
