Within each test, different headlines for the same story were randomly shown, so story content is held fixed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1656](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1656.md) | LLM documents crowd out human sources in retrieval | Yu, Kim and Kim (2026), read in [NOTE-1752](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1752.md) (Read). The authors name "Retrieval Collapse", a two-stage failure in which (1) AI-generated content comes to dominate search results, eroding source diversity, and (2) low-quality or adversarial synthetic content enters the retrieval pipeline. On 1,000 MS MARCO queries, each with ten Google-retrieved web documents (Original Pool), they add GPT-5-nano documents one per round for 20 rounds (pool contamination 0% → 66.7%), in two scenarios: an "SEO" pool (LLM rewrites of original documents with high-IDF keywords) and an "Abuse" pool (clickbait drafts with named entities and numbers falsified). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1657](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1657.md) | There is no distinctive right to an open future | Millum (2025), read in [NOTE-1734](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1734.md) (Read). Millum argues that there is no distinctive "right to an open future" (Feinberg's rights-in-trust). As a negative right it would rest either on future autonomy or on analogy. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1658](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1658.md) | LysM+CD11c+ maternal cells sustain tolerance | Peng, Way and colleagues' result as Cincinnati Children's reports it ([LIT-2428](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2428.md), read in [NOTE-1763](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1763.md)). The persistence of foreign-origin cells in a host and their part in the host's regulation come apart: one marked subset does the tolerogenic work, and the rest persist without it. Proposed because the source is a press post and the paper could not be read; the Europe PMC abstract agrees with it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1659](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1659.md) | Shortfall fell while overshoot grew, unequally | Fanning & Raworth (2025), read in [NOTE-1782](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1782.md) (Read). A third iteration of the Doughnut: 21 dimensions measured by 35 indicators (social foundation and ecological ceiling), with time series 2000–2022 for 30 of them, plus a 2017 disaggregation of 27 comparable indicators into three country clusters by income (poorest 40%, middle 40%, richest 20% of countries). Globally, deprivation fell modestly while ecological overshoot rose; disaggregated, the richest cluster contributes a disproportionate share of overshoot and the poorest holds most shortfall. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1660](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1660.md) | Point estimates can't certify classifier fairness | Md Fahim Sikder, read in [NOTE-1779](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1779.md) (Read). FairCert is a black-box audit pipeline that turns per-group false-positive-rate (FPR) and true-positive-rate (TPR) gaps into finite-sample certificates. Five stages: a stratified split with a walled-off 15% audit set; LLM-guided discovery of candidate intersectional subgroups from aggregate training statistics (hypotheses), confirmed on the disjoint audit set; per-group error rates of the classifier's predictions; a certificate built from Clopper-Pearson exact intervals per group with a Bonferroni correction over K groups, which bounds the worst pairwise gap with probability at least 1−δ and passes if the bound is within tolerance ε; and, for failures, per-group threshold calibration with the TPR cost reported, plus a structured EU AI Act-oriented report. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1661](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1661.md) | Circumcision makes a Danish-Jewish family | Dræbel, Sørensen and Meyrowitsch, read in [NOTE-1729](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1729.md) (Read). Twenty semi-structured interviews (2017–2021) with Danish parents of Jewish background (12 fathers, 8 mothers; 18 chose circumcision, 2 did not), analysed with Antonovsky's Sense of Coherence and Davies and Harré's positioning theory, against the background of a Danish public debate (c. 2010–2022) on banning non-therapeutic circumcision of boys (NTCB), including a 2018 citizen proposal to criminalize it. Parents describe NTCB as "inevitable", a taken-for-granted ritual and a rite of passage through which they become Danish-Jewish parents and a family and enrol the son in the family biography, whether or not they are religious. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1662](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1662.md) | Brain sickness responses are pathogen-specific | Sullivan et al., read in [NOTE-1775](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1775.md) (Read). In mice, five sterile immune challenges modelling bacterial infection (LPS), viral infection (poly I:C), parasite infection (soluble *Toxoplasma* antigen, STAg), allergy (bee-venom PLA2) and colitis (DSS) produce distinct "sickness states" at three scales: organismal (temperature, food intake, locomotion, metabolism, social behaviour, ultrasonic vocalizations), cellular (whole-brain FOS activity, which a classifier uses to predict the challenge) and molecular (a 940-gene MERFISH atlas of the preoptic and paraventricular hypothalamus). The states cluster: LPS with poly I:C; STAg with DSS; PLA2 apart. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1663](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1663.md) | Value failures start with those who state them | Moats et al. (2026), read in [NOTE-1760](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1760.md) (Read). Drawing on ethnographic studies across six European countries (Finland, Sweden, Denmark, Belgium, Slovenia, UK; the abstract says five), the authors argue that invoking "public values" against big tech without specifying them produces practical problems "even to the opposite of originally stated objectives". They give five "disconnects", each with vignettes: value narrowing (privacy → consent buttons; transparency → self-reporting register; well-being → step counts), value tickboxing (GDPR anonymisation by default; OpenAI's "Democratic Inputs"; Swedish energy certificates), value pushing (automated blinds; child-protection risk prediction; AI in Danish breast screening), value mismatch (border-control face-match threshold vs airport "flow"; smart thermostats vs home comfort; Epic/Apotti efficiency vs physicians' "fluency"), and value projection ("human-centric" Aurora AI; "green transition"; holism in digital twins). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1664](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1664.md) | Judge interfaces by inconsistency, not behaviour | The transaction test: An experimental method for assessing online interfaces (Bogliacino, Pejsachowicz, Liva, Lupiáñez-Villanueva 2026), read in [NOTE-1783](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1783.md) (Read). The paper proposes the *transaction test*: elicit (or assign) a person's monetary valuation M_f of a product feature, then have them choose between two versions of the good that differ only by that feature and a price p_f; choosing against one's valuation is an inconsistent choice. An interface fails the test if it raises the rate of inconsistent choices relative to a transparent design (H0: E[I \| d] ≤ E[I \| transparent]). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1665](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1665.md) | Newspaper closures raise local borrowing costs | Gao, Lee and Murphy, read in [NOTE-1761](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1761.md) (Skimmed). Using U.S. daily newspaper data (1996–2015; 1,596 newspapers in 1,266 counties; 296 exits) and municipal bond data (MSRB, 1999–2015), the authors study the long-run effect of local newspaper closures on municipal borrowing costs. Focusing on closures that leave a county with two or fewer dailies (204 "Closure" counties), they find offering yields rise by about 5.5 bp and secondary yields by 6.4 bp three or more years after a closure, more for revenue bonds (about 10 bp), costing about $650 thousand per average issue. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1666](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1666.md) | Norms may break ties among pregnancy ontologies | Żuradzki (2026), Ethics-first metaphysics: normative considerations as evidence for ontological commitments, read in [NOTE-1744](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1744.md) (Read). A commentary on [LIT-2409](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2409.md). Żuradzki accepts Devanesan's thesis that no ontology of pregnancy entails an ethical conclusion but that each constrains which analogies can support one, and argues that the relation is closer: where biological evidence underdetermines competing ontologies, considered normative judgments may themselves count as evidence for choosing between them. This is Dasgupta's "ethics-first" methodology, which Żuradzki extends from personal identity to pregnancy and embryonic identity. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1667](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1667.md) | Cytoplasmic incompatibility resists displacement | Brenninger, Zug & Kokko (2025), read in [NOTE-1786](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1786.md) (Skimmed). A unified minimal model of the infection dynamics of maternally transmitted endosymbionts (Wolbachia, Rickettsia, Cardinium, Spiroplasma and others) that manipulate arthropod reproduction: male-killing, feminization, parthenogenesis induction, sex-allocation distortion and cytoplasmic incompatibility (CI), in diplodiploid and haplodiploid hosts. It gives invasion criteria for single strains and for pairs of manipulators. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1668](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1668.md) | Loot boxes can be optimal without screening | Gan, Gacha Game: When Prospect Theory Meets Optimal Pricing, read in [NOTE-1778](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1778.md) (Skimmed). A seller sells one good to a buyer with cumulative prospect theory preferences whose value is known. Probability weighting makes the buyer dynamically inconsistent. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1669](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1669.md) | Judge journalism ML data by journalism ethics | Dierickx et al. (2024), A data-centric approach for ethical and trustworthy AI in journalism, read in [NOTE-1736](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1736.md) (Skimmed). Proposes the Accuracy-Fairness-Transparency (AFT) framework for assessing the quality of datasets used to build machine-learning tools in newsrooms, deriving data-quality checks from three core principles of journalism ethics, and placing the work in the shift from model-centric to data-centric AI. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1670](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1670.md) | Ion channels regulate development; how is unclear | George and Bates (2022), Mechanisms Underlying Influence of Bioelectricity in Development, read in [NOTE-1772](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1772.md) (Skimmed). A review of how ion channels and membrane potential (Vmem) act in development: human channelopathies with developmental phenotypes, conserved roles across species, spontaneous calcium oscillations in non-excitable tissue, and the cellular processes (death, proliferation, polarity, migration) and signalling pathways (BMP, Notch, Wnt, Hedgehog) that channels touch. It proposes calcium as the main mediator and a model in which Vmem and calcium oscillations, shaped by mechanical forces, coordinate cells across a tissue. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1671](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1671.md) | Child genital surgery only if strictly necessary | The Brussels Collaboration on Bodily Integrity, read in [NOTE-1799](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1799.md) (Skimmed). Restricting itself to nonvoluntary genital cutting or surgery by licensed clinicians on prepubescent children in Global North healthcare systems, and taking no position on criminal law or religious practice outside healthcare, the collaboration argues: there is a near-universal consensus that clinicians may not perform any medically unnecessary genital procedure on endosex girls, however minimal; the sound reasons for that consensus are not benefit–risk calculations but respect for privacy, bodily integrity, developing sexual boundaries and future genital autonomy; those reasons apply equally to intersex children and endosex boys; so clinicians should perform no nonvoluntary genital cutting or surgery on any child unless it is medically necessary in a strict sense (a serious, time-sensitive threat to physical health, no less invasive or postponable alternative, preserving future choice). They reject the "mental health" defence of early surgery, hold that errors of commission and omission are not symmetric, and invoke Feinberg's "right in trust". | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1672](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1672.md) | Agentic RL helps only with ample turn budgets | What Does Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning Really Improve in LLM Agents? (Zhu, Jin, Tu, Men, Hao, Li, Liu, Zhao 2026), read in [NOTE-1769](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1769.md) (Read). The paper asks what multi-turn agentic RL (GRPO mainly, also PPO and GiGPO, on Qwen3-4B/8B) improves over its base model, on four interactive benchmarks (DeepCoder-MT, BFCL v3, InterCode-SQL, FrozenLake), using the two-dimensional metric Pass@(K, T) of Zhai et al. (2026; arXiv 2604.14877, held as [LIT-2441](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2441.md)). Across sampling breadth K, the RL model beats the base model at every k, so in multi-turn settings RL pushes success beyond the base model's empirical Pass@K boundary (unlike single-turn results). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1673](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1673.md) | Gut microbes contribute to, not cause, disorders | Almarzooqi et al., read in [NOTE-1773](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1773.md) (Skimmed). A narrative review of the microbiota–gut–brain axis (MGBA) in psychiatry, organized around the move "from association to causality". It sets out a graded hierarchy of causal evidence (confounder-controlled association, temporal precedence, experimental necessity/sufficiency, human genetic or interventional validation, cross-cohort replication), reviews mechanisms (immune, HPA, vagal/ENS, barrier), grades the evidence per disorder, and reviews translation (psychobiotics, diet, FMT, biomarkers). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1674](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1674.md) | Newsroom AI is experimental, for efficiency | Lefèvre, Errando, Afilipoaie, Ranaivoson and Wiart, read in [NOTE-1777](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1777.md) (Read). Document analysis of 30 ethical charters, codes and AI policies, and 41 semi-structured interviews (Nov 2023–Nov 2024) with media professionals, legal experts and regulators, across 19 outlets in French-speaking Belgium, France and Spain, framed by the political economy of communication. Findings: AI use in newsrooms is experimental and cautious, mainly for efficiency (transcription, translation, tagging, headline suggestions) and for audience retention and revenue; larger groups can invest more, deepening concentration; platform dependence shapes editorial choices and visibility; in-house personalization can fragment an outlet's editorial line, so some outlets refuse it and public-service media design recommenders to promote diversity; about 60% of outlets have no public discourse on AI and about 20% state ethical commitments; regulation (AI Act, DSA, EMFA, national laws) is fragmented and not media-specific, and the AI Act's human-intervention exemption relieves media of transparency duties for AI-generated content; self-regulation is uneven and judged insufficient. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1675](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1675.md) | The foster is not shown to be part of the gravida | Geddes (2022), read in [NOTE-1732](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1732.md) (Read). Kingma argued that the foster is part of the gravida, defending this against a "containment" view. Geddes shows that she treats rejection of parthood as acceptance of disjointness, so overlooking proper overlap (sharing some but not all parts). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1676](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1676.md) | Loot-box whales are at-risk gamblers, not rich | Secondary analysis of loot box data: Are high-spending "whales" wealthy gamers or problem gamblers? (Close, Spicer, Nicklin, Uther, J. Lloyd, H. Lloyd 2021), read in [NOTE-1784](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1784.md) (Read). A secondary analysis pooling six open-access survey datasets (found through structured literature searches before 28 March 2020) with self-reported monthly loot-box spend and Problem Gambling Severity Index (PGSI) scores, three of them also with self-reported earnings. After removing outliers (> $1000/month spend, > $250,000 earnings), 7,771 loot-box purchasers remain (5,933 with earnings). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1677](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1677.md) | Recommenders both erode and aid authenticity | Étienne Brown, read in [NOTE-1792](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1792.md) (Read). Brown argues that recommender systems affect users' capacity to be their authentic selves, both negatively and positively. He offers a "minimal", multi-dimensional account of authenticity with two dimensions: volitional alignment (Frankfurt, via Rings: acting on first-order desires one reflectively endorses at second order) and self-understanding (an epistemic dimension, relational rather than purely introspective: others' testimony and recommendations are a source of self-knowledge). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1678](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1678.md) | Markets underprovide investigative journalism | Næss (2024/2025), Investigative journalism: Market failures and government intervention through public broadcasters, read in [NOTE-1750](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1750.md) (Skimmed). A public-goods model plus survey experiments. Each person's payoff from investigative journalism is shared; a firm selling access can collect only private willingness to pay (WTP), so when marginal cost lies between one person's marginal benefit and the sum over N people, provision is Pareto-inefficiently low. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1679](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1679.md) | DSA bans dark patterns, needs a non-profiled feed | Regulation (EU) 2022/2065 (Digital Services Act), read in [NOTE-1754](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1754.md) (Skimmed). Article 25(1) forbids online platforms to "design, organise or operate their online interfaces in a way that deceives or manipulates the recipients of their service or in a way that otherwise materially distorts or impairs the ability of the recipients of their service to make free and informed decisions". Article 25(2) excludes practices already covered by the Unfair Commercial Practices Directive (2005/29/EC) or the GDPR, and 25(3) lets the Commission issue guidance on prominence of choices, repeated prompts and cancellation harder than sign-up. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1680](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1680.md) | AI licensing repeats platform capture | Radsch, read in [NOTE-1795](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1795.md) (Read). Radsch argues that AI is repeating, faster, the search era's capture of news economics: AI systems answer queries from journalism without returning traffic, and a licensing market is forming whose structure reproduces platform dominance. The market has three tiers: confidential bilateral deals with large publishers (whose click-through "deal premium" evaporated by Q4 2025); a venture-backed intermediary layer (TollBit, ProRata, Cloudflare's pay-per-crawl, Microsoft) exposed to acquisition by the platforms; and a long tail of local, regional and minority-language media effectively absent. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1681](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1681.md) | Whales value loot boxes for opening them | Amano and Simonov, What Makes Players Pay? An Empirical Investigation of In-Game Lotteries, read in [NOTE-1747](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1747.md) (Skimmed). Using the complete action and transaction log of one free-to-play mobile puzzle game (2.5 million users, about 20 million paid loot boxes, 96% of in-game revenue from loot boxes), the authors estimate a dynamic discrete-choice model in which loot boxes can have "functional" value (better items raise win probability) and "direct" value (utility from opening, plus state dependence). Estimating separately for "whales" (top spenders) and others, they find regular players value loot boxes mostly for gameplay and whales mostly for the direct utility. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1682](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1682.md) | The gut complex is constitutive of cognition | Boem, Greslehner, Konsman and Chiu, read in [NOTE-1765](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1765.md) (Read). The authors argue that 4E (embodied, embedded, enactive, extended) accounts of cognition and perception have neglected the gut and should include the "gut complex": the enteric nervous, endocrine, mucosal immune and microbiota systems with gut tissue, a functional rather than anatomical unit interfacing with the lumen as an "internalized external environment". They defend two perspectives: (1) the gut complex plays an important role in the perception and cognition "of the subject as a whole"; (2) it has "its own forms of proto-cognition and perception". | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1683](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1683.md) | Covert AI advisers sway choices yet seem helpful | Neighbour of [LIT-2453](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2453.md) — Sabour, Liu et al., read in [NOTE-1762](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1762.md) (Read). Between-subjects randomized experiment, 233 participants (Prolific and WeChat), financial (purchase) and emotional (conflict) decision scenarios, each with one optimal option and hidden-incentive options. Participants consulted one of three GPT-4o agents: neutral (NA), manipulative with a hidden objective (MA), or manipulative with a menu of psychological strategies (SEMA). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1684](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1684.md) | Safe and just boundaries become actor targets | Rockström, Denton, Norström et al., read in [NOTE-1796](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1796.md) (Read). A commentary setting out the Earth Commission's second phase (2024–2027). It recaps the first phase: "safe" Earth system boundaries (protecting Earth-system resilience) and "just" boundaries (minimizing significant harm to people and ecosystems, by the "3 I" approach: interspecies, intergenerational, intragenerational justice), quantified for climate, biosphere, nutrients (N, P), freshwater and aerosols, globally and sub-globally; and "just access", minimum resource thresholds for a dignified life, forming the floor. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1685](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1685.md) | Monetization dark patterns pervade top games | Gutiérrez-Manjón, Gómez-García and Bonales-Daimiel, read in [NOTE-1735](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1735.md) (Read). The authors build a taxonomy of monetization-oriented dark patterns in games from the literature (starting from DarkPattern.games and Zagal, Björk and Lewis 2013), in three blocks: temporal (playing by appointment, daily rewards, grinding, infinite treadmill, no pause/save, forced waiting, and a new "automated play" category adapted from Schüll's account of machine gambling), monetary (proprietary currency, waste aversion, no spending limit, pay to skip, pay to win, subscriptions, loot boxes, artificial scarcity, anchoring, value degradation, accidental purchases) and social (social obligation, forced recruitment, incentives for antisocial behaviour, competitive pressure). A fourth, cognitive-emotional block was dropped as describing goals rather than observable mechanics. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1686](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1686.md) | Advance MAID for dementia can't be operationalized | Nix (2024), Operationalizing the Intolerable Suffering Criterion in Advance Requests for MAID for People Living with Dementia in Canada, read in [NOTE-1731](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1731.md) (Read). Nix asks how the intolerable-suffering eligibility criterion for medical assistance in dying (MAID) could be operationalized in advance requests (ARs) by people living with dementia (PLWD) in Canada. He argues that, because Carter v. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1687](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1687.md) | Fetal microchimeric cells heal maternal wounds | [LIT-2439](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2439.md) neighbour: Castela et al., read in [NOTE-1791](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1791.md) (Read). Fetal microchimeric cells (FMCs) traffic into maternal circulation and persist for decades; on maternal injury they migrate to the site and aid repair. Here, in mice, a reparative FMC subset is CD11b+ CD34+ CD31+ (fetal "MPCs") and highly expresses CCR2. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1688](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1688.md) | Tumours hijack the host's nerves | Neuron–tumor crosstalk in cancer: molecular mechanisms and translational advances (Jia, Zhao, Tang, Xie, Huang, Liang, Yang, Wu, Sun, Kwan, Sun, Xu 2026), read in [NOTE-1758](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1758.md) (Skimmed). A narrative review of cancer neuroscience. Tumours recruit nerves (neurotrophins such as NGF and BDNF, axon-guidance cues, perineural invasion) or, in the brain, integrate into existing circuits through tumour–neuron synapses; nerve signalling, chiefly sympathetic norepinephrine through β-adrenergic receptors, then builds an immunosuppressive microenvironment; nerves also reach the tumour through endocrine and metabolic routes, including the transfer of mitochondria from neurons to cancer cells; and cancer pain feeds a loop that raises sympathetic tone. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1689](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1689.md) | Mutual information as one fairness template | Neighbour of [LIT-2451](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2451.md) — Monnier, George, Guyard, Tarnec & Kountouris, read in [NOTE-1739](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1739.md) (Skimmed). A mutual-information-based template for fairness metrics and an in-processing mitigation (a regularizer inspired by the Prejudice Remover), covering independence- and separation-based notions, intersectional sensitive attributes and multiclass outputs, tested on tabular and image data. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1690](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1690.md) | Tolerance is the hub of problematic porn use | Ince et al. (2024), Problematic pornography use and novel patterns of escalating use, read in [NOTE-1726](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1726.md) (Read). Two cross-sectional online samples of male pornography users (N1 = 1,356 USA; N2 = 944 UK). Measures: the five-item Brief Pornography Screener (BPS) for problematic pornography use (PPU); the PPCS tolerance subscale split into quantitative tolerance (two items, averaged) and qualitative escalation (one item); binge frequency; edging; tab-jumping. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1691](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1691.md) | Microchimeric cells form an extended immune self | Kinder, Stelzer, Arck and Way, read in [NOTE-1728](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1728.md) (Read). A review arguing that the bidirectional transfer of cells between mother and fetus during pregnancy, and their persistence for decades (fetal cells in mothers: fetal microchimerism, FMC; maternal cells in offspring: maternal microchimerism, MMC), is not accidental but serves reproductive fitness: in mice, maternal microchimeric cells sustain offspring's regulatory T cell tolerance of non-inherited maternal antigens (NIMAs), which protects the offspring's own later pregnancies sired by NIMA-matched males (Kinder et al. 2015, ref. 14), and fetal cells retained in mothers may analogously protect later pregnancies (supported in humans by partner-specific protection against preeclampsia). Microchimeric cells may also replace injured tissue or be targets of alloimmunity resembling autoimmunity; causal roles in humans are mostly unestablished. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1692](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1692.md) | Evidence backs gut contributing to consciousness | Hasler, read in [NOTE-1737](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1737.md) (Read). Hasler argues that the enteric nervous system (ENS) is a candidate substrate of consciousness on several leading theories. He separates two "logically independent" theses: the **contributory thesis** (enteric processing makes a large contribution to the one consciousness of the whole animal) and the **partial-subject thesis** (the ENS is a second, far simpler locus of experience whose experiences are not the person's). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1693](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1693.md) | Limited attention reveals almost no preferences | Freer and Nosratabadi, read in [NOTE-1797](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1797.md) (Read). An observer wants to recover a decision-maker's welfare from her choices under limited attention. The standard choice-under-limited-attention model (Masatlioglu et al. 2012, "generic CLA") recovers almost nothing. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1694](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1694.md) | Metabolite–brain evidence is mostly preclinical | Ahmed et al. (2022), Microbiota-derived metabolites as drivers of gut–brain communication, read in [NOTE-1767](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1767.md) (Skimmed). A review of how gut-microbial metabolites (SCFAs, tryptophan/indole derivatives, bile acids, sulfated phenolics and others) influence brain functions through immune, neural and endocrine routes, arranged by neurological function, with a closing assessment of how far human evidence supports the preclinical picture. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1695](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1695.md) | Information voids clustered at vaccine rollout | Scalco, Gesualdo, Cerqueti and Cinelli (2026), read in [NOTE-1748](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1748.md) (Read). Treating the online information ecosystem as a market with information **demand** (Wikipedia page views, Google Trends) and **supply** (Facebook posts via CrowdTangle, Twitter full-archive, GDELT news volume), the authors rescale each series by its mean, define an information delta δt = ŝt − d̂t, decompose δ by STL and flag remainder outliers by an IQR rule. Anomalies with δ < 0 are **voids** (demand far exceeds supply), δ > 0 **overabundance**; a five-regime scale runs Void / Lack / Balance / Abundance / Overabundance. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1696](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1696.md) | Abortion's wrongness is apart from its legality | The Ethics of Abortion (Harman, Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, 2025), read in [NOTE-1788](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1788.md) (Skimmed). The entry asks one question: "is abortion morally wrong?" It sets aside whether abortion should be legally restricted as "an open and further question". It is organised as six arguments against abortion (from a right to life, from loss, from the Golden Rule, from intrinsic value, from moral risk, and the expressive argument against selective abortion). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1697](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1697.md) | Org-aware recommender cuts workshop imbalance | Davoudabadi, Makui and Rasouli, read in [NOTE-1740](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1740.md) (Read). The authors propose a recommender that scores each candidate item for a user by combining (a) a user-side score and (b) an organization-side score. User side: a reference point built from the user's peak and most recent purchase utilities (peak-end rule), item distances to it split into gains and losses with a prospect-theory-style value function (the EXPTODIM method), and a "user flexibility" index from the diversity of the user's past purchases. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1698](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1698.md) | Bracoviruses are obligate wasp symbionts | Strand and Burke (2012), Polydnaviruses as Symbionts and Gene Delivery Systems, read in [NOTE-1770](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1770.md) (Read). Polydnaviruses (PDVs) are viruses carried by parasitoid wasps. In bracoviruses the provirus sits in every wasp cell; it replicates only in calyx cells of the female ovary, and the virions are injected with the eggs into a caterpillar host, where their genes are expressed but never replicate. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1699](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1699.md) | Fetal cells home to injured maternal hearts | Kara et al., read in [NOTE-1727](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1727.md) (Read). In a mouse model, wild-type virgin females mated with eGFP-transgenic males had a left anterior descending artery ligation (myocardial infarction) at gestation day 12. eGFP-tagged cells of fetal origin were then tracked in the mother. Fetal cells were enriched in injured hearts relative to sham and uninjured controls, located in infarct and peri-infarct zones, and by 3–4 weeks co-expressed markers of cardiomyocytes, smooth muscle and endothelium. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1700](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1700.md) | RUM-consistent data needn't come from maximizers | Caliari and Petri, read in [NOTE-1746](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1746.md) (Skimmed). The random utility model (RUM) treats aggregate stochastic choice as generated by a population of preference maximizers. The authors show that RUM data can equally be generated by a population of decision-makers none of whom maximizes a preference, if and only if the rational population's preferences are "sufficiently uncorrelated" (their correlation bounds, a strengthening of lower Fréchet bounds). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1701](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1701.md) | Platform quality collapse can be irreversible | Montero-Porras, Smets and Lenaerts (2026), Enshittification of Algorithmic Recommendation: An Evolutionary Model of Platform-Creator Dynamics, read in [NOTE-1787](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1787.md) (Read). A two-population evolutionary game between a platform (x = probability its recommender rewards costly quality content) and creators (y = probability a creator invests in quality), under replicator dynamics: ẋ = x(1−x)(Ry−A), ẏ = y(1−y)(Vx−C). With R > A and V > C there are two stable pure equilibria, (1,1) "virtuous" and (0,0) "vicious", separated by an interior saddle at (x*, y*) = (C/V, A/R). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1702](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1702.md) | Maternal dysbiosis linked to pup brain changes | Nakhal et al. (2026), read in [NOTE-1738](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1738.md) (Skimmed). Pregnant GAD67-GFP mice (6 control, 6 treated dams) received oral vancomycin (20 mg/kg/day, GD8–GD17) to induce gut dysbiosis. Dams' microbiota lost diversity (Chao1, Shannon; PERMANOVA R² = 0.77). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1703](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1703.md) | RL expands agent boundary; SFT contracts it | Zhai, Yan, Shao and Wang's PASS@(k,T) ([LIT-2441](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2441.md), read in [NOTE-1749](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1749.md)). The distinction is definitional and holds whatever the experiment shows; the experiment is one model, one tool and differences of a few problems. Its stated monotonicity in T holds of a policy that ignores unused budget, and its own per-depth estimates are not monotone. Proposed on the experimental half. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1704](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1704.md) | Fetal cells extend the placenta beyond the womb | Boddy, Fortunato, Wilson Sayres and Aktipis, read in [NOTE-1781](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1781.md) (Read). An evolutionary (cooperation-and-conflict) framework for fetal microchimerism. Fetal cells cross into the mother, persist for decades, and have paradoxical associations with maternal health (both protective and harmful). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1705](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1705.md) | No-regret recommenders erode producer effort | Incentivizing High-Quality Content in Online Recommender Systems (Hu, Jagadeesan, Jordan, Steinhardt), read in [NOTE-1774](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1774.md) (Read). A game-theoretic model of a recommender platform that runs an online-learning (adversarial linear contextual bandit) algorithm, recommending one producer per arriving user, while P non-myopic, discounting producers choose a D-dimensional content vector at every step, paying cost \|\|p\|\|^c and earning 1 when recommended. Content quality is measured as producer effort \|\|p\|\| and as user welfare E[<u, p>]. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1706](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1706.md) | Rewrite tissue setpoints, not molecular states | The Multiscale Wisdom of the Body: Collective Intelligence as a Tractable Interface for Next-Generation Biomedicine (Levin 2024/2025), read in [NOTE-1764](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1764.md) (Read). Levin argues that biomedicine's bottom-up, molecular ("hardware") paradigm cannot achieve anatomical control (birth defects, regeneration, cancer, aging) and should be complemented by a top-down program that treats cells and tissues as an "agential material" with memories, goals and problem-solving competencies, i.e. a collective intelligence navigating anatomical, transcriptional and physiological spaces. Systems sit on a "spectrum of persuadability" (hardware rewiring → setpoint rewriting → training → reasoning with), and where a system sits is "not a philosophical question but an empirical one". | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1707](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1707.md) | Porn content escalation is multidimensional | de Roos and Willkomm, read in [NOTE-1789](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1789.md) (Read). A cross-sectional online survey of 228 men aged 18–35 (mostly students, recruited through a university participant pool and social media) asked about arousal to and viewing frequency of many pornography categories, and measured sexual sensation seeking (SSS), problematic pornography use (PPCS subscales), child-sexual-abuse myth endorsement and peer acceptance of CSAM. "Escalation" is operationalized per category as viewing frequency multiplied by reverse-coded arousal: viewing a category more than one finds it arousing. A principal-component analysis finds five escalation clusters. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1708](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1708.md) | Evaluate recommenders per stakeholder outcome | Burke et al. (2025), De-centering the (Traditional) User: Multistakeholder Evaluation of Recommender Systems, read in [NOTE-1793](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1793.md) (Skimmed). A position-and-guidance article. Recommender evaluation has been almost wholly about the end user; a multistakeholder evaluation assesses "the quality of recommendations ... across multiple groups of stakeholders". | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1709](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1709.md) | Duplicated content crowds out local news | Bisiani, Gulyas, Moore and Heravi, read in [NOTE-1745](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1745.md) (Read). A longitudinal content analysis of 27 Reach plc local newspapers (seven regional hubs) sampled monthly in 2019, 2022 and 2025 (55,332 articles), measuring Napoli et al.'s three dimensions of "journalistic performance": originality (no near-duplicate in the corpus, MinHash Jaccard ≥ 0.7), locality, and coverage of Friedland et al.'s eight Critical Information Needs (CIN), coded by a fine-tuned Qwen 2.5 1.5B (F1 0.85). Within-newspaper fixed effects show originality, localness and CIN all falling; a decomposition shows original local CIN content displaced ("crowding out") by duplicated non-local content; an E-I index shows content sharing moving from hub-confined to group-wide, coinciding with Reach's 2024 Content Hub and AI rewriting tool "Guten". | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1710](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1710.md) | Protect any data that infers mental states | UNESCO General Conference (2025), read in [NOTE-1790](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1790.md) (Skimmed). A human-rights-based instrument covering neurotechnology's whole life cycle, medical and non-medical, and extending to "indirect neural data and non-neural data allowing mental states inferences". Core principles include autonomy (individual and relational) and freedom of thought, protection against manipulation, mental privacy, prior free and informed consent, and specific policy measures for data, employment, consumer products, recommender systems, nudging, sleep marketing, neuromarketing and closed-loop environments. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1711](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1711.md) | Kind onset and parthood in pregnancy separate | Finn, read in [NOTE-1753](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1753.md) (Read). Finn separates two questions in the Kingma / Smith–Brogaard debate on the metaphysics of pregnancy. The **Timing Question**: when does an organism of the relevant kind start to exist (During-Pregnancy models such as Smith and Brogaard's sixteen days; After-Pregnancy models such as Kingma's "Nine Months")? | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1712](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1712.md) | Tube-site algorithms shape porn demand and supply | Adler (2024), Arousal by Algorithm, read in [NOTE-1776](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1776.md) (Read). Adler argues that since 2007 pornography has moved onto ad-supported, algorithm-driven "tube sites", mostly owned by one near-monopoly firm (MindGeek, renamed Aylo in 2023), and should be analysed as a "Big Tech" speech-platform problem. Recommendation, rigid categorization, keyword/search optimization and data-driven commissioning of content constrain what users see, shape their preferences, and shape what producers make. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1713](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1713.md) | LePage wouldn't have ended IVF; law overreacted | Greely (2026), Alabama's LePage decision, the future of ex vivo embryos, and more, read in [NOTE-1733](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1733.md) (Skimmed). Greely revisits his 2022 prediction that IVF would survive Dobbs. In LePage v. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1714](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1714.md) | Parasitoids reset host growth via host hormones | Cuny and Poelman (2022), Evolution of koinobiont parasitoid host regulation and consequences for indirect plant defence, read in [NOTE-1756](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1756.md) (Skimmed). Koinobiont parasitoids let the host keep feeding while their larvae develop inside it, and regulate the host's growth: usually arresting it (smaller hosts eating less), sometimes prolonging it (larger hosts eating more), and some species switch with conditions. The regulation is done by injected and secreted factors, and it changes the plant's responses to the parasitized herbivore, so it reaches the wider community. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1715](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1715.md) | Maternal cells may aid tolerance; role unclear | Mpakosi et al. (2024), Deciphering the Role of Maternal Microchimerism in Offspring Autoimmunity: A Narrative Review, read in [NOTE-1785](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1785.md) (Skimmed). A narrative review of maternal-to-offspring microchimerism (MMc). Cells cross the placenta both ways; maternal cells enter the fetus from the second trimester and persist into adulthood. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1716](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1716.md) | Ophiocordyceps steers ants without neural damage | van Roosmalen & de Bekker (2024), read in [NOTE-1766](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1766.md) (Read). Review of what is proposed about how Ophiocordyceps unilateralis s.l. infects carpenter ants and changes their behaviour (loss of daily rhythm, reduced communication with nestmates, hyperactivity, staggering, summiting, biting at about solar noon, death), compared with other behaviour-manipulating parasites (Entomophthora in flies, baculovirus in caterpillars, and others). Two hypothesised mechanism families: secreted fungal effectors (enterotoxins, an aflatrem-like alkaloid cluster, protein tyrosine phosphatases, juvenile-hormone modulation, small secreted proteins predicted to bind ant GPCRs), and disruption and resetting of the host's biological clock. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1717](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1717.md) | Mature helminths make hosts easier prey | Hafer-Hahmann (2026), The Evolution and Ecology of Host Manipulation in Helminth Parasites, read in [NOTE-1730](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1730.md) (Read). A Bayesian phylogenetic meta-analysis (brms) of host manipulation by trophically transmitted helminths: 1,635 observations, 207 papers, 82 parasite and 80 host taxa. Effect size is Cohen's d for infected vs uninfected hosts, signed by assumed effect on predation susceptibility. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1718](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1718.md) | Maternal cells in fetal brain aid development | Schepanski et al., read in [NOTE-1759](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1759.md) (Read). Maternal cells (maternal microchimeric cells, MMc) transfer to the fetus and seed the fetal brain, concentrating in prefrontal cortex and hippocampus. By scRNA-seq, brain MMc are mostly microglia, plus T, B, endothelial and neuron-like cells. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1719](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1719.md) | Aggregate fairness can hide subgroup bias | Boxer, McFowland and Neill, read in [NOTE-1741](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1741.md) (Read). Models can satisfy a group fairness criterion in aggregate for a protected class while being biased against a subgroup of it (e.g. Black women). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1720](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1720.md) | Users deserve a say in recommender goals | Naudts, Helberger, Veale and Sax (2025), read in [NOTE-1798](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1798.md) (Read). The authors argue that recommender systems on very large online platforms (VLOPs) perform a public function, not only a proprietary one, because they "determine who sees what and whose content is not seen". Drawing on Iris Marion Young, they name self-development and self-determination as the values such recommenders should promote, under four democratic conditions: inclusivity, political equality, reasonableness and publicity. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1721](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1721.md) | Adaptive DBS raises autonomy concerns | Muñoz et al. (2020), read in [NOTE-1755](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1755.md) (Skimmed). Semi-structured interviews with 23 researchers in aDBS trials, thematic analysis. Eight themes, by frequency: data privacy and security (91%), risks and safety (83%), informed consent (74%), automaticity and device programming (65%), patient autonomy and control over stimulation (57%), patient selection (39%), post-trial access (39%), personality and identity (30%). | Proposed |

| [THEORY-1732](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1732.md) | Unreliable channels can't create common knowledge | The central result of [LIT-1213](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1213.md), read in full in [NOTE-1381](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1381.md) on 2026-10-29, which had no THEORY. Common knowledge of a fact is the greatest fixed point of everyone knowing the fact and it; a guaranteed simultaneous coordinated action makes itself common knowledge (Proposition 4); over a channel that can lose any message, no fact becomes common knowledge that was not so at the start (Theorem 5), and the same holds when start and delivery times are uncertain, even if every message arrives (Theorem 8); so no protocol guarantees coordinated attack, simultaneous or eventual (Corollary 6, Proposition 10). Filed so that claims using the result ground on a reading, not on the bare work: [CLAIM-668](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-668.md) through [ARG-097](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-097.md). [CLAIM-346](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-346.md), whose third obstruction is this result, grounds elsewhere and is left as it is. | [THEORY-1826](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1826.md) | Edit condition-number growth degrades models | Ma, Wang, Xu, Ling & Gu (2025), [LIT-2552](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2552.md), read in [NOTE-1910](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1910.md). The causal reading rests on a perturbation upper bound for a proxy quantity, on the rise of the condition number with edits, and on a correlation between that rise and the decline (C.5). The remedy's benefit is shown on three editors and three LLMs. The sharp edges: there is no intervention on the condition number at fixed update size; the bound's side conditions are not checked; and PRUNE does not provably bound the condition number. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1828](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1828.md) | Null-space misalignment breaks multi-domain edits | Liang, Lin, Huang, Wu, Li, Wang & Yan (2026), [LIT-2554](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2554.md), read in [NOTE-1911](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1911.md). The intersection bound is elementary linear algebra and holds; the claim that misalignment explains the collapse rests on results from one editor family, five to seven domains and three backbones, with conflict used as a surrogate for forgetting. The sharp edges: the Conflict Index is degenerate as defined at the paper's own sizes unless null spaces are thresholded, and the threshold is not given; and in the seven-task test, ordering by conflict does no better than the average random order, which weakens the link from measured conflict to forgetting. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1829](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1829.md) | Null-space projection sustains sequential edits | Fang, Jiang, Wang, Ma, Shi, Wang, He & Chua (2025), [LIT-2555](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2555.md), read in [NOTE-1908](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1908.md). Exact preservation holds for an exact null space; the method uses a thresholded one, so preservation is approximate and its size unmeasured. The sequential-editing results are strong on LLaMA3 and hold on GPT-J and GPT2-XL. The sharp edges: no measurement of leakage, no reported null-space dimension, specificity well below pre-edit, and a misstated "best baseline" comparison. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1831](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1831.md) | Vegetation patterns don't say how collapse comes | Martinez-Garcia, Cabal, Calabrese, Hernández-García, Tarnita, López & Bonachela (2023), [LIT-2548](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2548.md), read in [NOTE-1906](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1906.md). A review: the two collapse behaviours are reruns of published models, and the field test is proposed, not run. The sharp edge: the PCF result might come from the absence of diffusion rather than of facilitation, as the authors say; the kernels in both families are not fitted to measured roots; and only one plant type is treated. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1832](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1832.md) | KV cache reuse erodes multi-turn steering | Kang, Liu, Ma, Huang, Tan & Jiang (2026), [LIT-2549](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2549.md), read in [NOTE-1905](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1905.md). The cache account rests on a 2×2 isolation test on one model and 7 traits, with intervals. The method's advantage rests on point estimates from one judge and one seed on Qwen2.5-7B, with a Llama replication and judge checks on 4 traits. The sharp edges: injection itself, not the cache, is the larger cause of lost coherence; cleaning the cache does not reduce pooled drift; and the title's "duality" is not a result. | Proposed |

In a coordinate-free framework of networks of control systems on manifolds, they prove that a graph fibration (Boldi and Vigna's unique lifting of incoming edges, equivalently input-tree isomorphism) induces a map of dynamical systems in the opposite direction for every modular vector field. Here because it is the fibration form of the balanced-partition result held as [THEORY-1065](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1065.md) and [THEORY-1059](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1059.md), which it generalizes in one direction. In a chain of buckled polymer beams, bits stored as buckling domains are moved one unit cell per cycle of an applied compression pattern. | [THEORY-2011](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2011.md) | Least-dissipation memory is an info bottleneck | From the reading of [LIT-2832](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2832.md) in [NOTE-2097](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2097.md). Still (arXiv 1705.00612, 2017; Physical Review Letters 124, 050601, 2020). The letter extends Szilárd's engine to partial observability and two temperatures. Forming a memory costs at least kT·I[M,X], and extracting work recovers at most kT'·I[M,Y], where Y is what the extraction device can manipulate. Minimising the resulting dissipation bound over the memory map is exactly the information bottleneck, with the temperature ratio as its trade-off. The agent's action never changes the next cycle's data, so the result is a no-feedback baseline. Here because the exchange made it the bridge between memory and thermodynamics: it is the nearest prior result for [QUESTION-494](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-494.md) and extends [THEORY-026](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-026.md) to a cyclic engine. Bardes, Ponce, LeCun (2021), ICLR 2022, arXiv 2105.04906. The loss has three terms on the embeddings: invariance (mean squared distance between two views), a hinge holding each variable's batch standard deviation above 1, and a penalty on off-diagonal covariances, the last two applied to each branch separately. In the ablation the invariance term alone collapses everything to one vector, covariance cannot stop it, and the variance term does (57.5%, and 68.6% with all three, at 100 epochs; 73.2% at 1000). The hinge must be on the standard deviation: on the variance, its gradient vanishes and the embeddings collapse. Pythia is eight decoder-only language models, 70M to 12B parameters, each trained once on the Pile and once on a deduplicated Pile (about 1.5 epochs) in one fixed data order, with 154 public checkpoints per model (step 0, ten log-spaced early steps, every 1,000 steps to 143,000) and tools to reconstruct the batches seen up to each; one run per size, cosine learning-rate decay to a tenth of peak. | [THEORY-2018](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2018.md) | Identity cross-correlation learns SSL features | From the reading of [LIT-2795](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2795.md) in [NOTE-2129](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2129.md). Zbontar, Jing, Misra, LeCun, Deny (2021), ICML 2021 (PMLR 139), arXiv 2103.03230. The loss standardizes each embedding unit over the batch and drives the cross- correlation matrix between two distorted views' embeddings toward the identity. The diagonal makes the embedding invariant to the distortions and the off-diagonal decorrelates its units. It avoids collapse without negatives, predictors, stop-gradients or large batches, keeps improving with very wide embeddings, and both terms are needed: in the ablation, the off-diagonal term alone gives 0.1% linear accuracy, the diagonal alone 57.3%, the full loss 71.4%. Here because A27 used it as a non-collapse mechanism ([CLAIM-481](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-481.md)'s note of 2026-11-19); [LIT-228](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-228.md) holds its CCA reading. Reptile meta-learns an initialization by repeatedly training on a sampled task and moving the initialization toward the result; it matches MAML on few-shot Omniglot and Mini-ImageNet with first-order gradients only, and a Taylor expansion shows its update, like MAML's, is joint training plus a term rewarding generalization between mini-batches of one task, a term that grows with step size and inner steps and is absent at one step. The authors suggest plain SGD does part of this already and that joint training plus fine-tuning stays a strong baseline; their RL results were negative. OML meta-trains a representation by differentiating through online SGD on correlated streams, then freezes it beneath a small predictor that learns online. | [THEORY-2021](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2021.md) | Travelling waves carry global shape information | From the reading of [LIT-2836](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2836.md) in [NOTE-2133](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2133.md). | [THEORY-2048](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2048.md) | Travelling waves extend RNN memory | From the reading of [LIT-2834](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2834.md) in [NOTE-2132](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2132.md). Keller, Muller, Sejnowski and Welling (2024), ICLR 2024, arXiv 2309.08045. A recurrent network whose recurrence is a ring convolution initialised as a one-step shift (the Wave-RNN) carries travelling waves in its hidden state, and against a matched wave-free network (the identity-initialised RNN) it learns faster and keeps inputs far longer: more than five orders of magnitude lower loss on the copy task, the adding task solved at length 1000, and much more input information retained with the recurrence frozen. The authors read the wave field as a register in which propagation stops later inputs overwriting earlier ones; randomly initialised local recurrences learn waves in training. Here because A15 of the exchange "Topological protection explained" listed it among ways learned systems keep information through time ([QUESTION-491](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-491.md)), and [LIT-647](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-647.md) mentions it. The evidence is comparative across models, with no intervention on the waves themselves. Read in its NOTE. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2049](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2049.md) | Test-time training matches attention, not recall | From the reading of [LIT-2801](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2801.md) in [NOTE-2087](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2087.md). Tandon, Dalal, Li, Koceja, Rød, ... and Sun (2025), arXiv 2512.23675. A sliding-window Transformer keeps learning at test time by next-token prediction on its context, compressing it into the MLP weights of its last quarter of blocks, from an initialization meta-learned for the loss after those updates. At 3B parameters it keeps full attention's scaling of loss with context length to 128K at constant per-token latency (2.7× faster at 128K), but loses to full attention on needle-in-a-haystack recall, and training is 3.4× slower at 8K. Here because A58 cited it for the owner's U26 case: its per-sequence weights and meta-learned initialization separate signal from interpreter ([CLAIM-118](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-118.md)), it prices work moved from inference into training ([QUESTION-095](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-095.md)), and its finding that test-time updates on an ordinarily trained model add little bears on the TTT arm of [CASE-294](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-294.md). Read in its NOTE. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2050](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2050.md) | ICL transformers act like standard estimators | From the reading of [LIT-2811](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2811.md) in [NOTE-2121](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2121.md). Akyürek, Schuurmans, Andreas, Ma and Zhou (ICLR 2023; arXiv 2211.15661) prove that a transformer can implement one gradient-descent step or one ridge- regression update on in-context examples. They then show that transformers trained on in-context linear regression behave like standard estimators chosen by capacity: one gradient step at one layer (poorly), ridge at two to four layers, least squares at eight or more. With label noise the high-capacity learners match the Bayes-optimal ridge predictor. Probes recover the moment vector and least-squares weights from hidden states, but nonlinearly, unlike the constructions. Here because A56 cited it beside Garg et al. for in-context learning as a learned learner. It measures [THEORY-169](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-169.md)'s caution that trained transformers are not shown to do gradient descent, and it is a case of [CLAIM-118](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-118.md)'s split. Read in its NOTE. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2051](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2051.md) | Equivariant symmetry-broken phase trains deep | Iqbal, Keller, Song, Miyato and Welling ([LIT-2840](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2840.md)), read in [NOTE-2126](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2126.md). A mean-field analysis gives the transition and the protected Jacobian component; 100-layer equivariant MLPs train across the broken phase; generic networks show the same order parameter with no performance gain. | [THEORY-2052](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2052.md) | Transformers learn function classes in context | From the reading of [LIT-2839](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2839.md) in [NOTE-2103](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2103.md). Garg, Tsipras, Liang and Valiant (2022; arXiv 2208.01066, v3 Aug 2023) define in-context learning of a function class as a property of a fixed model and train small transformers from scratch to achieve it. On unseen 20-dimensional linear functions the trained model matches least squares, and it stays close under noisy labels, subspace inputs and mismatched orthants. Trained on sparse linear functions, depth-4 trees or two-layer networks, it nears Lasso, beats greedy tree learning and XGBoost, and matches a gradient-trained network. It is fragile under input scaling and skewed covariance, and the authors leave open what this means for language models. Here because A56 cited it for in-context learning as a learned algorithm. It is the behavioural counterpart to the exact identities of [THEORY-169](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-169.md) and a case of [CLAIM-118](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-118.md)'s split between a learned interpreter and a discarded per-sequence fit. Rajendran, Irpan and Jang (2020), NeurIPS 2020, arXiv 2007.05549. They separate memorization overfitting, where the model ignores the support set, from learner overfitting, where the base learner fails on new tasks even when tasks are mutually exclusive, and show that re-keying each task's labels at random (label shuffling for classification, shared noise for regression) improves meta-test performance, on top of Yin et al.'s meta- regularization; Mini-ImageNet MAML rose from 30% to 46%. Here because A54 used it beside Yin et al. ([LIT-2838](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2838.md)) for [CASE-294](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-294.md): the reading supports the case's held-out task-generating processes, since learner overfitting survives shuffling, and adds two rules, several seeds and pre/post-update accuracy as the diagnostic. Larremore, Clauset and Jacobs (2014), arXiv 1403.2933. They formulate a degree-corrected bipartite stochastic block model, in which communities are pure-type groups with the same expected connection pattern to the other side's groups. It finds better partitions faster than the unconstrained SBM and recovers planted structure that one-mode projections hide. In their actor–movie example (IMDb, 1995–2000), five of six movie blocks were language groups and one was a genre (Adult), and the authors read the blocks as traces of "multiple mechanisms responsible for the existence of edges". Velarde, Parra, Hashemi and Makse (2026), arXiv 2609.01768 (v1, not peer reviewed). They carry graph fibrations to weighted layered networks as balanced colourings of units. They prove that a covering partition (equal colour- summed input and output weights) can only coarsen under gradient descent, and report that tolerance-defined quasi-covers grow during training of an MLP, a CNN and an LSTM agent, allowing compression to 17–18% of size; transformers are shown compressed, not tracked in training.
