| [THEORY-2158](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2158.md) | Reservoir capacity sums to at most N | Dambre, Verstraeten, Schrauwen and Massar (2012), [LIT-2971](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2971.md), read in [NOTE-2244](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2244.md) with the supplement. The bound needs only i.i.d. input, a linear readout and infinite data; fading memory and full rank are the conditions for equality; unobserved noise is a further input and takes part of the total. The record uses it for [CLAIM-809](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-809.md)'s bound ([ARG-128](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-128.md)) and [CLAIM-814](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-814.md), which is an instance of Theorem 7 ([ARG-146](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-146.md)). Its edge is the undriven system's stability edge, and its sweep is input scaling. Proposed until the theorems are confirmed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2159](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2159.md) | Concept directions avoid top unembedding modes | Acharya, Rimal and Dhakal, [LIT-2959](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2959.md), read in [NOTE-2251](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2251.md). Where concept vectors point in the logit metric's eigenbasis, from the activation side and the vocabulary side. A placement of directions, not a measure of information or of importance; the paper's own effect measures run with the metric. Its sign flip is what Park, Choe and Veitch's map predicts ([CLAIM-852](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-852.md)). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2160](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2160.md) | LLC plateaus divide training into stages | Hoogland, Wang, Farrugia-Roberts, Carroll, Wei and Murfet, [LIT-2966](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2966.md), read in [NOTE-2248](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2248.md). Stages of transformer training read off pauses in the local learning coefficient, matched to behavioural and structural changes. Motivated by Bayesian singular learning, not derived from it; the coefficient's decreases are unexplained; the estimator is run at one fixed nβ and γ per setting. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2161](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2161.md) | SGD's top-Hessian component doesn't train | Song, Ahn and Yun, [LIT-2973](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2973.md), read in [NOTE-2250](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2250.md). Gradient alignment with the dominant Hessian subspace is not where training happens: the loss falls along a steep valley's flat floor, in the complement of the top k. A weak instance of a model's rankings of directions disagreeing ([CLAIM-835](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-835.md)), within one metric. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2162](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2162.md) | Low-amplified directions sway predictions most | Xu, [LIT-2967](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2967.md), read in [NOTE-2249](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2249.md). The logit metric WᵀW and the predictive Fisher pulled back to the final state disagree most along the unembedding's least-amplified directions, per unit of logit distance and against equal-length random changes; not a reversal, since the top band matters as much in total. The record's best evidence that [CLAIM-835](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-835.md)'s disagreement occurs in trained models. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2163](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2163.md) | Fisher singularities cause learning plateaus | Amari, Park and Ozeki (2006), [LIT-2960](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2960.md), read in [NOTE-2255](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2255.md). Where network singularities are and what they do to learning: critical sets at finite parameters, cone apices in the space of distributions, a Milnor attractor for gradient flow, a slow manifold that makes the plateau, and repulsion under natural gradient. With the truth at the singularity, the gradient along the degenerate direction is cubic (Eq. 5.13), so the approach is algebraic, u ∝ t^(−1/2) (the reader's derivation; the paper states no rate). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2164](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2164.md) | Overlap singularities are Milnor-like attractors | Wei, Zhang, Cousseau, Ozeki and Amari (2008), [LIT-3000](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3000.md), read in [NOTE-2254](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2254.md). Orbits, not time courses: a conserved quantity of the averaged flow fixes where learning goes near coinciding units, and the long plateau on the singularity is a noise-driven walk along a line of equivalent models, not a slow decay along a degenerate direction. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2165](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2165.md) | Sloppy spectra span decades in 17 bio models | Gutenkunst, Waterfall, Casey, Brown, Myers and Sethna (2007), [LIT-2999](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2999.md), read in [NOTE-2252](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2252.md). The empirical base of sloppiness: a two-part criterion (even spread over many decades, and skew from the bare axes), shown across a collection, and the argument that collective fits beat direct measurement for predictions, shown in one model. Across the collection the resolved span stays at 5–10 decades while the density of eigenvalues per decade grows with the number of parameters (the reader's computation from Dataset S1, recomputed by the filer). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2166](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2166.md) | Geodesics to manifold edges reduce sloppy models | Transtrum and Qiu (2014), [LIT-2979](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2979.md), read in [NOTE-2253](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2253.md). The manifold boundary approximation turns the hyper-ribbon into a reduction algorithm: boundaries are where a parameter combination reaches a limit (0, ∞, or two terms merging), the reduced model is a hypercorner, and the method requires nested edges and corners, which an ellipsoid with a hierarchy of widths lacks. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2167](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2167.md) | Hyperribbon ubiquity is empirical, not proven | The 2023 review of the sloppy-model programme, [LIT-2958](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2958.md), read in [NOTE-2256](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2256.md). Its sharp edges: "sloppy" needs widths as well as eigenvalues to be hierarchical; ΛCDM is sloppy and yet fully determined, because sloppiness is low-dimensional only against a demanded precision; the rigorous bound is for smooth least-squares models, restated from the 2019 paper ([LIT-3029](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3029.md), Deferred); and the review offers no single account of why simple effective theories exist. It grounds [CLAIM-820](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-820.md) ([ARG-164](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-164.md)) and is drawn on by [TERM-135](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-135.md) and [TERM-140](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-140.md). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2168](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2168.md) | Integration time moves optimum off criticality | Azizpour and colleagues, [LIT-2980](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2980.md), read in [NOTE-2259](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2259.md). "Criticality maximizes dynamic range" (Kinouchi and Copelli, [LIT-3027](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3027.md)) becomes "only for infinite integration time": every finite readout window has a subcritical optimum, different for the two measures. One transition (branching), one task family (discriminating stationary input rates); the paper itself says the side of the optimum depends on the task and the transition. Grounds [CLAIM-809](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-809.md)'s window- and task-dependence ([ARG-163](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-163.md)). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2169](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2169.md) | Fit power laws by MLE, not log-log regression | Newman (2005), [LIT-2976](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2976.md), read in [NOTE-2261](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2261.md). A tutorial review: its results are mostly other people's, with heuristic derivations the author flags. What the record uses is the catalogue of mechanisms with their exponents, which grounds items 2, 3, 6 and 7 of [CLAIM-795](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-795.md) and adds four mechanisms with no feedback (random typing, highly optimized tolerance, coherent noise, record dynamics), and its judgement that most observed power laws are probably not from phase transitions. It has no model comparison, and it calls the Yule process the most widely accepted theory for citations, cities and income. Proposed until the reading is confirmed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2170](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2170.md) | One update step leaves a spiked weight bulk | Dandi and colleagues, [LIT-2983](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2983.md), read in [NOTE-2258](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2258.md). The spike of one large gradient step is in the weights; in the features, learning shows chiefly as a reshaped bulk, with outliers from the means. Grounds [CLAIM-799](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-799.md)'s narrow point that the spiked picture of learned features is a theorem, and qualifies it ([ARG-166](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-166.md)). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2171](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2171.md) | Teacher spike detaches by a BBP transition | Park and colleagues, [LIT-2990](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2990.md), read in [NOTE-2260](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2260.md). A dynamical reading of the BBP transition: the outlier's appearance in the weight spectrum is a matter of step size and time, while the signal is in the weights from the first step. Its UTKFace experiments find the leading first-layer directions tracking the data's principal components only in the large-step regime. Grounds [CLAIM-799](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-799.md) ([ARG-171](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-171.md)) and the rival reading [CLAIM-855](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-855.md) ([ARG-174](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-174.md)). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2172](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2172.md) | Power-law degrees are rare in real networks | Broido & Clauset (2019), [LIT-2963](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2963.md), read in [NOTE-2263](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2263.md). The record's network-scale evidence that a power-law shape is weak evidence of mechanism, and a ground of [CLAIM-803](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-803.md). Its test is of a pure power law above k_min; the verdict is disputed by Voitalov and others ([LIT-3041](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3041.md), unread), who define a power law as a regularly varying tail, [TERM-142](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-142.md)'s sense 1. Proposed until the reading is confirmed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2173](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2173.md) | Log-log lines don't establish power laws | Clauset, Shalizi & Newman (2009), [LIT-2987](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2987.md), read in [NOTE-2262](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2262.md). The record's standard for fitting a tail, and the ground of [CLAIM-803](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-803.md)'s "fit first" clause. Its empirical lesson is that a power law and a lognormal are seldom distinguishable at realistic sample sizes (US city sizes among the undecided), and it defers the choice to mechanism without supplying dynamical tests. Proposed until the reading is confirmed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2174](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2174.md) | V1 eigenspectrum follows a 1/n power law | Stringer and colleagues, [LIT-2972](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2972.md), read in [NOTE-2257](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2257.md). V1's code of natural images sits just on the smooth side of the critical exponent 1 + 2/d: a spectrum decaying more slowly would put so much variance in fine directions that the code would stop being differentiable. The bound is strict and asymptotic in rank. It grounds [CLAIM-848](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-848.md)'s premise in that corrected form ([ARG-169](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-169.md)). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2175](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2175.md) | Jumping to lower states yields 1/i visits | Corominas-Murtra, Hanel and Thurner (2015), [LIT-2997](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2997.md), read in [NOTE-2266](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2266.md). Sample-space reduction as a route to Zipf's law, with the exponent as the share of nested steps. Proved for uniform jumps only; a Markov chain with no reinforcement. Proposed until the derivation is checked independently. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2176](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2176.md) | Gamma superstatistics gives Tsallis statistics | Beck and Cohen (2003), [LIT-2962](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2962.md), read in [NOTE-2265](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2265.md). A letter: the mixture-of-exponentials construction in physics, with a gamma density giving the Tsallis form exactly and a universality result at small variance. It never says "power law"; which densities give one is the assistant's [CLAIM-857](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-857.md). Proposed until the published text or a second source confirms it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2177](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2177.md) | Exponential growth killed at random is Pareto | Reed and Hughes (2002), [LIT-3007](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3007.md), read in [NOTE-2264](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2264.md). Killing exponential growth at a random time gives power-law tails; with noise the law is a double Pareto whose exponents solve a quadratic. Support for its applications is visual. Proposed until the general double Pareto is derived independently. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2178](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2178.md) | Credit accrues to already eminent scientists | Merton (1968), [LIT-3002](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3002.md), read in a scan of the AAAS reprint in [NOTE-2268](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2268.md). The source of the name the record's cumulative-advantage claims use ([CLAIM-817](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-817.md)), and of the sense [TERM-145](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-145.md) keeps apart from the formal one. The sharp edge: the Matthew effect proper is credit for a given contribution allotted by rank, not growth in proportion to size; Merton states no proportional rule, credits the growth implication to Price, and calls the communication side "a special application of the self-fulfilling prophecy". Proposed until a study that holds contribution fixed confirms the effect. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2179](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2179.md) | Threshold systems self-organize to criticality | Bak, Tang and Wiesenfeld (1987), [LIT-2992](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2992.md), read in full in [NOTE-2269](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2269.md). The founding letter of self-organized criticality: a critical point "reached by starting far from equilibrium", with the percolation-of-minimal-stability heuristic, the sandpile automaton, and power laws judged by eye over two decades. It states no slow-drive, time-scale or conservation condition. It corroborates [CLAIM-841](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-841.md)'s bullet that SOC reaches a critical point without outside tuning ([ARG-178](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-178.md)), and its finite-size cutoff, asserted without data, is reproduced in [CLAIM-858](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-858.md) ([ARG-181](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-181.md)). Proposed until the reading is confirmed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2180](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2180.md) | Growth plus preferential attachment gives k^−3 | Barabási & Albert (1999), [LIT-3004](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3004.md), read in the arXiv preprint in [NOTE-2272](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2272.md). The record's source for the base case of [CLAIM-817](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-817.md) and the premise of [CLAIM-830](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-830.md), and for A3's sentence that attachment alone does not guarantee a power law ([ARG-179](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-179.md)). The sharp edge: the proposal that the mechanism is generic rests on four networks whose slopes were drawn by eye, the premise Broido and Clauset test ([THEORY-2172](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2172.md)). Proposed until the print text and a replication confirm it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2181](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2181.md) | Only linear attachment gives a power law | Krapivsky, Redner & Leyvraz (2000), [LIT-2974](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2974.md), read in [NOTE-2267](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2267.md). The record's source for the regimes of the attachment kernel, which [CLAIM-817](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-817.md) and [CLAIM-806](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-806.md) state and [ARG-184](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-184.md) takes them from. The sharp edge: the power law is the borderline case, k^(−3) only for A_k = k exactly, and the authors themselves say that for 0.8 ≲ γ ≲ 1 a stretched exponential and a power law are hard to tell apart up to k = 1000. Proposed until an independent derivation confirms it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2182](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2182.md) | Matrix random recursions have power-law tails | Alsmeyer and Mentemeier (2012), [LIT-3045](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3045.md), skimmed (introduction only) in [NOTE-2273](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2273.md) as a stand-in for Kesten (1973), [LIT-3005](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3005.md). Their Theorem 1.1 is the matrix form of the Kesten tail; their Remark 1 attributes the statement to Kesten "with one extra condition". The record's second-hand access to Kesten's matrix theorem. Proposed until the reading is confirmed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2183](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2183.md) | X = AX + B has a Pareto tail, index EA^κ = 1 | Kevei (2016), [LIT-3043](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3043.md), skimmed in [NOTE-2271](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2271.md) as a stand-in for Kesten (1973), [LIT-3005](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3005.md). Its introduction states the one-dimensional theorem with Kesten's hypotheses, its two-sided tail (c+ + c− > 0, so a tail may sit on one side only), the fact that EA^κ = 1 forces log-contraction, Grey's result that with EA^κ < 1 a regularly varying tail can come from B alone, and Goldie's Theorem 5.2 for the max form. It is the record's ground for [CLAIM-824](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-824.md)'s Kesten half, at second hand. Proposed until the reading is confirmed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2184](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2184.md) | BA model needs growth and linear attachment | Barabási (2016), [LIT-2968](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2968.md), read in the author's web edition in [NOTE-2270](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2270.md). A secondary source for the kernel regimes of [CLAIM-817](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-817.md) and [CLAIM-806](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-806.md) beside [THEORY-2181](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2181.md), and the record's source for the measured attachment exponents (α ≈ 1 for the Internet and citations, 0.9 ± 0.1 for co-authorship and actors). The sharp edge: its claim that preferential attachment is "necessary and sufficient", and that "all known models and real systems that are scale-free" have it, is a framing that reads geometric and optimisation models as generating attachment, which the record does not adopt ([CLAIM-817](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-817.md), [THEORY-188](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-188.md)). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2185](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2185.md) | Neural collapse hides fine-class sub-clusters | Yang, Steinhardt and Hu, [LIT-2957](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2957.md), read in [NOTE-2276](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2276.md). Neural collapse on coarse labels leaves the fine classes in the residual variation, linearly decodable after label-free clustering. Grounds [CLAIM-800](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-800.md)'s point that a geometric measure can saturate while finer information persists ([ARG-186](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-186.md)), and qualifies [THEORY-788](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-788.md). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2186](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2186.md) | Spike outliers can't increase with depth | Wang, Wu and Fan, [LIT-2984](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2984.md), read in [NOTE-2274](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2274.md). At random weights an input spike survives each layer only past a BBP-type test, and depth can only lose outliers and alignment. After training the rank-one weight update exists for any step size, but the weights' top singular value separates only above one threshold and the kernel's outlier needs a second condition. Grounds [CLAIM-799](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-799.md) as a third case of signal before outlier ([ARG-188](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-188.md)). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2187](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2187.md) | Turbulent energy causality runs large to small | Martínez-Sánchez and colleagues, [LIT-2965](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2965.md), read in [NOTE-2275](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2275.md). SURD measures predictive information among time series of a physical flux, so it keeps transfer and dependence apart as objects; its "causality" is prediction. An instance of [CLAIM-335](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-335.md)'s point ([ARG-185](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-185.md)), and a fit to [CLAIM-810](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-810.md)'s turbulence row that does not test its separations ([ARG-187](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-187.md)). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2188](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2188.md) | InfoNCE converges to a convex free energy | Cai and colleagues, [LIT-2975](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2975.md), read in [NOTE-2277](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2277.md). InfoNCE's large-batch limit is a passive, variational energy over the representation's law: one free energy with a Gibbs equilibrium for one modality, one joint energy with a repulsive cross-modal term for two. Grounds [CLAIM-798](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-798.md)'s weak reading and gives nothing toward its strong one ([ARG-189](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-189.md)). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2189](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2189.md) | CNN representations have low intrinsic dimension | Ansuini and colleagues, [LIT-2998](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2998.md), read in [NOTE-2278](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2278.md). Representations of trained CNNs lie near curved low-dimensional manifolds: a nonlinear estimate of their dimension is far below width and below a linear PCA count, which does not tell trained from random networks apart. [TERM-136](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-136.md) takes its intrinsic sense from this reading. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2190](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2190.md) | Hyperbolic cones make embeddings compatible | Bui, Yang, Chen, Neves, Ju, Ying, Shah & Zhao (2025), [LIT-2989](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2989.md), read in [NOTE-2281](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2281.md). Temporal cone restriction as a soft regularizer, and it works. The sharp edges: the hinge is weighted 0.3 and cone satisfaction is never reported; the cones are per item, between two separately trained models; one run per configuration; and the clipping radius must rise at every update, which the authors list as a limitation and which follows from the cone geometry ([CLAIM-860](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-860.md)). Proposed until replicated. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2191](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2191.md) | Bayesian influence flips sign during training | Lee, Smith, Adam & Hoogland (2025), [LIT-3001](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3001.md), read in [NOTE-2279](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2279.md). Influence as a susceptibility that changes at stage transitions. The sharp edges: the theory is for a Bayesian posterior split between two phases, and the link to SGD is the paper's "primary theoretical gap"; peaks are predicted only "under some conditions"; in the toy, the order of the peaks is the order of the modes' strengths. A.2 names the "Type-B" transition, equal loss with a falling LLC, without testing it. Proposed until reproduced. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2192](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2192.md) | Hyperbolic prototypes learn from coarse labels | Ghadimi Atigh, van Spengler, Long, Ayoughi, Kasarla & Mettes (2026), [LIT-2993](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2993.md), read in [NOTE-2282](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2282.md). Supervision as a region whose narrowness matches the label's specificity, with depth by radius. The sharp edges: coarsening is simulated uniformly at random; some leaf labels always remain; the prototypes are fixed, so nothing moves but the images; and the radial placement has to be enforced by a separate Busemann term, which hurts when few labels are coarse. Its "coarse-to-fine" names a label projection, not an order of learning. Proposed until replicated. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2193](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2193.md) | Features split by pitchfork long before seen | Yang (2026), [LIT-2961](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2961.md), read in [NOTE-2280](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2280.md). Rose, Gurewitz and Fox's annealing threshold made dynamic, with the crossing separated from the visible split. The sharp edges: the pitchfork is the probe's, and the probe is detached ("the encoder's gradients never see the probe"); the bridge from the probe's split to the network's grokking plateau is a tilt the paper adds by hand and calls empirical; the per-atom choice is made by noise and cubic terms on a shared unstable subspace, not by small initial advantages compounding. Proposed until reproduced. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2194](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2194.md) | No magnetic order in D ≤ 2 Heisenberg models | Gelfert and Nolting (2001), [LIT-3057](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3057.md), skimmed in [NOTE-2290](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2290.md) as a stand-in for Mermin and Wagner (1966), [LIT-2985](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2985.md). The proof's outline and the graph version are both at second hand: the bounds are stated "as has been shown by Mermin and Wagner", and Cassi's theorem is reported in one paragraph. It is the record's ground for [CLAIM-842](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-842.md)'s d_s ≤ 2 criterion as a theorem of spin models ([ARG-200](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-200.md)). Proposed until the originals are read. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2195](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2195.md) | No continuous symmetry breaking in 1D or 2D | Nachtergaele (2006), [LIT-3050](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3050.md), read in full in [NOTE-2289](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2289.md) as a stand-in for the statement of Mermin and Wagner (1966), [LIT-2985](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2985.md). A general proof in course notes; it bears on [CLAIM-842](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-842.md) by showing the theorem does not need a regular lattice. Proposed until confirmed in a published source. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2196](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2196.md) | Every current obeys the uncertainty relation | Gingrich and colleagues (2016), [LIT-2981](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2981.md), read in [NOTE-2291](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2291.md). The general proof of the thermodynamic uncertainty relation that Barato and Seifert ([LIT-1885](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1885.md), [THEORY-1268](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1268.md)) proved only in linear response and for unicyclic networks and otherwise conjectured: for every current of a Markov jump network, far from equilibrium included, and as a bound on the whole rate function, so on rare fluctuations as well as the variance. Long-time, steady-state, reversible transitions only. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2197](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2197.md) | 2D XY low-T phase is critical throughout | Drouin-Touchette (2022), [LIT-3055](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3055.md), skimmed in [NOTE-2295](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2295.md) as a stand-in for Kosterlitz and Thouless (1973), [LIT-2969](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2969.md). Standard results, derived at a student level and credited to Kosterlitz (1974) and José et al. (1977). Grounds [CLAIM-841](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-841.md)'s XY row with Kosterlitz's lecture ([THEORY-2206](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2206.md)) ([ARG-198](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-198.md)), and the BKT case of [CLAIM-862](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-862.md). Proposed until checked against the primary papers. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2198](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2198.md) | KPZ exponents depend on dimension | Le Doussal (2025), [LIT-3062](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3062.md), skimmed in [NOTE-2293](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2293.md) for one passage (p. 4). A summary by a specialist of results it cites, not derived here. Used to scope [CLAIM-841](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-841.md)'s KPZ row to d ≤ 2 ([ARG-195](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-195.md)) and for [CLAIM-862](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-862.md)'s higher-dimensional case. Proposed until the cited literature is read. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2199](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2199.md) | Ordered flocks scale with new exponents | Toner and Tu (1998), [LIT-2970](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2970.md), read in [NOTE-2285](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2285.md) (§V.B's algebra and §VI skimmed). The linear theory's loss of order in d ≤ 2 and the relevance of the convective terms below d = 4 are calculations; the d = 2 exponents rest on a new symmetry argument and a flow the authors call "highly probable"; the equations are posited from symmetry. It grounds [CLAIM-841](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-841.md)'s ordered-active-matter row by the diverging structure factor ([ARG-197](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-197.md)), marks the equilibrium limit of [CLAIM-842](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-842.md)'s d_s ≤ 2 criterion, and is one case of [CLAIM-862](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-862.md). Proposed until the order and the structure factor are confirmed independently. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2200](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2200.md) | Excess entropy is past–future information | Crutchfield and Feldman (2003), [LIT-3010](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3010.md), read from the 2001 arXiv preprint in [NOTE-2286](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2286.md). One derivative-and-integral hierarchy of the block entropy gathers the entropy rate, the predictability gain, the excess entropy and a new transient information. Excess entropy is "one kind of memory": equal for processes the transient information tells apart, and small for a source whose optimal predictor has infinitely many states. Drawn on by [TERM-141](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-141.md); corroborates [CLAIM-805](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-805.md)'s separation of entropy from memory. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2201](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2201.md) | Turbulent liquid-crystal fronts follow GUE TW | Takeuchi and Sano (2010), [LIT-2982](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2982.md), read in full in [NOTE-2284](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2284.md). The exponents (α = 0.50(5), β = 0.336(11)) and the GUE Tracy-Widom skewness and kurtosis are measurements over 563 runs; the three factors that make this system show KPZ when most experiments do not are argued, not tested. Grounds [CLAIM-841](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-841.md)'s KPZ row with Kardar, Parisi and Zhang ([THEORY-2202](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2202.md)), and qualifies its "generically" for experiment ([ARG-195](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-195.md)). Proposed until confirmed independently. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2202](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2202.md) | KPZ nonlinearity is relevant in one dimension | Kardar, Parisi and Zhang (1986), [LIT-2978](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2978.md), read in full in [NOTE-2287](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2287.md). The equation is argued from locality and symmetry; the one-dimensional exponents are exact by a fluctuation-dissipation theorem the letter cites rather than shows; the two-dimensional conjecture of superuniversality later failed (Le Doussal, [THEORY-2198](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2198.md)). Grounds [CLAIM-841](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-841.md)'s KPZ row for d ≤ 2 ([ARG-195](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-195.md)) and is one of the three cases of [CLAIM-862](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-862.md). Proposed until confirmed by an independent derivation. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2203](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2203.md) | Mermin–Wagner forbids only true long-range order | Halperin (2018), [LIT-3054](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3054.md), read in full in [NOTE-2296](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2296.md) as a stand-in for Mermin and Wagner (1966), [LIT-2985](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2985.md). The theorem's scope and its exceptions, as an author close to it states them. Marks the limits of [CLAIM-842](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-842.md)'s criterion ([ARG-200](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-200.md)), and why [CLAIM-841](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-841.md)'s XY row does not rest on Mermin–Wagner. Proposed until a second source confirms the scope. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2204](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2204.md) | Random networks compute best near chaos line | The NIPS 2004 companion ([LIT-3058](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3058.md)) of Bertschinger and Natschläger's Neural Computation paper ([LIT-2991](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2991.md), unreachable), read in its place in [NOTE-2288](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2288.md). The edge of chaos here is a damage-spreading line, K·P_bf = 1, crossing a wide range of mean activity; order is fading memory, and chaos fails because the state carries "spurious" information about initial conditions. The optimum is averaged over many tasks by design, with no per-task optima, so it qualifies rather than defeats [CLAIM-809](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-809.md) ([ARG-196](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-196.md)). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2205](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2205.md) | Macrostates are causal states of observables | Shalizi and Moore (2003), [LIT-2996](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2996.md), read in [NOTE-2294](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2294.md). Their answer to whether macrostates are objective or subjective is "both": the observables are the observer's, the causal states reached from them are fixed by the dynamics. "A different set of initial variables will, generally, lead to a different set of causal states"; "Nature has no preferred questions." Their emergence is a coarse-graining predicted more efficiently (argon: 0.87 against 0.5), held in [TERM-146](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-146.md). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2206](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2206.md) | 2D rotors have a topological ordered phase | Kosterlitz (2016), [LIT-3053](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3053.md), read in full in [NOTE-2283](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2283.md) as a stand-in for Kosterlitz and Thouless (1973), [LIT-2969](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2969.md). The first author's restatement, with the 1973 paper's errors named. It grounds [CLAIM-841](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-841.md)'s XY row with Drouin-Touchette ([THEORY-2197](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2197.md)) ([ARG-198](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-198.md)); it gives [CLAIM-694](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-694.md) the barrier condition; and it is one case of [CLAIM-862](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-862.md). Proposed until the primary papers are read. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2207](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2207.md) | Flow is higher at work, happiness at leisure | Rheinberg et al. (2007), [LIT-3071](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3071.md), read in [NOTE-2297](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2297.md). One of the record's two read in-episode studies of flow and affect, both found by [LEAD-054](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-054.md). Flow and happiness/satisfaction rated at each signal correlate r = .36 raw, .30 within-person, so some of flow's positivity is reported during the episode; it corroborates [CLAIM-441](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-441.md)'s premise that flow is reported as positive, against its third exit, weakly, since the correlation is pooled and flow is a continuous score. The sharp edge is the dissociation: goal-directedness lifts flow and not happiness. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2208](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2208.md) | Flow doesn't predict later valence | Engeser and Baumann (2014), [LIT-3070](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3070.md), read in [NOTE-2298](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2298.md). The more direct of the record's two read in-episode studies of flow and affect, both found by [LEAD-054](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-054.md). Within persons flow correlates .31 with valence and .59 with positive activation at the same signal, and does not raise valence at the next. It corroborates [CLAIM-441](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-441.md)'s premise that flow is positive during the episode, against the third exit that the positivity comes after it. The sharp edges: a continuous flow score with no enjoyment item, a two-hour lag, and a sample it appears to share with Rheinberg et al. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2209](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2209.md) | Ketamine raises approach under threat | Vestring et al. (2026), [LIT-3079](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3079.md), read in [NOTE-2300](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2300.md). The nearest design of a second kind that [LEAD-047](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-047.md)'s search found: a drug intervention on the arbitration of approach and avoidance with the objective threat fixed. The represented threat is not measured. Proposed until replicated with the session order counterbalanced. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2210](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2210.md) | Withholding avoidance didn't change expectancy | Sridhar, Biagi & Wake (2026), [LIT-3076](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3076.md), read in [NOTE-2299](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2299.md). The nearest design [LEAD-047](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-047.md)'s search found to an intervention on what governs action with threat belief measured. Its expectancy null is clean; its avoidance effect is not. Proposed until the avoidance effect is shown confirmatorily. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2211](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2211.md) | Lab motor skills decay faster than real ones | Tatel (2023), [LIT-2079](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2079.md), and the coded data posted for Tatel & Ackerman (2025), [LIT-3080](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3080.md). For accuracy the decline is 0.16 SD a month on laboratory tasks and about 0.05 on real-world tasks; the dissertation finds "less evidence" that real-world domains differ from one another, and in the posted data medical and dental tasks decline by 0.04 a month while sports and military or transport tasks show no measurable decline over intervals of a year at most. Speed shows the same trend, not significant. Task type is confounded with complexity and with the range of intervals studied. Proposed: one synthesis, by the same author, and the article unread. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2212](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2212.md) | Expected group continuity lowers prejudice | Simić, Sacchi and Perugini (2025), three Italian studies, the third a preregistered experiment (N = 252), read in full ([NOTE-2302](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2302.md)). The continuity is the group's with its own future, measured with future-self-continuity items; it correlated .14 with national attachment. The effects on prejudice and collective action needed a covariate outside the preregistration, and the moderation by attachment came from an analysis that left it. Nothing here concerns future people or legacy. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2213](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2213.md) | Negative impact frustrates without ill-being | Martela and Ryan, read in [NOTE-2303](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2303.md) (Read). Three preregistered MTurk experiments randomise a small gain or loss to the Red Cross within a key-pressing task. The loss is noticed, raising beneficence frustration (meta-analytic d = 0.84), but negative affect, anxiety and depression do not rise; the gain raises well-being. Registered as a stand-in, in part, for [LIT-1980](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1980.md). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2214](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2214.md) | Beneficence is an enhancer, not a need | Martela and Ryan, read in [NOTE-2304](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2304.md) (Read). Across three MTurk studies a new four-item beneficence-frustration scale correlates with every ill-being indicator but, entered after the three established frustration scales, adds no unique variance, and the three needs fully mediate it. The authors tentatively propose the category of basic wellness enhancer and call any conclusion about beneficence premature. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2215](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2215.md) | Identification buffers fans' commitment loss | Čater, Čater and Ivašković, read in [NOTE-2305](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2305.md) (Read). Two cross-sectional surveys (N = 172, 184) of fans recruited through fan clubs rate their commitment and loyalty now and, at once, if their club joined a Super League. All three identity dimensions predict a smaller imagined decline, cognitive most; commitment change carries loyalty change. The moderation by opposition is reported, but the simple slopes' signs do not plainly carry the authors' reading of it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2216](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2216.md) | Corporate agency must be moralised collectivism | Mulgan, read in [NOTE-2306](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2306.md) (Read). He sorts accounts of corporate agency into individualism and minimal, moderate and extreme collectivism, adds a "moralised" reliability condition, and argues from two imagined futures, broken and digital, that only moralised extreme collectivism is temporally robust. It reports Velasquez's individualism second-hand, enough to name its premises, not to assess them. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2217](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2217.md) | Recommenders inflate confidence via fluency | Dorsch, Coeckelbergh and Vierkant, read in [NOTE-2307](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2307.md) (Read). A theoretical paper, avowedly untested: since users of social media meet cross-cutting views, the harm of engagement optimization is not isolation but a recalibration of the metacognitive cues by which users judge their own beliefs, so that rejecting opponents feels warranted. The wording of the mechanism is the authors'; its central link, engagement as fluency, is assumed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2218](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2218.md) | Choice counts refine welfare's Pareto relation | Caliari, read in [NOTE-2308](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2308.md) (Read). An axiom on welfare methods, Informational Responsiveness, with neutrality, choice non-negativeness and Connection, characterizes weighted count refinements of the Bernheim–Rangel Pareto relation, correct for preference-monotonic choice models. In an experiment with 145 St Andrews students most violate WARP, and such methods cut expected false positives against stated rankings. Every welfare method is "implicitly model-based". | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2219](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2219.md) | Loot-box design features are largely unstudied | Ivern and Carbonell, read in [NOTE-2309](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2309.md) (Read). A PRISMA-ScR scoping review: 72 studies, 136 features in 22 subcategories and 6 categories, grouped by the problem they cause players and ranked by how often the literature names them. The authors find the impact and interaction of the features largely unstudied, and place the risk in interacting features within monetization systems rather than in any single one. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2220](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2220.md) | A flame self-maintains without closure | Mossio and Moreno, read in [NOTE-2311](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2311.md) (Read). A flame is far-from-equilibrium self-maintenance through one constraint; an organism has organisational closure, a set of constraints each maintaining another that maintains it. Closure is partial, holds among constraints not processes, and is direct. It is necessary for an organism, not sufficient. A stand-in, in part, for [LIT-536](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-536.md). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2221](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2221.md) | Regulation is second-order control | Bich, Mossio, Ruiz-Mirazo and Moreno, read in [NOTE-2310](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2310.md) (Read). Regulation is control exerted over the constitutive regime by a subsystem produced by it but dynamically decoupled from it, triggered by perturbations, that shifts the regime between viable states. Feedback depends on one constraint; closure is the mutual dependence of several. A stand-in, in part, for [LIT-536](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-536.md). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2222](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2222.md) | Risk of artificial suffering warrants a ban | Metzinger, read in [NOTE-2312](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2312.md) (Read). A moratorium until 2050 on research that aims at or knowingly risks synthetic phenomenology, on pathocentric and suffering-focused grounds; four necessary conditions of suffering (consciousness, self-model, integrated negative valence, transparency); and two designs that block suffering by blocking a condition. The conditions are stipulated from the author's self-model theory, not shown. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2223](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2223.md) | SDT continuum holds; integrated rung unmeasured | Howard, Gagné and Bureau, read in [NOTE-2313](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2313.md) (Read). Pooled correlations among the motivation types from 486 samples and 13 scales form a simplex that one dimension explains (99.75%), with unexplained heterogeneity near 99%. Integrated regulation correlates .913 with identified regulation, with overlapping intervals; the authors call it "practically indistinguishable" and ask for the theory or the measures to change. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2224](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2224.md) | Burning Man principles don't split self from gift | The 10 Principles, read in [NOTE-2314](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2314.md) (Read), from the organization's current page. Gifting "does not contemplate a return or an exchange for something of equal value"; decommodification is "In order to preserve the spirit of gifting"; Radical Self-reliance is only "discover, exercise and rely on their inner resources". The page has no revision date. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2225](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2225.md) | Future-self link to posterity is correlational | Syropoulos, Law, Coleman and Young, read in [NOTE-2315](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2315.md) (Read), from the 2024-05-21 manuscript. Self-oriented prospection correlates with responsibility for future generations across studies; mediation through identification is cross-sectional; and the two pre-registered experiments give a small effect on responsibility and then a null, with no effect on identification. The identification measure includes empathy and perspective-taking. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2226](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2226.md) | Winograd pair weakly violates CHSH | Lo, Sadrzadeh and Mansfield (2023), [LIT-3098](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3098.md), read in [NOTE-2316](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2316.md). The construction is theirs; that the response format leaves the marginals unobserved, so the test cannot see direct influences, is the reading's. The violation and its spread were recomputed from the paper's Table 1. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2227](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2227.md) | Frontoparietal rivalry activity tracks report | Brascamp, Blake and Knapen (2015), [LIT-3089](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3089.md), read in [NOTE-2317](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2317.md). Rivalry between two dot fields identical except for the eye they reach: switches occur, by matched alternation statistics, but are detected at chance; the fronto-parietal switch response then matches an eighth of the conspicuous response, with no causal remainder. It is the inconspicuous contrast [THEORY-094](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-094.md) names and supports that account's diagnosis for switch transients. Limit: BOLD and a switch transient, not percept-specific content, and six observers; it separates a perceptual change from awareness of the change, not experience from access. Proposed until confirmed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2228](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2228.md) | Prefrontal cortex tracks no-report rivalry | Kapoor, Dwarakanath, Safavi, Werner, Besserve, Panagiotaropoulos and Logothetis (2022), [LIT-3094](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3094.md), read in [NOTE-2318](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2318.md). 987 prefrontal units in two macaques, percept inferred from the optokinetic nystagmus, decoding up to 95%. It is report-free intracranial evidence that the content reaches prefrontal cortex. Limit: the switches were noticed ("unreported but clearly occurring"), so it does not remove post-perceptual cognition, and it neither promotes nor refutes [THEORY-094](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-094.md). Proposed until confirmed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2229](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2229.md) | Split-brain splits perception, not responses | de Haan et al. (2020), [LIT-3102](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3102.md), read in [NOTE-2319](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2319.md) as a stand-in for Pinto et al. 2017 ([LIT-3091](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3091.md)). "Perception appears to be more split, while responding remains largely unified"; "the body of evidence is insufficient" on the subject. It is independent evidence for the access half of [CLAIM-003](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-003.md) in a disconnected brain, argued in [ARG-202](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-202.md). Limit: a review, behavioural evidence, a lesioned brain, and no removal of post-perceptual cognition. Proposed until confirmed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2230](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2230.md) | A eukaryote can lack mitochondria entirely | Karnkowska, Vacek, Zubáčová and colleagues (2016), [LIT-1567](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1567.md), read in [NOTE-2320](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2320.md). Shown: none of 41 hallmark mitochondrial proteins and no credible candidate from broad searches, with Golgi proteins found as a control; SUF genes in the nucleus, with bacterial phylogeny shared with Paratrimastix. Not shown: that no organelle of wholly altered composition exists, which the authors say they cannot exclude. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2231](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2231.md) | Hodgkinia split six times in Tettigades | Łukasik, Nazario, Van Leuven, Campbell, Meyer, Michalik, Pessacq, Simon, Veloso & McCutcheon (2017/2018), [LIT-1586](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1586.md), read in [NOTE-2321](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2321.md). The authors also speculate, without testing, that splitting is nonadaptive for the host, begets more splitting, and makes the symbiont population harder to control; that reading is theirs and is not what this entry asserts. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2232](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2232.md) | Hodgkinia split differently in each cicada | Campbell, Łukasik, Simon & McCutcheon (2017), [LIT-1602](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1602.md), read in [NOTE-2322](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2322.md). The authors read the lack of convergence as evidence that the host does not dictate the splitting and that it is nonadaptive for the host; that reading is theirs. Not shown: whether the circles are separate cells. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2233](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2233.md) | Wasps deliver domesticated viruses to hosts | Strand, Coffman & Burke (2026), [LIT-2395](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2395.md), skimmed in [NOTE-2323](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2323.md). The domestication history is the review's report of others' work. It does not say that the wasp's control of the virus is complete: a wasp polymerase and wasp-derived virulence genes are part of the system. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2234](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2234.md) | Sign content comes from producer–consumer history | Millikan (2009), "Biosemantics", [LIT-3103](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3103.md), read in [NOTE-2324](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2324.md) from her pre-print. Her own short statement of the selection-based teleosemantics the record said it owed ([LEAD-018](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-018.md)). Teleology explains how a representation can be false; a mapping theory with producer and consumer explains what it represents. Corroborates [CLAIM-650](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-650.md) on its question (a), with a qualification argued in [ARG-204](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-204.md); grounds the objection [CLAIM-920](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-920.md) to [CLAIM-648](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-648.md). Proposed: one reading, of a compressed statement whose account of function is cited, not given. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2235](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2235.md) | Teleosemantics derives content from function | Neander and Schulte (2004; rev. 2022), SEP, "Teleological Theories of Mental Content", [LIT-3104](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3104.md), read in [NOTE-2325](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2325.md). A survey by two proponents, one of whom is surveyed. It reports the field's shape and its objections and settles little; the title asserts only what the survey reports. Read for [LEAD-018](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-018.md) beside Millikan's own statement ([THEORY-2234](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2234.md)). Proposed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2236](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2236.md) | Expecting repeat choices weakens self-control | Khan and Dhar (2007), [LIT-3113](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3113.md), read in [NOTE-2326](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2326.md) for [LEAD-078](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-078.md). A recurring choice is a licence unless it is seen as a precedent: the vice share rises from 46.6-57.5% in isolation to 70-90% when the same choice is announced for next week, and falls to 53% when the chooser is told this choice is the best indicator of the next. It bears on [THEORY-067](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-067.md)'s first promotion condition, in part, and on [QUESTION-034](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-034.md)'s bargaining route. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2237](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2237.md) | Choosing in a series raises patience | Schuhr (2015), [LIT-3114](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3114.md), read in part in [NOTE-2327](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2327.md) for [LEAD-078](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-078.md). In eight one-session treatments of about thirty students each, a free series of decisions raised the mixture probability of exponential discounting by 0.307 (p = 0.019), forcing the decisions together lowered it by 0.330, and stake size did not explain it. Evidence for bundling in humans without an imposed bundle; not for bundling by self-prediction, since every decision in the series is made at once. | Proposed |

Both near the efficiency bound of [THEORY-163](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-163.md). Stated without figures; later sources give 2018 and nine terms. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2239](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2239.md) | Bilinguals split green-blue without borrowing | Malik-Moraleda, Mahowald, Conway and Gibson (2023), [LIT-3108](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3108.md), read in [NOTE-2330](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2330.md) (supplement unread). Against 71 monolinguals, 30 bilinguals' Tsimane' colour terms have lower average surprisal (4.42 against 5.16), cover fewer chips, and overlap less with their neighbours; shandyes and yụshñus, one green-blue category for monolinguals (KL 0.10), separate (1.18). No Spanish term is borrowed. Between-group and colour only; the bilinguals also live in a more industrialised town. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2240](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2240.md) | Rising words displace neighbours if topic stable | Karjus, Blythe, Kirby and Smith (2020), [LIT-3105](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3105.md), read in full in [NOTE-2328](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2328.md). The equalization range (how far out in LSA space the neighbours' frequency losses sum to a rising word's gain) correlates with topical advection (the mean log frequency change of the word's top context words) in COHA, DTA, Estonian, Czech and Scottish Twitter corpora, p < 0.05 in each. airplane took its rise from aeroplane while aviation's topic was stable; famed and famous rose together with interwar celebrity. The measure is frequency, not range of use. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2241](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2241.md) | Brief mindfulness speeds responses briefly | Ge et al. (2024), [LIT-916](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-916.md), read in [NOTE-2331](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2331.md) for [LEAD-078](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-078.md). A dissociation of speed from discounting, not a test of whether discounting mediates a change in self-control: [ARG-206](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-206.md) holds that it does not show [CLAIM-156](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-156.md)'s route. | Proposed |

Proposed until replicated beyond one session and one small sample; it says nothing about cutting a person's own maintaining safety behaviour. | Proposed |

(2023), [LIT-3124](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3124.md), read in [NOTE-2333](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2333.md). Proposed until replicated in another sample; it is not evidence of hysteresis. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2245](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2245.md) | Common noise syncs uncoupled oscillator groups | From the reading of [LIT-2245](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2245.md) in [NOTE-2335](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2335.md), for [LEAD-023](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-023.md). Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |

Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2247](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2247.md) | Topological Kuramoto winding needs five cells | From the reading of [LIT-2253](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2253.md) in [NOTE-2338](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2338.md), for [LEAD-023](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-023.md). | [THEORY-2248](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2248.md) | Kuramoto locked states are cycle-flow solutions | From the reading of [LIT-2267](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2267.md) in [NOTE-2339](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2339.md), for [LEAD-023](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-023.md). The graph case of Bačić and colleagues' cell-complex result ([THEORY-2247](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2247.md)), by an overlapping group. Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2249](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2249.md) | Mori's GLE predicts nothing beyond its fit | From the reading of [LIT-2250](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2250.md) in [NOTE-2340](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2340.md), for [LEAD-023](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-023.md). Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |

| [THEORY-2251](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2251.md) | Balanced synchrony patterns form a lattice | From the reading of [LIT-2249](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2249.md) in [NOTE-2342](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2342.md), for [LEAD-023](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-023.md). The survey's landscape and cycle-space results, and its own list of what its methods do not cover. Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2253](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2253.md) | Wired sheaf machines are again machines | From the skimmed reading of [LIT-2258](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2258.md) in [NOTE-2344](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2344.md), for [LEAD-023](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-023.md). Composition preserves the conditions of realizability the paper defines; history-dependent validity does not glue. Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |

Extends Hansen and Ghrist's account ([THEORY-1088](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1088.md)) with selective rigidity and rate bounds. Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2256](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2256.md) | Switching agent networks form sheaf narratives | From the skimmed reading of [LIT-2262](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2262.md) in [NOTE-2347](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2347.md), for [LEAD-023](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-023.md). | [THEORY-2257](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2257.md) | Pairwise coupling yields higher-order phases | From the skimmed reading of [LIT-2239](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2239.md) in [NOTE-2348](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2348.md), for [LEAD-023](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-023.md). | [THEORY-2259](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2259.md) | Refinement types keep ML inference decidable | Freeman & Pfenning (1991), [LIT-3127](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3127.md), read in [NOTE-2350](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2350.md) for [LEAD-215](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-215.md). The paper that introduced refinement types. For the record it is the reading on which [CLAIM-949](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-949.md)'s correspondence of a descriptor with a refinement the entry inhabits can be tested ([ARG-209](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-209.md)), and on which its correspondence of the direction of fit with inferring against checking is found unsupported ([ARG-208](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-208.md), [CLAIM-965](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-965.md)). Proposed until the soundness theorem it states has a proof and the inference it describes an implementation. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2260](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2260.md) | Intersection types need a value restriction | Davies & Pfenning (2000), [LIT-3128](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3128.md), read in [NOTE-2351](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2351.md) for [LEAD-215](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-215.md). The paper that introduced bidirectional checking for intersection and refinement types. For the record it is the test, in a system where checking is a mode of its own, of [CLAIM-949](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-949.md)'s correspondence of the direction of fit with synthesis against checking, which it bears out narrowly ([ARG-211](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-211.md)), and of its clause that the move fitting a term to a type is elaboration or coercion, which it does not ([ARG-212](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-212.md), [CLAIM-974](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-974.md)). Proposed until its theorems are checked independently and its checker implemented as described. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2261](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2261.md) | Dual control trades performance for information |  | Proposed |

For the record it is the reading on which [CLAIM-949](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-949.md)'s descriptor as a refinement {x : A \| φ(x)} the entry inhabits is tested in the form the claim writes ([ARG-214](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-214.md)); on which inference is informative update and checking is not shown to be requirement ([ARG-213](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-213.md)); and which grounds [CLAIM-975](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-975.md), that a failed check does not show that the program fails. Proposed until its theorems' proofs are checked and its inference reproduced. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2263](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2263.md) | Value of information nonconcavity is an artifact |  | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2264](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2264.md) | Frontal tDCS raises mind-wandering | Axelrod, Rees, Lavidor and Bar (2015), [LIT-3135](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3135.md), read in [NOTE-2357](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2357.md). Two small experiments (n = 14 and 31). The causal clause is the authors' inference; the executive-capacity clause rests on a non-significant rise in target detection. The effect was replicated by the first author ([THEORY-2265](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2265.md)) and not in a pre-registered three-lab study ([THEORY-2266](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2266.md)), so the two accounts rival. It does not say that the stimulation changed the agent's awareness of its own thought or control, which was not measured, and so it is not a test of Metzinger's H1, which the 2017 chapter ([LIT-1945](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1945.md), p. 14) cited it for. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2265](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2265.md) | tDCS mind-wandering effect bypasses meta-awareness | Axelrod, Zhu and Qiu (2018), [LIT-3134](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3134.md), read in [NOTE-2355](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2355.md): a direct replication of [THEORY-2264](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2264.md)'s experiment (n = 85) with a meta-awareness probe added. The second clause is the authors' inference, that "at least in some cases mind-wandering might not be regulated by meta-awareness". It rivals the pre-registered null of [THEORY-2266](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2266.md). For the record it is the nearest the literature comes to Metzinger's H1, and it is not a test of it: the rated awareness is of attention's location, not of the capacity to end a thought, and it was not manipulated. It bears on [QUESTION-367](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-367.md) only as weak evidence that the rate of mind-wandering can move while the agent's self-rating does not. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2266](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2266.md) | Frontal tDCS fails to raise mind-wandering | Boayue and ten colleagues (2019/2020), [LIT-3133](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3133.md), read from the authors' preprint in [NOTE-2358](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2358.md): a pre-registered three-lab replication (n = 192) of [THEORY-2264](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2264.md)'s experiment, with d = -0.11 (HDI [-0.38, 0.17]), BF 10.65 for the null against a positive effect, and a replication Bayes factor of 0.002. The false-positive clause is the authors' inference. It rivals [THEORY-2264](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2264.md) and the first author's positive replication, [THEORY-2265](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2265.md), which it predates and does not discuss. Whether it corrects [THEORY-2264](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2264.md) is left to the owner. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2267](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2267.md) | Mandated digital friction can pass scrutiny |  | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2268](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2268.md) | Normative force is relative to constitution | Leffler, read in [NOTE-2360](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2360.md) (Read). Tested against invariance under desire change, ought-implies-can, ought-implies-can-fail and criticizability, only a reconstructed plight inescapability explains the force of norms constitutive of agency, and it makes that force relative to the agent's constitution: categoricity as constitution independence is out of its reach. The author calls the paper exploratory and defends none of the views as true. It is the adversarial test [LEAD-158](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-158.md) asked for; its application to organizations is [ARG-217](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-217.md). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2269](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2269.md) | Scaffolds can impose Darwinian properties first | Bourrat, Takacs, Doulcier, Nitschke, Black, Hammerschmidt and Rainey (2024), read in [NOTE-2362](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2362.md) (Read), a neighbour of [LIT-1940](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1940.md). A perspective piece: the two-peaks condition is borrowed from Doulcier et al. (2024) and the constructive route is proposed for future models. Its operative-cause definition assumes no feedback, which the constructive route is. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2270](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2270.md) | Transitions complete when scaffolds internalize | Bourrat (2022), read in [NOTE-2361](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2361.md) (Read). The criterion (§2, Table 1) grades collective properties as pseudo-Darwinian, Darwinian-like and Darwinian by the source of the mechanisms producing them; the model (§5-6) lifts one part of the scaffold, the migration ban, and leaves patches, their capacity and the periodic propagule generations in place. The author calls the result preliminary. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2271](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2271.md) | Neolithic was a transition in individuality | Shavit and Sharon (2023), read in [NOTE-2363](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2363.md) (Read). An opinion paper: the stage assignments are made by fit with a published archaeological synthesis, and the authors say they do not examine how far the case meets ETI criteria. It is the application of [LIT-188](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-188.md)'s sketch, not a test of it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2272](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2272.md) | Fairness meta-metrics can reverse rankings | Monnier et al., read in [NOTE-2364](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2364.md) (Read). A taxonomy of meta-metrics, m = f_a ∘ f_w ∘ f_c (comparison, weighting, aggregation), with synthetic and UCI Adult evidence that they reverse fairness rankings, and guidelines that match meta-metrics to the disparity pattern a context most needs to avoid. It takes the subgroups as fixed by prior deliberation, so it bears on how identified demands are weighed, not on who counts. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2273](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2273.md) | Entrenched elements resist evolutionary change | Wimsatt and Schank (2004), read in [NOTE-2365](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2365.md) (Read), a neighbour of [LIT-1926](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1926.md). The definition is the paper's; the simulations mostly assign selection coefficients by class rather than compute entrenchment, so they bear on differential selection in general. | Proposed |

On [QUESTION-129](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-129.md) it offers a procedural constraint on admissible perspectives, no self-certification and comparison across communities, for knowledge claims; whether it carries to normative standards is the question's. A survey's report of Griesemer, not Griesemer; one of its page citations points to the wrong paper. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2276](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2276.md) | Ott–Antonsen manifold attracts when Δ > 0 | Ott and Antonsen (2009), [LIT-3163](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3163.md), read in full in [NOTE-2378](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2378.md), as a supplement to the 2008 paper ([THEORY-2295](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2295.md)), whose open question it answers for the order parameter. The closed law is reached from outside the manifold whenever frequencies are spread; it fails without spread ([QUESTION-391](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-391.md)). It is what makes the 2008 reduction a serious candidate defeater of [CLAIM-478](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-478.md); the verdict is filed as alternatives ([CLAIM-1058](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-1058.md), [CLAIM-1088](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-1088.md)). Proposed until the attraction is confirmed independently. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2277](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2277.md) | PTSD delays first gaze to background context | Zidda, Steiger-White, Winkelmann, Ruttorf, Andoh, Nees & Flor (2025), [LIT-3174](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3174.md), read in full in [NOTE-2406](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2406.md). The nearest study found to the first half of [QUESTION-303](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-303.md); it has no recall manipulation, and its background does not disambiguate. Proposed until replicated. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2278](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2278.md) | Staple folding is cooperative in DNA origami | In "small origamis" of one 64-base scaffold and two staples, a staple's melting peak rises when the other is folded (48.5 to 51.5 °C outer, 41.5 to 50 °C inner, 67 to 72 °C and +1.5 °C for a second pair), and the inner position, where the path between a crossover's ends runs through the staple, costs more than the bulge-forming outer one. A model of local equilibria conditioned on bound neighbours, with a strong-correlation closure and no misfolds or kinetics, fits the annealing and melting curves and the hysteresis (4 to 10 K) of four rectangular M13 origamis. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2279](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2279.md) | Metastability is dynamics, not noise switching | Hancock, Rosas, Luppi, Zhang, Mediano, Cabral, Deco, Kringelbach, Breakspear, Kelso and Turkheimer (2024), [LIT-2266](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2266.md), skimmed from the accepted manuscript in [NOTE-2373](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2373.md). A review; the definition and the catalogue of routes are its own synthesis of the literature, the dwell-time test a proposal with computational support.
